proposals.risk: May still hit time limits or not run; test live first.

proposals.title: Wording honesty: placebo language, score vs probability, publishing rules
proposals.rationale: The placebo-statistics scripts set the honest vocabulary ('no detectable advantage'). B's replication shows PoT is mostly geometry, so users will often see '✕ NO EDGE' and conclude the tool is broken. TradingView forbids implying that a reverse-engineering attempt reproduces a closed script.
proposals.spec: README/description: EDGE = hit rate minus that of a matched random level at the same distance (placebo); state that PoT is mostly distance and volatility, and that the engine's value is which level and how far it delivers (ATR delivered). Terminal verdict: '✕ NO EDGE' becomes '≈ RANDOM' for z < 1 (2397-2398), keeping '~ WEAK' and '✓ EDGE'. Never call a score a probability; keep the 95% cap; never name the closed product or claim parity of results.
proposals.risk: None.

proposals.title: Balanced / no-draw ledger split and coverage (downgraded)
proposals.rationale: Abstention raises precision only when the selector carries information. B's replication found no gain (excess −0.1 pp balanced vs −1.1 pp clear, overlapping SEs). The display part moved into the COMP-4 hint; the measurement stays useful per chart.
proposals.spec: Ledger covN/covK (bars in the window and bars with an asserted DOL) giving coverage %; bool bal on Trial (set when dirSide == 0 and the buy and sell best scores are within balGap = 5), reported as CLEAR vs BALANCED excess and ATR delivered in Full view. Optional balMode 'Show both' draws the other side's best as a thin secondary via the 2170-2190 code; the default stays 'Show best' (decision history).
proposals.risk: balGap is arbitrary; adds ledger complexity.

result.summary: Wyckoff and supply/demand add almost nothing to "which liquidity is taken next" beyond race geometry and distance. Two independent detectors agree on 19 series (A's rolling frozen box; B's climax-anchored SC/BC → AR range). After a spring, the opposite edge is taken first at the same rate as geometry: excess −0.075 to +0.022 over nulls. UTADs, partial rises and declines, SOS/SOW and range edges are also null. Range edges, spring/UT extremes and the 50% AR level are reached at random-level rates, and extra touches add nothing. In the engine's density pillar, the inducement score is effectively a constant (≥ 2/3 on 86-98% of bars, 22 series) and coil is sign-unstable (≤ 1.6 pp). The registry re-entries (1848) and HTF FVGs (1862) also have a bug: they use the current bar's coil and inducement instead of the birth values. Pool age matters only at the ends: pools 5-10 bars old are reached 0.6-1.9 pp less, and intraday pools older than 300-500 bars 3-8 pp less. The maturation ramp at line 671 is about 10-15× too strong for young pools (≈ 4 score points, the size of the switch hysteresis). The only real signal is a price-only climax partial reversal on CME 5m: +6.6 pp vs bar-shuffled nulls and +6.8 pp vs a new time-of-day-stratified null, all 6 instruments positive. It sits in thin overnight and pre-open hours (+9 to +15 pp), not regular hours (−2 pp). It vanishes at 1H and flips to continuation on BTC 1H, consistent with liquidity-provision reversal (Nagel 2012). Volume adds nothing at 5m, 1H or daily, and the published volume conditioning of reversals conflicts in sign (Conrad-Hameed-Niden 1994 vs Cooper 1999). A new supply/demand test (10,019 zones) shows zones are revisited at random-level rates, and departure strength and base length have no consistent effect. Fresh vs tested differs by only 0-3 pp, for reaction only. Continuation zones react better than reversal zones, the opposite of the school's claim. Re-reading Bulkowski at the source confirmed A's partial rise/decline and busted-rectangle numbers (B1's corrections are reverted). None of them has a baseline, and "tall/wide patterns outperform" is volatility scaling. No published test of P&F count targets exists. The domain's contributions are subtraction (WYK-1, WYK-2), one learned timeframe-scoped climax bit (WYK-3), and an honest Wyckoff label layer that shows each event's per-chart rate against geometry (WYK-4). A's range gate and liqEvt fix are superseded by REG-3/REG-2 and ICT-9.

concepts.name: Trading range (TR), creek and ice
concepts.definition: Causal frozen box, two detectors. (1) Rolling: at confirmed bar t, hi = highest(high,N)[1], lo = lowest(low,N)[1], N 20-50. Qualify if 1.5·ATR ≤ hi−lo ≤ 6-8·ATR (slow ATR) with touches = bars within 0.25·ATR of an edge, ≥ 3 bars apart. Bulkowski requires ≥ 3 touches on one boundary and ≥ 2 on the other, which matches Lo-Mamaysky-Wang's 5 alternating extrema. (2) Canonical climax-anchored: SC/BC (new 20-bar extreme, range ≥ 2·ATR, vr ≥ 2.5 or a price-only variant), then an AR rebound ≥ 2·ATR within 10 bars, confirmed by a 1·ATR close back, width 2-8·ATR, 'confirmed' after 15 bars, failed after 3 closes > 1.5·ATR outside. Before the first ST, a swing beyond the AR edge extends the range (it is not a UT); above 8 ATR the candidate is a trend. A spring does not end the range.
concepts.dolRole: The edges are the two obvious pools. Wyckoff claims Phase D moves at least to the opposite edge. In data, which edge goes first is pure geometry.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Lo-Mamaysky-Wang 2000: rectangle-conditioned return distributions differ in shape, not direction (KS p ≤ 0.002; strong for shape only). A: first edge taken = geometry (−0.056 to +0.022); range edges reached at random-level rates (+0.001 ± 0.019, n 479); 2/3/4+ touches +0.000/−0.031/−0.084. quant_regime: ranges do not raise pool magnetism.
concepts.engineNotes: No horizontal or climax-anchored TR state. f_structure 708-782 is a leg-following dealing range. EQ merge at eqTol 0.10 ATR (1111-1137) and stacks at 0.75 ATR (1230-1251) turn range edges into ladders of pools. Regime selection is covered by REG-3/REG-2; labels by WYK-4.

concepts.name: Spring / shakeout
concepts.definition: low < frozen TR low, close back inside (lo < close < hi) on the bar or within a 3-bar reclaim deadline (8 in some detectors). Depth (lo−low)/ATR ≤ 1.5. Re-armed after a close ≥ 1·ATR off the edge. Optionally valid only after ≥ 1 ST. Volume class by vr = vol/SMA20[1]: light ≤ 0.8, moderate 0.8-1.5, heavy > 1.5. The type numbers are inverted between sources (Evans/Pruden #1 = heavy terminal shakeout; FibAlgo Type 1 = low volume), so label by words. A break on climax volume (vr ≥ 2.5) is a failed pattern per SRFX.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: target the opposite edge (creek), with the spring low as invalidation. Data: no directional information beyond geometry.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A (rolling box, 7 datasets, 4 settings): opposite edge first 12-37% vs geometry 16-26%; excess −0.075 to +0.016 (SE ≈ 0.04). B canonical range: +0.007 ± 0.032 (n 209), +0.018 ± 0.027 (n 301), +0.022 ± 0.040 (BTC). Turtle Soup (bias_dol): −0.129 to +0.082. Sibling Market Profile 80% rule: 25-28% vs a 27-29% base. No public backtest with a baseline exists (W14, W26, W31).
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt 1580-1582 casts every close-back-inside raid as a reversal vote into D (wL 0.30); the fix is ICT-9 (REJECT neutral). induceBar 892-895 counts mini-springs as density (WYK-1).

concepts.name: Upthrust / UTAD
concepts.definition: Mirror of the spring at the TR high: high > hi, close back inside within the reclaim deadline, depth ≤ 1.5·ATR. UTAD = an upthrust late in distribution that exceeds a prior UT high (or follows ≥ 1 ST).
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: target the range low (ice), with the UT high as invalidation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: excess −0.034 to +0.037 (n 79-186); range-low magnet −0.073 ± 0.032 / −0.013 ± 0.034. B canonical: −0.024 ± 0.038, −0.049 ± 0.032, +0.079 ± 0.044 (BTC). UT highs retaken at random rates.
concepts.engineNotes: Same liqEvt reversal mapping (1580-1582), superseded by ICT-9.

concepts.name: Failed breakout by close (busted range)
concepts.definition: A close outside the frozen TR, then a close back inside within 3 bars; the breakout extreme is the stop. Bulkowski 'bust': after the breakout, price moves ≤ 10%, reverses and closes beyond the opposite side.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: a strong move to the opposite edge and beyond.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bulkowski, re-read at the source in B2: '51% of rectangle tops will bust' (66% single, 3% double, 31% triple busts); single-busted downward breakouts rise 71% on average vs 51% for non-busted tops. These are % moves with no baseline; A's figures are confirmed and B1's correction reverted. price_action T4: closes back inside within 5 bars 53-64% vs null 48-53%, so failures are slightly more frequent than random. A: upthr_cl +0.09 to +0.16, but signs are mixed per dataset and spring_cl ≈ 0.
concepts.engineNotes: Only breakers from OBs that took liquidity (1646-1661) and iFVG on close-through (1599-1627). No range-level bust state; WYK-4 measures it per chart.

concepts.name: Selling/buying climax (SC/BC) and automatic rally/reaction (AR)
concepts.definition: SC: new 20-bar low, range ≥ 1.5-2.0·ATR[1], close in the upper half (or upper wick > 50% for BC), after a down-leg (SMA50 or regression slope); classic form vr ≥ 2-2.5. Price-only variant used in tests: new 20-bar extreme, range ≥ 2·ATR[1], close in the far half. AR = a rebound ≥ 2·ATR within 10 bars (or ≥ 0.5 retrace of the climax run); AR50 = 50% of the 21-bar leg. BC/AR mirror.
concepts.dolRole: After a climax, the AR (50% of the leg) is the first counter-draw, then the climax extreme is retested. This works only at ≤ 5m and in thin hours.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B, CME 5m price-only SC: AR50 first +6.6 ± 2.5 pp vs bar-shuffled null (6/6 instruments) and +6.8 ± 2.5 vs a ToD-stratified null (B2). By ET bucket: overnight +9.2 ± 3.1 (n 231), 08:30-09:30 +15 ± 9 (n 26), RTH −2 (n 102). BC +3.8 ± 3.2. CME 1H −2.6 / +3.4; BTC 1H −3.5 ± 2.2 / −6.5 ± 2.8 (continuation). A at 1H/daily: AR50 at random rates. Literature: drift bursts ~71% partial reversals in 5 min; Zawadowski: 60-min shocks retrace with t 7.9; Nagel 2012: reversal returns rise when liquidity is scarce. Volume splits change nothing.
concepts.engineNotes: Bar volume is used only in the volume profile (978-1015, 1945-1947). Add only as a learned, zero-prior ICT-1 bit (WYK-3), optionally split by session.

concepts.name: Secondary test (ST) / tests of a level
concepts.definition: Wyckoff ST: a revisit of the SC area on diminished volume and spread, holding at or above it; a confirmed swing inside the 30% of the range nearest the climax edge, up to 3 per range. Engine test: a bar within 0.30·ATR of a pool that does not take it, ≥ 3 bars after the previous test.
concepts.dolRole: Wyckoff: a held test means the edge holds, so target the other side. ICT: tests add stops, so the pool is a bigger draw. Neither is supported for reach.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: tests 0/1/2/≥3 edges −0.010/−0.011/+0.003/+0.027 (36,724 checkpoints); ict_liq T1 tests == 1 +1.4 ± 0.8 pp. B: after a confirmed AR on CME 5m, the climax extreme is traded through before the AR extreme +5 pp vs geometry, which contradicts 'the ST holds' at 5m; null at 1H and BTC.
concepts.engineNotes: track() 650-656 and 0.35·min(tests,6) in x (682): a positive weight without support; neutralised by ICT-10/OF-3/SMC-3.

concepts.name: SOS/SOW, JAC, BUEC/LPS/LPSY
concepts.definition: SOS: a close beyond the range high by ≥ 0.5·ATR (vr ≥ 1.5 if volume-gated), or within 10 bars of a spring a close above the range midpoint before the spring low breaks. JAC = the SOS through the creek; BUEC/LPS = the low-volume pullback to it. SOW/LPSY mirror.
concepts.dolRole: After a JAC the target is the next pool beyond the range; the LPS is an entry, not a target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: spring+SOS excess −0.145 to −0.006; UT+SOW −0.088 to −0.027 (small n). B canonical: SOS measured move −0.067 / −0.111 / +0.029, SOW +0.101 / +0.037 / +0.023 (sign-unstable). No published statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: BOS on a body close through the last swing (1542-1547), displacement (897-904) and the OB from the BOS leg (1663-1748) are the SMC restatement. No change; WYK-4 labels only.

concepts.name: Partial rise / partial decline
concepts.definition: Inside an established TR, a swing that turns before getting close to the opposite edge. Test: a 3-bar fractal low above lo + 0.33·height after the top was touched in the last N/3 bars; race top vs bottom.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed to predict the breakout side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bulkowski, re-read in B2 (bull markets 1989-2013, 5,959 patterns): partial decline → up 80% (rect bottoms) / 91% (tops); partial rise → down 74% / 57%. Rectangle pages: 75% / 77% / 79%. A's figures are confirmed and B1's correction reverted. None has a baseline: A's geometry gives 0.71-0.81 and the excess is inconsistent (−0.135 to +0.080).
concepts.engineNotes: Leave missing; proximity and race geometry already capture it.

concepts.name: Phases A-E / schematics
concepts.definition: A: stopping action (PS, SC, AR, ST). B: building the cause. C: test (spring, or a higher-low test). D: SOS/LPS ('price will move at least to the top of the TR'). E: markup. Re-accumulation ranges are shorter.
concepts.dolRole: Phase labels would name the draw edge (Phase D means the opposite edge).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Labels are provisional until markup confirms them. No public backtests (Villahermosa; MQL5: phase detection 'requires subjective judgment'). Markov-regime analogues (arXiv 1812.02527) and LSTM detection (arXiv 2403.18839) test no targets. The vendor engine W20 shows a multi-week stock drift; 5-day alpha is n.s.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended; WYK-4 shows events, not phases.

concepts.name: Composite operator
concepts.definition: Interpretive stance: read all action as if one large operator were accumulating or distributing.
concepts.dolRole: None observable; it motivates 'liquidity grabs'. The measurable mechanism is stop clustering and cascades (Osler 2003/2005), which allows both continuation and reversal.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Unfalsifiable.

concepts.name: Cause and effect: P&F horizontal count, measured move
concepts.definition: P&F count: columns across the TR from the LPS/spring leftward by whole phases; target = count × box × reversal (3), added to the low or LPS. Measured move: breakout edge ± range height.
concepts.dolRole: Sizes the next leg (a magnitude target, not a liquidity pool).
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published test of count-target accuracy (both B passes); StockCharts calls counts rough estimates. P&F signal rules: Anderson & Faff 2008, 'mixed statistical significance'. Bulkowski measured move met 78-79% up / 54-55% down with no baseline. Tall/wide patterns outperform in 85-100% of pattern types, but in % moves (volatility scaling). A: MM first 0.571 vs geometry 0.565; long vs short cause +0.015 vs −0.003.
concepts.engineNotes: Leave missing; no liquidity behind it and no evidence.

concepts.name: Effort vs result (volume, VSA, Weis waves)
concepts.definition: vr = vol/SMA20[1]; sr = (high−low)/ATR; clv = (close−low)/(high−low). Absorption: vr ≥ 2 and sr ≤ 0.8. No demand: a narrow up-bar on volume below the previous 2 bars. Weis wave: volume summed per zig-zag swing. On ≤ 5m, normalise vr by time of day. Guard symbols without volume with ta.cum(nz(volume)) == 0.
concepts.dolRole: Heavy effort without result at a level is claimed to mean the level holds (reversal); a low-effort breakout is suspect.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Baseline fact: volume rises with |Δp| (Karpoff 1987). The direction of volume conditioning conflicts between studies: high-volume reversal (CGW 1993, CHN 1994) vs decreasing-volume reversal (Cooper 1999). A: volume terciles do not change continuation or throwback at swept pools (n 1,823). B, 5m: low-effort climaxes revert at least as much as high-effort ones; relative volume adds ≤ 3 pp OOS R² at 1H and nothing at 5m. Bulkowski: high-volume breakouts 'failures triple', and rectangle bottoms do better on light volume.
concepts.engineNotes: Volume feeds only the profile path cost (1945-1947) and LVNs. Do not add volume weights; WYK-3 is price-only.

concepts.name: Range-bound density / coiling
concepts.definition: Engine: overlap = Σ(high−low,20)/(highest20 − lowest20); coil = clamp((overlap−2)/4, 0, 1), read at level birth. De-saturated display: ta.percentrank(overlap, 300)/100.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed (reference spec): pools formed after coiling are bigger draws.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A (6,246 pivots): high coil −0.019 vs −0.008. B (24,544): low/mid/high −0.022/−0.011/−0.006. The sign flips between studies (≤ 1.6 pp); quant_regime finds no effect on 23 series. Percentile terciles are flat.
concepts.engineNotes: 886-891; 0.25·coil (683), 0.30·coil for arrays (687). Bug: 1848 (registry re-entry) and 1862 (HTF FVG) pass the current coilScore; births at 1703/1744/1762/1774/1874/1884 are correct. WYK-1 replaces it with the population mean 0.55 by default.

concepts.name: Inducement sweeps (indScore)
concepts.definition: Engine: induceBar = wick through the 5-bar extreme with the close back inside; indScore = min(1, count over 20 bars / 3). De-saturated: a sweep of the prior 20-bar extreme by ≥ 0.10·ATR with the close back inside, counted over densLen.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: inducement before a pool forms makes it a bigger draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: indScore ≥ 2/3 on 86-98% of bars across 22 series in two implementations (median per-series mean 0.93): a constant. The de-saturated count 0/1/≥2 gives −0.022/−0.008/−0.013 (A) and −0.007/−0.014/−0.007 (B): no signal.
concepts.engineNotes: 892-895; 0.15·induce (683) and 0.20·induce (687) add a near-constant; same birth bug at 1848/1862. WYK-1: neutral constant 0.93.

concepts.name: Equal highs/lows build-up
concepts.definition: Engine: a new same-kind pivot within 0.10·ATR merges into a live pool (eqCount += 1) and the pool moves to the outermost print.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: more resting stops, so a bigger draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A (34,868 checkpoints): eqCount 0/1/≥2 edges −0.007/−0.028/−0.049. Sibling E6: equal prints add < 1 pp at matched distance; ict_liq T1: EQ +0.5 ± 1.6 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: Merge logic is fine (1111-1137); the 0.9·eqCount weight (682) is unsupported and is handled by ICT-10/OF-3.

concepts.name: Liquidity freshness / maturation
concepts.definition: Engine (671): fresh = (0.35 + 0.65·(1 − e^(−age/(0.25·halfLife))))·0.5^(age/(4·halfLife)), halfLife 150. That gives 0.43 at age 5, 0.69 at 30, 0.85 at 100, 0.56 at 500 and 0.32 at 1,000.
concepts.dolRole: Claims older, 'matured' pools are bigger draws.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: ≤30/31-150/151-500/>500 give −0.011/−0.007/−0.018/−0.001. B (≈190,000 checkpoints, 5 groups): age 5-10 is −0.6 to −1.9 pp in 4 of 5 groups; intraday age > 300-500 is −3 to −8 pp; middle ages are sign-unstable; daily equities retake very old highs more (trend). The ramp costs a new pool ≈ 4.2 points (= hyst), worth ≈ 15 pp of reach on the proximity scale, for a ≈ 1 pp effect.
concepts.engineNotes: 671: drop the ramp, keep the decay (WYK-2, also adopted by OF-3).

concepts.name: Supply/demand zones (RBR/DBR/RBD/DBD, base, departure)
concepts.definition: Base = longest run of k ≤ 6 bars with |body| ≤ 0.5·ATR[i−1] and combined range ≤ 1·ATR. Departure = the next m ≤ 3 bars all closing one way with body sum ≥ 1.5·ATR. Demand zone = [base low, highest base body]; supply mirror. Reversal type (DBR/RBD) if the 5 bars before the base moved against the departure. The odds enhancers (departure strength, time at level, freshness, profit zone, R:R, HTF) use a scoring that is not published (Online Trading Academy).
concepts.dolRole: An unfilled zone is claimed to be a retracement draw, and a strong departure a stronger zone.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2 test (sdzones.py, 15 series, 10,019 zones, nulls): proximal-edge reach vs S(d) +0.7/+1.6/+3.0/−0.7 pp (CME 1H/5m, BTC 1H, daily), i.e. random-level rates. Departure terciles and base length 1/2/3-6 show no consistent sign; the null-adjusted excess is volatility clustering, not zone memory. ICTPD-1: larger displacement lowers fill. No published quantitative test of odds enhancers.
concepts.engineNotes: OB = a 1-candle base from the BOS leg (1663-1748); departure = qual (910-912, 1692, 1735) adds density 0.5·qual (687), unsupported and neutralised by ICTPD-1. No multi-candle base: leave it.

concepts.name: Fresh vs tested zones
concepts.definition: A zone is fresh until its first touch (wick into the zone); later touches count only after price left by ≥ 0.5·ATR. The zone dies on a trade-through of its distal edge.
concepts.dolRole: First-touch zones as the preferred reaction points.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2: first-touch reaction (+1 ATR before distal − 0.1 ATR, vs geometry) excess +1.2/−0.6/+2.2/+0.6 pp; first minus second touch +2.5/+3.1/0.0/+0.6 pp (≤ 2σ). Reach is unaffected. S/R bounce memory points the other way (Garzarelli 2014; Chung-Bellotti 2021); vendor OB tests show fresh OBs react slightly more.
concepts.engineNotes: 673 (array half-life), 1566-1577 (partial-fill crop), 1693-1700 / 1736-1741 (skip mitigated OBs). Keep; no extra weight.

concepts.name: Zone type: reversal (DBR/RBD) vs continuation (RBR/DBD)
concepts.definition: Reversal if the 5 bars before the base moved against the departure direction; otherwise continuation.
concepts.dolRole: The school claims reversal zones are stronger. The data show with-trend (continuation) zones hold slightly better, which is a trend effect.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2: first-touch excess, continuation vs reversal: +0.055 vs −0.027 (CME 1H), 0.000 vs −0.013 (5m), +0.042 vs +0.003 (BTC), +0.059 vs −0.032 (daily). All 4 groups favour continuation (+1.3 to +9.1 pp), each ≤ 2σ. This is a reaction effect, not reach.
concepts.engineNotes: OBs mix both types (1663-1748). At most a measurement row (ICTPD-8); no score change.

concepts.name: Time at level / base length
concepts.definition: The number of base candles before departure; the school says fewer is stronger ('the less time at a level, the more out of balance').
concepts.dolRole: Ranks S/D zones.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2: reach by base 1/2/3-6: −0.3/+4.9/−0.1 pp (CME 1H), +2.3/+0.3/−0.0 (5m), +2.1/+3.3/+6.3 (BTC), −0.1/−2.0/−4.1 (daily). Reaction shows no pattern either. Moderate evidence of no effect.
concepts.engineNotes: Leave missing (correct).

concepts.name: Throwback / BUEC to a broken edge
concepts.definition: After a close-breakout from a TR, price returns to the broken edge within K bars.
concepts.dolRole: The broken edge as a near-term draw after a breakout.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bulkowski: 64-66% throwback/pullback (no baseline); throwbacks hurt performance in 97% of pattern types. A: 0.870 vs a random level at the same distance 0.872, i.e. pure proximity.
concepts.engineNotes: Swept pools are deleted (1583-1589); no special handling needed.

proposals.title: Coil and inducement: neutral constants at their population means, birth-value bug fix, de-saturated display and learned bits
proposals.rationale: indScore is a constant (≥ 2/3 on 86-98% of bars, 22 series, two implementations), and coilScore is sign-unstable (≤ 1.6 pp across three studies). Together they control up to 0.40 of pool density and 0.50-0.60 of array density, i.e. up to 5.5 points (pools) and 7-9 points (arrays) of noise, more than hyst. The siblings disagree: ICT-10 keeps the terms, ICTPD-1 raises them to 0.30/0.30, and OF-3 drops them while rescaling. Replacing them with population means removes the variance but keeps each family's mean, and so the pool-vs-array balance. Registry re-entries (1848) and HTF FVGs (1862) read the current bar's values instead of birth values, a bug in both modes. The B2 supply/demand test confirms that zone-strength attributes do not change reach.
proposals.spec:
1) Input after line 140: string densIn = input.string("Neutral", "Coil / Inducement Weight", options=["Neutral","Classic"], group=G_SCORE, display=display.none, tooltip=...).
2) Constants after 307: const float COIL0 = 0.55, const float IND0 = 0.93 (median per-series means).
3) evaluate() before 681: float cz = densIn == "Classic" ? this.coil : COIL0; float iz = densIn == "Classic" ? this.induce : IND0. Use cz/iz at 683 and 687, and in ICT-10's and ICTPD-1's replacement lines.
4) Birth fix: type Ext (365-372) gets float coil = 0.55, float ind = 0.93. In f_pushExt (1211-1225, inside if not dup): int off = bar_index − nz(aBar, bar_index); cB = off >= 0 and off <= 450 ? nz(coilScore[off], COIL0) : COIL0 (same for indScore); Ext.new(..., hlm, cB, iB). At 1848 pass e.coil, e.ind. At 1862: offH = bar_index − nz(aHF, bar_index), guarded ≤ 450. History offsets may be series int; the buffer is max_bars_back = 500 (line 32), and reading beyond it is a runtime error (limitations.md 375), hence the guard.
5) De-saturated display at global scope after 895: coilPct = nz(ta.percentrank(overlap, 300))/100 (length series int, reference/ta.md 1155-1166; 300 to stay clear of the 500 buffer); sweep20 = (high > hh20[1] + 0.10·atr[1] and close < hh20[1]) or the mirror; sweepN = math.sum(sweep20 ? 1 : 0, densLen). Tooltip: 'Coil pctl 71 · sweeps 2 (shown, not weighted)'.
6) If ICT-1 lands: bits COIL (birth coilPct ≥ 0.67) and SWEPT (birth sweepN ≥ 2), zero prior, gate |z| ≥ featZ and n ≥ 100. The score then rises only where this chart's ledger shows the effect, which is the honest form of the spec's 'density' claim.
7) Pick ICT-10's or OF-3's liquidity line, not both; under either, arrays use cz/iz (ICTPD-1 Neutral array dens = 0.844).
8) README: equal prints, tests, coiling and inducement are measured and shown, not weighted by default.
Measure via a Neutral vs Classic A/B on overall EDGE z (2385-2402), the per-family hit-vs-expected rows and the target switch rate (SMC-2).
proposals.risk: Low. The Classic option keeps the original. Individual scores move by at most ±5.5 (pools) / ±9 (arrays) points while family means are unchanged. Markets where coiling truly matters lose that until the ICT-1 bit learns it.

proposals.title: Liquidity freshness: drop the young-pool maturation ramp, keep the slow decay, learn age effects per chart
proposals.rationale: Line 671 gives a 5-bar-old pool fresh 0.43 vs 0.85 at 100 bars: ≈ 4.2 points at wFresh 10, equal to the switch hysteresis and worth ≈ 15 pp of reach on the proximity scale. The measured young-pool deficit is only 0.6-1.9 pp (4 of 5 data groups). Old intraday pools (> 300-500 bars) are reached 3-8 pp less, which the existing decay already reflects (0.56 at 500, 0.32 at 1,000). The ramp delays switching to new, nearer pools by 30-40 bars and turns structure changes into target lag.
proposals.spec:
Input after line 138: string freshLiq = input.string("Flat", "Liquidity Freshness", options=["Flat","Maturing"], group=G_SCORE, display=display.none, tooltip=...).
evaluate() 669-671: if this.isLiquidity(): float dec = math.pow(0.5, age/(4.0·halfLife)); this.fresh := freshLiq == "Flat" ? dec : (0.35 + 0.65·(1 − math.exp(−age/(0.25·halfLife))))·dec. Arrays are unchanged (673).
If ICT-1 lands: bits YOUNG (bar_index − bornBar ≤ 2·pivLen, hlMult-scaled for HTF/STF like line 667) and STALE (age > 300 hlMult-scaled bars), zero prior, gated. On daily equities the ledger can learn the opposite sign. OF-3 adopts the same Flat line, so implement it once.
Measure via a Flat vs Maturing A/B on DOL HIT %, EDGE z, BARS→HIT and the SMC-2 switch rate.
proposals.risk: Very low: it removes an oversized shape and keeps the evidence-consistent decay.

proposals.title: Price-only climax partial reversal as a learned, timeframe- and session-scoped candidate-ledger feature
proposals.rationale: On CME 5m, after a price-only selling climax, the 50% retrace of the leg comes before the extreme is retaken +6.6 ± 2.5 pp more than in bar-shuffled nulls, and +6.8 ± 2.5 pp more than in a time-of-day-stratified null (6/6 instruments). The effect sits in thin hours (overnight +9.2 pp, 08:30-09:30 ET +15 pp; regular hours −2 pp). That matches liquidity-provision reversals (Nagel 2012), drift bursts and Zawadowski. At 1H it vanishes, and on BTC 1H it flips to continuation (−3.5/−6.5 pp), so a fixed weight is wrong on half the charts; a gated learned lift is right on all of them. Volume adds nothing, so A's three volume features are replaced by two price-only bits.
proposals.spec:
Requires ICT-1 (candidate ledger); otherwise skip.
Global series (SERIES section): cxA = nz(atr[1], atr); scB = low < ta.lowest(low,20)[1] and high−low ≥ 2·cxA and close−low ≥ 0.5·(high−low); bcB = the mirror; legH = ta.highest(high,21); legL = ta.lowest(low,21).
State: var int cxBar = na, var int cxDir = 0, var float cxExt = na, var float cxMid = na, var bool cxOff = false. On confirmed bars (engine step 1, 1534-1547), if scB: cxBar := bar_index, cxDir := 1, cxExt := low, cxMid := low + 0.5·(legH − low), and cxOff := the bar is outside the main session when TIME-1's session state exists (else false). Mirror for bcB.
Bits at the probe snapshot when bar_index − cxBar ≤ 10: CLXREV (lv.side == cxDir and the near edge between close and cxMid + 0.5·atr) and CLXEXT (lv.side == −cxDir and the near edge within 1 ATR beyond cxExt). With TIME-1, set CLXREV only if cxOff.
Zero prior, ICT-1 gate (|z| ≥ featZ, n ≥ 100), bounded ±featB. ICT-1 grows from 16 to 18 bits; no volume variants.
Optional Terminal 'SC'/'BC' tiny labels sharing WYK-4's ring buffer.
Measure via ICT-1's per-bit lift and z. Expected: positive on ≤ 5m index futures off-session, ≤ 0 on 1H+ and crypto 1H.
proposals.risk: Feature-count creep and multiple comparisons in ICT-1 (mitigated by the gate and bounds). The CME 5m sample is only 3 months; the ledger, not this study, should decide per chart.

proposals.title: Wyckoff range layer: canonical range box, AR/Spring/UTAD/SOS/SOW labels and alerts with zero forecast weight and per-chart rates against geometry
proposals.rationale: Traders read ranges in Wyckoff terms, but the events do not predict the next draw: spring and UTAD excess is ≈ 0 across two detector families and 19 series, null-controlled. Published Wyckoff scripts paint 'SPRING' as a buy signal. The best of them shows per-chart counts (Spring → SOS, SOS → target) without a geometry baseline, which misleads because raw rates mostly reflect where price sits in the box (spring top-first 12-37% vs geometry 16-26%; partial declines 70-93% vs 71-81%). Showing 'rate here vs geometry (n)' is honest and differentiating. A's draw-neutral range gate, regime-split ledger and in-range liqEvt change are superseded by REG-3, REG-2 and ICT-9.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (new group 'Wyckoff', all display.none): useWyk false, wykVol true (volume gate when hasVol = ta.cum(nz(volume)) > 0), wykNeedST true, wykBox false.
Detector (confirmed bars, O(1), var state wM 0 idle / 1 climax / 2 range, wD ±1, wX, wY, wLo, wUp, counters):
- Idle → climax: an scB-like bar with close < ta.sma(close,50) (global), range ≥ 2·ATR[1], and vr ≥ 2.5 when volume-gated. Mirror for BC.
- Climax → range: extend wX on deeper extremes before the rebound (≤ 10 bars). Rebound ≥ 2·ATR within 10 bars; confirm on a 1·ATR close back; abandon after 30 bars; width 2-8·ATR else abandon. Emit AR.
- Phase A extension: before the first ST, a swing beyond the AR edge extends wUp/wLo (not a UT); re-check the 8·ATR cap and drop the candidate as a trend if it fails.
- ST: a confirmed pl/ph (879-880, no new ta call) in the 30% of the box nearest the climax edge, up to 3.
- Range: confirmed after 15 bars. Fail on 3 consecutive closes > 1.5·ATR outside or after 300 bars; 15-bar cooldown after a failure.
- Spring/UTAD: penetration ≤ 1.5·ATR, a close back inside within 3 bars, re-armed by a close ≥ 1·ATR off the edge, counted only after ≥ 1 ST if wykNeedST. vr ≥ 2.5 on the penetrating bar is labelled 'BREAK (heavy vol)'. Labels use words (light/heavy vol), never #1/#3, because the numbering is inverted between sources.
- SOS/SOW: a close beyond by ≥ 0.5·ATR (vr ≥ 1.5 if gated); the range ends.
- Name range-edge pools: a new Level field bool rngEdge set on the nearest BSL/SSL within 0.25·atr of wUp/wLo (f_findLiq 1090-1107); f_levelName (518-530) returns 'RANGE H'/'RANGE L'. No score change.
Honesty ledger, separate from f_book (the stN arrays have size 5, and f_book loops array.from(t.grp, 4) at 1470, so grp = 5 would be out of range and would pollute roll50/ttHit/raceSt/cluSt): type WEvt {int kind, int side, float tgt, float stp, float p0, int bar0}; var array<WEvt> wOpen (cap 20); var arrays wN, wK, wP of size 5 (AR, SPRING, UTAD, SOS/SOW, BREAK). Targets: AR → climax extreme (stop AR extreme); SPRING → range high (stop spring low); UTAD → range low; SOS/SOW → measured move (stop opposite edge). Resolve on confirmed bars: strict trade-through of tgt = win, of stp = loss; both in one bar, or bar_index − bar0 ≥ H, drop. On a decision wN += 1, wK += win, wP += p0.
Display: Terminal only, a 10-label ring buffer like the ghosts (1253-1263), e.g. 'SPRING · opp. edge first 29% vs 28% geo (n 14)', greyed below n 20. Clean shows nothing unless wykBox draws one dashed box at 88% transparency extended on tailBar.
Alerts: alert() with rate vs geometry and n, freq_once_per_bar_close, plus one alertcondition 'Wyckoff Event'.
Budget: 1 box, ≤ 10 labels, ≤ 20 open records, no request.* calls. State stays in var globals (functions cannot reassign fundamental-type globals).
An event type with a stable per-chart excess can be promoted to an ICT-1 bit.
proposals.risk: Label clutter (Terminal only, off by default) and small-n rates (shown with n, greyed below 20). The state machine needs care with var resets. Detection lags by the AR confirmation, which is acceptable for labels with zero weight.

result.summary: Auction market theory and profile levels add almost nothing to "which liquidity is taken next" once distance, clock time and volatility state are controlled. That is now replicated on CME, on BTC (B5) and by an independent distance-matched study on QQQ/SPY. Naked POCs are revisited 85% vs 84% for random prices at the same distance. HVN pull, poor-high repair, the 80% rule and a composite failed-auction rule are all null or negative (BTC far-edge −11.1 pp, z −5.6). The one concrete bug A found is confirmed, but its mechanism is corrected: the ×1.10 thin-path bonus (line 1947) goes to a class that is 63-86% made of targets beyond the composite range, put there only by the f_row clamp. Those beyond-range targets have no ranking edge (within-snapshot lift 0.99-1.06). In-range thin paths rank worse on CME (within-bar −5.8 / −6.8 pp at 120 / 240 h) and are neutral on BTC. The ×0.85 thick-path penalty is unsupported: its sign flips with depth and asset. So AMT-1 now uses thin ×0.97, thick ×1.00, beyond ×1.00, and returns na outside the range instead of clamping (A had beyond ×0.95). New: the largest bar-level effect in this domain is volatility state. By ATR14/ATR120 tercile, targets beat or miss the random level by +2.9 / −1.7 / −5.3 pp on CME and +6.1 / −1.9 / −7.7 pp on BTC (z up to −12). This explains away the composite-range effect and most of the pooled beyond-range deficit, and it strengthens REG-1 / QPOT-03. New methodological finding: pooled feature lifts, as ICT-1 specifies them, mix regime with ranking power (e.g. LVN_BAR pooled 0.60 vs within-snapshot 0.83 on BTC). Because lv.mult only re-ranks candidates within a bar, AMT-2 amends the ledger to cohort-demeaned lifts from synchronised snapshots every H bars. That also cancels bar-level pBase bias. A's acceptance damping flips sign on BTC, so it becomes a ledger bit only. LVN rejection weakens to +1.6-2.5 pp, and 0.0 for the SMC-7 trough definition, so LVN-based invalidation is dropped. A's poor-extreme eqCount idea is dropped: the null evidence and ICT-10 both argue against it. Two engine defects not in A's report: LVN zones that straddle the current price are never drawn, and on symbols with no volume every profile feature is silently disabled. AMT-4 and AMT-5 fix these.

concepts.name: Volume-profile path cost (LVN = fast path, HVN = wall)
concepts.definition: vf = mean smoothed composite volume over the rows between close and the target's near edge, divided by the profile mean (engine: rolling 120×1H composite, 48 rows, 60% of each bar's volume over its range, 40% over its body, 1-2-1 smoothing). Engine classes: vf<0.6 thin → ×1.10; vf>1.4 thick → ×0.85. Correct handling: a target outside [vpLo, vpLo+rows·vpStep] is 'beyond range' and gets no vf (na), not a clamped tail-row average.
concepts.dolRole: A ranking multiplier between candidates at the same bar. It should reflect whether a target behind thin or thick volume is reached more or less often than other candidates at the same distance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: That the current mapping is wrong is moderate evidence (4 datasets, within-snapshot design). The ×0.97 thin default rests on weak evidence. B1 (pooled, week clusters): 63-86% of the engine thin class is beyond range. In-range thin −3.5 pp (CME 120h, z −1.8), −0.7 (BTC). Thick +2.3 / +5.4 / −0.9 (CME 120/48/240h), +2.5 (BTC, z 3.2). B2 (within-bar, the relevant test): thin −5.8 (z −2.6) / −6.8 (z −3.0) / −2.4 n.s. on CME 120/240/48h, +1.1 n.s. on BTC. Thick +5.2 / +0.9 / −2.8 / −0.5 (sign flips). Beyond −0.8 / −0.2 / −0.6 / +2.5. B7: the pooled beyond deficit is mostly volatility ratio (BTC coefficient +0.06 n.s. with vr; CME −0.22, z −2.4). Speed through LVN: +7-9% at 15 min (A); +7.9 pp [+0.5, +15.8] NQ (ULTIMA); none at 1H.
concepts.engineNotes: 151-152 input and tooltip ('thin paths score higher'); f_row clamp 570-571; f_pathVol 1417-1424 (clamps targets outside the profile onto tail rows); multiplier 1945-1947. About 32% of pivot candidates get ×1.10 just for being outside the 120h composite; in-range thick targets get an unjustified ×0.85. README line 52 repeats the wrong claim. Fix: AMT-1.

concepts.name: Composite volume profile (and time-at-price fallback)
concepts.definition: Volume at price aggregated over a rolling window or several sessions, built from OHLCV by spreading each bar's volume over its range (60%) and body (40%) in equal-height rows, then smoothed. If the symbol has no volume, the Market Profile original (time at price: every bar weighted 1) is the natural substitute.
concepts.dolRole: The map from which LVN, HVN, POC and VA are derived. Infrastructure, not a predictive claim.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Infrastructure. Pine limits checked: request.security_lower_tf ≤ 100K intrabars on non-professional plans; request.footprint() is Premium/Ultimate-only and one call per script, so it is unusable in the main engine.
concepts.engineNotes: Present: 978-1015 (1H feed via request.security('60') with [1] and lookahead_on, or request.security_lower_tf above 1H), 1052-1057 cache, 1384-1414 f_profile, 1900-1909 rebuild. Missing: a no-volume fallback. lvV.push(nz(h1V)) at 997 / 1007 gives vpMean = 0, so on cash indices and CFDs every profile feature is silently off (AMT-5).

concepts.name: Point of Control (POC) and naked/virgin POC
concepts.definition: POC = the row with the most volume or TPOs (POC ties: CQG picks the row nearest the range midpoint). Naked POC = a completed session's POC that no later bar range has touched; it retires on the first touch (bar high ≥ POC ≥ bar low). Proper test: fill hazard by age against a random level at the same distance and clock time.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed magnet / DOL target ('84-87% revisited').
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null or negative against distance-matched baselines on three independent samples. CME (A): prior POC −1.5 pp (H=30, n 879); 83.6% vs 84.7% at H=115; naked POCs aged ≥2 sessions −2.3 / −4.7 pp. BTC (B5): naked POCs aged ≥2 days −2.7 (z −5.8) at 24h and −6.1 (z −5.3) at 120h; prior POC +2.2 at 24h, −0.3 at 120h. ULTIMA QQQ/SPY (721 sessions): naked POC 85% vs 84% random (+1.9 [−0.5, +4.3]); prior POC holds 19% = random. NQ practitioner +3.8 [−1.0, +8.6] n.s. tradeify: 77-79% revisit, median 1 session.
concepts.engineNotes: Not computed (vpSm max never exposed). Correctly absent as a target source; display or value-state context only (AMT-3).

concepts.name: Value area (VAH/VAL)
concepts.definition: The band around the POC holding about 70% of volume or TPOs. One-row expansion: start at the POC, repeatedly add the larger adjacent row (TradingView tie rule: the row closer to the POC, then the higher one; many tutorials: the upper row wins) until ≥ 70%. VAH = top of the highest included row, VAL = bottom of the lowest. Sierra / CBOT variant: compare pairs of rows. Edges are settings-sensitive (70%→80% moved the ES VAH on 31 of 49 sessions).
concepts.dolRole: Edges as targets or fades; value state as context; infrastructure for the IN_VALUE / EXT_FROM_VALUE ledger bits.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Against VA edges as targets. CME prior VAH/VAL 0.0 / −2.8 pp at H=30 (A); fine RTH −3.0 / −1.8. Bounce at VAH/VAL ≈ random (B8: −0.8 / +1.9 pp at 1 ATR). Value does not overlap the prior VA on 42% of sessions (tradeify).
concepts.engineNotes: Not computed. AMT-3 adds it as Terminal context only (default off), using one-row expansion in step 15 after vpCum (1909).

concepts.name: HVN / LVN nodes
concepts.definition: HVN = a local profile maximum (> 0.7·peak). LVN = a trough, typically between two HVNs. SMC-7 definition: strict local minimum over ±8% of the rows with depth ≥ 0.15·peak, tails excluded. The engine instead marks runs of rows < 0.30·peak (shoulders, not troughs).
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: HVNs stall or pull price; LVNs reject or are crossed fast; LVNs bound balance areas.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B8 (week clusters, distance-matched random levels): LVN (A's definition) bounce +2.5 pp (CME, z 2.0), +1.6 (BTC, z 1.7); SMC-7 troughs +1.7 (z 1.2) CME, +0.05 BTC. HVN +0.2 / +0.6; POC −0.9 / +1.1. External NQ: LVN reject-or-run −0.3 pp [−5.0, +4.4] (n 863); HVN pull +0.8 [−0.1, +1.7] (n 10,908); faster through LVN +7.9 [+0.5, +15.8]. A's +3.2 pp (z 2.9) was inflated by day clusters and a random baseline that was not distance-matched.
concepts.engineNotes: 2250-2287 draws threshold runs, off by default. Three defects: not distance-limited; a run straddling close is never drawn (the loops test zTop<close and zBot>close only); no semantics, while the tooltip and README imply acceleration. HVNs unused (correct). Fix: AMT-4 display; LVN_BAR ledger bit (AMT-2).

concepts.name: LVN barrier count in the path
concepts.definition: nBar = number of SMC-7 troughs strictly between close and the target's near edge (inside the composite).
concepts.dolRole: Candidate ranking feature: targets behind several thin troughs lie outside the current balance area.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Within-bar, ≥2 troughs: CME 120h −5.7 pp (z −2.5), BTC −3.5 (z −2.8); CME 48h / 240h ≈ 0. Pooled lift strongly confounded (BTC pooled 0.60 vs within-snapshot 0.83).
concepts.engineNotes: Not computed. Ledger bit LVN_BAR in AMT-2 (learned lift only, neutral prior).

concepts.name: Single prints and tails (excess)
concepts.definition: tradingstats definition: rows with exactly one 30-minute TPO, at tick resolution, forming a zone ≥ 2 ticks, excluding day extremes, sandwiched by multi-TPO areas; filled when a later day's range covers the whole zone. Tail/excess = ≥ 2 single rows at the session high or low.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed unfinished business to be filled; tails as completed auctions.
concepts.evidenceNotes: tradingstats (3,847 zones, no baseline): D+5 fill 63-67%, full reversal of the day 6-10%; after 7 days unfilled, P(ever) < 50%. A (n=98): full fill 53.1% vs 63.9% baseline (−10.8 pp). Tailed extremes vs baseline +0.3 to +1.7 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: The FVG origin lockout (135-137, 689-690) already encodes the continuation reading. No change.

concepts.name: Poor highs/lows (unfinished auction)
concepts.definition: TPO: ≥ 2 TPOs at the extreme row (flat, no tail). Bar proxy: ≥ 2 separated bars within tol·ATR of a session extreme, i.e. an equal high or low at the extreme (same geometry as EQH/EQL).
concepts.dolRole: Claimed strong magnet (the extreme should be repaired).
concepts.evidenceNotes: CME hourly proxy +1.6 pp (z 1.1; A). BTC: flat PDH/PDL −2.2 pp vs plain −1.8; touch count not monotonic (PDH 4+ −16.9). NQ practitioner study +1.0 pp [−2.8, +4.8] vs tailed extremes. ULTIMA QQQ/SPY: no better than random at the same distance. A's statement that no statistic exists is outdated.
concepts.engineNotes: Chart-swing EQ fold (95, 1111-1139); key-level trackers (807-863) keep only the extreme. Not worth closing: null evidence, and ICT-10 neutralises EQ density. At most an optional POOR_EXT ledger bit.

concepts.name: Initial balance and range extension
concepts.definition: IB = first RTH hour (09:30-10:30 ET, A+B). Range extension = trade beyond the IB; extension levels IB ± k·IB. Caution: tradeify's 589-session test used a 2-hour IB (09:00-11:00 hourly periods).
concepts.dolRole: IB extremes as same-day targets; extensions as profit targets; day-type handicap.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Descriptive (tradingstats 2015-25, verified): breaks 97.8% / 96.2%; median extension 63.6% / 55.6% of IB; ES 18.8% reach +100% up; C-period close beyond the IB → 45.5% reach 100%; first break failed 34%. IB-high-first days break down 44.8% vs up 24.0% (no baseline, partly geometry). As targets vs a clock-matched baseline: IBH −0.4, IBL +2.2 pp (A).
concepts.engineNotes: Not implemented and not worth it: hit rate equals random; RTH-specific.

concepts.name: 80% rule and composite failed auction ('look above/below and fail')
concepts.definition: 80% rule: open outside the prior VA, then two consecutive 30-minute periods back inside → reach the far edge. Composite version (B3): 1-3 hourly closes beyond the composite VAH (VAL), then a close back inside → target the far VA edge or the POC.
concepts.dolRole: Would make the far VA edge a high-probability target after a failed probe.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Evidence against the rule. tradeify: 25.0% / 28.1% vs a 28.7% / 27.2% base rate (hourly version); 30-minute version n = 5 / 8. A: 61.9% vs 54.0% (n 42, n.s.). B3: CME far edge −2.9 / +3.4 pp n.s.; BTC −4.0 (z −2.1) / −11.1 (z −5.6); race far-edge-first vs probe re-break 0.5 / −2.4 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; rejected.

concepts.name: Value migration / close vs value as bias
concepts.definition: Today's VA vs yesterday's (higher, overlapping-higher, inside, outside, overlapping-lower, lower); developing POC/VA drift; close location vs POC or VA.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed directional bias (which side's liquidity is taken next).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Evidence against the bias. 1,273 sessions, logit on log distance ratio (z 16.5) plus features: migration χ² 1.05, close vs POC 0.17, close vs VA 5.6 with mean-reverting signs (A). NQ practitioner: dPOC direction in the first two hours −0.5 pp [−3.0, +2.1] (n 1,482).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; rejected as a bias.

concepts.name: Acceptance beyond value (composite value state)
concepts.definition: Acceptance = ≥ 3 consecutive hourly closes beyond the composite VAH or VAL; probe = 1-2; rejection = back inside.
concepts.dolRole: AMT claims acceptance → continuation (targets further from value).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Within-bar, away-from-value vs toward-value targets at the same bar: CME −2.7 / −4.3 (z −2.0) / −3.2 pp (48/120/240h); BTC +2.3 (z +1.6). The sign flips across asset classes. Pooled lift CME 0.92-0.96, BTC 0.96.
concepts.engineNotes: No value state. A's damping multiplier (×0.95) is dropped; the bit EXT_FROM_VALUE goes in the AMT-2 ledger only.

concepts.name: Volatility state as confound (vol ratio)
concepts.definition: x = ln(ATR_fast / ATR_slow), e.g. ATR14 / mean TR over 120 bars, or REG-1's ATR5/ATR100. Captures volatility clustering plus mean reversion: the same ATR distance is 'far' right after a spike and 'near' in compression.
concepts.dolRole: Conditions PoT and the random-level baseline. Explains spurious 'level' effects (beyond range, wide composite, acceptance).
concepts.evidenceNotes: B7, hit vs clock-matched base by vr tercile: CME +2.9 / −1.7 / −5.3 pp (z 3.5 / −2.7 / −6.7); BTC +6.1 / −1.9 / −7.7 (z 10.7 / −4.1 / −12.0). log vr coefficient −0.85 (CME, z −9.9) and −1.32 (BTC, z −20). It absorbs the composite-range-width effect fully, and the beyond-range effect on BTC. Agrees with quant_regime (REG-1) and quant_pot (QPOT-03).
concepts.engineNotes: sUp/sDn (1061) are keyed by HTF regime only; f_empPoT / f_potModel / f_potBase (1284-1322) and trial pBase (1430) ignore volatility state. Owned by REG-1 (which includes f_potBase); AMT-2's cohort demeaning protects the feature lifts meanwhile.

concepts.name: Baseline / PoT time-of-day matching
concepts.definition: The random-level baseline and the PoT surface conditioned on clock time (or a volatility clock), because ATR-normalised reach varies strongly by hour.
concepts.dolRole: An honest PoT, an honest EDGE verdict, and fair feature lifts.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A, E-OWN-0: without clock matching every session-anchored family shows spurious −6 to −11 pp edges (PDH −11.6, z −9.3); with matching 0 to −3 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: 1059-1062 and 1284-1322 split by HTF regime only; trial pBase (1430) inherits the bias. Owned by TIME-2 / TIME-3.

concepts.name: Pooled vs within-snapshot (ranking) lift
concepts.definition: Pooled lift = ((k_b+2)/(e_b+2)) / ((k_all+2)/(e_all+2)) over all probes with bit b. Within-snapshot lift = 1 + Σ_b (y_i − pBase_i − r̄_snapshot) / Σ_b pBase_i, where r̄ is the mean residual of all candidates snapped at the same bar. This is the fixed-effects / conditional-logit identity.
concepts.dolRole: Multipliers (lv.mult) only re-rank candidates within a bar, so they must be fitted to within-snapshot effects. Pooled effects belong to the PoT key or calibration.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B6, pooled vs within on the same probes: VP_OUT 0.85-0.92 vs 0.99-1.06; LVN_BAR (BTC) 0.60 vs 0.83; IN_VALUE 1.04-1.12 vs 0.97-1.03; PATH_THICK 1.03-1.16 vs 0.97-1.06. Pooled estimates overstate effects or invert them.
concepts.engineNotes: f_calMult (1376-1382) uses a pooled per-family lift; ICT-1 / CAL-3 specify pooled per-feature lifts. Multiplier semantics: 657 (mult reset), 693-695 (score = raw × mult), 1303-1311 (PoT does not use mult). Fix: AMT-2 (cohort-demeaned lifts).

concepts.name: Open types (OD/OTD/ORR/OA) and day types
concepts.definition: Dalton open types classified from the first 30 minutes; day types from the IB extension (normal ~85% of the range in the IB; trend > 2×IB extension closing near the extreme; neutral = extension on both sides; etc.).
concepts.dolRole: Early handicap of trend vs rotation, and of which early extreme holds.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A second search again found no published hold-rate statistics. One TradingView script embeds private numbers.
concepts.engineNotes: RTH-specific and judgement-heavy; rejected.

proposals.title: Fix the volume-profile path cost: na beyond the profile (no clamp bonus), neutral thick, mild thin penalty
proposals.rationale: Line 1947 gives ×1.10 to a 'thin' class that is 63-86% clamped beyond-range targets, which have no ranking edge (within-snapshot lift 0.99-1.06). It also gives ×1.10 to in-range thin paths, which rank worse on CME (within-bar −5.8 / −6.8 pp at 120/240h, z −2.6 / −3.0) and are neutral on BTC. It gives ×0.85 to thick paths, whose within-bar sign flips (+5.2 / +0.9 / −2.8 / −0.5 pp). The subsystem is on by default, so it currently adds ±10-15% of wrong-signed noise to about 60% of candidates. About 32% of pivot candidates get ×1.10 just for lying outside the 120h composite.
proposals.spec: G_SCORE inputs, all with display = display.none: vpThinM = 0.97, vpThickM = 1.00, vpOutM = 1.00 (input.float, minval 0.5, maxval 1.2, step 0.01, with tooltips stating the measured semantics). Replace f_pathVol (1417-1424): res = na by default; if rows > 0 and vpStep > 0 and vpMean > 0 and b >= vpLo and b <= vpLo + rows*vpStep, compute the vpCum average as now. A clamped 'a' (close outside the profile) is acceptable. Replace 1945-1947 with: if usePathVP and vpSm.size() > 0 and vpMean > 0: float vf = f_pathVol(close, lv.nearEdge()); lv.mult *= na(vf) ? vpOutM : vf < 0.6 ? vpThinM : vf > 1.4 ? vpThickM : 1.0. Rewrite the usePathVP tooltip (151-152) and README line 52: thin paths get a small measured penalty, not a bonus. With AMT-2, the class maps to bits VP_OUT / PATH_THIN / PATH_THICK, and a gated learned lift replaces the input. Do not multiply both.
proposals.risk: Small effects (2-7 pp), measured on CME index futures, CL and BTC. Other assets may differ, hence the mild defaults plus learning. The change alters which pool wins in some states near the 4-point hysteresis threshold, so the overhaul verify step should compare SELECTION EDGE before and after.

proposals.title: AMT feature bits on the candidate ledger with cohort-demeaned (within-snapshot) lifts; amends ICT-1 / CAL-3's pooled estimator
proposals.rationale: Multipliers only re-rank candidates within a bar (657, 693-695; PoT at 1303-1311 ignores mult), yet ICT-1's pooled lift mixes regime with ranking. B6 on the same probes: VP_OUT pooled 0.85-0.92 vs within 0.99-1.06; LVN_BAR on BTC 0.60 vs 0.83; IN_VALUE 1.04-1.12 vs 0.97-1.03. A pooled fit would learn a wrong ×0.85-0.92 for VP_OUT. Centring each probe's residual by its snapshot's mean residual also cancels, to first order, the bar-level pBase biases from clock (−6 to −11 pp, A) and volatility state (±6-8 pp, B7). The lifts are then robust before REG-1 / TIME-2 land. Every AMT effect is ≤ 7 pp and sign-unstable across assets, so per-chart learning is the only honest default.
proposals.spec: Synchronised cohorts. Every H bars (na(cohBar) or bar_index - cohBar >= H), inside inCalc and past warmup, in step 17 after the evaluate loop (after 1948): (1) Finalise the previous cohort: unresolved probes get y = 0; skip cohorts with fewer than 2 probes; r̄ = mean(y - pBase); for each bit b: s_b = Σ_{i∈b}(y_i - pBase_i - r̄); fR[b] += s_b; fV[b] += s_b²; fN[b] += n_b; fE[b] += Σ pBase. (2) Clear and snapshot every pool level with 0.25 <= d/atr <= maxATR (cap 128) as Probe{side, liq, edge, pBase = f_potBase(d, side), mask, y = -1}; set cohBar := bar_index. Grading in step 2b on every confirmed bar, using f_step's hit rule (1436). Lift: 1 + fR/fE; z = fR/sqrt(fV); w = fN/(fN + featN0); m_b = |z| >= featZ and fN >= 100 ? clamp(1 + w(lift - 1), 1 ± featB) : 1. Reuse ICT-1's inputs (featN0 60, featB 0.15, featZ 2.0). Apply Π m_b, clamped 0.80-1.25, in the 1939-1948 loop. AMT bits: VP_OUT (na vf with a valid profile); PATH_THIN (in range, vf < 0.6); PATH_THICK (vf > 1.4); LVN_BAR (≥ 1 SMC-7 trough between close and the edge; troughs computed into var array<float> lvnPx at each profile rebuild); NEAR_EDGE (in range, ≤ 1 ATR from the composite edge on the target's side); IN_VALUE and EXT_FROM_VALUE (need AMT-3); optional POOR_EXT. type Probe goes after Trial (396); state goes after 1079. UX: Terminal 'PROFILE · this chart' block with lift, n and z per bit. Clean style unchanged.
proposals.risk: Probes in a cohort share a price path; the cohort-as-cluster variance handles it. Single-candidate cohorts are skipped, so sparse charts learn slowly while the gate keeps bits neutral. Must be merged with CAL-3 / CAL-4 into one ledger, not a second one. CPU: ≤ 128 × (NF + 6) operations per H bars and ≤ 128 hit tests per bar; negligible.

proposals.title: Composite value area and value state (POC / VAH / VAL; inside / probe / accepted) as Terminal context, default off
proposals.rationale: It is the infrastructure for the IN_VALUE and EXT_FROM_VALUE ledger bits and the context AMT traders expect. It is explicitly not a target source (POC/VA edges null on CME, BTC and QQQ/SPY) and not a bias (value migration χ² 1.05). Downgraded from A's P2 because the bits it feeds have null-to-mixed evidence (B4, B6).
proposals.spec: G_LVN inputs, display.none: useVA = false, vaPct = 70 (50-90), showVA = false. needVP (979) becomes showLVN or usePathVP or useVA; the rebuild condition at 1901 becomes (usePathVP or useVA) ? (newHour or h1Lower or vpSm.size() == 0) : tailBar. In step 15 after vpCum (1909): one-row expansion from pI = vSm.indexof(vSm.max()), adding the larger neighbour (ties to the upper row) until acc >= vaPct/100·sum, at most 48 iterations per hour. vpPOC = vLo + (pI + 0.5)·vStep; vpVAH = vLo + (hi + 1)·vStep; vpVAL = vLo + lo·vStep. Value state once per hourly close (h1C on newHour below 1H; close at or above 1H): p = cH > VAH ? 1 : cH < VAL ? -1 : 0; vaRun := p != 0 and p == vaPos ? vaRun + 1 : p != 0 ? 1 : 0; vaPos := p. Terminal row 'VALUE ▲ ACCEPTED ABOVE (4h) · POC x · VA a-b'. Optional lines from f_x(lvB.first()) to xR, only within maxATR of close. Tooltip: 'composite 1H, 48 rows, not a TPO VA; context, not a forecast'.
proposals.risk: Users may read it as a signal, and VA edges differ by platform (tie rule and VA % move edges on 20-65% of sessions); the tooltip mitigates both. No score impact.

proposals.title: Honest LVN display: troughs, draw the LVN price is in, distance limit, truthful tooltip (no invalidation change)
proposals.rationale: LVN zones are a reference-product feature, but the renderer (2250-2287) has three defects: (a) a run straddling close is never drawn, because the loops only test zTop < close and zBot > close; (b) no distance limit, so autoscale stretches; (c) it implies acceleration, while trough rejection does not replicate. B8: SMC-7 troughs +1.7 pp (z 1.2) on CME, 0.0 on BTC; external reject-or-run −0.3 pp [−5.0, +4.4]. A's proposal to anchor invalidation at LVNs is therefore dropped; only the faster-crossing property (+7-9% at 15 minutes) is supported.
proposals.spec: Input lvnMode = 'Troughs' (default) / 'Threshold'. Troughs from SMC-7: strict minimum over ±8% of the rows, depth ≥ 0.15·peak, tails excluded; shared with AMT-2's lvnPx. Zone = contiguous rows around the trough below trough + 0.5·(neighbour peak − trough), at least 1 row. Draw the straddling zone first (zBot <= close <= zTop), labelled 'LVN ·in'. Skip zones with |mid − close|/atr > maxATR. Keep lvnN per side. Tooltip: 'Low-volume node of the 1H composite. Measured: price moves ~8% faster through these at 15 minutes; it is not reliably rejected here; targets beyond them are reached no more often (slightly less on index futures).'
proposals.risk: None to scoring. Box count is unchanged (lvnN per side, plus at most one for the straddling zone).

proposals.title: Time-at-price (TPO-like) profile fallback when the symbol has no volume
proposals.rationale: On cash indices (SPX, NDX, DJI), many CFDs and some FX feeds, lvV holds zeros (lvV.push(nz(h1V)) at 997 / 1007). Then vpMean = 0 and f_pathVol returns 1.0, peak = 0 so no LVN is drawn, and any VA would be undefined. Every profile feature is silently disabled. Market Profile's original unit is time at price, which needs no volume, and the TPO-based tests here (E-OWN-2/5/6) behaved like the volume tests.
proposals.spec: In f_profile (1384), first compute float vTot = lvV.sum(). If vTot <= 0, use hv = 1.0 for every hour (same 60% range / 40% body allocation). Return or store a flag vpTPO = vTot <= 0 and show 'Profile: time-at-price (no volume)' in the Terminal and in the LVN / VA tooltips. Optional input vpSrc = 'Auto' / 'Volume' / 'Time' (display.none); 'Time' forces the TPO profile.
proposals.risk: Users may not notice which source is active, hence the readout. On symbols with intermittent zero-volume bars, the per-window sum test keeps the volume profile whenever any volume exists.

result.summary:
Combined study (researchers A + B), with B's corrections.

1. The literature on support and resistance memory holds up (Osler 2000: published FX levels 60.8% vs 56.2% for arbitrary levels; Garzarelli 2014; Chung & Bellotti 2021). But A's bar-level replication overstated the effect about three-fold. A's null shuffles bars within each day, which destroys volatility clustering. Against a stricter null that keeps the exact volatility path (each bar mirrored in place), the excess bounce at a pool shrinks from +5 to +8 pp to +1.5 to +3 pp on 1-minute charts. It is about 0 on 5m and 15m. The raw "a level that held more often holds again" pattern also appears in memoryless nulls (about 14 of its 15 pp are selection), so A's E(b,Δt) memory prior and the barrier-PoT proposal are withdrawn.

2. A's 1-hour results (gold +17.7 pp memory; crowding −6/−10/−29 pp) came from a corrupted GC 1H file that interleaves two contract months (692 jumps, 281 jump-and-back). They are invalid.

3. Path crowding (unswept same-side pools between price and the target) reproduces on clean 1m data (−1.3/−1.8/−3.9/−6.4 pp), but it is mostly a pool-age effect. With the engine's own 15-ATR ejection it nearly vanishes at 1m and 5m. It turns positive for pools under 4 hours old on 5m, stays moderately negative on clean CME/FX 1H, and is positive on BTC (sibling). It must be learned per chart, not hard-coded.

4. The most consistent level effect is staleness: chart-swing pools that survive about a day (intraday) or about 3 days (1H) are reached 8 to 14 pp less often than a random level at the same distance and trend. This holds on 1m, 5m, 1H CME and 1H NQ/GC/EUR. The engine measures freshness in bars (10 hours on 1m, 25 days on 1H), and its maturation ramp is about 10 times too strong. The engine's test bonus and its fixed "outermost pool is the draw" rule (inner ×0.70, +0.45·stack) are unsupported.

5. Stop cascades last 15 minutes to 2 hours of clock time (Osler 2005; 88% of forced selling within 30 minutes in crypto liquidations). The engine decays raid events in bars instead. A's pool-age weighting for raids rests on one non-monotone bucket and is downgraded.

6. The 52-week and all-time high are strong anchors only at daily to monthly horizons. The price-limit "magnet" is mixed (Wan et al. 2015 found a cooling-off effect in China), and gaps are not reliably filled.

7. The engine's random-level baseline (f_potBase) is adequate: a trend-conditioned baseline changes edges by 1 pp or less.

Proposals, best first: neutral stack and touch terms; a stale-pool reach ratio in trading time applied to reach and PoT, learned per chart; a two-stage ARRIVE / THROUGH-given-ARRIVE ledger; a learned crowding ratio with a neutral prior; a clock-time raid half-life; 52-week/ATH anchors on the shared N-day buffer.

Firecrawl web-search credits ran out during B's pass, and newyorkfed.org and upenn.edu were blocked by the network allowlist. Osler (2000) and Kavajecz & Odders-White (2004) numbers are therefore as A read them.

concepts.name: Support/resistance barrier: bounce vs penetration on arrival
concepts.definition: Osler 2000: a hit is the bid or ask within 0.01% of the level; a bounce means the rate is still on the near side 15 minutes later; the control is 10,000 arbitrary level sets. Garzarelli 2014: stripe of width mean|Δp| at τ = 45-180 s; a bounce enters the stripe and leaves on the same side; b_prev = prior bounces. Chung & Bellotti 2021: rolling-window max/min with zone γ = mean|Δx|. Bar version (A/B): pivot-5 swing, stripe g = mean|ΔClose| (≈0.6-0.76 ATR); penetration = high > P (the engine's sweep rule); bounce = leaving the stripe on the near side first.
concepts.dolRole: Would condition the last-mile P(through | arrival) of a pool. B shows that at bar resolution the conditional barrier effect is too small (≤3 pp, 1m only) to justify a PoT term. A level-agnostic PoT plus ledger measurement is right.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Existence is strong in tick/FX data: Osler 60.8% vs 56.2% (A read https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/epr/00v06n2/0007osle.html); Garzarelli p<0.0001 at 45-90 s and an fBm with H≈0.45 does not reproduce it (https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.5197). CORRECTED magnitude at bar level: against a volatility-path-preserving null (bars mirrored in place), the 1m excess is +1.5/+1.6/+2.0/+2.7/+3.0 pp for b_prev 1-5+ (overall +1.9, fresh <15 min +2.7, z 10). 5m: +0.1 overall; 15m: −0.6. A's day-shuffle null gives +5.1 to +8.0. Chung & Bellotti show stationary AR(1) inflates p(b|b_prev) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07410).
concepts.engineNotes: PoT (f_pot 434-445, f_empPoT 1284-1301, f_potModel 1303-1311, readout 2067) is level-agnostic, which the corrected evidence supports. CORRECTED from A's 'missing'. Measure via a two-stage ledger (ACAD-3) instead of a prior.

concepts.name: Pool staleness / age (survivorship)
concepts.definition: Age = trading time since the swing's pivot bar ((bar_index − bornBar)·chartS/3600). Reach edge = hit within H=30 minus the hit rate of random levels at the same checkpoints, the same 0.25-ATR distance bin and the same trend tercile (240/48/24-bar move toward the level).
concepts.dolRole: Old untaken pools lie where price has trended away from; they are reached much less often than distance implies. This is the most consistent level feature for 'which pool is reached next' and for an honest PoT.
concepts.evidenceNotes: NEW-B. 1m: <1h −1.1, 1-4h −1.9, 4-12h −3.0, 12-24h −6.9, 24-72h −10.4, >72h −8.1 pp. 5m: −1.4/+0.8/+0.4/−1.5/−9.9/−13.6. 1H CME clean: 4-12h −3.7, 12-24h +1.4, 24-72h 0.0, >72h −9.4. 1H NQ/GC/EUR: −2.0/+0.2/−2.1/−4.6 (SE 0.3-2.3, cluster by symbol-day). Agrees with sibling WYK B (young −0.6 to −1.9; >300-500 bars −3 to −8) and A's 1m (>12h since last test −7.5 ± 1.1). Mechanism consistent with hour-to-day trend persistence (Safari & Schmidhuber, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16772).
concepts.engineNotes: Freshness at 668-673: age in BARS/hlMult; ramp e-fold 0.25·halfLife = 37.5 bars (about 10× too strong); decay half-life 4·halfLife = 600 bars (10 h on 1m, 25 days on 1H). Registry key 1818 uses the same bar decay. The PoT readout (2067) ignores age.

concepts.name: Level memory decay and the stale-level sign flip
concepts.definition: Excess bounce on arrival versus a null, as a function of time since the last bounce. Chung & Bellotti micro decay: logit p = a + b·minutes (EURUSD b_prev=4: a = 0.402, b = −0.00179/min, p = 0.5 at about 225 min).
concepts.dolRole: Says whether a level approached after a long absence breaks more easily. A small 1-5m effect; it overlaps with trend persistence.
concepts.evidenceNotes: CORRECTED. Strict null: 1m stale (240-720 min) −2.3 (z −2.6), >720 min −1.7 (z −2.1), negative in 6/6 symbols; 5m >720 min −2.5 (z −2.1); 15m n.s. A's −3 to −8.6 pp against the day-shuffle null and the E(b,Δt) fit are withdrawn. Chung & Bellotti attribute their below-0.5 values to the 2018 bear trends.
concepts.engineNotes: No bounce timestamp is kept (lastTest is used only for 3-bar spacing, 650-658). Not worth a model term; at most a ledger bucket (ACAD-3).

concepts.name: Test count (touches without a take)
concepts.definition: Engine: a bar within testATR = 0.30 ATR of the pool, gap > 0 (exact touches excluded), at least 3 bars after the previous test (track 650-658). Academic equivalent: b_prev.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore says tests either add stops or weaken the level. The data support neither for reach; the raw rise in hold rate is survivorship selection.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A (1m, engine terms): reach edge −2.0/−1.9/−2.1/−7.3 ± 3.6 pp for 0/1/2/3+ tests. B: the memoryless null's raw bounce rate rises from 0.384 to 0.524 for b_prev 1 to 5+ (real: 0.399 to 0.555), so about 90% of the rise is selection. Vendor gold 1H data (weak): 56 → 70% raw hold rate.
concepts.engineNotes: Density x at 682 includes +0.35·min(tests,6), a monotone bonus with no support. Remove (ACAD-1, same as ICT-10).

concepts.name: Path crowding (unswept same-side pools between price and target)
concepts.definition: nIn = live, unswept same-side pools strictly between the close and the target's near edge with a 0.1-ATR margin; target 1-4 ATR away; reach within H=30 vs a distance- and trend-matched random-level baseline.
concepts.dolRole: Affects whether a far pool is reached before the market turns. It is heterogeneous by market, timeframe and pool age, so it is a per-chart learned feature rather than a prior.
concepts.evidenceNotes: CORRECTED. No ejection: 1m −1.3/−1.8/−3.9/−6.4; 5m −0.8/−1.3/−2.1/−10.6. With the engine's 15-ATR ejection: 1m −1.0/−0.8/−2.4/−2.8; 5m −0.5/+0.7/+1.1/−2.8; 1H CME clean −1.4/−2.6/−3.3/−12.1; 1H NQ/GC/EUR −1.1/−1.9/−5.8/−6.6. 5m pools <4h: +1.6/+4.8/+2.3 (positive); >24h: −7.2 to −18.3. Sibling: 5m +4.0/+4.3/+5.1, BTC 1H +2.2/+4.9/+8.0. Random levels behind the same pools are barely penalized (1m −0.2/0.0/−2.3). A's 1H −6/−10/−29 came from the corrupted GC 1H file.
concepts.engineNotes: No nIn count; the only path cost is volume-profile based (1946-1947). Add as a learned ratio with a neutral prior (ACAD-4).

concepts.name: Stacked pools: inner vs outermost
concepts.definition: f_stackSide (1230-1251): within clusATR = 0.75 ATR on one side, the pool closer to price is inner and the farther one gets stack += 1.
concepts.dolRole: Decides whether the DOL is the 'next' pool (inner, which geometry reaches first) or ICT's 'objective' (outermost).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Measured effects of being the outer pool of a stack are small and change sign across 1m, 5m, 1H and BTC (A, B, sibling ict_liq). The engine's ×0.70 inner penalty is about 10× larger than any measured effect.
concepts.engineNotes: Inner ×0.70 at 684-685 and +0.45·stack in density at 682. Neutral default with an 'Outermost (ICT)' option (ACAD-1 = ICT-10). The HTF objective (oKey, 1986) keeps the objective visible.

concepts.name: Stop-loss clustering and post-break cascades
concepts.definition: Stops sit just beyond levels and round numbers (Osler 2003: stop-buys 14.4% in 01-10 above a 00 vs 7.4% in 90-99); take-profits sit at them (9.3% at 00). The extra move after crossing a stop cluster lasts 15 min to 2 h (Osler 2005: +0.27 to +2.35 hundredths of a percent) and is gone at 1-2 days.
concepts.dolRole: How long a raid's continuation lean should persist in the draw vector: in clock time, minutes to hours.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong for FX round numbers (Osler 2003/2005). Crypto: 88% of forced selling in the Oct-2025 cascade landed within 30 min (https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03616). A's bar test: +1.1 pp hold beyond swing vs grid levels at 30/120 min (z ≈ 2). The '+5.1 pp for 4-12h-old pools' is one non-monotone bucket of 8 (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: Raid outcome into liqEvt (1578-1582), weighted by tier, decayed with liqHL = 24 BARS (159, 1535): 24 min on 1m, 4 days on 4H. Fix the units (ACAD-5); sign mapping via ICTS-2/BIAS-4.

concepts.name: Round-number psychological barriers
concepts.definition: Barrier tests on M-digit frequencies and conditional mean/variance shifts near round numbers (Donaldson & Kim 1993; De Grauwe & Decupere 1992; Aggarwal & Lucey 2007). Order imbalance at round numbers (Bhattacharya, Holden & Jacobsen 2012). Orders one tick ahead of clusters (Lallouache & Abergel 2014).
concepts.dolRole: Rounds slow price on approach and accelerate it after a cross. Sweep wicks stop short of a round just beyond a pool. They are not magnets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: USD/JPY yes, USD/DEM weak; gold yes, silver no. Jung & Lee 2026 (verified, https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34787): more resting depth at rounds, no longer depth-adjusted durations. Sibling OF-4: sweep wicks stop short (−4.2 pp).
concepts.engineNotes: No round-number logic. Owned by siblings ICT-3 / OF-4.

concepts.name: 52-week high/low and all-time-high anchoring
concepts.definition: Nearness = P / 52-week high (George & Hwang 2004); crossing the 52-week extreme (Huddart et al. 2009); IV compression on approach and expansion after a breakthrough (Driessen et al. 2013); recency (Bhootra & Hur 2013); 52-week (+) vs historical high (−) at index level (Li & Yu 2012).
concepts.dolRole: Widely watched extremes: barriers on approach and continuation triggers once broken. Natural HTF objectives in Swing mode; naming value intraday.
concepts.evidenceNotes: George & Hwang WML 0.45%/month (t 2.00) to 1.23%/month (t 7.06); Bhootra & Hur about 0.70%/month; Driessen ≥ +1 vol point after a break. Daily to monthly horizons, mostly stocks. Intraday reach untested; the sibling found 20/40/60-day extremes reached at baseline rates.
concepts.engineNotes: No 52-week or ATH source in the registry (1778-1822, f_tierW 506). ta.max() is documented (reference/ta.md:973-978). ACAD-6, one buffer shared with ICTPD-5/TIME-8.

concepts.name: Prior-high/low and trading-range breakouts
concepts.definition: Trading-range break: buy above the max of the prior n = 50/150/200 days with a 0-1% band (Brock, Lakonishok & LeBaron 1992). Intraday opening-range breakout (Holmberg et al. 2013). Horizontal S/R from local extremes (Zapranis & Tsinaslanidis 2012). Kernel-smoothed patterns (Lo, Mamaysky & Wang 2000).
concepts.dolRole: Breaking a prior extreme in the HTF trend direction is the continuation case. Breakout signals alone are not target signals.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Brock et al. significant 1897-1986, no out-of-sample advantage after 1986 (Sullivan, Timmermann & White 1999). MNQ: 0 of 14 OHLCV families pass after costs, ORB long T = 0.88 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04004, verified). ICT AMD on NQ: no information beyond the trend regime, right 62-71% with it and 25-30% against (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35887, verified). Zapranis & Tsinaslanidis: support beats resistance at interrupting trends, no excess return.
concepts.engineNotes: PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL and session pools are in the registry (944-961, 1797-1822) with hand-set tiers. Osler found published strength ratings useless, so calibrate via the ledger (ICT-1).

concepts.name: Trend vs reversion timescales
concepts.definition: Safari & Schmidhuber 2025: after removing tick-size reversion, weak trends revert up to about 15-30 min, persist from about 30 min to a few hours (overcoming tick reversion at a few hours), and trend from a few hours to a few years; strong trends revert.
concepts.dolRole: Reconciles minute-scale bounces with multi-hour continuation, and explains why stale pools are under-reached and stale levels break slightly more.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Futures tick data plus 30 years daily and 330 years monthly; verified in the full text (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16772, §3.4 and §5).
concepts.engineNotes: The D vector (1891-1895) uses HTF structure, which is the right scale. Pool staleness is not modelled in trading time (ACAD-2).

concepts.name: Null-model choice for level tests (volatility-path preservation)
concepts.definition: Three nulls, in order of strictness: (1) shuffled returns; (2) bars permuted within each day; (3) bars mirrored about their open in place, which keeps the exact bar-range sequence, intraday seasonality and clustering and destroys only direction. Only effects that survive null 3 are directional dependence (level memory, reversal, trend).
concepts.dolRole: Determines which priors are real. With a fixed stripe, bounce vs penetration depends non-linearly on bar size, so nulls 1-2 manufacture apparent memory.
concepts.evidenceNotes: NEW-B. 1m overall excess: +6.5 pp (null 2) vs +1.9 (null 3); 5m +2.8 vs +0.1. Garzarelli tested fBm and Chung & Bellotti tested AR(1), but neither tested volatility clustering.
concepts.engineNotes: For the engine's ledger: f_potBase (1314-1322) uses the real empirical excursion surface; a trend-conditional baseline changes edges by ≤1 pp, so it is adequate.

concepts.name: Conditional magnets (option pinning, price-limit magnet)
concepts.definition: Optionable stocks close near strikes on expiry (Ni, Pearson & Poteshman 2005); S&P futures are pinned to strikes (Golez & Jackwerth 2012); prices accelerate toward a price limit (Cho et al. 2003).
concepts.dolRole: The only documented cases of a known level attracting price. Both need a hedging or limit mechanism.
concepts.evidenceNotes: CORRECTED from strong: pinning is strong but conditional; the price-limit magnet is mixed. Wan et al. 2015 (PLoS ONE 10(4), China A-shares 2000-11) found a cooling-off effect, not a magnet.
concepts.engineNotes: Needs open interest, which Pine does not provide. Not proposed.

concepts.name: Timing of daily highs and lows
concepts.definition: Arcsine law: the time of the max of Brownian motion on [0,T] has density 1/(π√(t(T−t))); in business time (the U-shaped volatility clock) the open gets more mass. ES 09:30 segment: 17.2% of highs of day vs 3.7% uniform.
concepts.dolRole: When extremes form (timing of the draw). A volatility-clock effect, not a level property.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Sibling ict_time; Andersen & Bollerslev 1997/98; reproduced by an arcsine-plus-clock random walk.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed killzone affinities (f_kzAff 597-602, kz 975). Owned by TIME-1 / TIME-5.

concepts.name: Probability the previous day's high/low (or prior close) is exceeded or revisited
concepts.definition: Driftless walk: P(H1 before L1) = (C − L1)/(H1 − L1). Next-day base rates: PDH taken 51.3% (S&P) and 55.4% (NASDAQ), PDL 44.6% and 46.5%, either 87-91%. Gap fill = revisit of the prior close.
concepts.dolRole: Base rates for PDH/PDL targets. Geometry, not a magnet; gaps are not reliably filled.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Sibling bias_dol §2.1; Caporin, Ranaldo & Santucci de Magistris 2013 (cointegrated H/L, long-memory range). NEW-B: Plastun, Sibande, Gupta & Wohar (US indices 1928-2018) report gap-day continuation and contradict the gap-fill myth (not re-read; weak).
concepts.engineNotes: Handled by the PoT (f_potModel 1303). Base-rate display is BIAS-3.

concepts.name: Level depth mechanism (why levels hold)
concepts.definition: Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004: support is the lowest bid reached at least twice; S/R coincides with peaks in order-book depth; limit orders do not cluster there afterwards. Latent-liquidity models (Bouchaud et al.) give memory over several timescales.
concepts.dolRole: Explains small barrier effects and why equal highs/lows are not bigger magnets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 84% of level-depth series cointegrated at 5%; significant for 49-73% of stocks (RFS 17(4); as A read it, not re-opened by B).
concepts.engineNotes: EQ highs/lows merge to the outermost print (f_mergeAt 1111-1131) with a 0.9·eqCount density bonus (682). Siblings measured about 0 pp for EQ (ICT-10).

proposals.title: Neutral stack and touch terms (drop the outermost-is-the-draw rule and the test bonus)
proposals.rationale: Three hard-coded effects are unsupported or mixed in every dataset: inner ×0.70 (684-685), +0.45·stack (682) and +0.35·min(tests,6) (682). Measured effects are ±0-3 pp at ≤5m and change sign by market (1m/5m/1H CME, FX, BTC). A 30% score cut on the inner pool, which geometry reaches first, is far larger than that. Same change as sibling ICT-10; aligns with SMC-3, WYK-2 and SKEP-6.
proposals.spec: INPUTS (G_SCORE, after 152): string stackMode = input.string('Neutral', 'Stacked Pools', options=['Neutral','Outermost (ICT)'], group=G_SCORE, display=display.none). It is a global input declared before evaluate (661), so there is no forward reference. In evaluate (682): bool ictStack = stackMode == 'Outermost (ICT)'; x = 0.9*eqCount + (ictStack ? 0.45*stack : 0.0) + 0.8*min(1, prom/3) + 1.2*tier(). Remove the tests term in both modes. At 684-685: if this.inner and ictStack then mult *= 0.70. Keep the STK/T tags (tag 638-646). The HTF objective (oKey, 1986) still names the strongest draw-side pool, so ICT's 'objective' stays visible while the DOL becomes the 'next' pool. Update the README wording ('outermost pool in a stack is the draw', 'tests strengthen'). Measure with a ledger A/B of the two modes on EDGE and BARS→HIT, and as ICT-1 probe bits (stack>0, inner).
