proposals.risk: Changes a visible ICT convention; the option preserves it. Selection may switch to the inner pool more often; the 2-bar challenger and 2× flip hysteresis limit flicker.

proposals.title: Stale-pool reach ratio in trading time, applied to reach and the PoT readout, learned per chart
proposals.rationale: The most consistent level effect found: chart-swing pools that survive about a day (≤15m charts) or about 3 days (≥30m) are reached 8-14 pp less often than a random level at the same distance and trend. It holds on 1m (24-72h −10.4), 5m (24-72h −9.9, >72h −13.6), 1H CME (>72h −9.4) and 1H NQ/GC/EUR (>72h −4.6), and agrees with sibling WYK B. The engine decays freshness in bars (600-bar half-life: 10 h on 1m, 25 days on 1H), uses a ramp about 10× too strong, and its displayed PoT ignores age.
proposals.spec: INPUTS (G_SCORE, display.none): bool useAge = true; float freshHLh = 72.0 (trading hours). Level field: float rAdj = 1.0. Trial field: int ab = -1. PURE HELPERS (before 612): f_ageH(int bornBar) => float(bar_index - bornBar) * chartS / 3600.0 (chartS at 308); f_ageB(h) => h<12 ? 0 : h<24 ? 1 : h<72 ? 2 : 3; f_agePrior(b): when timeframe.in_seconds() <= 900, [0.98, 0.91, 0.80, 0.77], otherwise [0.95, 1.00, 0.98, 0.87]. Fresh pillar (671, liquidity branch) when useAge: fresh := pow(0.5, f_ageH(bornBar)/max(hlMult,1)/freshHLh), with no ramp. Reach term (665): multiply by this.rAdj (cap 1). STATE (next to stN, 1066): var array<float> agK, agE (size 4). STATE HELPER: f_ageMult(b) => f_clamp((agK[b] + 30*f_agePrior(b)) / (agE[b] + 30), 0.6, 1.15), shrinkage of hits over random-level expectation toward the prior. f_openTrial (1426): ab = isLiquidity and src==0 ? f_ageB(f_ageH(bornBar)) : -1. f_book (1461): if ab>=0, agK[ab] += y and agE[ab] += pBase. Step 17, before lv.evaluate (track resets mult at 657, and the ledger arrays are declared after evaluate, so the ratio must be computed here): lv.rAdj := useAge and lv.isLiquidity() and lv.src==0 ? f_ageMult(f_ageB(f_ageH(lv.bornBar))) : 1.0. Live PoT (2067): activePoT := sweptNow ? 0.95 : min(0.95, f_potModel(...) * activeLv.rAdj). Tooltip: 'age 1.6 d · stale −15%' when rAdj < 0.95. Full-view row: AGE bucket edges. Scope is src 0 (tested); extend to registry pools via ICT-1 probes.
proposals.risk: Only the active DOL is graded, so old-pool buckets fill slowly and the prior dominates for a long time. On ≥30m charts the 12-72h prior is about 1, so the effect only bites beyond 72h. Interaction with the draw vector D is handled by learning the residual. Trading-time age undercounts weekends by design.

proposals.title: Two-stage ledger: ARRIVE vs THROUGH-given-ARRIVE, with memory, age and crowding buckets
proposals.rationale: Support/resistance research measures what happens at the level, while the engine records only 'hit within H'. Splitting the outcome separates arrival skill from barrier behaviour ('got there but it held'). It is also the honest per-chart home for bounce memory, age and crowding, which are small or heterogeneous across markets.
proposals.spec: Input arrGam = 0.35 ATR (G_ACC, display.none); this equals the 0.5·mean|ΔC| stripe. Trial fields: bool arr, float gam, pArrB, pThrB, int mb, int cb. mb = (min(tests,2))*2 + (bar_index - lastTest < 15 ? 0 : 1), from existing fields; cb from ACAD-4. f_openTrial (1426): g = arrGam*atr; pArrB = f_potBase(max(d-g,0), side); pThrB = f_clamp(f_potBase(d, side)/max(pArrB,1e-6), .01, .99). S(d)/S(d−g) is the exact random-level (Osler arbitrary-level) analogue, so no new baseline state is needed. f_step (1434), before hit: arr := arr or (side==1 ? high >= edge - gam : low <= edge + gam). f_book (1461): accumulate arN/arK/arE (Σ pArrB), and for arrived trials thN/thK/thE (Σ pThrB) per memory bucket (6), age bucket (4) and crowd bucket (4), as var arrays in STATE. Terminal Full view: 'ARRIVE 71% (rand 66%) · THRU|ARR 58% (rand 74%)'; show cells only at n>=20. No effect on selection.
proposals.risk: Cells fill slowly (about 1 trial per H bars). ICT-1 candidate probes would speed this up 10-30×. Adds about 20 floats of state.

proposals.title: Learned path-crowding ratio with a neutral prior (replaces A's fixed crowding prior)
proposals.rationale: nIn predicts reach on 1m and on clean CME/FX 1H when old pools are kept. But with the engine's 15-ATR ejection it is about 0 at 1m/5m, it turns positive for young 5m pools and in BTC 1H, and much of it is pool age (ACAD-2). A's 1H prior came from a corrupted data file. What remains is chart-specific: learn it, do not assume it.
proposals.spec: Level field int nIn. Step 16 (after 1927; O(n²) with n ≤ poolMax 40; inCalc only): for each liquidity lv, count o.isLiquidity() and o.side==lv.side and o.id!=lv.id with nearEdge strictly between close and lv.nearEdge() minus 0.1*atr on the price side. STATE: var array<float> crK, crE (size 4). f_openTrial: cb = min(nIn,3) for liquidity trials. f_book: crK[cb] += y, crE[cb] += pBase. f_crowdMult(b) => r0 = (crK[0]+40)/(crE[0]+40); f_clamp(((crK[b]+40)/(crE[b]+40))/max(r0,1e-9), 0.8, 1.1). The prior is 1.0, so there is no effect until data accumulate. Step 17, after ACAD-2: lv.rAdj *= f_crowdMult(min(lv.nIn,3)) for liquidity pools. Full-view row 'CROWD 0/1/2/3+ edge'.
proposals.risk: Slow learning, and the effect is small at ≤5m. At most 1,600 compares on inCalc bars.

proposals.title: Clock-time half-life for raid (liquidity) events
proposals.rationale: liqEvt decays with liqHL = 24 bars (159, 1535), which is 24 minutes on 1m and 4 days on 4H. Stop-cascade evidence is 15 minutes to 2 hours of clock time (Osler 2005; 88% of crypto forced selling within 30 minutes; A's +1.1 pp continuation at 30-120 minutes). This fixes units only; the sign mapping is ICTS-2/BIAS-4, and A's age weighting is dropped (one non-monotone bucket).
proposals.spec: Input float liqHLm = input.float(60.0, 'Liquidity-Event Half-Life (minutes)', minval=5, group=G_FLOW, display=display.none). Replace 1535 with liqEvt *= math.pow(0.5, chartS/60.0/liqHLm) (chartS at 308). Keep the raid update at 1582, or the sibling's corrected mapping. Deprecate liqHL. Measure with a side hit-rate A/B via the BIAS-1 side ledger or the ICTS-1 gate.
proposals.risk: On 4H and above the raid term vanishes within one bar and D leans on structure, which is intended (no effect at 1-2 days).

proposals.title: 52-week and all-time extremes as anchor pools on the shared N-day buffer
proposals.rationale: These are the best-documented anchors in finance (George & Hwang, Li & Yu, Huddart et al., Driessen et al., Bhootra & Hur): barriers on approach and continuation once broken, at daily to monthly horizons. Their value is naming and Swing-mode objectives. The sibling found 20/40/60-day extremes reached at baseline rates, so there is no score boost.
proposals.spec: One request (the engine has 6 request.* calls): [h52, l52, ath, atl] = request.security(syminfo.tickerid, f_tfSafe('D'), [ta.highest(high,252)[1], ta.lowest(low,252)[1], ta.max(high)[1], ta.min(low)[1]], lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_on). This is [1]-offset and non-repainting; ta.max is documented in reference/ta.md:973-978 as the max since the first bar of the requested data, so label it 'ATH (loaded data)' on short histories. Use 365 instead of 252 when syminfo.type == 'crypto'. If ICTPD-5/TIME-8 build an N-day ring buffer, compute these from it instead. Registry (step 10, 1797-1822): src 8 = 52W, 9 = ATH/ATL; f_tierW 0.80 (same as PDH, because hand-set strength ratings carry no information per Osler); names '52W H/L', 'ATH', 'ATL'. Push via f_pushExt when f_changed(h52) (865) etc., anchored by f_anchorScan (1141) or bar_index − anchorMax. Measure the family EDGE for src ≥ 8.
proposals.risk: Low; these levels usually sit outside maxATR on intraday charts. Intraday reach value is unproven.

result.summary: Combined A+B study. Stop placement at round numbers is strongly documented (Osler: stop-buys at 01-10 above a "00" 14.4% vs 7.4%; take-profits at 00 9.3%). Stops just beyond swing highs/lows are only indirectly supported (S/R = limit-order depth; published S/R interrupts trends), so A's "strong" grade is split [CORRECTED]. A key engine correction: f_invalidation places the stop at lv.bottom - 0.10 ATR, and the opposing zone already extends 0.20 ATR, so the real stop is about 0.30 ATR beyond the pool. It is beaten by 41.0% of rejected sweeps (30-47% by dataset, 46-57% on BTC), not the 78.5% A reported, and A's 'Beyond Stop Band' spec would have double-counted the zone. Rejected-sweep depth must be learned per chart: median 0.16-0.19 ATR on daily equities, 0.23-0.27 on hourly FX/NQ/gold, 0.26-0.36 on BTC, with q80 about 2.2 x q50 everywhere; ATR normalisation is right (x2.2 spread across 11 series vs x20 in % of price). No pool-size proxy predicts which pool is reached next: equal prints, tests, age, stack, prominence, and (new B-test) pivot-bar or in-zone volume are all within about +/-1.5 pp, so reach 'size' reduces to source tier (adopt ICT-10/WYK-1/WYK-2 once). Sweep classes carry almost no direction: the new multi-bar RECLAIM (failed breakout, 21-29% of sweeps) leans reversal by only -1.5 +/- 0.7 pp against race geometry, so classes are labels and ledger cells. The strongest microstructure effect is timing: after any trade-through, intraday ranges are +15-23% larger over 3 bars even after matching on ATR5/ATR50 (absent on daily equities, larger on BTC). Because trials open right after sweeps, this also inflates the ledger EDGE on crypto by about 2-3 pp unless the baseline is conditioned too (OF-6, upgraded to P2). True Binance taker delta contradicts the absorption reading: 68.6% of rejection bars show aggression into the pool, and absorbed ones lean continuation (+4.7 +/- 2.2 pp). A Pine-buildable LTF candle-sign or BVC proxy matches the true delta sign only 60-66% of the time (OF-7 downgraded to an opt-in label). A taker-flow liquidation heatmap showed no magnet (+0.7 +/- 0.8 pp), so OF-8 is dropped. Round numbers are not magnets, but sweep wicks stop short of the 00/50 grid (-3.7 +/- 0.9 pp at half-grid; BTC -7.4 +/- 1.3), so zones are capped on that grid with no bonus. Fresh sweep wicks are re-taken within 5 bars 48-61% of the time before a pivot exists (OF-1). Stop hunting by dealers is documented in FCA final notices (2014-15).

concepts.name: Stop-loss clustering beyond obvious levels (the physical pool)
concepts.definition: Protective/breakout stops rest just beyond extremes: BSL above swing highs, SSL below lows, as a band not a price. Osler 2005: stops placed median 0.43% from market, median life 0.46 days, larger than take-profits.
concepts.dolRole: Defines WHERE the draw is: the band just beyond the most obvious unswept extremes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [CORRECTED split] Strong for stops just beyond ROUND numbers (Osler 2003/2005 bank order book). Moderate/indirect for swing extremes: S/R = limit-order depth (Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004), published S/R interrupts trends (Osler 2000); no study measures stops at swing highs/lows directly (practitioner sources only).
concepts.engineNotes: BSL zone [P, P+zoneATR*ATR] at 1762, SSL 1774, registry 1848; strict trade-through 623-624.

concepts.name: Take-profit/limit clustering at round numbers and front-running
concepts.definition: Take-profits/limits bunch exactly at 00/50; stops just beyond (01-10). Algos post one tick ahead (digits 1/9). Coarse step M = smallest {1,5}x10^k >= one daily ATR; the effective cap grid is M/2 (00 and 50).
concepts.dolRole: Rounds just beyond a pool cap the sweep wick; once a coarse round is reached it is passed slightly more often. Geometry, not a magnet.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Placement strong: Osler 14.4% vs 7.4% (p=0.029), TP 9.3% at 00; Bhattacharya et al. 2012; Lallouache & Abergel; Jung & Lee 2026; Donaldson & Kim 1993 (DJIA 100s); Cyree et al. 1999. Bar level: magnet mixed sign (T2); wick stops short -4.2 pp (T2d), B7 -3.7+/-0.9 at M/2, BTC -6.0 to -7.4 pp; pass-through +3.3 pp once reached.
concepts.engineNotes: No round-number logic (grep). OF-4 caps zones on the M/2 grid; no score bonus.

concepts.name: Stop cascades (running the stops)
concepts.definition: Crossing a stop cluster converts stops to same-direction market orders; acceleration for 15 min-2 h, partial reversal at 1-2 days.
concepts.dolRole: Timing: nearby pools become reachable sooner for a few bars. Not a fixed outermost-is-the-draw rule.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2005 Table VI.A (extra move after round crossings, negative at 1-2 d; A-read); CFTC stop orders on volatile days; crypto 88% of forced selling within 30 min, OI -25-70%, 63% absorbed by backstop (Garcia Seuma 2026); predatory trading theory.
concepts.engineNotes: Stack logic 1230-1251, inner x0.70 at 684-685 (unsupported magnitude, ICT-10); raid read 1580-1582 has the wrong sign (ICT-9).

concepts.name: Stop band depth (pen beyond the level), ATR not ticks
concepts.definition: pen = (sweep high - P)/ATR[1]. Core band [P, P+q50], outer edge P+q80, learned from REJECT sweeps only (close back inside). Prior q80 = 2.2 x q50.
concepts.dolRole: Zone drawing, stop placement and sweep-class threshold. Does not change which pool is taken.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A-test 7 datasets: REJECT q50 0.233, q80 0.518 (daily equities 0.16-0.19, hourly 0.23-0.27). B-test BTC: q50 0.26-0.36, q80 0.56-0.82. q80/q50 2.15-2.48 everywhere. In % of price the median spans x20 across series vs x2.2 in ATR, so ATR is the right unit.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed zoneATR 0.20 (93) used via wPx at 1520, 1762, 1774, 1848. Zone depth also leaks into the confluence window (675-676) and the HOLD read (1581).

concepts.name: Engine's effective stop distance (invalidation)
concepts.definition: f_invalidation sets inv = lv.bottom - 0.10*ATR beyond the opposing pool's zone, i.e. about P -/+ (0.20*ATR_birth + 0.10*ATR_now), about 0.30 ATR beyond the pool price.
concepts.dolRole: Honest R:R/WIN readout and how much stop-hunt exposure the ledger's race shows.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [CORRECTED A] B1: 41.0% of REJECT sweeps go deeper than 0.30 ATR (30-47% by dataset; BTC 46-57%), not 78.5%. A's T4 'engine 0.10' row is mislabelled; the engine sits between the 0.25 and 0.50 rows (win 42.5-43.7%, mean R -0.012 to -0.015). Expectancy is invariant to the buffer (martingale).
concepts.engineNotes: 1343-1356 (buf 1344, lv.bottom - buf 1352, swing fallback 1356). No 'beyond band' option. A's OF-2 spec would have stacked q80 on the zone; fixed in the final OF-2.

concepts.name: Pool size (growth with time, touches, volume)
concepts.definition: Claim: more watchers means more stops (tier, prominence, touches, equal prints, age, volume traded in the zone). Final model for reach: source tier only (ICT-10 Evidence x = 1.2*tier + 0.4*min(1,prom/3)); everything else is display plus learned ledger bits.
concepts.dolRole: Tie-breaker magnitude only; size proxies do not predict which pool is reached next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: HF bounce memory decays in hours (Chung & Bellotti full text: EURUSD 0.5 at about 350/900 min; LLOY slow; BRENT 1-bounce predicts penetration). A-T3: equal prints/tests/age null for the post-sweep path. ict_liq: EQ reach +0.3+/-1.8 pp, prominence negative at 1H. B6: pivot-bar relative volume high-low -1.5 pp, zone volume -0.5 pp, sign differs by market. Prominence relates only to post-take run size (+0.21 vs +0.06 ATR).
concepts.engineNotes: Density x = 0.9*eqCount + 0.45*stack + 0.35*min(tests,6) + 0.8*prom + 1.2*tier (682); freshness maturation ramp (668-671).

concepts.name: Fresh-extreme liquidity and pool decay after a sweep
concepts.definition: A trade-through spends stops between P and the wick; new stops form at once beyond the new wick. Residual stops beyond the wick are weak.
concepts.dolRole: The sweep wick is an immediate new pool and the natural place for a counter-target's stop.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A-T6: 60.8% of REJECT wicks re-taken within 5 bars (only 38.3% ever become pivLen-5 pivots). B8 BTC 48-54% (next bar 27-30%). K3 edge +4.3+/-1.0 pp (A), BTC +4.6 to +5.7; about 0 at K30. Residual after pokes +2.6+/-1.6 pp (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: Binary removal on trade-through 1583-1596 is correct. New extremes become pools only via ta.pivothigh/low after pivLen bars (1753-1776): gap, fixed by OF-1.

concepts.name: Sweep vs breakout classification incl. multi-bar RECLAIM
concepts.definition:
At the sweep-bar close (BSL): POKE close

=P+q50*ATR. RECLAIM(n): a PROBE/ACCEPT that closes back inside within n<=3 bars (failed breakout / outbreak-and-retest).
concepts.dolRole: Labels, alerts and ledger cells; no directional forecast weight.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A-T1: depth buckets within +/-2.6 pp of null. B4 race vs driftless geometry over 9 datasets: REJECT +0.5+/-0.6, any RECLAIM -1.5+/-0.7 (n 4,253, per-dataset +4.4 to -6.2), HOLD-beyond -0.6+/-0.8. RECLAIM is 21-29% of sweeps. Siblings: no reversal edge after REJECT (ICT-9).
concepts.engineNotes: HOLD = close>lv.top (depends on display input zoneATR), REJECT = close<lv.price, fixed +/-tier into D (1580-1582). No depth, POKE/PROBE or RECLAIM; only a live touch alert (1504-1509, 2087-2088).

concepts.name: Post-sweep volatility burst (timing of stop runs)
concepts.definition: For a few bars after any pool trade-through, excursions in both directions exceed the distance-matched null, beyond what a fast volatility ratio predicts.
concepts.dolRole: WHEN: short-horizon PoT/race/ETA should widen after sweeps; the ledger baseline must be conditioned the same way to keep EDGE fair.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A-T1 K3 re-take +4.1, throwback +3.2 pp, +0.145 ATR (8 sigma). B2 BTC K3 +4.9 to +7.3 pp, excursion +0.23-0.36 ATR. B10: after ATR5/ATR50 decile matching, intraday 3-bar range x1.15-1.23, 10-bar x1.08-1.15, 30-bar x1.04-1.10; daily equities x0.96-0.99. B11: random 1-3 ATR level from sweep bars hit +2.1 to +3.4 pp above baseline on BTC, about 0 elsewhere.
concepts.engineNotes: potSig is a 50-bar stdev (916); f_potModel/f_potBase (1302-1322) and the race (1360-1363) are unconditional; trials open right after sweeps, so crypto EDGE is flattered.

concepts.name: Absorption, exhaustion, delta divergence
concepts.definition: Absorption = aggressive volume into/through a level without progress, then a close back inside; exhaustion = delta spike then volume dries up; divergence = new price extreme with weaker delta.
concepts.dolRole: Context label at sweeps only; no validated directional role at bar scale.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B3 (BTC 1H, true Binance taker delta): 68.6% of REJECT bars show delta into the pool (absorption is the norm). Absorbed REJECTs lean CONTINUATION (+4.7+/-2.2 pp wick re-take at K30, throwback 0), contradicting the reversal reading. D1: LTF candle-sign/BVC proxies agree with true delta sign 60-66% (corr 0.19-0.34). Literature: OFI is contemporaneous (Cont et al.); BVC loses to the tick rule (Chakrabarty et al. 2015).
concepts.engineNotes: Volume only in the 1H profile (978-1009). request.footprint is Premium/Ultimate-only and one call per script (reference/request.md 168-170).

concepts.name: Icebergs and hidden liquidity
concepts.definition: Displayed size refilled at one price (native exchange-managed or synthetic). Detectable only from market-by-order data.
concepts.dolRole: None buildable on TradingView data.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Zotikov & Antonov 2019 (ES, 1 week): native icebergs 0.06% of orders but about 4% of volume; tranches refill in under 1 s. Frey & Sandas 2017: icebergs attract matching market orders.
concepts.engineNotes: No MBO feed in Pine; refills are faster than any bar.

concepts.name: Liquidity holes / thin volume paths
concepts.definition: Large moves happen across book gaps. Bar proxy vf = mean volume-profile volume between price and target / profile mean.
concepts.dolRole: Small reachability modifier at most.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Farmer et al. 2004 (mechanism). A-T5: thin (vf<0.6) +1.3 to +3.6 pp (unstable); thick (vf>1.4) -1.5 to +1.4 pp, so the HVN penalty is unsupported.
concepts.engineNotes: x1.10 thin / x0.85 thick at 1947; the 0.85 is unsupported (OF-5). Same line as ICT-5's opposing-FVG path cost.

concepts.name: Crypto liquidation levels (leverage-implied clusters, heatmaps)
concepts.definition: Long liq ~ entry*(1-1/L+mmr), short ~ entry*(1+1/L-mmr); heatmaps project estimated new positions to leverage tiers, decay them and delete bins when crossed.
concepts.dolRole: Mechanical forced-order pools on perps; no demonstrated value as targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanics moderate: BitMEX 3.51%/1.89% of OI per day, 60x average leverage of the liquidated; Oct 10 2025 about $19 bn liquidated, $2.1 bn ADL in 12 min; OI misquoted on some exchanges. B9: taker-flow heatmap, heaviest bin edge +0.7+/-0.8 pp (n 10,792), i.e. no magnet. No published hit-rate test.
concepts.engineNotes: No OI source; A's OF-8 dropped (null test, contested src code, extra request).

concepts.name: Equal highs/lows as pooled stops
concepts.definition: Two or more prints within tolerance (0.10 ATR) form one pool, with stops beyond the OUTERMOST print (not the average used by some open-source libraries).
concepts.dolRole: Location of the pool; not a size multiplier.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kavajecz & Odders-White define support as reached at least twice. Reach +0.3+/-1.8 pp (ict_liq B2); post-sweep path unchanged (A-T3, +0.6+/-2.3 pp). The smartmoneyconcepts library uses a whole-dataset range (look-ahead) and an average level.
concepts.engineNotes: f_mergeAt outermost merge 1104-1131 is correct but one-sided (a right-higher print sweeps the pool first; ICT-11). OF-1's eqCount carry-over fixes it. Over-weighted at 682 (0.9*eqCount).

concepts.name: Tests (touches without a take)
concepts.definition: A bar within 0.30 ATR of the pool without trading through, at least 3 bars after the previous test.
concepts.dolRole: Neutral at bar scale; HF bounce memory decays within hours.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Garzarelli 2014; Chung & Bellotti 2021 (decay). Bar level: no monotone effect (A-T3 tests>=2 +2.9+/-1.6 pp at K10, n.s.; ict_liq 1H/5m mixed).
concepts.engineNotes: 0.35*min(tests,6) magnitude in density (682); track() 650-658.

concepts.name: Stop hunting / predatory trading
concepts.definition: Deliberately pushing price through a known stop cluster to fill size against the triggered orders.
concepts.dolRole: Justifies drawing to the obvious pool (already the engine's premise).
concepts.evidenceNotes: [CORRECTED] Intent is documented: UK FCA final notices (Nov 2014, five banks, GBP 1.1 bn of fines; Barclays May 2015) record G10 FX traders who attempted to trigger clients' stop-loss orders. Mechanism strong (Osler cascades; Brunnermeier & Pedersen). Frequency unknown.
concepts.engineNotes: Core premise; no change.

concepts.name: Magnet effects near forced-order triggers (price limits, option strikes)
concepts.definition: Price accelerating toward a level where forced orders will trigger.
concepts.dolRole: None at bar level; supports the 'rounds are not magnets' reading.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Chinese A-shares: cooling-off, not magnet (Wan et al. 2015, 2018); ChiNext reform: no magnet (Qi 2023). Strike pinning on expiry exists in the literature, but single-case hedging explanations are disputed (Bar-Yam et al. 2014).
concepts.engineNotes: No strike/OI data in Pine; nothing to build.

concepts.name: Open-source pool/sweep definitions (Liquidity Swings / Liquidity Sweeps / smartmoneyconcepts)
concepts.definition: Liquidity Swings: zone = swing-candle wick extremity or full range, with revisit count and accumulated (intrabar) volume, filterable. Liquidity Sweeps: 'wick' (pierce and close back) and 'outbreak & retest' (close through, retest, opposite wick). smartmoneyconcepts: >=2 swings within a global-range band, average level, swept when beyond level + band.
concepts.dolRole: Benchmarks for the engine's definitions; their size and outbreak ideas were tested here.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitions only. B6: count/volume as size is null. B4: the outbreak-retest (RECLAIM) class is -1.5+/-0.7 pp vs geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: Engine zone lies beyond the extreme (right for stops); strict trade-through sweep; no multi-bar class. OF-2 adds classes, OF-1 the fresh wick.

proposals.title: Instant sweep-wick pools: a rejected sweep's wick becomes a pool at bar close (map, stack and stops at once; DOL-eligible after pivLen bars by default)
proposals.rationale: Stops form beyond every fresh extreme at once, but the engine registers a new extreme only after a pivLen-5 pivot. 61% (A) and 48-54% (BTC) of rejected-sweep wicks are re-taken within 5 bars, at +4 to +6 pp above null in the first 3 bars, so the map misses the most obvious level. f_invalidation also cannot put a counter-target's stop 'beyond the sweep high'. Carrying the swept pool's eqCount on micro-pokes also fixes the one-sided relative-equal merge (ICT-11).
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_LIQ after 99, display.none): useWick (true), wickTgt (false). Types: Level adds bool wick=false (after induce, 340); Trial adds bool wick=false (after liq, 389). Step 3 (1563-1589): before the loop declare float wkH=na, wkL=na and int wkEqH=0, wkEqL=0. Inside 'if hit and lv.isLiquidity()' (1580): back = side==1 ? close<lv.price : close>lv.price; if useWick and back then wkH:=high (or wkL:=low), and if pen<=eqTol then wkEq := max(wkEq, lv.eqCount+1). New step 4b after the registry drop (after 1596; never push while step 3 iterates): if not na(wkH) and not f_mergeLiq(pool,0,high,0,eqPx,(high-llR)/atr,1.0,false,bar_index,-1,-1), then create f_newLevel(nextId,0,0,high+wPx,high,high,bar_index,bar_index,coil,ind) with prom, wick=true and eqCount=wkEqH; mirror for SSL. When the pivot confirms pivLen bars later, f_mergeAt sees samePx and inBar (pivBar == bornBar), so it counts no equal print (1112-1114). Selection step 19 (1971-1983): canT = wickTgt or not lv.wick or bar_index-lv.bornBar>=pivLen; gate elig, the gI fallback and the objective with canT. f_invalidation iterates pool unfiltered, so stops use wick pools at once. tag() appends ' · WICK'. Ledger: f_openTrial passes wick; wkSt=[n,hits,sumPBase] booked in f_book (1461), shown in the Full view when wickTgt is on. Confirmed bars only, so non-repainting.
proposals.risk: More near-price pools, contained by poolMax eviction (1951) and by wickTgt off. Expected EDGE about 0 at H=30; its value is coverage, correct stops and correct EQ labels. Outside bars that reject both sides create both pools, which is correct.

proposals.title: Learned stop band, corrected stop placement and sweep classes incl. RECLAIM (absorbs ICT-7)
proposals.rationale: Rejected-sweep depth differs by market (q50 0.16-0.36 ATR; crypto deepest), so a fixed 0.20 fits only some charts. The engine's real stop is about 0.30 ATR beyond the pool (zone 0.20 + buffer 0.10) and is beaten by 41% of rejected sweeps (BTC 46-57%). A deeper stop only trades R for win rate (T4), so the honest fix is to show the band and offer the choice. A's spec added q80 beyond the zone edge (about 0.77 ATR, double counted); corrected here. Classes give alerts and ICT-2/ICT-9 a data-driven threshold. RECLAIM labels failed breakouts (21-29% of sweeps) without claiming an edge.
proposals.spec: Inputs: zoneATR stays 0.20 as the prior (tooltip lists market medians); zoneLearn (true); invBufM ['Tight','Beyond Stop Band'] default Tight (G_DOL); all display.none. STATE before 1343: var array<float> penRej; var float bandQ50, bandQ80; RECLAIM queue rcPx/rcSd/rcBr/rcAct (cap 8). At 1520 replace wPx: bandOK = zoneLearn and penRej.size()>=30; bandQ50 := bandOK ? penRej.percentile_linear_interpolation(50) : zoneATR; bandQ80 := bandOK ? ...(80) : 2.2*zoneATR; wPx = zoneATR<=0 ? 0 : f_clamp(bandQ50,0.05,0.60)*atr; a1 = nz(atr[1],atr). Start of step 3: walk the RECLAIM queue; if close is back inside within age<=3, set swAlert 'failed break · reclaimed after n bars'; remove an entry when reclaimed or at age>=3. In the hit branch (1580): pen=(side==1?high-P:P-low)/a1; clB=side*(close-P)/a1; cls = clB<0 ? (pen<=0.05 ? POKE : REJECT) : clB<bandQ50 ? PROBE : ACCEPT; push pen to penRej for clB<0 (cap 300), else enqueue for RECLAIM; if active target, swAlert = class + depth. f_invalidation 1343-1356: far = lv.bottom-buf / lv.top+buf (unchanged); bnd = lv.price - tgt.side*(nz(bandQ80,0.5)+0.05)*atr; inv = Tight ? far : farther of (far, bnd); the swing fallback uses (bandQ80+0.05)*atr when deep. string swAlert='' declared near 1510; ALERTS: alert(swAlert, alert.freq_once_per_bar_close); the live touch alert stays. Terminal line 'STOP BAND q50 · q80 (n) · stop x ATR beyond'. Decouple the zone from scoring: for liquidity, the confluence window at 675-676 is anchored on price +/- confTol plus the fixed zoneATR side; ICT-9's HOLD uses holdATR (or bandQ50), never lv.top. Classes and RECLAIM become ICT-2 cells with prior 0. Self-check: about 80% of penRej <= bandQ80.
proposals.risk: Thin histories use the prior until n=30. A deeper stop lowers the displayed R:R, which is honest. Without the confluence decoupling, learned deeper zones would silently raise the conf pillar on crypto.

proposals.title: Post-sweep volatility state applied to PoT, race, ETA AND the ledger baseline
proposals.rationale: After any pool trade-through, intraday ranges are +15-23% larger over 3 bars than bars with the same ATR5/ATR50 ratio (+8-15% at 10 bars, +4-10% at 30). The effect is absent on daily equities and largest on BTC. The engine's sigma (50-bar stdev) and empirical surface are unconditional, so short-horizon readouts are under-dispersed after sweeps. Because new trials open right after the old target is swept, the ledger baseline is too low exactly then: random levels are hit +2.1 to +3.4 pp above baseline on BTC, which flatters EDGE.
proposals.spec: STATE: var int lastSwp=-100000; var float vb3=1, vb10=1, vbAll=1. Step 3: lastSwp := bar_index on any liquidity hit. Each confirmed bar: rB=(high-low)/a1; vbAll := 0.995*vbAll + 0.005*rB; age 1-3 updates vb3 (0.97/0.03); age 4-10 updates vb10 (0.98/0.02). Helper f_sigEff(int h), declared before f_potModel (1302) and reading globals only: f3=clamp(vb3/vbAll,0.8,1.6), f10=clamp(vb10/vbAll,0.8,1.4); s2 = sum over k=1..h of f(age+k)^2; return nz(potSig)*sqrt(s2/h). This is a variance sum, so the effect fades naturally at H=30. Compute var float sigH = f_sigEff(H) once per confirmed bar. Use sigH in f_potModel (1304) AND f_potBase (1315), and query the empirical surface at d/(atr*sigH/potSig) in both (1307, 1318). Use it in f_invalidation (1360) and in the evaluate call (1948). TIME-4 / ETA use f_sigEff(h) with their own h. Ledger: Trial.swAge plus swCal=[n,hits,sumPBase] for post-sweep (<=3 bars) vs other trials in the Full view. At most a 30-iteration loop once per bar; no new request.
proposals.risk: Low: clamped, learned per chart (about 1.0 on daily equities), decaying. Must multiply with REG-1 / TIME-1 volatility clocks. Applying it to the model but not the baseline would bias EDGE the other way.

proposals.title: Round-number layer: cap zones on the 00/50 grid (M/2), optional stop snap past the round, no score bonus (amends ICT-3)
proposals.rationale: Order clustering at rounds is the best-documented fact in the domain (Osler; Bhattacharya et al.; Lallouache & Abergel; Donaldson & Kim; Cyree et al.), but on bars it is geometry. Rounds are not magnets (mixed sign). Sweep wicks stop short of a round beyond a pool: -4.2 pp at A's grid, -3.7+/-0.9 at half that grid, BTC -7.4+/-1.3 at 2,500 and -6.0+/-0.6 at 500. A coarse round once reached is passed +3.3 pp more. A capped at M only; B shows the M/2 (00/50) grid works and M/5 fades.
proposals.spec: Inputs (display.none): rnMode ['Off','Auto','Manual'] (Auto), rnMan, rnConf (false, G_SCORE). Global: newDayRN = timeframe.change('D'); atrD = nz(atrSlow)*sqrt(max(1, 86400/chartS)); once per day rnStep = smallest {1,5}x10^k >= atrD via math.log10/math.pow (Manual overrides); rnG = rnStep/2. Zone cap at 1762, 1774, 1848 and OF-1 step 4b: BSL R=ceil(P/rnG)*rnG; if P<R<P+wPx, zone top = R; SSL mirrors with floor. The hit rule is unchanged. Stop snap in f_invalidation after OF-2: if a grid level R lies beyond the opposing pool within +/-0.15 ATR of the computed stop, inv := R - tgt.side*0.03*atr. Confluence anchors at ceil/floor(close/rnG)*rnG only if rnConf (1931). Ledger bit RN (target within 0.35 ATR inside a grid level), rnSt=[n,hits,sumPBase] in the Full view.
proposals.risk: The auto step can be off on exotic symbols (Manual covers it). The stop snap is weak-to-moderate; verify with raceSt. ICT-3 must drop 'extend past the round' and use this cap.

proposals.title: Pool-size model = one evaluate() edit adopting ICT-10 Evidence + WYK-1 + WYK-2; no new size terms (volume rejected)
proposals.rationale: Every size proxy is null for reach at bar resolution: equal prints, tests, age, stack, prominence (negative at 1H), and the new B6 volume tests (pivot relative volume -1.5 pp, zone volume -0.5 pp, sign differs by market). Density (682) gives up to 5-15 unsupported points and the freshness ramp (671) about 4. A's original OF-3 formula conflicted with its siblings (dropped coil/induce, kept stack and prominence rewards) and is withdrawn.
proposals.spec: In evaluate (661-696): ev = magModel=='Evidence' (ICT-10); cz/iz = densIn=='Classic' ? coil/induce : COIL0 (0.55) / IND0 (0.93) (WYK-1). Liquidity freshness: dec = 0.5^(age/(4*halfLife)); fresh = freshLiq=='Flat' ? dec : classic ramp * dec (WYK-2). x = ev ? 1.2*tier + 0.4*min(1,prom/3) : classic x; dens = 0.60*(1-e^-x) + 0.25*cz + 0.15*iz; inner x0.70 only when not ev. Add no volume term. Display-only size tooltip ('tier HTF · prom 2.1 ATR · zone vol 1.8x'). Equal prints, tests and YOUNG/STALE become ICT-1 ledger bits with zero prior. Ship in the same edit as OF-2's confluence decoupling (675-676).
proposals.risk: Visible change: inside a 0.75-ATR stack the nearer pool often wins. The README line 'outermost is the draw' must change, or keep 'ICT Classic' as default if the user prefers the old behaviour.

proposals.title: Volume-profile path cost: small thin-path bonus, drop the HVN-wall penalty
proposals.rationale: A thin path gives +1.3 to +3.6 pp (unstable); a thick path gives -1.5 to +1.4 pp. The engine's x0.85 is worth 4-6 points on no evidence and can flip a selection. Traded volume is not resting liquidity in the path (Farmer et al.: gaps, not volume, drive large moves).
proposals.spec: At 1947 (edited together with ICT-5's opposing-FVG cost): lv.mult *= vf<0.6 ? vpThin : vf>1.4 ? vpThick : 1.0. Inputs vpThin=1.05 and vpThick=1.00 (G_SCORE, display.none, evidence tooltip). A/B on overall EDGE.
proposals.risk: Negligible.

proposals.title: Opt-in delta context label at sweeps (BVC from >=24 intrabars), no 'absorption = reversal' claim, graded by the ledger
proposals.rationale: Traders ask for delta confirmation and competitors offer it, but true Binance taker data contradicts the usual reading. Absorption is the norm on rejection bars (68.6%), and absorbed rejections lean continuation (+4.7+/-2.2 pp at K30). Pine-buildable proxies match the true delta sign only 60-66% of the time. A's ABSORBED/EXHAUSTED/DRIVEN tags would mislabel often and imply an edge that does not exist. request.footprint is Premium/Ultimate-only with one call per script.
proposals.spec: Input useDelta (false, G_FLOW), disabled when syminfo.volumetype=='n/a'. ltfD = timeframe.from_seconds(max(60, int(timeframe.in_seconds()/24))); [ltO, ltC, ltV] = request.security_lower_tf(syminfo.tickerid, ltfD, [open,close,volume], ignore_invalid_timeframe=true): one extra unique request; 100K intrabars / 24 covers about 4,000 chart bars (limitations.md 263-271). On confirmed sweep bars only: BVC delta = sum of V_i*(2*Phi(dP_i/sigma_ltf)-1). Label 'delta into pool x% of vol' / 'delta away', with a tooltip giving this chart's base rate and the ledger outcome per cell (ICT-2 cells, prior weight 0). Never feeds D or the score.
proposals.risk: Users over-trust delta, so the honest tooltip is mandatory. FX has tick volume only. The extra request and loop run on sweep bars only.

result.summary: The engine's closed-form PoT and race maths (f_pot, f_race, f_raceH) are correct. A's Monte Carlo check confirms this, and B re-derived the f_raceH flux series line by line. The inputs are the problem. The 0.5 x 50-bar drift is the largest error in the PoT and, new from B, in the displayed WIN<=H race. Removing it improves PoT log-loss by +3.66% (95% day-block CI +2.99..+4.32; +2.32..+4.82 clustered by calendar day) and race log-loss by +3.58%, on all 6 CME symbols. Today WIN<=H is badly over-confident (calibration slope 0.69). On 479k decided races, a driftless f_raceH fed the forward volatility-time sigma_eff = sqrt(V_H/H) is calibrated (slope 1.00) and beats the current engine by +4.29%. The martingale value b/(a+b) is only right for close barriers: horizon conditioning moves wide, asymmetric races by up to 9 pp. On real bars the reflection identity holds almost exactly: P(touch within H) = 2.00 x P(finish beyond at H) across 0.5-4 ATR. So bar highs and lows are the continuous path maximum (touches need no correction), and fat tails act only through the terminal distribution. Close-based events do need the Broadie-Glasserman-Kou shift of 0.5826 sigma, which is also the expected overshoot of a Gaussian random walk (+6.28% LL; confirmed by Monte Carlo). Better still, close-based events can get their own cheap empirical close-excursion surface. The default Empirical surface is calibrated but blind to time and volatility state. A volatility-state split with partial pooling gives +1.79% (all 6 symbols), and the HTF-regime rows (no side skill) should be shrunk the same way. The volatility clock is real, but as a displayed PoT it loses on CL and GC, so it is P1 as an input (race, ETA, close-beyond, state) and gated per chart. It must be keyed to the session time zone, not UTC, and walk the real future-bar calendar: Pine's time(bars_back = -j) gives that up to 500 bars ahead. Range-based sigma alone is not significant (+0.28%, CI includes 0), and published real-data efficiencies are 1.2-5x, not 5-14x. The displayed PoT is never graded; add grading, but recalibrate only behind a prequential gate, because learners trained on selected targets lose on clean data. B also corrected a sibling ETA formula: (d/1.2816)^2 is the 20% quantile, not the 80%. The 95% cap, live remaining-time and beyond-grid issues are real but each is under 1 pp.

concepts.name: One-barrier first passage (reflection principle) with drift
concepts.definition: X_t = mu*t + sigma*W_t, barrier d>0, horizon h bars: P(touch) = Phi((mu*h - d)/(sigma*sqrt h)) + exp(2*mu*d/sigma^2)*Phi((-mu*h - d)/(sigma*sqrt h)). Driftless: 2*Phi(-d/(sigma*sqrt h)), i.e. touch = 2 x finish-beyond. In volatility time replace sigma^2*h by the integrated forecast variance V: P = 2*Phi(-d/sqrt V). Edge cases: d<=0 -> 1; compute the exp term in log space.
concepts.dolRole: The core 'how likely within H' number for any target; also drives proximity reach and the close-beyond and race readouts.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Textbook result; A's Monte Carlo matches (e.g. 0.3613 vs 0.3600). B on CME bars: touch/finish-beyond ratio is 2.00/2.00/2.02/2.01/2.01/1.99 at 0.5/1/2/3/4/6 ATR (5-min, H=30) and 2.00-2.01 to 3 ATR on 1-hour. Practitioner option studies (tastylive, about 20 years of SPY) report the same ~2x (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: f_pot 434-444 is correct, with log-space f_expPhi 421-429. The 0.95 cap sits inside (444) and the inputs are noisy: the trailing sigma at 916 and the drift at 917.

concepts.name: Two-barrier race, infinite horizon (martingale race)
concepts.definition: P(+a before -b) = (1 - e^{kb})/(e^{-ka} - e^{kb}), k = 2*mu/sigma^2; driftless value b/(a+b). For any continuous martingale this holds by optional stopping, whatever the stochastic or seasonal volatility, provided the race is eventually decided.
concepts.dolRole: Which of two liquidity pools is taken first, as the horizon goes to infinity; also the limit for close barriers.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Theory strong. A: within 0.4-1.2 pp of b/(a+b) for pairs up to 3 ATR (~28k races per cell). B reproduced it: 1/1 0.495, 1/2 0.662, 2/1 0.321, 1/3 0.755, 3/1 0.225.
concepts.engineNotes: f_race 447-462 is correct, and so is the limit when |k(a+b)| < 1e-6.

concepts.name: Finite-horizon race conditioned on 'decided within H' (WIN<=H)
concepts.definition: P(target first | one barrier hit within H) = P_W(H)/(P_W(H)+P_L(H)), with P_W(h) = P_inf - tail(h) and tail(h) = e^{mu*a/sigma^2} * sum_n (sigma^2*n*pi/L^2)(-1)^{n+1} sin(n*pi*b/L) e^{-(lambda_n+nu)h}/(lambda_n+nu), lambda_n = sigma^2 n^2 pi^2/(2L^2), nu = mu^2/(2 sigma^2), L = a+b. Conditioning favours the nearer barrier, which is decided earlier. The size of that effect depends on the horizon variance, so the race needs FORWARD variance (sigma_eff = sqrt(V_H/H)).
concepts.dolRole: The displayed WIN<=H (target before invalidation), and the 'next liquidity taken' race.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B, 5-min CME, H=30: 598k races, 479k decided, 14 barrier pairs. Slope: b/(a+b) 1.20, f_raceH sigma50 0.89, engine with drift 0.69, vol-time sigma_eff 1.00. LL: engine 0.6359 -> no drift 0.6131 -> vol-time 0.6086, which is +4.29% (CI +3.38..+5.11; calendar-day +2.69..+5.85). Example a/b = 2/6 ATR: observed 0.813, b/(a+b) 0.750, sigma50 0.865, vol-time 0.822. Brownian motion over-predicts P(decided) by 3-7 pp. Theory: B re-derived the series.
concepts.engineNotes: f_invalidation 1343-1364 uses f_raceH (466-482, correct maths) with drift potMu*side (1361-1363) and the trailing potSig. f_raceAdj 1367-1373 is intercept-only and cannot fix a slope of 0.69. The ledger raceSt (1487-1492) already measures the conditional form.

concepts.name: Discrete-monitoring continuity correction (Broadie-Glasserman-Kou) and expected overshoot
concepts.definition: A barrier checked only at bar closes is priced with the continuous formula after shifting the barrier away by beta*sigma_bar, beta = -zeta(1/2)/sqrt(2*pi) ~ 0.5826; the error falls from O(1/sqrt m) to o(1/sqrt m). The same constant is the limiting expected overshoot of a driftless Gaussian random walk (Chang-Peres). It does not apply to high/low touches.
concepts.dolRole: Probability that price CLOSES beyond a pool (break, BOS, iFVG inversion) versus merely wicking it (sweep).
concepts.evidenceNotes: BGK 1997 Math. Finance; Chang & Peres 1997; Janssen & van Leeuwaarden. B's Monte Carlo at z=1: walk 0.272, BGK 0.269, continuous 0.317. A's data (5-min, H=30): realised 0.453, continuous 0.583, BGK 0.517. B's bootstrap: LL +6.28% (CI +5.88..+6.67; calendar-day +5.69..+6.85).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent for touches (touched() 621-623 uses highs/lows). No close-beyond probability exists anywhere.

concepts.name: Time-to-touch distribution and ETA quantiles
concepts.definition: Driftless in vol time: F(tau) = 2*Phi(-d/sqrt V(tau)). Unconditional q-quantile: first tau with sqrt V >= d/Phi^-1(1-q/2) (median 0.6745, 80% 0.2533). Conditional on a touch within H: first tau with F(tau) >= q*F(H), i.e. sqrt V >= d/Phi^-1(1 - q*F(H)/2). With drift: inverse Gaussian.
concepts.dolRole: WHEN the target is likely to be reached (bars and clock time), and 'PoT to session end'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A, 5-min, H=60: rank correlation of actual T with predicted median is -0.09 (constant sigma) vs +0.11/+0.16/+0.22 (vol time, at 1/2/3 ATR); 45-47% of hits come at or before the predicted median. B corrected sibling TIME-6: '(d/1.2816)^2' is the 20% quantile, not the 80%.
concepts.engineNotes: 2116-2126: median bars-to-hit of past DOL hits within +-0.5 ATR of the current distance. Time-blind; no quantiles or clock time.

concepts.name: Fat tails, stochastic-volatility mixture and jumps
concepts.definition: PoT(d) = E_sigma[2*Phi(-d/(sigma*sqrt h))]. Against a Gaussian with the same variance, a volatility mixture lowers near-level and raises far-level touch probability. Because the reflection identity holds, PoT(d) = 2*P(X_H > d) for the actual terminal law. Jumps add overshoot (Kou-Wang double exponential), and stop cascades (Osler) act right at the level.
concepts.dolRole: Correct probabilities for far targets (HTF objective, PW levels) and near ones.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Perello, Gutierrez-Roig & Masoliver 2011 (paper read; transaction data on 6 futures, 1-120 min): the Wiener model under-estimates for x >~ v_t and over-estimates for x <~ 0.1 v_t; curves collapse up to 10 v_t; Student-t tail beyond ~5 v_t. A: at 6 ATR the analytic gives 0.118 vs 0.150 realised (H=30); at 1-2 ATR it over-predicts by 3-4 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: The empirical surface captures fat tails inside the 15-ATR grid. The beyond-grid fallback (1292-1293) is Gaussian, but it is rarely used: only when d > 15 x ATR14 in quiet sessions.

concepts.name: Range-based volatility estimators (Parkinson, Garman-Klass, Rogers-Satchell, Yang-Zhang)
concepts.definition: Per-bar variance proxies: Parkinson (H-L)^2/(4 ln2); GK 0.5(H-L)^2 - (2ln2-1)(C-O)^2; RS (H-C)(H-O)+(L-C)(L-O); YZ sigma_o^2 + k*sigma_c^2 + (1-k)*sigma_RS^2 with k = 0.34/(1.34+(n+1)/(n-1)). Add the gap term (O-C[1])^2 and winsorise roll gaps.
concepts.dolRole: Lower-noise per-bar variance proxy feeding a seasonal, clustered forecast. Not a stand-alone upgrade.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Theoretical efficiency 5.2/7.4/~6/highest (strong). Real-data efficiency is much lower: 1.2-5x on index data, with no consistent winner (Vinte et al. 2022); Shu & Zhang 2006 (moderate). B's bootstrap: YZ vs close-to-close +0.28% LL, CI -0.10..+0.66, not significant.
concepts.engineNotes: potSig = ta.stdev(chg, potLen) at 916. Switching estimators alone is not worth it; use the range proxy inside the clock (QPOT-05).

concepts.name: Intraday seasonality and volatility (business) time
concepts.definition: r = sigma_day * s(tau) * q * z (Andersen-Bollerslev; Engle-Sokalska daily x diurnal x intraday GARCH; Dacorogna theta-time). Forward variance V(j) = sum_{i<=j} s^2(tau_{t+i}) * [L_s + phi^i (L_f - L_s)], where tau_{t+i} are the REAL future bar times (sessions, weekends, the daily halt), keyed to exchange/NY time, not UTC.
concepts.dolRole: The same distance is far more reachable when the next H bars include the cash open than overnight. This drives PoT, race, ETA and close-beyond.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ES 5-min variance is 4.67x the day mean at 09:30 ET and 0.20x at 23:30 ET (A). About 75% of daily S&P 500 variance falls in the cash hours (Hansen et al. 2012). Crypto is high near 16 UTC and low near 5 UTC, with spikes at the 00/08/16 UTC funding times (Hansen-Kim-Kimbrough 2024; primary source verified). TIME-3's NY-keyed clock scored +3.9% vs +3.5% for UTC. As a displayed PoT, the calibrated vol-time model gains +1.46% on average but loses on CL (-1.8%) and GC (-1.2%), and the sibling clock loses 9.8% on GC 1-hour.
concepts.engineNotes: Killzone multipliers affect scoring only. The PoT horizon is a flat H bars with a trailing sigma. The tz input (219) exists. Pine time(timeframe.period, '', bars_back = -j) returns expected future bar times for j up to 500.

concepts.name: Volatility clustering forecast (EWMA / GARCH-lite / HAR / CARR)
concepts.definition: EWMA sigma^2_t = lambda*sigma^2_{t-1} + (1-lambda)*x_t. GARCH term structure E[sigma^2_{t+j}] = Lbar + phi^j (sigma^2_t - Lbar). HAR cascade. CARR: a GARCH-type recursion on the range. In Pine: a fast and a slow EWMA of the deseasonalised range proxy, with mean reversion phi = 0.5^(1/30).
concepts.dolRole: Forecasts how volatile the NEXT H bars will be, not the last 50.
concepts.evidenceNotes: RiskMetrics; Corsi 2009; Chou 2005 (CARR beats GARCH out of sample on S&P 500). A: deseasonalised log-range ACF on ES is 0.63 at lag 1 and 0.27 at one day. Ablation: seasonality with a flat level gives LL 0.6003 vs 0.5659 with clustering (H=30).
concepts.engineNotes: Flat ta.stdev window at 916. atrSlow (875) is used only for ejection.

concepts.name: Drift estimation and short-horizon predictability
concepts.definition: mu_hat from n bars has SE sigma/sqrt n. With weight w in an H-bar formula it shifts the standardised barrier by w*sqrt(H/n)*Z (0.39 Z at H=30, n=50, w=0.5). Set it to 0, or shrink it with positive-part James-Stein so it stays zero unless |t| > 1.
concepts.dolRole: Directional tilt of PoT and race. When noisy it randomly favours one side and double-counts the Draw pillar.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou 2018: R^2 1.6% in sample, 1.2% out of sample. PoT: +3.66% LL from removing the drift (CI +2.99..+4.32; calendar-day +2.32..+4.82; every symbol +3.1..+4.1%). Race: +3.58% (calendar-day CI +1.98..+5.02; every symbol). Driftless simulation: drift raises LL 5.4%, slope 0.83.
concepts.engineNotes: potMu = ta.sma(chg,50)*driftW (917; driftW default 0.5 at 185). It enters evaluate 665 (via 1948), f_potModel 1304 (via 2067, 2184) and f_invalidation 1361-1363.

concepts.name: Variance ratio (trend vs mean reversion)
concepts.definition: VR(q) = Var(q-bar return)/(q*Var(1-bar)) ~ 1 + 2*sum(1-j/q)*rho_j. VR < 1 means mean reversion: far levels are less reachable than sqrt(H) scaling implies.
concepts.dolRole: Scales reachability of far levels per symbol.
concepts.engineNotes: sqrt(H) scaling is acceptable; the empirical surface absorbs the residual.

concepts.name: Empirical excursion surface with overlap-aware sample size
concepts.definition: For each completed H-bar window: up/down max excursion from the start close, in ATR at the window start, counted on a 0.25-ATR grid out to 15 ATR. Survival counts give the empirical PoT. Overlapping windows: nEff = n/(0.6H).
concepts.dolRole: Symbol-specific, calibrated reach probabilities and reach bands.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: ECE 0.004, slope 0.99; VIF/H 0.21-0.83. calib_ml: distance-matched baseline slope 0.93-1.04 on 13/14 datasets.
concepts.engineNotes: sUp/sDn 1058-1062, f_bump/f_surv/f_empPoT 1265-1300, update 1527-1532. It learns on all loaded bars (outside inCalc) with htfBias[H] and atr[H] (leak-free). No forgetting.

concepts.name: State conditioning with partial pooling
concepts.definition: p_cell = (nE_c*p_hat_c + m*p_parent)/(nE_c + m), nE = n/(0.6H), m = 30, in three levels: global -> HTF regime -> state. State = tercile of q = sqrt(V_H)/(ATR*sqrt H), or an 8 x 3-hour block in tz.
concepts.dolRole: Adds 'when' and 'in what volatility' resolution at a fixed ATR distance while staying calibrated. It also shrinks the HTF-regime rows, which have no side skill.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A/B: vol-state split +1.79% LL (CI +1.45..+2.13; calendar-day +1.14..+2.44), all 6 symbols better, ECE <= 0.004; 1-hour H=12 0.5268 -> 0.5086; 1-min 0.5517 -> 0.5484. TIME-2 tod8: Brier +0.1..+5.9% in 24/24 tests. ATR14/ATR200 alone gives almost nothing. Efron-Morris shrinkage cut total squared error about 3.5x.
concepts.engineNotes: Only the 3-row HTF-regime split exists, used unshrunk once n >= nMin; the pooled row is a fallback only (f_empPoT 1284-1300).

concepts.name: Bayesian blending of model and empirical rates
concepts.definition: Beta-binomial posterior mean (k + m*p0)/(n + m), with the analytic model as a prior worth m effective windows and nEff = n/(0.6H).
concepts.dolRole: Stable PoT during warm-up and in sparse cells.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard conjugate Bayes. The prior keeps 3-10% weight at typical history (nEff ~300-1,100) and ~48% at the nMin gate.
concepts.engineNotes: f_potModel 1303-1311 (priorM 30) has the correct form, but the prior carries the drift and the cap. f_potBase 1314-1322 is driftless.

concepts.name: Calibration and proper scoring of the displayed PoT (gated)
concepts.definition: Brier, log-loss, Murphy REL-RES+UNC, 10-bin reliability/ECE, calibration slope, BSS vs the distance-matched base rate. Recalibrate with an intercept logit shift, Platt, beta calibration (which contains the identity map) or isotonic (>= ~1,000 points), applied ONLY when it beats the raw model prequentially.
concepts.dolRole: Makes the headline PoT trustworthy and self-auditing per chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005; Kull et al. 2017; Murphy 1973. A: Platt on vol time, slope 0.89 -> 1.01, ECE 0.062 -> 0.024. calib_ml: learners on selected targets lose 0.15-5.5% LL on clean data; a gate costs <= 0.26% and recovers 8.8% on broken data.
concepts.engineNotes: Trial 375-395 has pBase and pRace but no pPot. f_book 1461-1499 never grades the displayed PoT. f_raceAdj does an intercept shift for races only.

concepts.name: Liquidity levels vs random levels (stop clustering, S/R memory)
concepts.definition: Stops and take-profits cluster at salient levels: take-profits reverse trends, and stops accelerate moves once crossed. Bounce probability rises with prior bounces and decays with time.
concepts.dolRole: Explains any departure of real pools from random-level PoT; the ledger EDGE measures it per chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2003/2005. Chung & Bellotti 2021 (paper read): with 1 prior bounce the effect decays to 0.5 at ~350-minute windows, with 4 at ~900 (EURUSD 2018). calib_ml: engine-like pools hit at the random-level baseline +-2 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: EDGE vs a distance-matched random level exists (f_potBase 1314; panel 2375-2389) but is not fed into the displayed PoT.

concepts.name: Expected reach d*PoT(d)
concepts.definition: For driftless BM, d*2*Phi(-d/s), s = sigma*sqrt H, peaks where Phi(-z) = z*phi(z): z ~ 0.75, PoT ~ 45%.
concepts.dolRole: A principled shape for the proximity/reach pillar (distance delivered x probability).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Maths checked by B (Phi(-0.75) = 0.2266 vs 0.75*phi(0.75) = 0.2259). calib_ml: a max-d*PoT picker delivers 1.10-1.43 ATR per target vs 0.86-1.09 for the engine-like score.
concepts.engineNotes: evaluate 662-667 blends a linear term with the drift-laden reach f_pot(...)/0.95 and a taper; this is ad hoc.

concepts.name: Future-bar calendar for horizon variance (Pine feasibility)
concepts.definition: Horizon variance must sum over the next H TRADING bars. time(timeframe.period, '', bars_back = -j) returns the expected timestamp of the j-th future bar (j <= 500; session-aware, no holidays). An alternative is a learned open-cell grid walk.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents counting weekends or the daily halt as trading time (e.g. on Friday afternoon) in PoT, ETA and session-end PoT.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Local Pine v6 docs (reference/time.md; concepts/sessions.md loop example with time_close(..., bars_back = -i)). A's backtest used the actual future bars, while A's Pine spec walked clock time; B corrected the spec.
concepts.engineNotes: No forward calendar is used. potH max 450 fits the -500 limit.

concepts.name: 95% probability cap
concepts.definition: Display convention of the reference product. Mathematically a near level's PoT approaches 1, so the cap should sit only in text, plots and the minPoT filter.
concepts.dolRole: Display only.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Spec convention. B measured the impact: <= 0.4 pp in f_potBase once warm and <= 5% relative in the reach term.
concepts.engineNotes: Inside f_pot 444 and f_potModel 1310; evaluate divides by 0.95 (665). The effect is cosmetic.

proposals.title: Remove the 50-bar drift from every probability (PoT, proximity reach, race)
proposals.rationale: The drift is the largest single error: PoT log-loss +3.66% (CI +2.99..+4.32, calendar-day +2.32..+4.82) and race log-loss +3.58% (CI +2.74..+4.41) when removed, on all 6 symbols. It also double-counts the Draw pillar inside proximity.
proposals.spec: Set the driftW default (line 185) to 0.0, hidden with display = display.none, or set line 917 to float potMu = 0.0. If the input is kept, shrink the raw mean: muRaw = ta.sma(chg, potLen); tD = muRaw/max(potSig/sqrt(potLen), 1e-12); potMu = driftW*muRaw*max(0, 1 - 1/max(tD^2, 1e-12)) (positive-part James-Stein). Call sites then carry zero drift: evaluate via 1948, f_potModel via 2067/2184, f_invalidation 1361-1363. No other change is needed; f_potBase is already driftless.
proposals.risk: Selection shifts slightly because proximity becomes side-symmetric. Direction still flows through the Draw pillar and the regime rows of the surface.

proposals.title: Make WIN<=H a calibrated finite-horizon race (driftless f_raceH with forward sigma_eff)
proposals.rationale: The displayed WIN<=H has calibration slope 0.69. A driftless f_raceH is +3.58% better; with forward volatility-time sigma_eff it reaches slope 1.00 and is +4.29% better (CI +3.38..+5.11; calendar-day +2.69..+5.85). b/(a+b) is too timid for wide or asymmetric barriers (up to 9 pp off).
proposals.spec: In f_invalidation (1343-1364): sg = clkUse ? close*sqrt(fwdV/H) : nz(potSig); pW = f_raceH(d, risk, sg, 0.0, H); pL = f_raceH(risk, d, sg, 0.0, H); return pW+pL > 1e-9 ? pW/(pW+pL) : risk/(d+risk). Keep f_raceAdj. Add a Sigma(p-y)^2 slot to raceSt so the Full panel shows the race Brier and slope. Do not display the unconditional P(decided within H): Brownian motion over-predicts it by 3-7 pp. If wanted, show the ledger's undecided share instead.
proposals.risk: Minimal. The last +0.7% needs QPOT-05 (sigma_eff); the sigma50 form works stand-alone.

proposals.title: State-conditioned empirical surface with three-level partial pooling (global -> HTF regime -> time block or vol state)
proposals.rationale: The default surface is calibrated but time- and volatility-blind. A vol-state split gives +1.79% LL (CI +1.45..+2.13; calendar-day +1.14..+2.44) on all 6 symbols, and sibling TIME-2's time-of-day split improved Brier in 24/24 tests. HTF-regime rows (no side skill) are used unshrunk today. This merges A-03, TIME-2 and REG-1.
proposals.spec: Input potKey ['Off', 'Time block', 'Vol state'] (G_POT, display.none). Constants NS=8, NS1=9 (row 8 = state-pooled), POOLM=30. Series: stNow = 'Time block' and intraday and chartS <= 3600 ? int(hour(time, tz)/3) : 'Vol state' ? vsNow : NS. vsNow = tercile of ln q, q = sqrt(fwdV)/(atr/close*sqrt H), using an EWMA mean/sd (alpha = 1-0.5^(1/2000)), cut at m +- 0.43 s. State: sUp/sDn = array.new<int>(3*NS1*NB1), row = regime*NS1 + state. Step 0 (1528-1532): bump the pooled row (bH+1)*NS1+NS, and the cell when stNow[H] < NS. f_empPoT(dAtr, side, bias, st): n0/k0 summed over the three regimes' pooled rows (global parent; nMin gate on n0); pR = (nR/dv*pR_hat + 30*p0)/(nR/dv + 30); p = (nC/dv*pC_hat + 30*pR)/(nC/dv + 30), dv = max(1, 0.6H); return [p, n0]. f_potModel/f_potBase pass stNow; f_reachD uses the cell when its count >= nMin. Memory 3.3k ints; 3 O(NB) bumps per side per bar.
proposals.risk: Slower per-cell warm-up (handled by pooling). The 'Vol state' key needs QPOT-05. Choose the key per chart through the TIME-4 scorecard.

proposals.title: Grade the displayed PoT in the ledger; recalibrate only behind a prequential gate
proposals.rationale: The headline 'PoT: 70.1%' is never checked against outcomes. Grading is cheap and makes the product self-auditing. Blind recalibration on selected targets loses on clean data (calib_ml), so it must be gated.
proposals.spec: Trial (375-395): add float pPot = na, set in f_openTrial (1426-1431) to f_potModel(d, lv.side, 0.0) (uncapped). STATE: potSt[9] = [n, Sigma(p-y)^2, Sigma(pBase-y)^2, SigmaLL, Sigma p, Sigma y, prequential SigmaLL(raw) - SigmaLL(cal), K, Psum], plus rbN/rbP/rbY[10] reliability bins. f_book (1461): before using y, compute delta = n >= 30 ? f_logit((K + 20*Pbar)/(n + 20)) - f_logit(Pbar) : 0 and pc = f_sigm(f_logit(p) + delta); add LL(p,y) - LL(pc,y) to potSt[6]; then update the sums and bin int(p*10). Show the calibrated value only if n >= 50 and potSt[6] > 2.0; optionally use beta calibration once n >= 300. Terminal Full row: 'PoT CAL pred 44% · obs 46% · Brier .201 vs base .215 · n 212' plus a 10-cell reliability strip. Clean style shows it in the tooltip only.
proposals.risk: Overlapping trials make the effective n small; keep the gate conservative and use 2H-bar blocks (as in cluSt) for any z-score.

proposals.title: Forward-variance engine: robust tz-keyed volatility clock over the real future-bar calendar (input to race, state, ETA, close-beyond; display use gated)
proposals.rationale: Every time-aware readout needs V(j). Seasonality x clustering is the only analytic model that approaches the empirical surface. As a stand-alone displayed PoT it averages +1.46% (CI +0.85..+2.11) but loses on CL/GC and GC 1-hour, so it is an input everywhere and the display model only behind the TIME-4 scorecard. B corrects A's spec: tz not UTC, additive floored update, real calendar.
proposals.spec: Adopt the sibling TIME-3 robust code. Proxy: log GK + gap, winsorised at 25x the slow level. Bucket by tz time of day (max(15/30 min, chart TF)) x weekday factor: additive EWMA of the deseasonalised ratio, 1/n warm start, floors 0.05/0.2, daily renormalisation. Fast level L_f (span ~potLen) and slow level L_s (~5 days), L_f >= 0.2 L_s, phi = 0.5^(1/30). V(j) = sum_{i<=j} s^2(bucket(t_i), weekday(t_i))*[L_s + phi^i(L_f - L_s)], with t_i the i-th FUTURE bar. On scoring bars use TIME-3's open-cell grid walk (~H/bpb iterations). On barstate.islast use the exact int ti = time(timeframe.period, '', bars_back = -i), i <= min(H, 500), filling var array<float> vCum. Outputs: series fwdV = V(H) (so fwdV[H] exists), vCum, clkUse (warm >= 5 days, intraday <= 4H).
proposals.risk: Holidays and early closes overstate V (label clock outputs with '≈'). Jump-prone or roll-gapped data (GC 1H) needs the gate. Loop cost is bounded (H <= 450).

proposals.title: ETA quantiles in volatility time and 'PoT to session end' (corrected quantile formulas)
proposals.rationale: Traders need WHEN. The current bar-count ETA ranks time-to-touch wrongly (-0.09); vol time ranks it correctly (+0.11/+0.16/+0.22). Sibling TIME-6's ETA80 constant is wrong (1.2816 gives the 20% quantile).
proposals.spec: F(j) = 2*Phi(-d/sqrt V(j)), V from vCum (times close^2 for price units). Conditional ETA_q = first j with F(j) >= q*F(H), i.e. sqrt V(j) >= d/Phi^-1(1 - q*F(H)/2); show q = 0.5 and 0.8 (binary search over vCum, <= 9 steps). Unconditional median uses 0.6745, unconditional 80% uses 0.2533. Clock label: str.format_time(time(timeframe.period, '', bars_back = -j), 'HH:mm', tz). Session end: loop time_close(timeframe.period, sess, bars_back = -i) until na (<= 500), then PoT_S = surface/analytic at z = d/sqrt V(j_end). HUD: 'PoT 30b 64% · →16:00 71% · ETA ≈10:35 (80% by 11:20)'. Ledger: store T and ETA50/80 for hits and show coverage (targets 50%/80%). Fallback without the clock: the current ETA.
proposals.risk: Holiday calendars are unknown (show '≈'). Requires QPOT-05.

proposals.title: Close-beyond probability ('sweep vs break'): empirical close-excursion surface with a BGK prior
proposals.rationale: Raids are wick events and breaks are close events. The continuous formula over-states close-beyond by 13 pp. The BGK shift fixes most of it (+6.28% LL, CI +5.88..+6.67). An empirical close surface removes the remaining level bias at almost no cost.
proposals.spec: Series: fwdHiC = ta.highest(close, H), fwdLoC = ta.lowest(close, H). State: var array<int> cUp/cDn = array.new<int>(NB1, 0). Step 0 (same guard as 1528): f_bump(cUp, 0, (fwdHiC - close[H])/aH) and the mirror for cDn. f_closePoT(d, side): sb = clkUse ? close*sqrt(fwdV/H) : potSig; pA = sb > 0 ? f_erfc((d + 0.5826*sb)/(sb*sqrt(2H))) : 0; blend (nE*f_surv/n + priorM*pA)/(nE + priorM) with nE = n/(0.6H). HUD/tooltip for liquidity targets: 'PoT 71% · close-thru 52%'. PoT minus close-thru is the chance of a wick-only raid within H.
proposals.risk: One more HUD field. Warms with the same windows as the touch surface.

proposals.title: 'Next liquidity taken' race readout (nearest BSL vs nearest SSL) with ledger tilt
proposals.rationale: This is the literal DOL question as a two-barrier race. With QPOT-02's model it is calibrated, and the ledger's deviation from it measures per-chart liquidity magnetism.
proposals.spec: On confirmed bars, take the nearest unswept kind <= 1 pool above (a) and below (b), both >= minDistATR*atr. pUp = f_raceH(a,b,sg,0,H)/(f_raceH(a,b,sg,0,H) + f_raceH(b,a,sg,0,H)), with sg as in QPOT-02. Ledger var array<float> nxSt[4] = [n, upWins, Sigma p, Sigma(p-y)^2]: one open record per new pair, resolved on the first strict trade-through (ties by the bar-path rule), dropped after H bars if undecided. Apply a logit shift like f_raceAdj when n >= 30. Terminal row 'NEXT ▲ BSL 62% · ▼ SSL 38%'; optional alert() when one side >= 70% at bar close.
proposals.risk: Pools very near price resolve in 1-2 bars (hence the minDist gate). Adds one panel row.

proposals.title: Display-only 95% cap and small hygiene items
proposals.rationale: The cap belongs to display. Its measured impact on scoring and the EDGE baseline is <= 0.4 pp, so this is a consistency fix only. The live remaining-time correction (< 1 pp) is dropped.
proposals.spec: f_pot (444) and f_potModel (1310) return uncapped values. Apply math.min(0.95, p) only at the label 2225, HUD 2240, panel 2354, alert 2081, plot 2446 and the minPoT comparisons 2068/2185. evaluate 665: reach = f_pot(dist, sig, 0.0, potH) without /0.95. f_potBase uncapped. Beyond the grid (1292-1293): mixture 0.5*f_erfc(d/(0.8*sH*sqrt2)) + 0.5*f_erfc(d/(1.17*sH*sqrt2)), or widen bStep so the grid covers the eject distance in ATR14 units.
proposals.risk: Negligible.

proposals.title: Two-expert model mixture (surface vs clock z-surface) instead of a fixed logistic stack
proposals.rationale: A's stack had the best pooled log-loss (0.5503 at H=30) but was fragile. Unregularised online logistic loses 3.6-5.5% elsewhere (calib_ml). An exponential-weights mixture keeps most of the upside and is bounded by the better expert.
proposals.spec: Experts: e1 = QPOT-03 surface, e2 = QPOT-05/TIME-3 clock z-surface. w_i ∝ exp(-eta*L_i), eta = 0.25, fixed share 0.005, where L_i is the probe log-loss from TIME-4's probe ring buffer (6 probes per bar, resolved at t+H). PoT = w1*p1 + w2*p2. Full panel shows 'PoT MODEL mix 0.7/0.3'. Re-evaluated daily; non-repainting.
proposals.risk: Extra state from the TIME-4 probe ring buffer ((H+1)*18 floats). Depends on QPOT-03/05.

result.summary: Researcher B checked A's sources, code and engine line references, ran four new tests (random-walk noise floors; 13 reach-surface designs on 5 families including BTC 1H; a higher-timeframe trend regime; displacement and NR7-break continuation), and merged everything into one corrected report. A's core thesis holds: trend and range labels (ER, ADX, CHOP, Hurst) do not persist and add no side information beyond race geometry. That is also true for a higher-timeframe efficiency regime on all five families. On a pure random walk ER20 ≥ 0.40 appears on 15.7% of bars, ADX ≥ 25 on 38%, and CHOP averages 46.9 (A said ≈ 50). A's biggest error is REG-1. Volatility-tercile rows are not the right fix. The engine's ATR14-unit surface over-predicts reach by 5.5-8.2 pp in expanded volatility on 15m/1H/BTC (this replicates sibling amt B7). Measuring the surface in √(ATR14·ATR100), a horizon-matched unit, together with TIME-2's time-of-day rows cuts out-of-sample log-loss by 3.0% (5m), 5.8% (15m), 0.65% (1H) and 1.2% (BTC), and cuts that bias to −0.8..−3.1 pp. Vol rows add nothing on top and dilute the time-of-day rows. Daily charts keep ATR14. A's efficiency gate on D "recovers geometry" only because it acts on 0.3-0.5% of races, so in practice it switches D off. A's soft gate is worse than a hard gate, and A's spec would have changed the Draw Flip alert. The other D components are null too: displacement bars do not continue (0.48-0.52 vs null, one ≈2σ cell on CME 1H), and NR7 breaks slightly fail intraday. The counter-trend pool handicap A found on 1H/D does not replicate with a higher-timeframe trend definition, so its grade drops to weak and ctrMult should be 0.85, not 0.50. A's proximity-reach patch was a forward reference: evaluate (661) cannot call f_potModel (1303). It is fixed by passing the value in. Source corrections: Safari-Schmidhuber's trending regime starts at a few hours, not 30 minutes. The SPY lag-1 paper is daily data. The MNQ ORB T-stat is 1.17-1.50. The 0/160 result is about foundation models, not regime rules. New sources were added: Baltussen et al. 2021, Li-Sakkas-Urquhart 2022, Campbell-Grossman-Wang 1993, LeBaron 1992, Nystrup et al. 2020, Le 2026 (direction ≈ random walk, volatility structured in 61 instruments), Bulkowski NR7 and Holmberg ORB. The Firecrawl credits ran out mid-study and most hosts were blocked for direct fetch, so the report marks the citations that could not be re-opened.

concepts.name: Kaufman efficiency ratio (ER) and signed ER
concepts.definition: ER_n = |C_t − C_{t−n}| / Σ_{i=t−n+1..t}|C_i − C_{i−1}| ∈ [0,1]; sER_n = (C_t − C_{t−n})/Σ|ΔC| ∈ [−1,1]. KAMA uses n=10, fast 2, slow 30. Cutoffs (≥0.3-0.6 trend, <0.15-0.3 chop) are practitioner conventions, not Kaufman rules. Random walk: ER_n ≈ |Z|·√(π/(2n)); n=20: mean 0.225, P(≥0.40)=15.7%, P(≥0.30)=29%, P(<0.15)=40% (simulated). Guard a zero path; use close-to-close changes.
concepts.dolRole: Describes the last n bars. Used only as a gate (legacy D gate in REG-3), a display label and a ledger stratum (REG-2). It does not forecast the next window.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [A-test] Next-window corr −0.04..+0.01 (null −0.03..+0.03). sER added to geometry worsens OOS LL 0.01-0.66%. [B-test] Random-walk base rates confirm A's analytic 15%. Hard ER gate on D matches geometry, but it acts on only 0.3-0.5% of races. B found no source giving a fixed Kaufman threshold (TA-Lib, LuxAlgo).
concepts.engineNotes: No ER in the engine. coilScore (886-891) is a related overlap ratio used only in density (683, 687).

concepts.name: ADX / DMI (Wilder)
concepts.definition: +DM = H_t−H_{t−1} if that is > L_{t−1}−L_t and > 0 (−DM mirrors it); ±DI = 100·RMA(±DM,14)/RMA(TR,14); DX = 100|+DI−−DI|/(+DI+−DI); ADX = RMA(DX,14). ADX>25 trend, <20 no trend.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore trend filter for preferring with-trend liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [B-test] On a Gaussian random walk ADX≥25 holds on 38% of bars (mean 24.1, ≥40 on 7.5%). The double smoothing alone gives corr 0.22 at 28 bars. [A-test] 42-50% real vs 35-49% null; an ADX gate on D loses 2.5-3.5 pp. Gurrib 2018 (FX, weekly/monthly): high share of negative returns. oxfordstrat/algolab: no added value (not re-opened).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; do not add it as a gate.

concepts.name: Choppiness Index (Dreiss)
concepts.definition: CHOP_n = 100·log10(ΣTR_n/(HH_n−LL_n))/log10(n), n=14; >61.8 chop, <38.2 trend (Fibonacci conventions). Continuous-time random walk ≈ 50. [CORRECTED] On discrete bars the mean is 46.9, with 21% of bars ≤38.2 and 7% ≥61.8.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore 'range regime' marker (both sides raided, edges magnetic).
concepts.evidenceNotes: [A-test] Next-window corr −0.13..0.00. High CHOP does not raise distance-matched P(both pools): 1H 0.436 vs 0.540 for low CHOP. No pool-magnet effect. [B-test] Random-walk noise floor above.
concepts.engineNotes: coilScore (886-891) is a CHOP-like ratio feeding density at pool birth (683, 687). Pools printed while coiling are not more magnetic. WYK-1 owns the fix.

concepts.name: Hurst exponent (R/S, DFA, VR-implied)
concepts.definition: Var(r_q) ∝ q^{2H}; H=0.5 random walk, >0.5 persistent, <0.5 anti-persistent. VR-implied H ≈ 0.5 + ln VR(q)/(2 ln q). With q=4 and w=96 the SE of VR ≈ 0.19 and the simulated Hurst SD = 0.069.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore classifier of trending vs mean-reverting regime.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [A-test] Mean 0.47-0.48 on real and null data; next-window corr ≈ 0. [B-test] A random walk reads H>0.55 on 12-16% of bars. Literature on short-sample bias (Kristoufek 2012; Barunik & Kristoufek 2012) was not re-opened by B; B's simulation agrees.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Variance ratio test (Lo-MacKinlay)
concepts.definition: VR(q) = Var(q-bar returns)/(q·Var(1-bar)), with the heteroskedasticity-robust z*. The homoskedastic z over-rejects at 10-12% under GARCH. VR>1 means positive autocorrelation.
concepts.dolRole: Diagnostic of trend vs reversion at a scale.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong as a test (Lo & MacKinlay 1988: weekly equal-weighted AC 0.30, 1962-85). [CORRECTED] Portnaya 2026 (SPY ρ1 = −0.081 magnitude-driven, sign test p=0.11) uses daily/weekly data, not intraday. Le 2026: the VR test cannot reject a random walk for most of 61 instruments. As a rolling classifier: none.
concepts.engineNotes: Not needed in Pine.

concepts.name: Volatility state: compression/expansion (ATR5/ATR100, BB width, NR4/NR7, TTM squeeze)
concepts.definition: volr = ATR5/ATR100 or an EWMA z of ln(ATR5/ATR100) with tercile cutoffs ±0.43σ and hysteresis. BB squeeze: 4σ20/SMA20 at a low percentile. TTM squeeze: 2σ20 < 1.5·ATR20, 'fires' on release. NR4/NR7: smallest range of the last 4/7 bars.
concepts.dolRole: Sets how far price travels in ATR14 units over H bars (vol clustering plus mean reversion). It carries no direction. Best used through the surface unit (REG-1); kept as a display tag, ledger stratum and expansion alert (REG-2, REG-5).
concepts.evidenceNotes: [A-test] Persistence corr 0.49-0.80. Reach ≥3 ATR, compressed vs expanded: 1H 0.50→0.39, 15m 0.46→0.33, 5m flat. [B-test] Vol-tercile rows as the PoT key change OOS LL by +0.27% (5m), −0.64% (15m), −0.11% (1H), −0.50% (BTC), +0.12% (D). On top of a horizon-matched unit they add −0.23..+0.36 pp; on top of time-of-day rows they hurt. Directionless; the null reproduces it. Bulkowski NR7 (1,201 stocks): 46-47% failure in both directions.
concepts.engineNotes: Only atrE = max(ATR14, ATR200) at 878 for ejection gates (1578, 1654, 1834, 1859). Not used for PoT, reach, the ledger or display.

concepts.name: Horizon-matched volatility unit (HAR logic) [B-NEW]
concepts.definition: Measure empirical-surface distances in a forecast of forward volatility instead of ATR14: u = ATR14^a·ATR100^(1−a), default a=0.5, so u = √(ATR14·ATR100), on intraday charts; ATR14 on D+. A cheap stand-in for QPOT-02's vol-time and TIME-3's clock.
concepts.dolRole: Removes the volatility-state bias from PoT, proximity reach, reach bands, reach classes and the EDGE baseline pBase in one change.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [B-test, 2-fold OOS, pool-touch events] Unit alone: −0.40% (5m), −2.79% (15m), −0.45% (1H), −1.21% (BTC), +0.66% (D). With TIME-2 tod rows: −3.04 / −5.82 / −0.65 / −1.23%. Expanded-tercile bias (hit − PoT) goes from −5.5..−8.2 pp (engine-like) to −0.8..−3.1 pp. On 5m it over-corrects without tod rows. HAR concept: Corsi 2009 (strong).
concepts.engineNotes: Step 0 bumps with aH = atr[H] (1528-1532); queries use d/atr (1307, 1318); reach bands use reach·atr (2195-2199); reach classes use dist/atr (2236, 2352).

concepts.name: Realised vs implied volatility ratio (variance risk premium)
concepts.definition: VRP = IV² − E[RV²]; RV/IV > 1 marks stress regimes.
concepts.dolRole: Possible stress flag for index futures.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Predicts index returns at monthly-quarterly horizons (Bollerslev, Tauchen & Zhou 2009). Nothing at DOL horizons. Needs CBOE:VIX, so it is not generic.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended.

concepts.name: Time-series momentum and fast trend-following
concepts.definition: sign(past 1-12 month return) predicts the next month (MOP 2012, 58 futures). Fast variant: EWMA(τ) − EWMA(4τ) normalised by its 16τ dispersion, clipped ±2 (daily τ = 5-50).
concepts.dolRole: Would justify a persistent directional draw if trends persisted at DOL horizons.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Verified Kurth et al. 2026 Table 1: Sharpe 0.84±0.27→0.12±0.24 (τ=5d) … 0.70→0.40 (τ=50d), ~100 futures 1995-2025. Small-tick (index, FX) completely degraded; large-tick 1.0-1.2. Trends better in low vol; the break comes from large-return days. These are daily signals, outside intraday DOL horizons.
concepts.engineNotes: The structure component of D (1892) assumes a persistence the data do not show at DOL horizons.

concepts.name: Trend-strength nonlinearity by time scale (Safari & Schmidhuber)
concepts.definition: φ_T = trend t-statistic; next return ≈ a + bφ + cφ³ (+ a quintic term and a tick-size jump below 1h). [CORRECTED] Below ~15-30 min weak trends revert and strong persist (b<0, c>0). Linear term turns positive near 30 min; the trending regime proper is from a few hours to a few years (b>0, c<0).
concepts.dolRole: Continuation is weak and nonlinear; trends 'revert before they become statistically significant', i.e. about when a chart label like ER≥0.4 switches on.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Verified (arXiv 2501.16772): 14 y ticks, 30 y daily; Table 6 b=+0.132%±0.046, c=−0.039%±0.014; tiny R². [A-test] Adding φ24, φ24³ to geometry worsens OOS LL 0.08-1.00%.
concepts.engineNotes: Not worth fixed rules; at most a learned feature (REG-6).

concepts.name: Intraday momentum (session effect)
concepts.definition: The first half-hour return (or the rest-of-day return) predicts the last half-hour return.
concepts.dolRole: Late-session draw direction; a time-of-day effect, not a trend regime.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gao et al. 2018: SPY R² 1.6% IS / 1.2% OOS (verified). [B-NEW] Baltussen et al. 2021: >60 futures 1974-2020, driven by negative-gamma hedging, reverts over the next days. Li, Sakkas, Urquhart 2022: 12/16 markets, stronger with high vol and low liquidity. MNQ 2021-25: 0/14 OHLCV families pass walk-forward; ORB long T 1.17-1.50 [CORRECTED from 0.88].
concepts.engineNotes: Belongs to sibling TIME-9 as a ledger-gated feature, not the regime classifier.

concepts.name: Short-term reversal and volatility/volume-conditioned serial correlation
concepts.definition: Sub-hour reversal from bounce and imbalance. Serial correlation falls with predictable volatility (LeBaron 1992) and with volume (Campbell, Grossman, Wang 1993). Unexpected volatility raises it intraday (Bianco, Corsi, Renò 2008).
concepts.dolRole: Explains why short-horizon trend labels fade. Would argue for a conditional continuation weight; the sign of the conditioning differs across horizons.
concepts.evidenceNotes: LeBaron 1992 and CGW 1993 confirmed via search (daily). Daily-scale trend profits are better in low vol (Kurth), but intraday session momentum is stronger on high-vol days (Gao; Li et al.). [A-test] ER≥0.4 with-trend excess by vol is inconsistent across families.
concepts.engineNotes: No action beyond REG-6 learned features.

concepts.name: Claim C1: in trends opposite-side liquidity holds and the draw continues
concepts.definition: In an efficient trend, the with-trend pool is reached first more often than distance implies, and counter-trend pools are touched less.
concepts.dolRole: Justification for D-first selection, the Draw pillar (weight 30) and the counter-draw penalty.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [A-test] Geometry already points with the trend 76-82% (null 78-83%). Only 1H chart-ER ≥0.4 shows +6.1±2.5 pp (one of ~20 gates). D-first loses 9-12 pp first-touch. [B-test] HTF efficiency regime: with-trend excess +0.7..+4.1 pp, all within ~1-1.5σ of the null on 5 families. Counter-trend handicap: A's 1H/D −6.7 pp does not replicate with an HTF trend (1H +2.0±2.5, BTC −3.9±1.3 vs null −1.2).
concepts.engineNotes: D (1891-1895) gates selection (elig 1975), sets the Draw pillar (691) and halves counter levels (ctrMult 0.50, 162, 692-693) whenever |D|≥0.35; '⚠ COUNTER-DRAW' (2029, 2237). The hard ER gate (REG-3) is safe but acts on only 0.3-0.5% of races.

concepts.name: Claim C2: in ranges both sides get raided
concepts.definition: In low-efficiency or high-CHOP regimes P(both nearest BSL and SSL taken within H) and pool magnetism exceed what distance and volatility imply.
concepts.dolRole: Would justify range-edge bonuses and draw-neutral selection in ranges.
