concepts.evidenceNotes: [A-test] ER and CHOP add nothing OOS to P(both); 1H high-CHOP 0.436 vs low 0.540, the opposite of the claim. The two-sided effect comes from volatility compression (OOS −0.97% 1H, −2.95% 15m), reproduced by the null; it is absorbed by the surface unit (REG-1).
concepts.engineNotes: No range regime. Use WYK draw-neutral range handling and REG-5's stop-run readout, not a range bonus.

concepts.name: Claim C3: compression precedes expansion; trade the break
concepts.definition: After NR4/NR7, an inside bar or a BB/TTM squeeze the next move is large, and the break of the narrow range gives its direction.
concepts.dolRole: Timing and magnitude of the next raid; direction claimed from the break or squeeze momentum.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Magnitude in ATR14 units: yes on 15m/1H (vol clustering and mean reversion). Direction: none. [B-test] NR7 break continuation 0.482±0.006 (5m, null 0.495), 0.485±0.011 (1H, null 0.509), 0.486±0.008 (BTC), 0.502 (15m), 0.515 (D), i.e. slight intraday failure. Squeeze direction: no peer-reviewed test found. Holmberg et al. 2013 ORB crude oil positive (one market).
concepts.engineNotes: Add as volatility state (REG-1 unit, REG-5 alert), never as a draw input (REG-7).

concepts.name: Claim C4: a raid that holds means continuation, one that rejects means reversal
concepts.definition: After price trades through a pool: a close beyond it means continuation, a close back inside means reversal.
concepts.dolRole: Feeds liqEvt into D (30% weight).
concepts.evidenceNotes: [A-test] Symmetric ±1 ATR race, hold/reject: 5m 0.507/0.510, 15m 0.508/0.510, 1H 0.497/0.509. Daily all-sweeps 0.539±0.016 vs null 0.497.
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt sign rule at 1579-1582; owned by BIAS-4 / ICT-9; regime does not rescue it.

concepts.name: Claim C5: a displacement / expansion bar starts a draw in its direction [B-NEW]
concepts.definition: Engine rule (897-904): a bull/bear bar with body ≥ 1.2·ATR[1] and body/range ≥ 0.6, or a two-bar leg; its direction decays (half-life 12) into mV, 20% of D.
concepts.dolRole: Breakout-regime vote in the draw vector.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [B-test] Symmetric ±1 ATR race in the displacement direction: 0.500 (5m), 0.484 (15m), 0.516 (BTC), 0.506 (D), matching nulls 0.49-0.52. CME 1H 0.548±0.015 vs null 0.509 is the only ≈2σ cell. ICTS B6: 51.3% (n 4,347). MNQ Asia expansion bars reverse next bar (T −10.96).
concepts.engineNotes: mV at 1893 with wM 0.20 (156) steers selection through D. REG-7 sets wM default to 0 for selection.

concepts.name: PoT drift conditioned on regime
concepts.definition: Analytic first-passage touch probability with per-bar drift μ = driftW·SMA(ΔC,50) toward the level, vs μ=0, or drift only when ER≥0.4.
concepts.dolRole: Tilts PoT, proximity reach and races toward the trend side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [A-test] Log-loss is worse with drift in every regime (ER≥0.40: 1H 0.614 vs 0.590, 5m 0.694 vs 0.669, 15m 0.686 vs 0.653; all bars +1.2-4.0%). Agrees with QPOT-01 (1.2M windows) and BIAS-8 (races 0.4-6.9% worse).

concepts.name: Empirical PoT surface key (HTF bias vs time of day vs volatility rows)
concepts.definition: Excursion survival surface S[r][j] per side. Today r = htfBias with/neutral/against. Candidates: NY 3-hour block (TIME-2), volatility tercile, or both, with partial pooling toward the pooled row.
concepts.dolRole: Makes the headline PoT and the EDGE baseline pBase condition-aware.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [B-test, OOS] Trend-state rows (htfBias analogue) never help (−0.02..+0.41%). Tod rows: −2.27% (5m), −4.06% (15m), −0.48% (1H), −0.04% (BTC). Vol rows are small and dilute tod rows (tod×vol 15m −2.38% vs tod −4.06%). Best: blended unit + tod (−3.0/−5.8/−0.65/−1.2%). [CORRECTED] A's REG-1 vol-row key is replaced.
concepts.engineNotes: Rows keyed on htfBias at 1060-1062, f_empPoT 1284-1301 (r mapping 1286), calls 1307/1318, step-0 bump 1530-1532, f_reachD 2112-2115.

concepts.name: Markov-switching / HMM / statistical jump models
concepts.definition: Latent states with their own mean and variance and a transition matrix (Hamilton 1989). Jump models add a persistence penalty and online greedy classification (Nystrup, Kolm, Lindström 2020).
concepts.dolRole: Principled latent-regime probability for modulating draw and PoT.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No documented OOS intraday directional value. [B-NEW] Nystrup et al.: the states that persist out of sample are built on realised intraday volatility features, consistent with 'volatility persists, direction does not'. Le 2026: direction sector never beats its random-walk null in 61 instruments; the volatility sector beats every null.
concepts.engineNotes: Feasible in Pine as a 2-state forward filter but not recommended; the O(1) vol z-score plus the surface unit covers the useful part.

concepts.name: Regime-split accuracy ledger and calibration audit
concepts.definition: Grade each asserted DOL by regime at assertion. E class: RANGE/MIXED/TREND-WITH/TREND-AGAINST. V class: COMPRESSED/NORMAL/EXPANDED. Report hit %, EDGE = (K−ΣpBase)/n and z = (K−ΣpBase)/√ΣpV, plus mean shown PoT per V class.
concepts.dolRole: Shows per chart whether regime matters, tests claim C1 via the TREND-AGAINST cell, and detects the volatility calibration bias of the PoT.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A stratified version of the engine's distance-matched baseline method. B shows why the V split matters: the engine-like surface is off by up to −8 pp in expanded volatility.
concepts.engineNotes: The ledger splits only by family: Trial 375-395, f_openTrial 1426, f_book 1461-1499, stN/stK/stPE/stPV 1066-1070.

proposals.title: Horizon-matched unit √(ATR14·ATR100) and an informative key (time of day, no HTF-bias rows) for the empirical PoT surface; vol rows only as a scorecard option [A, CORRECTED and REPLACED]
proposals.rationale: The htfBias key carries no reach information (trend rows −0.02..+0.41% OOS LL). The ATR14 unit is biased by volatility mean reversion: hit − PoT is −5.5..−8.2 pp in expanded vol on 15m/1H/BTC (replicates amt B7), and the bias reaches PoT, proximity reach, reach bands, reach classes and the EDGE baseline. B's OOS tests: the blended unit with TIME-2 time-of-day rows gives −3.0% (5m), −5.8% (15m), −0.65% (1H), −1.2% (BTC) log-loss and cuts the bias to −0.8..−3.1 pp. A's vol-tercile rows give +0.27/−0.64/−0.11/−0.50% and dilute tod rows. Supersedes QPOT-03's 9-row key and BIAS-6.
proposals.spec: INPUT (G_POT, display.none): surfUnit ['Blended','ATR'] default Blended. SERIES after 878: atr100 = ta.atr(100); aU = surfUnit == 'Blended' and timeframe.isintraday and not na(atr) and not na(atr100) ? math.sqrt(atr*atr100) : atr. STATE 1061-1062: rows = TIME-2's NQ1 tod rows (or 1 pooled row); drop the 3 htfBias rows. Step 0 (1527-1532): aH = aU[H]; always bump pooled row NQ, plus row todQ[H] when < NQ. f_empPoT(float dU, int side, int q) blends cell q with pooled row NQ (TIME-2 partial pooling, nE = n/(0.6H), m = 60); remove the bias mapping at 1286. Callers f_potModel (1307) and f_potBase (1318) pass d/aU (guard nz(aU) > 0); the analytic prior is unchanged (price units via potSig). f_reachD returns u-units: reach bands 2195-2199 multiply by aU; reach classes compare dist/aU (2236 dAtr, 2352 dA). Proximity reach, compile-safe: evaluate (661) cannot call f_potModel (1303; reads sUp/sDn at 1061), so add parameter float reachP: reach = dAtr >= maxATR ? 0 : not na(reachP) ? math.min(1, reachP/0.95) : sig > 0 ? f_pot(dist, sig, 0.0, potH)/0.95 : lin; at the call site 1948: lv.evaluate(close, atr, anchors, confTol, dSel, nz(potSig), 0.0, f_potModel(math.max(0.0, lv.distance(close)), lv.side, 0.0)) (≤ poolMax 40 O(1) lookups). lin, maxATR and ejection keep ATR14. Optional 'Volatility' sub-key (3 vState rows, partial pooling) and {ATR, Blended, Clock} offered to TIME-4's scorecard; TIME-3's clock replaces aU when it wins. Daily+ charts: ATR14, pooled. aU is a global series, so aU[H] is valid; closed-bar state only, so no repainting.
proposals.risk: On 5m the unit alone over-corrects (compressed −5.1 pp), so ship with TIME-2 rows and QPOT-04 recalibration. ATR100 warm-up of 100 bars (falls back to ATR14). The best exponent varies by TF (15m ≈ 0, 5m ≈ 0.75); 0.5 is the robust default. Old surfaces change meaning, but the surface is rebuilt on load. Coordinate with TIME-2 (same arrays) and OF-6 (σ factor on top).

proposals.title: Draw vector does not steer target choice without measured skill: hard efficiency gate as the legacy 'Structure (gated)' option; zero drift everywhere [A, CORRECTED]
proposals.rationale: D-first selection loses 9-12 pp first-touch and 5-8 pp hit-within-H intraday (5/3 pp daily) vs geometry on 23 series and the null. All three D components test null: structure, displacement (B-T4; ICTS B6 51.3%) and raid sign (BIAS-4). A's 'gate recovers geometry' holds only because the hard gate acts on 0.3-0.5% of races. A's soft gate is 0.2-0.8 pp worse. A's spec would also have silently changed the Draw Flip alert and left the panel reading ungated D. Drift hurts in every regime. BIAS-2 / ICTS-1 own the default draw source; this is the fallback and legacy option.
proposals.spec: INPUT (G_FLOW): regGate bool default true (tooltip: steers only in an efficient trend that agrees, which is rare). STATE: var float drawSel = 0.0. Step 14 after 1894: dSel = regGate ? (erA >= erTrend and math.sign(drawD) == math.sign(erS) ? drawD : 0.0) : drawD; drawSel := dSel; rawSide = drawD >= dGate ? 1 : drawD <= -dGate ? -1 : 0, used for the flip logic 1896-1898 (Draw Direction Flip alert keeps its meaning); dirSide = dSel >= dGate ? 1 : dSel <= -dGate ? -1 : 0 (1895) drives elig (1975), ctrHold (2001), curElig (2004), activeCtr (2029) and the HTF objective. Step 17 (1948): lv.evaluate(..., dSel, nz(potSig), 0.0, reachP), so the Draw pillar (691) and ctrMult follow dSel with zero drift; dSel = 0 makes every Draw pillar 0.5 (neutral). driftW default 0.0 (QPOT-01, BIAS-8) with a tooltip saying drift was tested and lowers accuracy in every regime. Panel 2338: show 'DRAW ▲ +0.62 (gated: no efficient trend)' when |drawD| ≥ dGate and drawSel = 0. erA/erS/erTrend come from REG-2 (declared before 1518). O(1).
proposals.risk: A far with-trend pool a trader expects is chosen only if it is also the best-scoring level; the data back that. Legacy behaviour stays one toggle away. Needs REG-2's ER series.

proposals.title: Two-axis regime classifier (efficiency × volatility) with a regime-split ledger, a calibration-by-volatility audit and base-rate tooltips [A✓, sharpened]
proposals.rationale: Traders expect regime awareness. The data say trend labels describe the past window, so the honest feature labels the regime and measures per chart whether it matters. The TREND-AGAINST cell tests claim C1 on the user's chart. [B-NEW] The volatility split also reveals the B7-type PoT bias (hit vs mean shown PoT by vol class) before and after REG-1. It is the reporting layer for REG-1/3/4/5/7.
proposals.spec: INPUTS (group 'Regime', display.none): erLen 20, erTrend 0.40, erRange 0.15. Tooltip: 'On a random walk Efficiency ≥ 0.40 appears on ~16% of bars (ADX ≥ 25 on 38%); the label describes the last N bars.' SERIES: erPath = math.sum(math.abs(ta.change(close)), erLen); erS = erPath > 0 ? (close - close[erLen]) / erPath : 0.0; erA = math.abs(erS); atr5 = ta.atr(5); vLn = math.log(nz(atr5/atr100, 1.0)). STATE: var int eState = 0, var int vState = 1, var float vMu = na, var float vVar = 0.04. Engine step 0 (confirmed bars): eState := erA >= erTrend ? int(math.sign(erS)) : erA < erRange ? 0 : (eState != 0 and erA >= erTrend - 0.08 ? eState : 0); aV = 2/2001; dv = vLn - nz(vMu, vLn); vMu := nz(vMu, vLn) + aV*dv; vVar := (1-aV)*(vVar + aV*dv*dv); vz = (vLn - vMu)/math.sqrt(math.max(vVar, 1e-6)); hysteresis enter ±0.43, leave ±0.30 → vState 0/1/2. Ledger: Trial (375-395) gains int eCls, int vCls, float pPot (shared with QPOT-04). f_openTrial (1426): eCls = erA < erRange ? 0 : erA < erTrend ? 1 : (int(math.sign(erS)) == lv.side ? 2 : 3); vCls = vState; pPot = shown PoT. New arrays rgN/rgK int[7], rgPE/rgPV/rgPP float[7]; f_book (1461) updates indices eCls and 4+vCls next to stN/stK/stPE/stPV. Full view rows, shown once n ≥ 20, with Wilson intervals: 'REGIME RNG 44% +1.2 · MIX … · TR+ … · TR− …' (hit %, EDGE pp, z) and 'VOL CMP 55% (PoT 51) · NRM … · EXP …'. Terminal: 'REGIME TREND ▲ · ER .52 · VOL CMP'. Clean: optional 4th row 'Regime | TREND ▲', off by default. Data window: plot(erS), plot(vState) with display.data_window.
proposals.risk: Thin cells (minimum n, Wilson intervals). Users may over-read labels; tooltips disclose base rates. Negligible CPU and memory.

proposals.title: Scope and soften the counter-draw penalty to efficient trends (ctrMult 0.85) [A, evidence DOWNGRADED]
proposals.rationale: ctrMult 0.50 halves every level opposite D whenever |D| ≥ 0.35. A's only support is chart-TF efficient trends on 1H/D (−6.7 pp vs null −1.5/−1.7). B's HTF-trend test does not replicate it (1H +2.0±2.5 vs null +2.2; 15m −2.2 vs +4.4; BTC −3.9±1.3 vs −1.2). On a ~50% base, −5 pp is about ×0.85-0.90.
proposals.spec: Default ctrMult (162) 0.50 → 0.85. With REG-3, dirD = dSel already confines the penalty to gated trends. activeCtr := not na(activeLv) and dirSide != 0 and activeLv.side != dirSide and eState != 0 (2029); the '⚠ COUNTER-DRAW' head (2237) follows. Hold and eviction logic (2001-2007) unchanged. Under BIAS-2 'Calibrated', A/B test 0.85. Measured by REG-2's TREND-AGAINST EDGE; users can lower ctrMult if it stays ≤ −1σ.
proposals.risk: Low; slightly more counter-trend near targets shown in strong trends.

proposals.title: Stop-run readout from the surface, SQZ/EXP tag and a volatility-expansion alert (claim C2 done right) [A, simplified]
proposals.rationale: Both sides get raided under compressed volatility, not in ranges (P(both) OOS −0.97% 1H, −2.95% 15m). The race WIN≤H (f_invalidation 1343-1366) says which barrier comes first, not how likely the stop beyond the opposing pool is to be traded at all within H, which is what traders ask.
proposals.spec: HUD (Terminal) and Clean label tooltip: 'STOP-RUN ≈ p%' with p = f_potModel(risk, -activeLv.side, 0.0), risk = |close − inv| from f_invalidation, one O(1) call at global scope after 1303 (uses the REG-1 surface). Tag SQZ/EXP from REG-2's vState. Optional alert 'Volatility Expansion' via alert() on bar close: vState goes 0 → 2 within ≤ 10 bars, or (2*ta.stdev(close,20) < 1.5*ta.atr(20)) turns false after ≥ 6 true bars; latched once per state; message 'range expansion likely in ATR terms; direction not forecast'. Optional grading (P3): on booking a trial whose target hit before H, push inv, side, bar0+H and p into srInv/srSide/srEnd/srP (≤ H+64); each confirmed bar loop once, resolve the stop touch (side == 1 ? low <= inv : high >= inv) or expiry, accumulate Brier, remove; Full view 'STOP-RUN cal · Brier .21 · n 120'. O(H) per bar, far below the loop limit.
proposals.risk: One more HUD line; alert noise if the transition rule is loose (latch). Array bookkeeping in the optional grading part.

proposals.title: Breakouts and displacement are volatility events, not draw votes: wM default 0 for the selection draw; no squeeze/NR7/ORB continuation logic [B-NEW]
proposals.rationale: B-T4: displacement bars (engine rule) do not continue on 4 of 5 families (0.484-0.516 vs nulls 0.49-0.52); CME 1H 0.548 vs 0.509 is one ≈2σ cell. ICTS B6 51.3% (n 4,347). B-T5: NR7 breaks slightly fail intraday (0.482-0.486 on 5m/1H/BTC). MNQ: Asia expansion bars reverse (T −10.96) and ORB fails walk-forward. Yet mV is 20% of D and D steers selection.
proposals.spec: Change the 'D · Displacement' input default wM (156) from 0.20 to 0.0, so mV (1893) no longer enters drawD by default. Displacement keeps its mechanical roles: FVG quality (fvgQBase 907-912), OB leg quality and origin lockout. Do not add squeeze-direction, NR7-break or ORB-continuation terms to D or the score. If ICTS-1's per-component skill gate is built, it sets wM per chart (ICTS names wM the first candidate for 0). The panel may still show the last displacement as context. Measured by ICTS-1 component skill and REG-2's ledger.
proposals.risk: Removes a trader-intuitive input from D. Users who prefer it can set the weight back.

proposals.title: Regime features for the learned side model (only with BIAS-1), zero prior weight [A✓, extended]
proposals.rationale: Weak, timeframe-specific signals exist and none replicates across timeframes: 1H with-trend excess +6.1±2.5 pp (chart-TF ER); 5m trend-aligned sweep continuation +5 pp vs null; BTC 1H with-HTF-trend excess +2.9±1.4 pp (null +0.6) [B]; CME 1H displacement continuation 0.548 vs 0.509 [B]. They belong in a per-chart learned model with shrinkage, not in fixed rules.
proposals.spec: Add to BIAS-1's online logistic (over the geometry logit, L2 shrinkage toward 0, prequential scoring) features oriented to the buy-side candidate, each in [−1,1]: x1 = gE·sign(erS) with gE = clamp((erA−0.25)/0.20, 0, 1); x2 = x1·[last bar swept a pool on that side]; x3 = sign(htfErS)·[htfErA ≥ 0.4], with HTF ER10 added as one element of the existing HTF request.security tuple ([1]-offset, lookahead_on; no new request); x4 = mV; x5 = clip(vz, −2, 2)/2 (direction-free, should learn ≈ 0). Zero initial weights. Full view shows learned weights ± SE, and 'regime: no skill on this chart' if the side-ledger Brier skill vs geometry is ≤ 0 after n ≥ 200. O(1) per update.
proposals.risk: Overfitting, controlled by shrinkage and prequential scoring. Depends on BIAS-1. Adding an element to the HTF tuple must keep the [1] offset.

result.summary: Combined A+B result. The engine's distance-matched random-level baseline (f_potBase) is already well calibrated: slope 0.93-1.04 and calibration-in-the-large −1.4 to +2.0 pp on 13 clean datasets (76k probes), confirmed by quant_pot (slope 0.99, ECE 0.004). No learner beats it out of sample on clean data, so the learner's job is protection and honest measurement, not hidden edge. B tested a new tier-1 calibrator on A's stored probes: online Platt scaling (2-D Online Newton Step, Gupta & Ramdas 2023 defaults) behind a prequential gate. It costs 0.00 to −0.23% log-loss on clean sets and gains +5.6% on the roll-gap-corrupted GC 1-hour base. That is 64% of the 12-feature probit's rescue (+8.8%) with a 2×2 matrix instead of feature vectors. Ungated learners all lose (SGD −3.6 to −5.5%, naive-Bayes lifts −0.6 to −2.1%, binning/calibeating −1.4 to −3.1%). This protection matters because TradingView continuous futures are not back-adjusted by default. f_calMult (1376-1382) is mostly noise (≥10% off in 47-66% of families under the null at n 10-40), learns only from selected targets, and tilts family selection by up to ±20% of the score. Replace it with an overlap-aware empirical-Bayes multiplier (α 60) gated by a time-uniform confidence sequence. The EDGE verdict (2390) suffers from peeking (false EDGE 10-20%). Howard et al.'s eq. 14 boundary (verified) fixes it, but it is only asymptotically valid with an estimated variance and needs a few-clusters guard: at H = 450 there are only about 5 blocks of 2H bars. B corrected three of A's claims. After Holm correction only the EQ lift (1-hour) survives, so confluence, draw and external are 'unsupported', not 'contradicted'. A's top-1 data show no systematic optimizer's curse on the PoT. The displayed PoT is f_potModel with a 50-bar drift, not the driftless baseline, and that drift is the one real selection-bias channel. B also found a new scoring bug: PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL pools count their own anchor as confluence (+5.25 points, 10.5 when PDH = PWH). The key infrastructure is still a candidate (shadow) ledger. It turns bandit feedback into full information (SE about 1 pp per 5,000 bars) and is the only way to reach the ≥100 events and ≥100 non-events that calibration assessment needs (Collins 2016). It also enables the nearest, random, runner-up and mirror baselines. Target choice remains a utility decision: maximising d·PoT(d) delivers 1.10-1.43 ATR per target against 0.86-1.09 for the hand score, at an honest hit rate.

concepts.name: Distance-matched random-level baseline (offset)
concepts.definition: p0(d,side,regime)=P(a random level d ATR away is touched within H), from the empirical excursion surface (3 HTF regimes x 61 bins of bStep, completed windows only), blended with the driftless analytic first-passage prior (priorM 30, nEff=n/(0.6H)), clamped to [0.01,0.99].
concepts.dolRole: The null model and the offset of every learner. A liquidity concept has value only if hits exceed p0. Because of the regime rows, it already includes the HTF-direction effect.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's replica: slope 0.93-1.04 on 13/14 sets. B: calibration-in-the-large −1.43..+2.02 pp clean, −4.25 pp on GC 1h (roll gaps). quant_pot.final: engine surface slope 0.99, ECE 0.004 on 1.2M 5-min rows. The replica surface had no regime split.
concepts.engineNotes: f_potBase 1313-1322, f_empPoT 1284-1300, surface bump 1527-1532. No guard against roll gaps or bad prints (CAL-10).

concepts.name: Offset (lift-over-baseline) model
concepts.definition: logit P = logit(p0) + b'x, or probit Phi(Phi^-1(p0) + mu'x). b = 0 reproduces the baseline, so every coefficient is a lift beyond distance.
concepts.dolRole: Makes 'no information' the default and measures family or pillar value net of proximity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard GLM offset.
concepts.engineNotes: Only implicit in f_calMult k/e (1376-1382).

concepts.name: Proper scoring rules (Brier, log-loss, BSS vs p0, CRPS via threshold decomposition)
concepts.definition: B=mean(p-y)^2; LL=-mean[y ln p+(1-y)ln(1-p)]; BSS=1-B/B_ref with p0 as the reference. The Brier sum over same-side probes is a discretised CRPS of the max-excursion forecast.
concepts.dolRole: The only honest way to grade the displayed PoT and to compare models prequentially. The candidate ledger grades the whole ladder of levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gneiting & Raftery 2007; Hersbach 2000. Grade the uncapped PoT, because the 95% cap makes a capped forecast improper near d=0.
concepts.engineNotes: Trial (375-395) has no PoT field; the displayed PoT is never graded.

concepts.name: Calibration hierarchy and minimum samples
concepts.definition: Mean (CITL) -> weak (Cox intercept/slope) -> moderate (reliability curve) -> strong. Assessing calibration needs >=100 events and >=100 non-events (ideally 200), divided by deff.
concepts.dolRole: Decides what the ledger may show: CITL first, slope only with enough events, bins only with >=30 effective samples per bin.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Van Calster et al. 2016 (moderate calibration implies non-harmful decisions); Collins, Ogundimu & Altman 2016 resampling study.
concepts.engineNotes: The verdict uses only nA<20 (2390). The active ledger takes about 250 trials to reach 100 events and 100 non-events.

concepts.name: Murphy decomposition, reliability diagram, ECE, Spiegelhalter z
concepts.definition: B=REL-RES+UNC; bins of forecast vs observed; plug-in ECE is biased at small n (use equal-mass bins or the debiased estimator); Spiegelhalter Z=sum(y-p)(1-2p)/sqrt(sum(1-2p)^2 p(1-p)).
concepts.dolRole: Shows whether PoT 70% means 70% on this chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Murphy 1973; Broecker & Smith 2007; Roelofs et al. 2020; Kumar et al. 2019. B: Spiegelhalter is weak against an intercept shift (GC 1h: z 2.45, about 0.9 after deff 7.7), so the cluster-robust excess test is primary.
concepts.engineNotes: No bins, slope or z in the panel (2378-2425).

concepts.name: Platt / intercept recalibration
concepts.definition: p'=sigma(a+b logit p) with smoothed targets; intercept-only delta=logit((K+m Pbar)/(N+m))-logit(Pbar). Platt on logit p contains the identity (a=0,b=1); Kull et al.'s objection applies to Platt on raw scores.
concepts.dolRole: Corrects systematic PoT bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Platt 1999. Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005 (wording not re-verified). Replica: selected-only ungated −0.36..+0.28% LL on clean data. B: intercept-only m=100 on candidates −0.11..+0.12% clean, +2.05% on broken base.
concepts.engineNotes: f_raceAdj 1367-1371 applies to races only (m=20), ungated, used at 2130.

concepts.name: Online Platt scaling (OPS) with an Online Newton Step
concepts.definition: 2-D online logistic regression on logit p: grad=(sigma(a+b z)-y)[1,z]; A+=gg'; theta-=(1/gamma)A^-1 g; gamma 0.1, rho 100, start at the identity; O(log T) regret vs the best fixed Platt map for any sequence.
concepts.dolRole: The cheapest safe self-calibration of the displayed PoT, which adapts to drift without a forgetting parameter.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gupta & Ramdas ICML 2023 (verified). B replica: ungated −0.6..−1.8% clean, +5.6% GC 1h; gated 0.00..−0.23% (mean −0.02%) clean, +5.6% broken. Final slope 0.83-1.11.
concepts.engineNotes: Proposal CAL-4 (a 2x2 matrix in var arrays).

concepts.name: Calibeating / histogram tracking
concepts.definition: Bin an expert's forecasts and replace each by the running outcome mean of its bin (tracking) or hedge between bins (HOPS); Brier = refinement + calibration.
concepts.dolRole: Nonparametric calibration with adversarial guarantees.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Foster & Hart 2023 (theory, strong). B replica: TOPS −1.4..−3.1% ungated on clean data (too noisy at ledger sizes); gated 0.00, +4.7% broken.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended at ledger sizes.

concepts.name: Isotonic regression / Venn-Abers
concepts.definition: PAV monotone fit; Venn-Abers runs isotonic twice to give a calibrated interval under exchangeability.
concepts.dolRole: Nonparametric PoT calibration.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Needs large sets (A: about 1,000 points, not re-verified; Kumar 2019: binning needs O(B/eps^2)). Overlapping windows violate exchangeability.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended.

concepts.name: Poisson-gamma / beta-binomial shrinkage
concepts.definition: Posterior lift=(k+alpha lambda0)/(e+alpha) with e=sum p0; prior sd lambda0/sqrt(alpha) (alpha 60 gives about ±13%); divide k and e by deff.
concepts.dolRole: Stops per-family hit rates from overreacting to small samples.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's null simulation, re-run by B: the engine (alpha=2, n>=10 cliff, clamp) is >=10% off in 66/47/33% of families at n=10/40/80; EB has lower RMSE everywhere.
concepts.engineNotes: f_calMult 1376-1382: alpha=2, deff ignored, n>=10 cliff, clamp [0.8,1.2], selected trials only.

concepts.name: Empirical Bayes / James-Stein / Tweedie selection-bias correction
concepts.definition: Shrink estimates toward the pooled mean by s^2/(s^2+tau^2). Tweedie: E[mu|z]=z+sigma^2 (log f)'(z) de-biases the largest of many estimates.
concepts.dolRole: Honest per-family and per-pillar readouts; guards against the winner's curse when users read the biggest number.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Efron & Morris 1975 (about 3.5x lower squared error; A's 17.56 -> 5.01 not re-verified); Efron 2011. With 4 families tau^2 is unstable, so use a fixed alpha plus a gate.
concepts.engineNotes: No pooling; CAL-7 reports shrunk values.

concepts.name: Online logistic regression (SGD/AdaGrad/FTRL)
concepts.definition: w+=eta(y-p)x-eta lambda(w-w0); per-coordinate rates (AdaGrad, FTRL-Proximal).
concepts.dolRole: Could learn pillar weights from the ledger.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Replica: unregularised constant-eta SGD −3.6..−5.5% LL on clean data; AdaGrad+L2 about −0.4..−1.0%.
concepts.engineNotes: Good that it is absent in this form.

concepts.name: Bayesian online probit (adPredictor)
concepts.definition: Gaussian weights; P=Phi((o+mu'x)/sqrt(1+sum x^2 v)), o=Phi^-1(p0); mu_j+=t x_j v_j/Sigma v(z), v_j*=1-x_j^2 v_j/Sigma^2 w(z); optional epsilon dynamics toward the prior; temper by omega for overlap.
concepts.dolRole: Leak-free pillar-lift learner shrunk toward the hand-set prior; best rescuer of a broken base; best per-chart pillar readout.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Method strong (Graepel 2010; A's RIG figures not re-verified). Replica: −0.15..−0.79% ungated clean; gated 0..−0.26%; +8.8%/+10.5% (mixture) on broken base.
concepts.engineNotes: CAL-9 (second tier, measure first, applies to PoT only).

concepts.name: Naive-Bayes multiplicative lifts
concepts.definition: P proportional to p0 times the product of per-feature lifts, assuming conditional independence.
concepts.dolRole: Simple per-feature calibration (ICT-1, f_ctxMult designs).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Ng & Jordan 2002; replica −0.6..−2.1% LL.
concepts.engineNotes: Proposed by sibling reports; replace with CAL-7/CAL-9.

concepts.name: Elo / Glicko / Bradley-Terry
concepts.definition: Elo is SGD on the Bradley-Terry likelihood (K = learning rate); Glicko adds a rating deviation (approximate Bayes).
concepts.dolRole: Could rate families by race wins.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kiraly & Qian 2017; adds nothing beyond the Bayesian probit.
concepts.engineNotes: Subsumed.

concepts.name: Pine kNN (Lorentzian) and Pine 'logistic regression' scripts
concepts.definition: Lorentzian: sum ln(1+|dx|), accepts neighbours with d >= running threshold, skips i%4==0, label = negated past 4-bar move of the same bar, var FIFO across bars. capissimo LR v4: hypothesis evaluated with weight 0, synthetic deterministic labels.
concepts.dolRole: Analog or ML probability claims in Pine.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Code inspection by B: Lorentzian v2 port lines 335, 339-344, 394-413; capissimo v4 lines 89-97, 115-121. Neither is a statistical learner producing forecasts.
concepts.engineNotes: Do not adopt; the engine's histogram surface is the principled kNN-like estimator.

concepts.name: Learning to rank (pointwise + utility)
concepts.definition: Pairwise RankNet and listwise Plackett-Luce vs calibrated pointwise P_i ranked by expected utility P_i*u_i (Bayes-optimal for decomposable utility).
concepts.dolRole: Choosing ONE target among candidates.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Decision theory; Burges 2005; Cao 2007.
concepts.engineNotes: The hand score (694) ranks candidates; there is no explicit utility.

concepts.name: Expected-reach utility d*P(d)
concepts.definition: E[U]=d*P(hit within H|d); driftless BM argmax at d=0.752 sigma sqrt(H), P=0.452, E=0.340 s; empirical argmax_j (j bStep) S_j/n.
concepts.dolRole: Principled proximity pillar: trades hit rate against distance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Replica: 1.10-1.43 ATR delivered vs hand score 0.86-1.09 and nearest 0.66-0.93 (13 sets); hit rates match their baseline ±3 pp except EURUSD hand score −6 pp. B re-derived the optimum.
concepts.engineNotes: prox 662-667 is an ad-hoc lin/reach(with drift)/taper blend.

concepts.name: Optimizer's / winner's curse
concepts.definition: The argmax of noisy unbiased estimates disappoints on average; shrink before the argmax.
concepts.dolRole: Bias of selected-target statistics.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Theory strong (Smith & Winkler 2006), but engine relevance is weak. B: A's top-1 hand-score excess has mixed signs on clean sets (mean about −0.3 pp). The PoT is a shared distance surface, not idiosyncratic noise. The real channel is the drift in f_potModel and in the proximity reach.
concepts.engineNotes: Handled by grading (CAL-6) and the gated selected intercept (CAL-4); readouts are shrunk (CAL-7).

concepts.name: Bandit feedback / selection bias
concepts.definition: Grading only chosen targets conditions statistics on the policy; down-weighted arms stop being observed.
concepts.dolRole: Explains why active-only learning cannot learn family or feature lifts.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Li et al. 2011. Replica: the candidate ledger gives 2,477-3,473 probes per 5,000 bars, SE 0.87-1.38 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: f_calMult learns from selected trials only (1461-1474, 2038-2045).

concepts.name: Overlapping labels, design effect, few clusters
concepts.definition: Cluster-robust variance in 2H blocks (deff=V_cl/V_ind), or HAC with lag H-1 (Hansen-Hodrick). With G<20-40 blocks the variance is biased down: apply G/(G-1) and require G>=20.
concepts.dolRole: Honest intervals and effective sample sizes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Lopez de Prado 2018; Hansen & Hodrick 1980; Cameron, Gelbach & Miller 2008. Replica deff 1.4-2.8 for candidates, about 1 for selected trials, 7.7 on GC 1h. Engine: G about 78 at H=30, 23 at H=100, 5 at H=450.
concepts.engineNotes: cluSt 1077 and 1463-1469 are used in the panel (2385-2387), but not in f_calMult; there is no block count or small-G guard.

concepts.name: Peeking / confidence sequences
concepts.definition: Two-sided normal mixture: P(for all t: |S_t| < sqrt((V+rho) ln((V+rho)/(rho alpha^2)))) >= 1-alpha; tightest at V=m with m/rho=-W_-1(-alpha^2/e)-1 (about 8.2 rho at alpha .05). Asymptotic CS when V is estimated.
concepts.dolRole: An EDGE verdict that can be looked at on every bar.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Howard et al. 2021 eq. 14 and Props 3/5 (verified). Johari et al.: Type I error 'can easily increase fivefold'. Waudby-Smith 2021; Ge & Liu 2026 for dependent data. A's simulation: false EDGE 10/15/20% vs CS <=1.4%.
concepts.engineNotes: Verdict at 2390 uses fixed z thresholds re-evaluated every bar.

concepts.name: Prequential evaluation
concepts.definition: Predict with the pre-outcome state, score after resolution, learn only from resolved outcomes.
concepts.dolRole: Guarantees no look-ahead and gives honest model comparison.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Dawid 1984.
concepts.engineNotes: The ledger is prequential and leak-free (2038-2045, 1549-1557, 1527-1532); there is no model-vs-model scoring.

concepts.name: Safe aggregation (gate / exponential weights / fixed share)
concepts.definition: Weights proportional to likelihood^eta; Bayes mixture regret <= ln N; fixed share tracks switches; the gate is follow-the-leader between base and model.
concepts.dolRole: Lets a learner help when the base is wrong without hurting when it is right.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Cesa-Bianchi & Lugosi 2006. Gate(BP) 0..−0.26%, gate(OPS) 0..−0.23% clean; +8.8%/+5.6% broken; MIX(BP) +10.5%.
concepts.engineNotes: CAL-4, CAL-9, CAL-11.

concepts.name: Selection baselines (nearest, random candidate, runner-up, mirror)
concepts.definition: Shadow-grade simple rules at each DOL open. The mirror is the same distance on the opposite side; its paired residual cancels shared miscalibration.
concepts.dolRole: Answers whether the scoring beats 'nearest pool' and whether the base itself is off.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Replica: hand score vs nearest vs random top-1 excess all within about ±2 SE. Mirror control from skeptic SKEP-2.
concepts.engineNotes: Only the random level at the same distance exists (1313-1322).

concepts.name: Pillar priors vs measured lifts (multiplicity-corrected)
concepts.definition: Pooled offset-logistic lifts beyond distance for engine-like features, Holm-corrected over 22 tests.
concepts.dolRole: Whether confluence, tier, draw and EQ raise hit probability.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B-fix: only EQ on 1h (+0.29, Holm p 0.007) and age (sign flips between timeframes) survive. External (Holm 0.07), confluence (0.11), draw (0.23) do not. Pooled-all confluence −0.04 (t −0.7). LODO cross-market prior −1.17% LL.
concepts.engineNotes: wConf=15 and 1.2*tier (682) assume positive lifts that are unsupported (not proven harmful); wDraw=30 has no lift beyond distance; EQ 0.9*eqCount (682) is supported.

concepts.name: Self-confluence of key levels
concepts.definition: A level must not count its own source price as a confluence anchor.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps the confluence pillar from double-counting with tier.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B code inspection: PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL pools are pushed at pdH/pdL/pwH/pwL (1793-1799), which are also anchors (957-960, 1931); evaluate (676-680) has no exclusion. That gives conf>=0.35, i.e. +5.25 points (10.5 when PDH=PWH).
concepts.engineNotes: CAL-5.

concepts.name: Displayed PoT vs baseline (drift channel)
concepts.definition: The label shows f_potModel (empirical surface plus an analytic prior with 0.5x 50-bar drift, capped at 0.95); the EDGE baseline is driftless f_potBase.
concepts.dolRole: The number the user sees is less calibrated than the baseline, and the drift-carrying proximity reach favours the same side: the real selection-bias channel.
concepts.evidenceNotes: quant_pot: drift is the largest PoT error (+3.66% LL; analytic slope 0.66). A's report wrongly said the displayed PoT was the random-level model.
concepts.engineNotes: 2067 vs 1313-1322; reach at 665. Fixed by QPOT-01, then CAL-4/CAL-6.

concepts.name: Concept drift / forgetting
concepts.definition: Exponential discounting, adPredictor epsilon dynamics, fixed share; OPS adapts via regret against the best fixed map.
concepts.dolRole: Adapts to regime changes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Replica: epsilon=1e-3 worse on 10/14 sets, better on 4 (<=0.2 pp, plus GC 1h).
concepts.engineNotes: roll50 is display only (1478).

concepts.name: Learning-window path dependence
concepts.definition: Learned state built from a start tied to last_bar_index changes when the chart reloads with more bars.
concepts.dolRole: Reproducibility of past targets when the score uses ledger-learned multipliers.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Pine reference: last_bar_index 'will change when new real-time bars appear' and 'can cause indicator repainting'.
concepts.engineNotes: Ledger start at 2038. Gated learners (neutral until proven) minimise the effect.

concepts.name: Base integrity (roll gaps, bad prints)
concepts.definition: Exclude excursion windows that contain abnormal open gaps (for example >4 ATR) from the surface; hint to enable back-adjustment.
concepts.dolRole: Fixes the only situation in which learners beat the baseline, at the source.
concepts.evidenceNotes: GC 1h replica (CITL −4.25 pp, deff 7.7); TradingView help centre: back-adjustment disabled by default.
concepts.engineNotes: Surface bump 1527-1532 is unfiltered (CAL-10).

proposals.title: Neutralise f_calMult: overlap-aware, evidence-gated empirical-Bayes family multiplier
proposals.rationale: The current ((k+2)/(e+2))/((K+2)/(E+2)), clamped to [0.8,1.2] after n>=10, is >=10% off 1 in 47-66% of families under the null at n 10-40. It learns only from selected targets and ignores deff. It tilts family selection by up to ±20% of the score, more than the 4-point hysteresis. Cost as a probability proxy: −0.2..−1.8% LL.
proposals.spec: PURE HELPERS after f_sigm (~489): f_csBound(v,rho,alpha)=sqrt((max(v,0)+rho)*ln((max(v,0)+rho)/(rho*alpha^2))). INPUT calPrior=60 (G_SCORE; update the useCal tooltip). Replace f_calMult 1376-1382: gl=(K+2)/(E+2); vCl=max(vInd, cluSt[2]+cluSt[1]^2); deff=max(1,vCl/vInd); post=(k/deff+calPrior*gl)/(e/deff+calPrior); S=k-gl*e; V=deff*stPV[g]; cm = (V>0 and |S|>=f_csBound(V,10,0.10)) ? clamp(post/gl,0.85,1.15) : 1. Remove the n>=10 cliff. Once CAL-3 lands, take k, e, V and deff from the candidate ledger (cdSt/cdClu); per-family n rises to about 600-900 per 5,000 bars. Full-panel family rows show 'hit% · exp% · ×cm' with * when the gate is open. Measure: count target switches before and after.
proposals.risk: Slow to detect real family lifts on the selected ledger (a true 7% lift reaches 4.4% at n=320). Acceptable because measured lifts are below the noise floor, and CAL-3 fixes the sample size.

proposals.title: Peeking-safe EDGE verdict with a few-clusters guard and expected rates in family rows
proposals.rationale: The z>=2 / z>=1 verdict (2390) is re-evaluated after every booking: false EDGE 10-20% and false WEAK 45-65% under the null. Block variance with few 2H blocks (about 5 at H=450) is biased down. Family rows hide the expected hit rate.
proposals.spec: cluSt (1077) gains a 4th slot G (closed blocks), incremented in f_book (1463-1468) when blk changes and the old id >= 0. Panel 2383-2397: cG = G>=2 ? G/(G-1) : 1; V=cG*vEdge; S=kA-stPE[4]; bnd=f_csBound(V,rho,0.05) with rho 10 (tightest near 370 trials) or 5 (near 190 trials; m≈8.2 rho, Howard Prop. 3). Verdict: nA/deff<30 or G<20 -> CALIBRATING ('H too long' when G binds); S>=bnd -> ✓ EDGE; S<=-bnd -> ✕ NEGATIVE; else ~ UNPROVEN ±100*bnd/nA pp. Keep Wilson as the fixed-time interval. Family rows: hit% / exp% (100*stPE[g]/stN[g]). Label the CS as asymptotic, since V is estimated (Waudby-Smith 2021).
proposals.risk: Wider band (z about 3.0-3.7), so the verdict shows UNPROVEN more often, which is honest. Long-H users see CALIBRATING until the window holds 20 blocks.

proposals.title: Candidate (shadow) ledger with nearest/random/runner-up/mirror baselines and ATR delivered
proposals.rationale: Full-information grading removes bandit-feedback bias. It gives 2,477-3,473 probes per 5,000 bars (SE 0.87-1.38 pp) and is the only route to the >=100 events and non-events that calibration assessment needs. It answers whether the DOL beats nearest pool, a random candidate, the runner-up or the mirror, and it is the data source for CAL-1, CAL-4, CAL-6, CAL-7 and CAL-9. Supersedes ICT-1's mechanics.
proposals.spec: TYPE Probe after Trial (~396): lvId, grp, side, liq, edge, bar0, pb (f_potBase), pm (displayed-model PoT before the 95% cap; = pb after QPOT-01), d0, pO=na (CAL-4), pM/pG=na (CAL-9), role (0 routine, 1 DOL, 2 nearest, 3 hash-random, 4 runner-up, 5 mirror), array<float> x. Level gains lastProbe. STATE after 1080: var array<Probe> probes (cap 256), cdSt[5*4]=[n,k,Σpb,Σpb(1-pb)] per family+ALL, rlSt[6*5] (+Σy*d0), cdClu=[block,open Σres,Σclosed res²,G] keyed by floor(bar0/(2H)). Snapshot in step 17 after evaluate (inCalc, past warmup): for each lv with bar_index-lastProbe>=H and 0.25<=dA<=maxATR, push a routine probe. Role probes at each new Trial (2045): DOL; nearest with dA>=minDistATR; idx=int(abs(sin(bar_index*12.9898)*43758.5453))%pool.size(); second-highest score; mirror = virtual level at close-side*(edge-close) with the opposite side's pb. Roles never feed learning. Grading: new step 2b after 1550-1557 (strict hit for pools, touch for arrays; or H elapsed) -> f_probeBook (STATE HELPERS after f_potBase). Full panel rows: CANDIDATES hit/exp ±band; DOL vs NEAREST/RANDOM/#2/MIRROR paired excess with the CAL-2 band; ATR DELIVERED.
proposals.risk: Shared paths across probes (handled by cdClu). The cap may bind on huge pools (drop the farthest routine probes first). About 90 lines.

proposals.title: Gated online Platt scaling of the displayed PoT on the candidate ledger, plus a gated selected-target intercept
proposals.rationale: The displayed PoT is never graded or corrected, and roll-gap charts are the TradingView default. B's replica: gated OPS (ONS, gamma 0.1, rho 100) costs 0.00..−0.23% LL on 13 clean sets and gains +5.6% on the broken base, with two parameters and a 2x2 matrix. Calibrating on candidates gives about 10x the active ledger's data; the selected stage corrects only what is specific to the selection rule, behind its own CS test. Replaces A's CAL-6 calibrator and QPOT-04/SMC-1 recalibration.
proposals.spec: INPUT calPot Off/Measure/Auto (when proven), G_ACC. STATE: opsTh=[0,1] (a,b on logit p, identity start), opsA=[100,0,100] (rho I), opsSt[7]=[n,ΣLL raw,ΣLL ops,Brier raw,Brier ops,Σpm,Σy], selSt[4]=[n,Σy,ΣpShow,ΣpShow(1-pShow)], var float selDelta. STATE HELPERS after f_potBase: f_opsMap(p)=f_sigm(a+b*f_logit(p)); f_ll; f_opsUpdate(p,y): z=f_logit(p), r=map(p)-y, g=[r, r z], A+=gg', theta-=10*A^-1 g in closed form (det=a11 a22-a12^2), clamp a to [-1,1] and b to [0.5,1.5]; f_opsOn()= Auto and n>=200 and ΣLL ops < ΣLL raw - 1. Snapshot: probe.pO=f_opsMap(pm). f_probeBook (role 0): book sums with stored pm and pO, then f_opsUpdate(pm,y). Trial gains pShow; f_book books selSt; once per bar selDelta = (n/deff>=30 and |Σy-Σp| >= f_csBound(deff*Σp(1-p),10,0.05)) ? logit((Σy+100 Pbar)/(n+100))-logit(Pbar) : 0. Live 2067: pCal = f_opsOn() ? f_opsMap(pRaw) : pRaw; activePoT = min(0.95, f_sigm(f_logit(pCal)+selDelta)). Terminal: 'PoT CAL ✓ on · a +0.04 b 0.97 · ΔLL +0.8% · n'. Data window: PoT raw / shown.
proposals.risk: The broken-base evidence rests on one dataset; possible gate flicker (1-nat margin); depends on CAL-3 (without it, OPS on active trials rarely passes the gate, which is safe).

proposals.title: Remove self-confluence of PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL pools from the confluence pillar
proposals.rationale: Key pools are created at exactly the anchor prices (957-960, 1793-1799), so evaluate (676-680) counts each as confluent with itself: +5.25 points at default weights, 10.5 when PDH=PWH. Tier already rewards them (682), and the measured confluence lift is <=0.
proposals.spec: Step 17 (1930-1933): anchors = array.from(aPDH,aPDL,aPWH,aPWL,dayEQ,midOpen,ldnOpen,nyOpen,htfEQ), keeping na slots so the index identifies the anchor. evaluate 676-680: for [k,a] in anchors: own = this.src>=6 and k<=3 and math.abs(a-this.price)<=syminfo.mintick; if not na(a) and not own and a>=aLo and a<=aHi -> hits+=1. oKey (1986) is fixed automatically. Ledger check: share of key-level DOLs, EDGE, CAL-7 conf readout.
proposals.risk: Key levels become DOL slightly less often, which is the intended correction; tier and EQ still reward them.

proposals.title: One PoT scorecard (QPOT-04) plus a candidate scorecard, shown by the calibration hierarchy
proposals.rationale: The number the user sees must be graded. QPOT-04 specifies the active-trial scorecard. Adding the candidate version and showing only what the sample supports (mean, then slope once events and non-events are each >=100, then bins with >=30) avoids the noisy small-sample ECE and slope.
proposals.spec: Implement QPOT-04 (Trial.pPot, potSt, bins) once. Add candidate sums from CAL-3/CAL-4 (opsSt). Display (Full): mean CITL pp with the CAL-2 band when n_eff>=30; slope = OPS b (candidates) or 3 Newton steps on 10-bin sufficient stats (active) only when events and non-events >=100/deff; 5 equal-mass bins with n_eff>=30 as pred->obs; Brier, BSS vs p0, LL; Spiegelhalter z/sqrt(deff) as a secondary check. Example: 'PoT GRADE mean −0.8pp ±2.1 · slope 0.97 · BSS +0.3% · n 2,140 cand / 212 DOL'.
proposals.risk: Panel width (Full only).

proposals.title: Pillar information readout: which pillars carry information on this chart (shrunk, multiplicity-controlled)
proposals.rationale: Traders want to know which ICT claims hold on their symbol. Lifts are small and heterogeneous, and after Holm only EQ survives pooled, so per-chart measurement with multiplicity control is the honest product. Measurement only, so it cannot overfit the score.
proposals.spec: At CAL-3 snapshot record tertiles of fresh/conf/dens/draw and bits EQ/EXT/KZ. At resolution book [n,k,e,v] into pilSt[7*3*4]. Readout = excess(top third) − excess(bottom third) in pp, shrunk by V_prior/(V_prior+V) with prior sd 3 pp, starred when |diff| passes the CAL-2 boundary at alpha 0.05/7. Full row: 'PILLARS dens +1.2 · conf −3.4* · draw +0.4 · fresh −0.8 · EQ +4.1*'.
proposals.risk: Users may over-read single stars; shrinkage and alpha/7 keep false stars rare.

proposals.title: Expected-reach proximity pillar and a Target Objective input
proposals.rationale: PoT is geometry, so target choice trades hit rate against distance. d*P(d) from the chart's own surface peaks near 0.75 sigma sqrt(H) at about 45% PoT. Replica: 1.10-1.43 ATR delivered vs 0.86-1.09 for the hand score, with the hit rate matching its forecast.
proposals.spec: evaluate (661-667) gains parameters pR (f_potBase(dist, side), computed at the call site 1948 because evaluate precedes STATE) and erMax (once per bar: max_j (j*bStep)*S_j/n of the regime row, else 0.34*sigma*sqrt(H)/atr). erN=clamp(dAtr*pR/erMax,0,1). Input tgtObj Hit Rate/Balanced(default)/Reach: prox = legacy / sqrt(legacy*erN) / erN. Book Σy*d0 per family and per CAL-3 role, plus a data-window plot. With QPOT-01 the legacy reach becomes driftless too.
proposals.risk: The headline hit % falls (for example 60% to 45%) and users may read that as worse; default Balanced and show ATR delivered next to it.

proposals.title: Second-tier learner: Bayesian online probit pillar lifts with a hand-set prior, measure first, applied to PoT only
proposals.rationale: This learns pillar weights with shrinkage to the hand-set prior and is the best rescuer of a broken base (+8.8%, +10.5% mixed) and the most informative per-chart readout. On clean data it adds no skill (gated 0..−0.26%). Applying lifts to the score is not validated by a proper score, so Apply touches PoT only, mixed against the CAL-4 output.
proposals.spec: Inputs lrMode Off (default unless accView Full)/Measure/Apply to PoT when proven; lrSd 0.15; lrOmega 0.25 or 1/deff. 11 features at CAL-3 snapshot (bias, ext, fvg, obk, eq, fresh-.5, conf, dens-.5, draw-.5, kz>1, (dA-2.5)/2.5); prior means 0 except pillars kappa*w/wSum (kappa 0.3). var arrays lrMu, lrV, lrMix (2 log-weights), pqSt. Helpers f_npdf, f_phinv (Acklam, A's sketch), f_lrPred -> [m,s], f_lrUpdate (adPredictor, tempered, v floor). Snapshot: pM=Phi(m/s) with offset Phi^-1(pO); pG=pi*pM+(1-pi)*pO. Resolution (role 0): prequential sums, mixture (eta .25, fixed share .005), then update. Apply: PoT = pi*Phi((Phi^-1(pCal)+L)/s)+(1-pi)*pCal while n>=200 and LL model < LL reference. Full: 'LEARN ΔLL · π · n' and 'LIFT top-4 mu±sd'. Build only if CAL-7 shows real stars.
proposals.risk: About 120 lines; must be skipped entirely when Off; overlaps CAL-7.

proposals.title: Base-integrity guard: keep roll gaps and bad prints out of the excursion surface
proposals.rationale: The only case where any learner beat the baseline is a corrupted base (GC 1h roll gaps: CITL −4.25 pp, deff 7.7). TradingView continuous futures are not back-adjusted by default, so fixing the input beats learning around it. Coordinate with quant_pot.
proposals.spec: SERIES near 919: gapBar = |open-close[1]| > gapK*nz(atr[1],atr), gapK input 4.0 (G_POT, display.none); var int lastGap updated on gap bars. Step 0 (1527-1532): skip f_bump when lastGap > bar_index-H. Optional Terminal notice '⚠ ROLL GAPS — enable B-ADJ' when syminfo.type=='futures' and a gap was seen in the last 2,000 bars.
proposals.risk: Removes genuine gap windows on gap-prone symbols (fewer surface samples); the threshold needs a sibling check on equities and FX.

proposals.title: Gate f_raceAdj behind the same prequential test
proposals.rationale: f_raceAdj (1367-1371, used at 2130) applies an m=20 intercept shift unconditionally; ungated recalibration of calibrated bases loses log-loss (−0.36..+0.28% for selected trials).
proposals.spec: Trial gains pRaceA (adjusted race probability at open). raceSt gains [ΣLL raw, ΣLL adj] booked in f_book for decided races. Use the shift only while ΣLL adj < ΣLL raw − 1 and decided races >= 100. Coordinate with QPOT-02.
proposals.risk: Minimal; the shift is mostly inactive, which is honest.

result.summary:
B verified A's study, replicated it on new data, and ran four new causal tests. The combined report is session_stats.final.md.

1. A's central finding holds and is now stronger. Session, day and week key levels (PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL, Asia/London/NY ranges, HOD/LOD session, weekday of the weekly extreme) are taken at the rate that geometry plus the volatility clock predicts, within about ±3 pp. B re-ran A's code on EURUSD 2022-23 and every table matched its null again. Mok, Lam & Li (2000) find the same for the timing of the S&P futures daily high/low.

2. A overstated the after-break residuals. Day-clustered pooling of the four index futures, which share the same 250 days, gives the Asia two-sided raid +4.2 pp with SE 2.1 (z = 2.0, five ranges tested), not about 3 SE. The PD and London residuals flip sign out of period. Only the small "one-sided NY afternoon" lean keeps its sign in all 8 datasets.

3. ADR exhaustion is false, and the ADR profile is Brownian motion plus stochastic volatility. A BM + SV benchmark reproduces P(range >= 1 ADR) of about 43% and the fat tail. ADR is a good unit (sigma_day ≈ ADR/1.55, measured 1.53-1.57) and a bad cap.

4. Correction to A's top proposal: multiplying the engine's trailing σ by the day-state "today factor" makes PoT worse. Brier rises 2.2-4.9% on 1h and 4.6% on 5m index futures (CI excludes 0), because the trailing σ already holds today's activity. Day state belongs only in a clock-based variance level, and for the engine's main H-bar PoT the TIME-3 fast deseasonalised level is as good or better. The today factor helps only day-end horizons, best as a geometric blend.

5. A's 432-cell learned hazard surface adds nothing. Prequentially it scored 0.1-1.1% worse than one global calibration offset on every CME symbol. That single offset matters only where the analytic level is biased (BTC -9%).

6. Horizon matters as much as distance. An untaken PDH 0.2-0.35 ADR away is taken today 64% of the time from Asia but 19% from NY PM (7% on EURUSD), and the fixed-H PoT cannot express that. In ADR terms the engine's maxATR covers only 0.16-0.20 ADR on 1m and 0.41-0.50 on 5m, so on low timeframes key levels drop out of the pool.

7. New engine bug: old PDH/PWH/session highs keep their src code and their "PDH" label after a new day starts.

8. Gaps show no magnet beyond distance in FX or BTC. Index futures show only a small, dated opening reversal (Fung-Mok-Lam 2000, Grant-Wolf-Yu 2005); a recent MNQ gap-fade test fails.

9. The best proposals: key-level "PoT today / this week" (SESS-1), demoting stale labels (SESS-2), neutral session affinity and tiers (SESS-3), plus alerts, ADR units and a day-boundary input.

concepts.name: PDH/PDL taken next day (by open location and distance)
concepts.definition: P(the next exchange-day high strictly exceeds the prior-day high), and the same for the low, both or neither, conditioned on where the day opens (above PDH, upper half, lower half, below PDL) and on the open-to-level distance in ADR14 units. Day = the TradingView daily session (CME 18:00-17:00 ET, FX 17:00 ET, crypto 00:00 UTC). A gap beyond the level counts as taken at the open.
concepts.dolRole: Base rate for the most-used key-level target. The drivers are distance in ADR and the time left in the day.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A [this study]: ES 58.8/44.4% vs null 57.0/43.7; NQ 59.6/43.6; YM 52.4/48.8; RTY 49.2/46.8; CL 51.1/41.6; EURUSD 17-18 56.2/40.6; BTC 48.6/41.4 (null 51.6/44.0). B replicated on EURUSD 2022-23 (238 days): 50.4/49.6 vs 52.5/50.7. 'Both taken' is below the null in 7 of 8 datasets, but only by -0.5 to -5.8 pp, each with SE ≈ 2-2.5. The nearer side is taken first 76-81% of the time. External: Elite Trader ES at least one side 90.32% (n=186); edgeful (snippet) yesterday's H/L reached 81-88% of NY sessions. The no-magnet conclusion is strong.
concepts.engineNotes: f_rangeTrack 807-832, pdNew 945, aPDH/aPDL 952-958, registry pushes 1790-1794, tier 0.80 (f_tierW 506-515). Probability uses the fixed-H PoT (f_potModel 1303-1311): no day-end horizon and no ADR unit. On D charts pdNew fires every bar (known overhaul P1).

concepts.name: Session of first take; session that prints the HOD/LOD; first-hour extreme
concepts.definition: The NY-time session (Asia 18-02, London 02-08, NY AM 08-12, NY PM 12-17) holding the first strict through-trade of PDH/PDL, and the session holding the bar that prints the day's high/low (first print). The academic form tests the distribution of high/low times against the arcsine law of an intraday random walk.
concepts.dolRole: Timing priors ('London makes the high', 'NY takes PDH') and the rationale for killzone affinities.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: equals a clock day-bootstrap null within ±2.5 pp on 6 datasets (ES HOD NY PM 45.6 vs 46.1). B: EURUSD 2022-23 within ±1.2 pp. Mok, Lam & Li 2000 (RQFA 14(4):381-397): S&P 500 futures high/low times are consistent with a random walk; HSI futures show an excess in the first 15 minutes. Copeland, Lam & Jones 2004 (JFM 24(4):337-357): FTSE/CAC futures reject the random walk (overreaction). So deviations are market-specific. S&P first-hour HOD/LOD 70.5% vs a random baseline of 68.5% (885 days, snippet).
concepts.engineNotes: f_kzAff 597-602, applied at 1941, hard-codes ×1.05-1.20 raid priors (London×Asia pools, NY AM×London/PD, NY PM×NY AM). They are unsupported, and B's prequential test found no learnable session residual.

concepts.name: Asia range raids (20:00-00:00 ET engine window)
concepts.definition: High/low of the Asia window. After it closes, record whether each side is traded through before the day end (single/both/none), and after the first break whether the opposite side is also taken.
concepts.dolRole: Session-pool target; the 'London/NY raid Asia' heuristic.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: high 73-92%, low 72-85%, both 47-74%, within ±3 pp of the null. B: EURUSD 22-23 both 64.3 vs 65.5. The two-sided raid on index futures (opposite side after the first break) pools to +4.2 pp with a day-clustered SE of 2.1 (z = 2.0, five ranges tested), so it is weak; A's 'about 3 SE' assumed the four index futures were independent. Absent on CL, EURUSD and BTC. Mesfin 2026 (MNQ): Asia liquidity-grab fade and continuation both fail (gross 0.2-0.8 pts).
concepts.engineNotes: sessAs input 107, f_sessTrack 835-863, push 1801-1803 (tier 0.55), only on charts ≤ 1H (intraOK 947). Old Asia highs keep src 3 and the 'ASIA H' label on later days (stale-label bug S19).

concepts.name: London range taken later (NY)
concepts.definition: High/low of the London window (engine 02:00-05:00 NY). P(each side is traded through later the same day): single, both or none.
concepts.dolRole: Session-pool target; the 'NY takes London' heuristic behind f_kzAff.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: ES high 83.6/82.2, low 76.0/76.0, both 59.6/58.9 (real/null), within ±3 pp everywhere except EURUSD 17-18 both 28.6 vs 33.4. B: EURUSD 22-23 both 38.7/40.6. The after-break residual flips sign across periods (EURUSD -6.5 in 17-18, +2.1 in 22-23). Vendor numbers (TradeThatSwing single 70.66%; edgeful YM double 4.8%) use other windows and are not comparable.
concepts.engineNotes: sessLo 108, push 1804-1806 (tier 0.60). The f_kzAff ×1.20 for London pools in NY AM is unsupported.

concepts.name: NY AM range and the afternoon
concepts.definition: NY AM window high/low (10:00-12:00 on 1H; engine 09:30-12:00), and whether one or both sides are taken in the afternoon.
concepts.dolRole: Afternoon target choice: the late-morning range tends to resolve to one side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 'Both' is below the null in all 8 datasets (ES 13.6 vs 19.1; EURUSD 22-23 4.6 vs 8.2), and single is +3 to +10 pp. The day-clustered pooled opposite-after-break on index futures is -2.5 ± 1.7 pp. The sign is consistent but the effect is small; a narrow NY AM range resolves one-sided (ES 19.3 vs 35.9, n=83).
concepts.engineNotes: sessNA 109, push 1807-1809. The window is wrong on 1H charts (bar-open time() test, wrong extreme on 76% of days; ict_time TIME-1). There is no NY PM range.

concepts.name: Overnight range (ONH/ONL) taken in RTH
concepts.definition: The 18:00-09:30 ET high/low; P(either side is traded through during RTH).
concepts.dolRole: First RTH targets on index futures.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: 'none' broken 4.0% vs 8.2% (ES) and 3.6% vs 7.4% (NQ) under the null, so RTH breaks at least one side slightly more than random. tradingstats NQ: at least one side 94.2%; NexusFi 96%. B: EURUSD 22-23 none 17.6 vs 19.2 (no natural overnight in FX).
concepts.engineNotes: No overnight range source exists. ict_time TIME-7 proposes it (src 8, tier ≤ PD, Auto on futures and indices).

concepts.name: Opposite side after the first break of a range
concepts.definition: For a range [L,H] (PD, PW, Asia, London, NY AM, ON), after the first strict through-trade of one side, P(the other side is also taken by day or week end), compared with a null continued from the break bar. Same-bar double breaks are excluded.
concepts.dolRole: Whether to discount (or boost) the sibling pool once its range has broken: continuation vs Judas reversal.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: PD -1.9 pp on average, NY AM -3.1, PW -1.6 to -6.5, Asia on indices +3.5 to +6.2. B, day-clustered pooled on indices: PD -0.5±1.7, London +1.7±2.2, NY AM -2.5±1.7, ON 0.0±1.8, Asia +4.2±2.1. EURUSD 22-23 PD +1.9 and London +2.1, so signs flip out of period. Under a calibrated clock × day-state model the sibling-taken residual is inconsistent across symbols (indices slightly under-predicted). fxbacktest: FX Asian-break fade 49.4%. Taylor 2026: no AMD direction beyond the trend.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent: no change needed. Raid outcomes feed only the draw vector D (liqEvt 1581-1582).

concepts.name: Time-of-day hazard of an untaken key level (PoT to day end)
concepts.definition: P(an untaken PDH/PDL is traded through by day end | distance now in ADR, clock time of the forecast). Analytic form: driftless reflection p = erfc(d / sqrt(2·V_rest)), with V_rest = σ_day² × the share of the day's clock variance still to come × a day-state factor, and σ_day ≈ ADR/1.55.
concepts.dolRole: The 'will it go today?' probability; it decays a stale target toward the close and fixes the meaningless fixed-H horizon for key levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A, pooled indices at 0.2-0.35 ADR: 64% (Asia) → 57% (London) → 47% (NY AM) → 19% (NY PM). B, EURUSD 22-23: 62/57/47/7%, and the real table matches the clock null overall (0.283 vs 0.287). The shape follows from the volatility clock and Brownian scaling. The far tail (≥ 1 ADR) is 2× the null in Asia/London because big days cluster. Causal Brier (1H IDX, day-end horizon): clock with an adaptive level beats the trailing σ by 5.0-6.2%; on 5m IDX by 11-14%.
concepts.engineNotes: H = potH bars (183/305), time-blind potSig (916); the ledger horizon is t.bars >= H (1455). On 5m H=30 is 2.5 h; on 1h it is 30 h. TIME-6/QPOT-06 add the analytic session-end horizon; SESS-1 adds key-level day and week odds independent of the pool.

concepts.name: ADR distribution, ADR↔σ conversion, and distance units
concepts.definition: ADR(N) = mean of the prior N full-day ranges (N = 14). Brownian range constant: E[max-min] = sqrt(8/π)·σ·√T = 1.596·σ·√T. Measured ADR14/σ_close-to-close ≈ 1.55. Chart ATR(14)/ADR14 by timeframe converts the engine's ATR settings into ADR.
concepts.dolRole: Symbol- and timeframe-independent distance unit and the level of the variance prior. It shows what the engine's candidate radius means on each timeframe.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: day range/ADR median 0.87-0.97, P(≥ 1) 38-46%, P(≥ 1.5) 10-16%, P(≥ 2) 2.4-7.3%. B: a constant-vol BM gives 0.95/43.7%/8.2%/1.0%; with lognormal day vol (sd 0.35, AR 0.6) it gives 0.91/42.5%/15.3%/5.2% and lag-1 0.30, matching reality. ADR/σ_cc: CME 1.53-1.54, EURUSD 1.56-1.57, BTC 1.54-1.55; cash SPX/NASDAQ 1.31/1.22 because the RTH range excludes the gap. ATR14/ADR: 1m 0.016-0.020, 5m 0.041-0.050, 15m 0.079-0.090, 1h 0.167-0.186. A script-author claim that '1/4-1/3 of days exceed ADR' is contradicted. Feller 1951; Parkinson 1980; Martens & van Dijk 2007 (realized range scaled by the average daily range).
concepts.engineNotes: No ADR anywhere; every distance is in chart ATR (maxATR 129, evaluate 661-667, eject 1521/1578, re-entry 1834). maxATR = 10 is 0.16-0.20 ADR on 1m, 0.41-0.50 on 5m and 1.7-1.9 on 1h, so key levels with a 17-29% chance today are out of the pool on low timeframes.

concepts.name: ADR exhaustion / ADR-remaining cap
concepts.definition: Folklore: once the day has used its ADR, further extension is unlikely. Tested as P(extend beyond the running extreme by x·ADR before day end) vs range used so far, against an ADR-scaled null.
concepts.dolRole: Whether to cap reach or eject targets when 'the ADR is used'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: the sign is reversed. Used ≥ 1 ADR gives +4 to +10 pp extension over the null (IDX x=0.10 26.3 vs 20.4; BTC x=0.25 15.7 vs 6.6). Logistic log(used): +0.215 IDX, +0.230 BTC, +0.10 CL, -0.03 EURUSD 17-18; A's SEs are naive because records overlap. B: EURUSD 22-23 +4.9/+2.9 pp at ≥ 1.3 ADR used, otherwise at the null. The weekly version agrees (SPX 23.9 vs 15.0, n=94). Explained by BM + stochastic volatility.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; it must never be added as a cap or eject rule.

concepts.name: Day state: today factor vs fast deseasonalised level
concepts.definition: Today factor f = clamp((range so far/ADR) / E[range so far/ADR at this clock time], 0.5, 2.5), shrunk by the share of the day elapsed. B: E[range so far](t) ≈ E[R]·sqrt(Vcum(t)/Vday), within 0.02-0.03 ADR on ES/NQ/BTC. The alternative is TIME-3's fast level: an EWMA (span 50 bars) of bar Garman-Klass variance ÷ the clock's slot expectation. The blend is sqrt(fast level × f).
concepts.dolRole: Scales forward variance to today's activity (volatility clustering), so key levels stay alive on expansion days and fade on dead days.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: clock × today beats the flat σ by 1.8-4.8% Brier (day-end). B correction: today factor × the engine's trailing σ is worse everywhere (1h IDX +2.2%, CL +4.9%, EURUSD +4.8%, BTC +3.3%; 5m IDX +4.6%, CI +1.8 to +7.5%). For H-bar PoT, TIME-3's fast level beats the today factor (5m IDX by 2.5%, 5m CL by 11%, 1h by about 1%). For day-end, the today factor wins on 5m IDX (-7.4% vs the fast level) and loses on 5m CL (+19.8%); the blend is best on 1h and near-best elsewhere. FX day-to-day range persistence is weak in every era (OANDA 2002-26 lag-1 0.01). Literature: Engle-Sokalska 2012, Andersen-Bollerslev 1998, Alizadeh-Brandt-Diebold 2002.
concepts.engineNotes: potSig = ta.stdev(chg, 50) at 916 already holds most of today's state on ≤ 15m charts, so a multiplier would double count. What is missing is a clock (TIME-3) with an adaptive level and, for day-end horizons, an ADR × day-state level (SESS-1).

concepts.name: Per-chart learned key-level calibration surface
concepts.definition: Cells of (time bucket × sibling-taken [× distance bin]) holding logit offsets over an analytic day-end PoT, learned online and shrunk to a parent offset (m = 20).
concepts.dolRole: Would learn market-specific session residuals and after-break effects on the user's chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B prequential test, 8 snapshots per level-day, 1h 2025-26 CME plus BTC 2017-24: cell surfaces were 0.1-1.1% worse than one global offset on ES/NQ/YM/RTY/CL. The global offset helps only where the analytic level is biased (BTC -9.0%; CME -0.1 to +0.9%). A 5,000-bar 5m chart holds about 17 days, so cells never fill. A's estimator also counted overlapping 30-minute snapshots as independent.
concepts.engineNotes: Do not build it. Use one gated global offset per horizon (QPOT-04 style), inside SESS-1.

concepts.name: Weekday of the weekly high/low; ICT weekly profiles
concepts.definition: The weekday (full 5- or 7-day weeks) on which the weekly high/low first prints, plus claims such as 'Tuesday low of week'.
concepts.dolRole: Would set weekday priors for weekly targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: U-shape Mon/Fri 23-34%, Tue-Thu 12-18%, equal to a day-order shuffle (SPX/NASDAQ 1999-2018, EURUSD 2002-26). 'Low by Tuesday in up weeks' 71.9-75.2% vs null 76.0-76.9%. Arcsine baseline Mon 29.5 / Tue 14.1 / Wed 12.8 / Thu 14.1 / Fri 29.5. Only a weekday variance factor is real (Monday range 0.38-0.40 vs Thursday 0.41-0.46 AWR). No published multi-year counter-evidence found (B).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent as a direction prior. The weekday variance factor belongs to TIME-3 clkD.

concepts.name: PWH/PWL during the week
concepts.definition: P(the previous week's high/low is traded through during the current week), the weekday of the first take, and the opposite side after the first break.
concepts.dolRole: HTF objective targets with a week-end horizon.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: SPX PWH 58.2/55.5, PWL 44.7/45.3; EURUSD 49.6/52.0, 48.6/48.5; BTC 53.5/54.1, 38.0/40.3. Both below the null everywhere (BTC 8.6 vs 13.6). The cumulative take by weekday matches the null. Opposite side after the first PW break 1-4 SE below the null. Week range used ≥ 1.1 AWR gives +9 to +12 pp more extension (n≈94).
concepts.engineNotes: Source present (946, 959-961, 1795-1799, tier 0.92), but scored with the fixed-H PoT and no week horizon. Old PWH/PWL keep src 7 after the next week starts (S19).

concepts.name: Gap fill and opening reversal (RTH, weekend FX, BTC 'CME gap')
concepts.definition: Fill = price trades back to the pre-gap close within a window. Mirror = price travels the same distance in the gap's direction. Fill minus mirror isolates any magnet effect. Opening reversal = intraday returns run against a large opening price change.
concepts.dolRole: Whether a gap origin deserves a target prior beyond its distance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: BTC CME gap 4-week fill 86.7% vs mirror 89.4% (>1 ADR 43.5 vs 78.3); EURUSD weekend 73.2 vs 73.0; index RTH +6.9 pp (n=204). B literature: Fung, Mok & Lam 2000 (JBF 24(7)) and Grant, Wolf & Yu 2005 (JBF 29(5), S&P futures 1987-2002) find reversals after large opening changes, weakened after costs. Mesfin 2026 (MNQ 2021-25): gap-fill fade T -0.32 to -0.59. Plastun et al. 2020: gap-direction momentum. Caporale & Plastun 2017: mostly efficient, with an FX exception.
concepts.engineNotes: No gap levels; ICTPD-6 proposes them. Recommendation: no fixed gap prior; grade with the ledger.

concepts.name: Opening range breakout (Crabel) / initial balance
concepts.definition: ORB: stop entries at the open ± a stretch, where the stretch = 10-day SMA of min(high-open, open-low) (definition verified; signed vs absolute variants differ). IB = the 09:30-10:30 RTH range and its extensions.
concepts.dolRole: Early-session direction and a morning-range unit.
concepts.evidenceNotes: London ORB follow-through 50.3% over 92,947 breaks (fxbacktest). MNQ ORB 09:30-09:55: best T = 1.50, year-unstable; pullback entries stopped out 80.7% (arXiv 2605.04004, re-read by B). Holmberg et al. 2013 (FRL): crude oil ORB profitable 1983-2011, mostly in the last decade. IB broken on ≥ 1 side 96-98%; IB extremes hit at the random-level rate. Smaller-side excursion from the open has a median of 0.17-0.22 ADR (the stretch in ADR units).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent as a source; the NY AM range covers the morning and the IB is in AMT-2's candidate ledger.

concepts.name: Inside day / NR7 follow-through
concepts.definition: Inside day: H ≤ H[1] and L ≥ L[1]. NR7: the smallest range of the last 7 bars. The claim is that contraction leads to expansion.
concepts.dolRole: Breakout and both-sides risk for the next day.
concepts.evidenceNotes: bias_dol: next range above the 20-bar median after NR7 0.26-0.45 vs base 0.48-0.50, so contraction persists. Both prior extremes taken 0.16-0.29 vs base 0.08-0.14 (geometry). edgeful SPY inside days: PDH 52%, PDL 40%, both 15.3% (72 days).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; geometry already covers the both-sides risk.

concepts.name: Monday range
concepts.definition: P(Monday's high/low is traded through Tuesday-Friday).
concepts.dolRole: Weekly 'Monday range' targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: high 73-77%, low 65-71%, both 40-48%; within ±5 pp of the week-bootstrap null, with mixed sign (SPX both +4.9, EURUSD -2.5, BTC -3.6).
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended as a special source.

concepts.name: Source tier as a hit-probability prior for key levels
concepts.definition: f_tierW weights (PW 0.92, PD 0.80, session 0.55-0.60, HTF 0.65, STF 0.45, chart 0.25) raise density (1.2·tier), the liqEvt weight and registry retention.
concepts.dolRole: Ranks key levels above chart swings.
concepts.evidenceNotes: PD/PW/session take rates equal distance-matched random paths (±3 pp, 8 datasets). calib_ml: per-family lifts cannot be learned on the selected-target ledger (family SEs 3-5 pp exceed the lifts). A tier is defensible as 'importance' (retention, display, tie-break), not as probability.
concepts.engineNotes: 506-515, density 682, liqEvt 1582, eviction 1818, display key 2053. The ledger pools all external liquidity into grp 1 (635-637).

concepts.name: Stale key-level identity (engine semantics)
concepts.definition: A PD/PW/session extreme should carry its 'PDH/PWH/ASIA H' identity only while it is the most recent one of its period. Older untaken extremes are ordinary or old liquidity.
concepts.dolRole: Truthful target labels and tiers. A trader will reject an engine that labels a three-day-old high 'PDH'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A correctness issue verified by code reading; there is no forecasting evidence for any tier of old extremes.
concepts.engineNotes: f_pushExt (1211-1223) only upgrades src on a duplicate; f_mergeAt (1127-1128) likewise. Registry entries keep src 6/7/3-5 until swept or evicted (cap 60, 1813), and f_levelName (518-521) names them PDH/PWH/ASIA H, while the true aPDH (957) differs.

proposals.title: Key-level PoT to day end and week end ('Today %', 'This week %') from the clock with a day-state level and one gated calibration offset (replaces A's SESS-1/2/5)
proposals.rationale: P(an untaken PDH 0.2-0.35 ADR away is taken today) falls from 64% (Asia) to 19% (NY PM) on indices and to 7% on EURUSD, and the fixed-H PoT (183/305) cannot say that. On 1-5m charts the key levels are not even in the pool (maxATR = 0.16-0.50 ADR). Among causal day-end models, the clock with an adaptive level beats the engine-like trailing σ (with the same horizon) by 5.0-6.2% Brier on 1h IDX and by 11-14% on 5m IDX. An ADR × day-state level adds value on index futures at 5m (-7.4% vs the fast level) but fails under level shifts (5m CL), so a geometric blend is the robust choice. A learned cell surface adds nothing (0.1-1.1% worse prequentially); one gated global offset fixes crypto's level bias (BTC -9%). This corrects A: day state applied to potSig raised Brier 2.2-4.9%.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_KEY, display.none): useKeyPoT bool (true); adrLen int (14).

SERIES (after 950): dADR = request.security(syminfo.tickerid, f_tfSafe("D"), ta.sma(high - low, adrLen)[1], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on) and wAWR = the same on "W" with length 10. That is 2 new requests on the engine's non-repainting pattern. kOK = useKeyPoT and timeframe.isintraday and nz(dADR) > 0.

Clock:
(a) With TIME-3: V_T3 = close² × fwdVar from now to time_close("D") (time.md l.378), and rest = the remaining share of Σ clkA·clkD.
(b) Standalone: kvB/kvT float arrays of NKB = ceil(1440/max(30, chartMin)) NY-clock buckets. Per confirmed bar, kvT[kb] += Garman-Klass(bar)/dADR². On timeframe.change("D"), kvB = EWMA(0.1) of kvT, then reset kvT and the running day extremes kHi/kLo. rest = (Σ kvB from the current bucket to the bucket of time_close("D"), plus the unfinished part of the current bucket) / Σ non-na kvB; one walk of ≤ 48 iterations per bar at global scope. V_ADR0 = dADR² · vDay · rest.

Day state (Brownian scaling, so no extra learned curve): done = max(0.02, 1 - rest); fRaw = ((kHi - kLo)/dADR)/sqrt(done); fD = 1 + sqrt(done)·(clamp(fRaw, 0.5, 2.5) - 1); V_ADR = V_ADR0·fD; Vday = na(V_T3) ? V_ADR : sqrt(V_T3·V_ADR).

Week: Vwk = Vday + nLeft·dADR²·vDay, with nLeft = round((time_close("W") - time_close("D"))/86400000); crypto weekend days × 0.75.

Per level: pK = d <= 0 ? 1 : min(0.95, f_erfc(d/sqrt(2V))) (f_erfc 411; driftless as in QPOT-01).

Tracked slots (≤ 10, independent of the pool and eject): aPDH/aPDL, aPWH/aPWL, today's finished Asia/London/NY AM H/L captured at asEnd/lnEnd/nyEnd (948-950), plus ONH/ONL if TIME-7 lands. kTk[slot] = the bar of the first strict through-trade today, updated on confirmed bars.

Calibration: when tb = int(8·done) changes, push (slot, pK) for each untaken slot (≤ 80 per day, one per level-day per bucket). At the rollover, y = kTk ≥ 0; N++, K += y, E += pK; Br0 += (pK-y)², Br1 += (pCal-y)². δ = f_logit((K + 20E/N)/(N + 20)) - f_logit(E/N). Apply pCal = f_sigm(f_logit(pK) + δ) only when ≥ 30 days have resolved and Br1 < Br0 (QPOT-04 gate).

Display: one Terminal row 'KEY PDH 38% · PDL 9% · ASIA H ✓ | WK PWH 22%' (the table at 2291 has 22 rows; raise it to 24). The Clean tooltip shows 'Today 38% · This week 61%' for key-level targets, and the face stays two lines. With TIME-6 potHor = Day End, pCal is the headline PoT for key-level targets and trials store hT.

Guards: never multiply potSig, the ATR surface, reach (665) or the race (1360) by fD; never cap or eject because 'the ADR is used up'.
proposals.risk: Holidays and early closes: time_close("D") follows the regular session, so odds are slightly high on half days; label them '≈'. Level shifts (CL early 2026) are handled by the blend and the calibration gate. FX range persistence is weak, so fD matters little there. There is no gain for the main H-bar PoT; that is TIME-3's job.

proposals.title: Demote stale PD/PW/session labels and tiers when a new day, week or session starts
proposals.rationale: Bug found by B: f_pushExt (1211-1223) and f_mergeAt (1127-1128) only ever upgrade src, so yesterday's untaken PDH keeps src 6 ('PDH', tier 0.80, f_kzAff) until swept or evicted. The same holds for PW (7) and Asia/London/NY (3-5). The engine can therefore show 'Target: PDH' for a three-day-old high while the real PDH (aPDH, 957) is elsewhere. That is a credibility problem for traders, and it pollutes per-family statistics.
proposals.spec:
Add src codes 9 (older day extreme, 'OLD PDH/PDL'), 10 (older week, 'OLD PWH/PWL') and 11 (older session, 'OLD SESS H/L') to f_levelName (518-521), f_shortName (532), the src comment (316) and f_tierW (506-515): 9 → 0.65, 10 → 0.75, 11 → 0.40, as importance only. f_kzAff returns 1.0 for them automatically.

In the engine block, immediately before the pushes at 1790/1795/1800: if pdNew or pwNew or asEnd or lnEnd or nyEnd, loop extReg and pool. Set src 6 → 9 on pdNew, 7 → 10 on pwNew, and 3/4/5 → 11 on asEnd/lnEnd/nyEnd respectively. Then push the fresh levels as now; the duplicate check (1216-1219) re-upgrades an entry whose price equals the new PDH.

No UDT change is needed (src is a mutable field of Ext and Level). The cost is one O(60 + poolMax) loop per period change.
proposals.risk: Fewer pools labelled PDH/PWH. Older extremes keep their liquidity role under a truthful name. Gate by timeframe.isintraday so D/W charts are not affected (S22).

proposals.title: Session affinity neutral by default; no learned session or sibling multiplier; tier means importance, not probability
proposals.rationale: f_kzAff (597-602, applied at 1941) adds ×1.05-1.20 for 'London raids Asia / NY raids London and PD'. First-take timing, HOD/LOD timing and session raids equal the clock null within ±2.5-3 pp on 8 datasets (A's day bootstrap, ict_time's clock walk, B's EURUSD 22-23 replication). A's learned replacement (mKey from the surface) and TIME-5's 'Learned' option have nothing to learn: prequential cell offsets lost 0.1-1.1% and there is no consistent sibling residual. Tiers add up to 1.2 × 0.92 to density (682) for pools whose take rates are pure geometry.
proposals.spec:
1) Adopt TIME-5's kzAffMode with default 'Off', keeping 'Fixed (legacy)'. Drop 'Learned', or have it return 1.0.
2) Density at 682: use 1.2·(tierMode == 'Probability (legacy)' ? this.tier() : 0.25). Keep the tier for registry eviction (1818), display ordering (2053) and a tie-break of +0.5·tier score points. Coordinate with OF-3/WYK-1, which touch the same pillar.
3) Per-family key-level statistics (PD, PW, session, old key) go to CAL-3's candidate (shadow) ledger with CAL-1 EB shrinkage, display only. f_calMult (1376-1384) stays on its four groups or becomes CAL-1.

No new requests; edits only at 682, 1941 and in input declarations.
proposals.risk: Fewer 'London raids Asia' picks in killzones, which is the honest outcome. The legacy modes preserve the old behaviour for ICT-narrative users.

proposals.title: Key-level 'taken' alerts and a day/week context row
proposals.rationale: Traders reason in session terms (PDH taken? Asia high taken? how much of the ADR is done?). The engine tracks these levels but shows none of their state, and the alert set (2077-2094) has no key-level event, a frequent request in competitor threads. The probabilities come from SESS-1, which is graded.
