proposals.spec:
On a confirmed bar, when a SESS-1 slot's kTk changes from -1 to bar_index: alert("DOL Engine ▸ " + name + " taken · " + oppName + " today " + str.tostring(pOpp*100, "0") + "% · next " + nextKeyName + " " + str.tostring(dNext/dADR, "0.00") + " ADR · " + syminfo.ticker, alert.freq_once_per_bar_close). Add alertcondition(keyTaken, "Key Level Taken", ...).

Terminal context row: 'DAY 0.72 ADR · busy ×1.3 · PDH ✓ · PDL 12% | WEEK 0.81 AWR', where the word is from fD (busy ≥ 1.25, quiet ≤ 0.8). It must fit the 22-row table at 2291 (raise it to 24 if needed).
proposals.risk: Panel clutter; keep it to Terminal style and the Clean tooltip.

proposals.title: ADR as a unit wherever a distance is shown, plus an optional ADR distance radius
proposals.rationale: The engine's 10-ATR radius is 0.16-0.20 ADR on 1m, 0.41-0.50 on 5m, 0.79-0.90 on 15m and 1.67-1.86 on 1h, and H = 30 bars spans 0.5 h to 30 h. 'The DOL' therefore means a different universe on each timeframe. ADR distances are comparable across symbols and timeframes (σ_day ≈ ADR/1.55) and are what traders read.
proposals.spec: HUD/tooltip distances show '0.42 ADR' beside ATR, using SESS-1's dADR. Optional inputs: distUnit = input.string("Chart ATR", "Max Distance Unit", options = ["Chart ATR", "ADR"], group = G_SCORE) and maxADR = input.float(1.0, ...). In ADR mode, per bar maxD = kOK ? maxADR·dADR/atr : maxATR. Pass maxD into evaluate as a new parameter: inside the method (661) the global dADR would be a forward reference, because the request is at ~950. Use maxD at the eject (1521/1578) and re-entry (1834) tests. The default 'Chart ATR' keeps current behaviour.
proposals.risk: In ADR mode on 1m charts the pool fills with far levels and selection changes, hence P3 and off by default. There is no evidence for which radius is 'right'.

proposals.title: Day-boundary choice (Exchange / NY Midnight / NY 17:00)
proposals.rationale: PD levels and SESS-1's day use the exchange day (945): CME 18:00 ET, FX 17:00 ET, crypto 00:00 UTC. ICT-style crypto users anchor at NY midnight or NY 17:00. Levels change with the anchor, but no anchor is better under the null. This is consistency and UX, not edge.
proposals.spec: dayAnchor = input.string("Exchange", "Day Boundary", options = ["Exchange", "NY Midnight", "NY 17:00"], group = G_KEY). newDay: Exchange = timeframe.change("D"); NY Midnight = dayofmonth(time, tz) != dayofmonth(time[1], tz); NY 17:00 = hour(time, tz) >= 17 and hour(time[1], tz) < 17, or a calendar-day change in tz. Feed f_rangeTrack(newDay) at 945 and SESS-1's rollover. With a non-exchange anchor, SESS-1 computes ADR from the chart's own day ranges (≥ 5 days) instead of the daily request.
proposals.risk: Changing the anchor changes the levels. The default keeps current behaviour.

result.summary: Researcher B re-tested A's main finding and overturned it. The weekly-pivot "path barrier" behind A's P1 proposal CL-1 is reproduced by meaningless weekly-scale levels: random prices inside last week's range give -6.70 pp (z -6.1) on CME, against -6.25 pp for the real pivots. With controls for the volatility unit and for distance in prior-week-range units, the real weekly levels add nothing on CME (-0.006 logit). Only the BTC weekly PP keeps about -0.17 to -0.19 logit (z about -3), so CL-1 is withdrawn. The generic driver is the engine's ATR14 reach unit: pool edge against the random-level baseline spans +3 to -10 pp on CME and +10 to -12 pp on BTC across ATR14/ATR200 quintiles. Sibling REG-1's blended unit cuts pool-event log-loss by 1.6-2.6%, and a three-term unit that adds the prior-week range helps a further 0.4-0.7% in 3 of 4 sets (CL-7 candidate). No classic level is a magnet beyond its distance: floor, Camarilla, Fibonacci, Woodie and DeMark pivots are reached at placebo rates, and this holds under the better unit. The one positive effect is a small prior-session value pull (CME settlement +3.45 pp, z 3.7; prior-day mid +3.96, z 3.6; BTC CPR top +2.13, z 3.6). It survives the unit change and beats liquidity pools at matched distance by about 5-6 pp, which is the basis for the widened CL-4 value target (pivot, day EQ or exchange settlement via ticker.modify settlement_as_close, optional gap gate, one object with the gap proposal ICTPD-6). Confluence with reference levels is never positive: period opens at a pool lower its sweep rate in 4 of 4 sets, and every key pool is self-confluent. CL-2 therefore sets wConf 15 to 0, with minScore 35 to 41 and hysteresis 4 to 4.7 so nothing else changes. Large gaps fill more than distance predicts (NDX +7.9 pp), but published evidence is mixed: Grant, Wolf and Yu find opening reversals, while Plastun et al. find gap-day continuation. BTC "CME gaps" are obsolete since CME went 24/7 on 29 May 2026. VWAP must not become a static target, and the folklore rules (narrow CPR means a trend day, above the reference means bullish) fail. Pine v6 offers ta.pivot_point_levels and settlement_as_close, and the engine uses only 6 of its 40 request calls. Lesson for the synthesis: any "levels between price and target" feature must be tested against scale-matched placebo levels and the corrected volatility unit, and CL-3 builds that control into the per-chart ledger.

concepts.name: Classic floor pivots (daily PP/R1/S1/R2/S2/R3/S3)
concepts.definition: PP=(H+L+C)/3 of the prior session; R1=2PP-L; S1=2PP-H; R2=PP+R; S2=PP-R; R3=H+2(PP-L); S3=L-2(H-PP), R=H-L, fixed for the next session. TradingView 'Traditional' continues to R5/S5; 'Classic' R3=PP+2R. Pine v6: ta.pivot_point_levels("Traditional", timeframe.change(tf)) returns [P,R1,S1,...,R5,S5]. Edge cases: settlement vs last-trade close, RTH vs ETH template, DST, crypto UTC day.
concepts.dolRole: Practitioners use R1/S1 as first targets or fades, R2/S2 as extensions, and 'above PP = bullish'. If they were magnets they would say which level is reached next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Moderate evidence of NO effect. A's T1 (CME 1h about 1,500 days, BTC about 3,300 days, distance-matched): R1 -0.1/-1.5 pp, S1 -0.5/-1.1, R2 -3.0 (z -3.1, CME), range-scaled placebos the same. B re-ran T1 against REG-1's blended-unit baseline: R1 -0.08/-1.94, S1 +0.03/-1.40, R2 -2.97/+0.67, essentially unchanged. Published: mypivots (ES/YM/ER2/NQ, 630 days) finds pivot bands 'only marginally more probable than a random system' (ES 34.2% random vs 34.6/37.3%). Lund thesis (Johnsson & Frykmer 2019): not profitable in standard form. Bulkowski's 53-58% not re-verified. Vendor R1/S1 touch rates have no distance control.
concepts.engineNotes: grep finds only swing ta.pivothigh/pivotlow (709, 879). Keeping pivots out of scoring is correct; display-only overlay via ta.pivot_point_levels (CL-6).

concepts.name: Central pivot range (CPR) and narrow-CPR trend-day rule
concepts.definition: BC=(H+L)/2, TC=2PP-BC, width=|2C-H-L|/3. Folklore: a narrow CPR (bottom quartile of 20-50 sessions) foretells a trend day, a wide one a range day; price above the CPR is bullish.
concepts.dolRole: Would set how far price runs (PoT scale) and the side bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's T6, n=8,699 days: next-day range is 0.92 ATR after a narrow CPR vs 1.10 after a wide one; trend days 34.6% vs 37.7%, i.e. reversed. Controlling for the prior range the sign is inconsistent (BTC +0.42 t 5.2, NDX -0.27 t -4.2). No published test exists. CPR BC (= the engine's dayEQ) as a level is a prior-value magnet (see that concept).
concepts.engineNotes: dayEQ (967) = CPR BC, used only as a confluence anchor (1931). The width rule is absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Camarilla pivots
concepts.definition: H_k=C+R*m_k, L_k=C-R*m_k with m=1.1/12, 1.1/6, 1.1/4, 1.1/2 (0.0917, 0.183, 0.275, 0.55); TradingView adds R5=(H/L)*C. Folklore: fade at H3/L3, breakout through H4/L4; '70% of moves inside H3-L3, 90% inside H4-L4'.
concepts.dolRole: Intraday reversal and target rungs.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null. A's T1: H3 +0.6/+0.1, L3 -0.3/-0.6, H4 +0.3/-1.2, L4 -1.2/-0.5 pp. B's blended-unit re-run: CME -0.6 to +0.5, BTC -1.7 to 0.0. Not path barriers (T8). The containment percentages are unsourced vendor copy (none).
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, which is correct; display option only (CL-6).

concepts.name: Fibonacci, Woodie and DeMark pivots
concepts.definition: Fibonacci: PP +/- 0.382/0.618/1.0 R. Woodie: PPw=(H+L+2C)/4, R1=2PPw-L, S1=2PPw-H, R2/S2=PPw +/- R. DeMark: X=2H+L+C if C>O, H+2L+C if C<O, else H+L+2C; PP=X/4, R1=X/2-L, S1=X/2-H. Pine 'DM' returns only P/R1/S1, and Woodie cannot be 'developing'.
concepts.dolRole: Alternative S/R target rungs.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null to negative: placebo-like edges. On BTC the blended-unit re-run shows FIB_R1 -2.27 (z -2.9) and FIB_S1 -2.64 (z -3.3), i.e. reached less often than random. CME FIB/Woodie/DeMark between -0.5 and +1.2 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Weekly floor pivots / weekly references as path barriers
concepts.definition: Floor formulas on the prior week's H/L/C (futures week from Sunday 18:00 ET, crypto from Monday 00:00 UTC), fixed for the week; 'crossed' = a level strictly between price+0.1 ATR and the target's near edge-0.35 ATR.
concepts.dolRole: A claimed a target beyond a weekly pivot is less likely to be reached (-0.25 logit per level). B: mostly a geometry and volatility-unit artefact.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [B-fix: moderate to weak for a level-specific effect.] A's T8 raw effect reproduced: CME -6.25 pp (z -5.3), BTC -5.45 (z -7.1). Scale-matched placebos (B1) give the same on CME: random prices inside the prior week's range -6.70 (z -6.1), pivots shifted 0.12-0.25 R_week -6.34, 3-week-stale pivots -5.54. On BTC the placebos are smaller (-2.5 to -3.6). Offset logit with controls (ATR14/ATR200, distance in prior-week-range units, inside-PW, week move, momentum): real weekly pivots CME -0.041 (t -0.6). Against a 3-term volatility-unit baseline with placebos: CME -0.006 (H24) / -0.06 (H8); BTC weekly PP only -0.185 (t -2.9) / -0.169 (t -2.6); R1/S1 and the weekly open null. Osler 2000 and Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004 (strong) concern firm-published S/R and book depth, not formula pivots. Weekly pivots as levels: baseline (T2).
concepts.engineNotes: Not computed. Correct not to hand-code a barrier (A's CL-1 withdrawn). Record XWPP/XW bits against phantom twins in the ledger (CL-3); the generic part goes to the reach unit (REG-1, CL-7). pwH/pwL already exist via f_rangeTrack (946); the prior-week close is close[1] on pwNew.

concepts.name: Weekly-scale geometry and the volatility unit (new mechanism)
concepts.definition: The reach baseline measures distance in ATR14 at the window start (f_empPoT/f_potBase 1284-1322). Volatility mean-reverts, so ATR14 over- or under-states the next H bars' movement. Distance measured in prior-week-range units (dw=d*ATR/R_week) carries an extra gradient. Counts of weekly-scale levels between price and target correlate 0.47-0.64 with dw.
concepts.dolRole: Determines PoT calibration and, through proximity reach, target choice. It explains apparent 'barrier' features.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2: pool edge vs the ATR14 baseline by ATR14/ATR200 quintile: CME +3.3 to -9.9 pp, BTC +10.0 to -11.7. By dw: CME +3.5 to -9.5, BTC +5.1 to -12.3. B3: blended unit sqrt(ATR14*ATR100) lowers pool-event log-loss 1.6% (CME H24), 2.6% (BTC H24), 2.5% (CME H8), 1.9% (BTC H8). Adding the prior-week range as a third geometric term helps a further 0.7%/0.4%/0.7% but is 0.3% worse on BTC H8. In-sample, two markets; the concept (HAR, volatility mean reversion) is strong.
concepts.engineNotes: ATR14 unit at 1527-1532 (surface), 1306/1318 (lookups), 665 (proximity reach). Fix: sibling REG-1 (blended unit); CL-7 adds a weekly-range term as a scorecard candidate.

concepts.name: Monthly pivots
concepts.definition: Floor and Camarilla formulas on the prior month's H/L/C.
concepts.dolRole: HTF S/R targets for swing traders.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's T2 on daily bars (SPX/NDX 1999-2018 + BTC): M_PP -1.75 pp (z -3.0) at 5 days, -3.28 (z -2.8) at 20 days, i.e. reached less often than random. Not re-run by B (REG-1 keeps ATR14 on daily charts).
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Naked / virgin pivots
concepts.definition: A pivot (PP or CPR) not traded during its own session; folklore says it acts as a magnet until touched.
concepts.dolRole: 'Unfinished business' targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null. A's T1: CME +0.8 (n 345), BTC -1.0. Blended-unit re-run: CME +0.04, BTC -0.77, CME H8 -1.27. Sibling amt_profile: naked POCs -2.3 to -4.7 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Round numbers / psychological levels
concepts.definition: Grid with auto step S=10^floor(log10(2*daily ATR)) plus the half step (ES 100/50, BTC 1,000/500, EURUSD 0.01/0.005, gold 10/5). Stops cluster just beyond rounds and take-profits sit at them.
concepts.dolRole: Where stops sit and where sweep wicks stop short: a barrier or zone-depth cap, not a magnet.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Order placement: Osler 2003/2005 (TP 9.3% at 00; stop-buys 14.4% vs 7.4%) and Bhattacharya, Holden & Jacobsen 2012. [B-new] Index and commodity barriers: Donaldson & Kim 1993 (DJIA 1952-1990, none in Australia); Aggarwal & Lucey 2007 and O'Connor & Lucey 2016 (gold yes, silver no). BTC: Urquhart 2017 (more than 10% of prices end in 00, no return pattern after rounds); Lee & Seong 2019 (barriers at 1,000/10,000). Bar tests: not magnets; wicks stop short (-4.2 pp, OF-4); A's T5 pools near rounds -1.0 to -1.4 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: Owned by sibling OF-4/ICT-3 (cap the zone at the round). Never a positive confluence anchor; ATRN bit in CL-3.

concepts.name: Option-strike pinning / 0DTE gamma levels
concepts.definition: Expiry-day price clustering at heavily traded strikes through delta-hedging flows.
concepts.dolRole: Would make strikes magnets on expiry days.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Historical pinning is strong (Ni, Pearson & Poteshman 2005; Golez & Jackwerth 2012: S&P futures 1992-2009, at least $115 m per expiry, attributed to last-minute ITM sales by individuals). Absent 2016-2025 (Elms 2026, 2,294 days, via a summary). [B-new] Cboe: 0DTE hedging is 0.04-0.17% of daily S&P futures liquidity.
concepts.engineNotes: Needs open interest, which Pine does not have; do not add.

concepts.name: Session VWAP and deviation bands
concepts.definition: VWAP_t=sum(tp*v)/sum(v) from the anchor, tp=hlc3; sigma=sqrt(sum(v*tp^2)/sum(v)-VWAP^2). Pine v6: ta.vwap(source, anchor) or ta.vwap(source, anchor, stdev_mult) -> [vwap, upper, lower]; anchor is a bool, e.g. timeframe.change("D").
concepts.dolRole: 'Return to value' target; 'above VWAP = buyers in control' bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's T4 (H8): frozen VWAP CME +1.5 (z 2.9), BTC +0.3. The moving VWAP's extra touches over a moving TWAP are +8.5 to +10.7 pp on CME, largely mechanical. +/-2 sigma bands: CME about 0, BTC -1.7/-1.4 (z -4.3/-3.7). Zarattini & Aziz 2023 verified (QQQ 2018-Sep 2023 +671%, Sharpe 2.1, MDD 9.4%; decay reported by third parties): a bias use, not targets. No peer-reviewed test of return-to-VWAP probability found.
concepts.engineNotes: grep vwap: none. Correct as a target: a moving target would inflate the ledger edge against the static f_potBase (1314-1322). Display-only option in CL-6.

concepts.name: Anchored VWAP (week, month, prior day, event)
concepts.definition: The VWAP sum started at a chosen anchor (week or month start, prior day, swing, gap, earnings); the final prior-day value = PD_VWAP.
concepts.dolRole: Dynamic S/R or 'cost basis' targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's T1, re-run by B: W_AVWAP CME +2.42 (z 2.0) / BTC -2.56 (z -3.3); M_AVWAP +0.91 / -2.35 (z -3.3). Inconsistent sign, negative on BTC. Published: definitions only.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, which is correct.

concepts.name: Prior-session value levels (settlement, PP, CPR/day EQ, prior-day VWAP)
concepts.definition: Levels at the prior session's centre of value: settlement or RTH close (CME ES = 30 s VWAP ending 15:00 CT since 26 Oct 2020), PP=(H+L+C)/3, D-EQ=(PDH+PDL)/2, CPR TC, PD VWAP.
concepts.dolRole: A small mean-reversion pull over the next 8-24 bars: a candidate target type that beats liquidity pools at matched distance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's T1, confirmed by B against the blended-unit baseline. CME H24: SETT +3.45 (z 3.7), CPR_BC +3.96 (z 3.6), PD_VWAP +2.84 (z 2.6), PP +2.27 (z 2.2). CME H8: SETT +3.60, PP +3.06. BTC: CPR_TC +2.13 (z 3.6), PP +1.73 (z 2.4). Placebos near the prior close are about 0, while placebos near the PP show the same pull: a value-centre effect. SETT, CME CPR_BC and BTC CPR_TC pass a Bonferroni cut. Pools at matched distance: -2.5 pp (CME) and -1.2 (BTC).
concepts.engineNotes: dayEQ (967) is only a confluence anchor; no settlement tracking and no value target. CL-4 adds an optional value target, with the settlement taken via ticker.modify(..., settlement_as_close = settlement_as_close.on).

concepts.name: Opening gaps / gap fill
concepts.definition: Gap = session open minus the prior close or settlement (Caporale & Plastun use open vs prior close); filled when price trades back to the prior close within the session or N sessions. ICT NDOG (17:00 to 18:00) and NWOG (Friday to Sunday) are the chart-visible futures variants.
concepts.dolRole: The prior close as a target after a gap, plus timing within the session.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's T3: NDX cash gaps of at least 0.5 daily ATR 30.6% vs 22.7% (+7.9 pp, z 4.5); gap-downs +12.0, gap-ups +0.3; small gaps about distance. Sibling ICTPD-6 B: CME gaps of at least 0.5 ATR +7.4 (z 2.2). Literature mixed: Grant, Wolf & Yu 2005 (strong; reversals larger after up opens, weak after costs) vs [B-new] Plastun et al. 2020 (US indices 1928-2018: gap-day moves continue in the gap direction, 'contrary to the myth' of filling). Vendor fill rates (77-85% small gaps; Linnsoft prior close touched on 58.1% of 1,803 days) have no distance control.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent. One object with ICTPD-6/PA-2: kinds 8/9, src 11-14, size-gated, graded in a separate REF family (CL-4).

concepts.name: BTC 'CME gap' (weekend futures gap)
concepts.definition: The price gap between CME Bitcoin futures' Friday close and Sunday reopen; folklore says '98% fill'.
concepts.dolRole: A crypto gap-fill target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [B-new] No methodology behind the folklore numbers; anecdotes only (6 of 6 filled in early 2025, mean 29 h). CME moved crypto futures to 24/7 trading on 29 May 2026 (press release 1 Jun 2026), so no new gaps form.
concepts.engineNotes: Do not build: obsolete, and it would need an extra request.

concepts.name: Period opens (daily/midnight, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly)
concepts.definition: The first trade of each period: futures week from Sunday 18:00 ET, crypto from Monday 00:00 UTC; month, quarter and year starts.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore: magnets and 'above the open = bullish'. Measured: not magnets, not bias, and negative as confluence at a pool.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's T2 (daily): QOPEN -1.9 (z -3.8) at 5 days, -4.1 (z -3.2) at 20 days; MOPEN -3.2 (z -3.0) at 20 days. B6 (blended unit) weekly or monthly open within 0.35 ATR of a pool: CME -6.25 (z -3.2) and -4.22 (z -4.6), BTC -3.39 (z -2.8) and -1.61 (z -2.7). As a path barrier after B's controls: weekly open null; monthly open CME -0.26 (t -2.6) vs BTC +0.14 (t +1.9), opposite signs. Midnight open is not special (ict_time B: +0.3 +/- 1.1 pp). No bias value beyond geometry (T7, bias_dol).
concepts.engineNotes: Only midnight/London/NY opens (220-222, 964-966), used as positive confluence anchors (1931), which is wrong. CL-2 removes them; never add weekly/monthly opens as anchors or targets.

concepts.name: Previous day / week high and low (PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL) and source tier
concepts.definition: Extremes of the completed prior day/week, live as pools until traded through (strict). The engine tier f_tierW gives PW 0.92 > PD 0.80 > HTF 0.65 > sessions > STF 0.45 > chart 0.25.
concepts.dolRole: Primary external liquidity targets; the tier says which is drawn first.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B5 pool edge by source (H24, ATR14 / blended / 3-term). CME: swings -3.24/-2.50/-1.86, PDH/PDL -3.35/-2.50/-1.79, PWH/PWL -6.90/-5.40/-3.82. BTC: swings -1.04/-1.13/-1.44, PD -1.58/-1.40/-1.69, PW -1.71/+0.45/+1.13. H8 similar (BTC PW +1.26 z 2.6 blended). [B-fix] The PW tier is market-specific (worst on CME, best on BTC), not simply 'unsupported'. calib_ml: tier/external lifts not significant after Holm.
concepts.engineNotes: 945-961, 1790-1799 (f_rangeTrack, registry src 6/7); tier 506-516 and 1.2*tier at 682. No hand reorder; learn TIER per chart (CL-3).

concepts.name: Previous month / quarter / year highs and lows
concepts.definition: Extremes of the completed calendar month/quarter/year, live while untaken (strict trade-through).
concepts.dolRole: Swing-horizon external liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's T2: PMH +0.3 / -3.6 (z -2.1), PML +0.3 / +1.8, PQH/PQL and PYH/PYL about 0 at 5 days. Baseline reach. Grade = moderate evidence of no edge.
concepts.engineNotes: f_rangeTrack only for D and W (945-946). CL-5 (optional Swing-mode completeness: src 9, f_tierW(9)=0.80).

concepts.name: 52-week / all-time / N-day extremes
concepts.definition: Max high / min low over 252 sessions, the full history, or 20/40/60 days (IPDA).
concepts.dolRole: Anchoring and attention points; volatility barriers.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong at monthly horizons in stocks (George & Hwang 2004; Li & Yu 2012). [B-new] Driessen, Lin & Van Hemert 2013: implied volatility and beta fall on the approach; variance +19% / +43% the day after a 52-week high / low break: volatility barriers. At DOL horizons A's T2 is baseline (252dH -0.2/+0.9 pp).
concepts.engineNotes: Absent. If siblings ACAD-5/6 or ICTPD-5 add them, tier at most 0.80 (not 0.95/1.0).

concepts.name: Confluence with reference anchors (engine pillar)
concepts.definition: conf = min(1, 0.35*hits) over anchors within confATR=0.35 ATR of the zone, weight 15/100. Anchors: aPDH, aPDL, aPWH, aPWL, dayEQ, midOpen, ldnOpen, nyOpen, htfEQ.
concepts.dolRole: Meant to raise targets that coincide with key reference levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No anchor family is positive. A's T5: engine pools as anchors CME -4.8 (z -3.6); EQ/opens +0.6 / -2.6 (BTC H8 -3.3); weekly pivots -6.1 / -3.8; opens -7.4 / -4.5; rounds -1.4 / -1.0. B6 (blended unit): opens at a pool negative 4/4. [B-fix] calib_ml's -0.25 logit is not significant after Holm (pooled -0.04, t -0.7): 'unsupported, not proven harmful'. [B-new via CAL-5] Key pools are self-confluent (pushed at their own anchor price: +5.25 points, 10.5 when PDH = PWH).
concepts.engineNotes: 139, 143, 674-680, 963-968, 1930-1934, 1986, 2208; key pools 1793-1799 vs anchors 957-960. CL-2: wConf 0, minScore 41, hyst 4.7, skip anchor build, CAL-5 exclusion if re-enabled.

concepts.name: Above / below reference bias rules (pivot, VWAP, AVWAP, weekly / monthly open)
concepts.definition: Bullish if price is above the reference, bearish below.
concepts.dolRole: Would pick which side's liquidity is taken first.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's T7 (which of PDH / PDL is traded first): geometry-only out-of-sample accuracy 0.664 (CME, n 1,945) and 0.718 (BTC, n 3,227). Adding any reference side changes Brier by -0.0006 to +0.0061: no gain. The rule's 68-72% accuracy is geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: Not in the draw vector D (correct; do not add).

concepts.name: Previous settlement (official close) and Pine access
concepts.definition: Exchange daily settlement: CME ES 30 s VWAP ending 15:00 CT (effective 26 Oct 2020; previously 15:15 CT). Pine v6: ticker.modify(syminfo.tickerid, settlement_as_close = settlement_as_close.on) makes 'close' on 1D+ the settlement for supported futures; request.security(tk, "D", close[1], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on) is non-repainting.
concepts.dolRole: The prior-value magnet and gap-fill target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definition strong (CME FAQ, verified date and time; the SER id A cited was not re-checked). Magnet: CME SETT +3.45 pp (z 3.7) at H24 and +3.60 at H8 against the blended unit (B4).
concepts.engineNotes: No settlement tracking. The engine uses 6 of 40 request.* calls (923-925, 939, 981-982), so one more is affordable. CL-4.

proposals.title: Neutralise the Confluence pillar, remove self-confluence, and never add reference levels as positive anchors
proposals.rationale: No anchor family raises the sweep rate (A's T5, 2 markets x 2 horizons). Period opens at a pool lower it in 4/4 sets under the better baseline (B6: CME -6.25 z -3.2, -4.22 z -4.6; BTC -3.39 z -2.8, -1.61 z -2.7). Weekly levels and round numbers proposed as anchors are negative. calib_ml finds the pillar unsupported after Holm. Every PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL pool is confluent with its own print, which adds about 5 points and double-counts tier. Together, 15/100 of the score tilts selection toward pools that are not more likely to be taken.
proposals.spec: (1) wConf (143) default 15 -> 0; keep the input with display = display.none and a tooltip citing the test. (2) Rescale thresholds so conf = 0 levels behave the same: wSum (304) falls from 100 to 85, so scores x1.176, hence minScore (146) 35 -> 41 and hyst (147) 4.0 -> 4.7; kzHx (163/976) and the 2x side flip (2012) scale automatically. (3) Step 17 (1930-1934): build anchors only if wConf > 0; otherwise pass an empty array<float>, so evaluate's loop (677-679) costs nothing and conf stays 0. (4) If a user re-enables wConf, apply calib_ml CAL-5: anchors = array.from(aPDH, aPDL, aPWH, aPWL, dayEQ, htfEQ) with fixed slots, and in evaluate skip slot k <= 3 when this.src >= 6 and math.abs(a - this.price) <= syminfo.mintick; drop midOpen, ldnOpen, nyOpen from the defaults. (5) Hide 'Confluence' in the tooltip breakdown (2208) when wConf == 0; oKey (1986) is unaffected. (6) README: Confluence row becomes 'default off; overlap with reference levels was tested and does not raise reach'. (7) Never push weekly pivots, weekly/monthly opens, round numbers or daily pivots into anchors (coordinate with ICT-3/OF-4). Ledger check: DOL share by family, EDGE, CL-3 TIER bit.
proposals.risk: Score levels shift; the threshold rescale keeps conf = 0 levels identical. FVG/OB arrays also lose confluence credit, which was not tested here; the per-family f_calMult still adapts.

proposals.title: Prior-session value target (D-PIV / D-EQ / SETT) with an optional gap gate, one object with ICTPD-6
proposals.rationale: The only classic levels reached more often than random from the session start are the prior session's value levels, and this survives REG-1's volatility-unit fix (B4): CME SETT +3.45 pp (z 3.7), D-EQ +3.96 (z 3.6), PP +2.27, repeated at H8; BTC PP +1.73 (z 2.4), CPR TC +2.13 (z 3.6). Liquidity pools at matched distance are at -2.5 pp (CME) and -1.2 (BTC), so a value level is the better bet at similar distance. Large gaps add more (NDX +7.9 pp z 4.5; CME of at least 0.5 ATR +7.4 z 2.2 per ICTPD-6 B). D-EQ is ICT's daily equilibrium, so it fits the product's vocabulary.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_KEY, display = display.none): useVal=false; valSrc in ['Pivot' (HLC/3, positive in both markets), 'Day EQ', 'Settlement']; valGap=0.0 x daily ATR (0 = every session, 0.5 = gap-fill mode). Series after 968, one new request (6 -> 7 of 40): tkSet = ticker.modify(syminfo.tickerid, settlement_as_close = settlement_as_close.on); [dC1, dH1, dL1, dAtr1] = request.security(tkSet, f_tfSafe("D"), [close[1], high[1], low[1], ta.atr(14)[1]], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on); dNew = timeframe.change("D") at global scope; valOK = useVal and timeframe.isintraday and not na(dC1) and dAtr1 > 0. Engine step 12c (confirmed bars, next to 1790-1799): if valOK and dNew, then vPx = Settlement ? dC1 : Day EQ ? (dH1+dL1)/2 : (dH1+dL1+dC1)/3; gD = |open - dC1| / dAtr1; dV = |vPx - close| / atr. If gD >= valGap and minDistATR <= dV <= maxATR, create f_newLevel(nextId, vPx > close ? 8 : 9, 14, vPx + 0.05*atr, vPx - 0.05*atr, vPx, bar_index, bar_index, 0, 0) with qual = valGap > 0 ? min(1, gD/1.5) : 0.6 and hlMult = sqrt(max(1, 86400/chartS)). Expire src-14 levels at the next dNew, or on touch. Touch points: f_newLevel side map (1085) add 'or kind == 8'; delivery block (1566) add 'and lv.kind <= 7'; grp() (635) maps kinds 8/9 to a new family 4 'REF' (f_grpName adds 4 => 'REF'; stats arrays 1066-1071 sized 6; ALL index 4 -> 5 at 1380-1381, 1470, 2375-2403, 2443; loop 2411 to 4; add const int GALL = 5); names: src 14 -> 'SETT' / 'D-EQ' / 'D-PIV' in f_levelName/f_shortName, sharing ICTPD-6's src 11 NDOG / 12 NWOG / 13 ORG. No origin lockout (src != 0); f_kzAff and f_tierW defaults. Ledger: REF family EDGE; f_calMult demotes it if the edge is <= 0.
proposals.risk: Tested from the Globex/UTC day start on 1h bars only. Near lines (0.5-1.4 ATR) are limited by the minDistATR taper. Published gap evidence is mixed (Grant-Wolf-Yu reversal vs Plastun gap-day continuation). Overlaps ICTPD-6/PA-2: build one object. Off by default.

proposals.title: Reference-context feature bits in the candidate ledger, each graded against a scale-matched phantom-level control
proposals.rationale: B1-B3 show how a reference feature looks predictive when it only proxies longer-scale distance or the volatility state: A's weekly-barrier claim would have been 'confirmed' by a raw per-chart lift. Market-specific residuals still exist (BTC weekly PP -0.17 to -0.19 logit; CME monthly open -0.26; PW tier sign differs by market), so each chart should measure them. Pairing each bit with a phantom twin isolates the level-specific part.
proposals.spec: On top of calib_ml CAL-3's candidate ledger (fallback: per-trial bits on active trials). Global state: wPP/wR1/wS1 from pwH, pwL, close[1] on pwNew (946); wOpn on timeframe.change('W'); mOpn on timeframe.change('M'); wkIx += 1 per week; three deterministic phantoms ph_k = pwL - 0.25R + 1.5R*frac(wkIx*0.6180339887 + k*0.381966), k = 0..2. Bits per graded candidate (tol = confATR*atr; 'between' = strictly between price+0.1 ATR and the near edge-tol): XWPP; XW = count of {wPP, wR1, wS1, wOpn} between, capped at 2; XPH = phantom count between (control); ATO = weekly/monthly open within tol; ATPH = phantom within tol (control); ATRN = round level within tol (OF-4 step); ATV = PP/dayEQ/settlement within tol; TIER class 0-4. For each cell accumulate n, k, E = sum(pBase); lift = ((k+2)/(E+2)) / ((K+2)/(E_all+2)) (f_calMult algebra, 1376-1383). Report net lift = lift(XW>=1)/lift(XPH>=1) and lift(ATO)/lift(ATPH) with n and a delta-method 95% CI on the log scale. Full-view row, e.g. 'CTX W-REF x0.94 (412) . PHANTOM x0.96 (390) -> net 0.98 +/-0.08 . OPEN@ 0.90 . TIER PW 1.03'. Display only by default; optionally multiply lv.mult by the net lift clamped to [0.85, 1.05] when both twins have n >= 200 and the CI excludes 1. About 20 floats of state, O(8) per candidate, no request.*.
proposals.risk: Multiple comparisons: show n and CI, default display only. Phantoms are weekly, so cells need months of history. Depends on CAL-3 for sample size.

proposals.title: Prior-week range as the third term of the reach unit (a scorecard candidate for REG-1 / TIME-4)
proposals.rationale: Even with REG-1's blended unit, distance measured in prior-week-range units keeps a strong gradient (about -1 logit per weekly range, t -3.7 to -4.2), the generic part of A's 'weekly barrier'. A three-term geometric unit (ATR14 x ATR100 x weekly range)^(1/3) cut pool-event log-loss a further 0.73% (CME H24), 0.73% (CME H8) and 0.37% (BTC H24) beyond the blended unit, but was 0.30% worse on BTC H8 (B3). This is HAR logic (daily, weekly, monthly volatility components), but the result is mixed, so it is a per-chart scorecard option rather than a default.
proposals.spec: Requires REG-1 (aU, atr100). Global: var float pwR = na; var int wBars = 0; var int wBarsPrev = na; on pwNew set pwR := pwH - pwL, wBarsPrev := wBars, wBars := 0; then wBars += 1 every bar. aW = pwR / sqrt(wBarsPrev) (weekly range in per-bar scale under random-walk scaling, which keeps the unit about ATR-sized so the surface grid bStep (307) keeps its resolution). aU3 = timeframe.isintraday and not na(aW) and nz(atr100) > 0 ? math.pow(atr * atr100 * aW, 1.0/3.0) : aU. Add 'Blended + Week' to REG-1's surfUnit options, or maintain a parallel surface sUp3/sDn3 (2 x 3 x 61 ints) as a TIME-4 scorecard candidate model; f_empPoT/f_potBase callers pass d/aU3 when selected.
proposals.risk: In-sample only, 1h bars; mixed sign on BTC H8. No weekly range during the first week (falls back to aU); holiday weeks give a short wBarsPrev.

proposals.title: Monthly high/low pools (PMH/PML) for Swing mode, tier no higher than PD
proposals.rationale: In Swing mode (W/D/4H) PDH/PWH are often already near or taken, and monthly extremes are the external liquidity swing traders watch: a completeness gap users expect filled. Measured reach is at baseline (T2: +0.3 pp at 5 days; -3.6/+1.8 at 20 days), so the value is coverage, not edge, and the ledger grades them.
proposals.spec: [pmNew, pmH, pmHB, pmL, pmLB] = f_rangeTrack(timeframe.change("M")) at global scope next to 945-946. Input useKeyM = input.bool(false, 'PMH / PML', group = G_KEY, display = display.none). Registry push like 1795-1799 with src 9: f_pushExt(extReg, pmH, true, 9, pmHB, (pmH - pmL)/atr*0.5, math.sqrt(math.max(1.0, 2592000.0/chartS))), and the same for PML. f_tierW (506-516) add 9 => 0.80 (the default would otherwise be 0.40; must not exceed PW 0.92). f_levelName (520-521): src == 9 ? 'PMH' / 'PML'. f_kzAff default 1.0. Low-TF anchors are clamped by f_x (404-405). Avoid src 11-14 (ICTPD-6, CL-4).
proposals.risk: Low: adds candidates graded at the baseline rate. Anchors clamped to 5,000 bars on low timeframes.

proposals.title: Optional display-only reference overlay on ta.pivot_point_levels (plus session VWAP) with honest tooltips
proposals.rationale: Traders look for pivots, Camarilla and VWAP, and competitors plot them. A Pine v6 built-in now makes all six pivot types one call. Showing them with measured tooltips (distance-only; value pull near PP/settlement; VWAP mechanical) adds familiarity without polluting the score.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_DISP, display = display.none): refOv = Off / Daily / Weekly / Daily + Weekly (default Off); refType = Traditional / Fibonacci / Woodie / Classic / DM / Camarilla; refN = 1-3 levels per side (default 1); showVW = false. Global every bar: pivD = ta.pivot_point_levels(refType, timeframe.change("D")) and pivW = ta.pivot_point_levels(refType, timeframe.change("W")), storing bar_index at each change as the left anchor; [vw, vwU, vwL] = ta.vwap(hlc3, timeframe.change("D"), 1.0); plot(showVW ? vw : na, 'Session VWAP', display = display.pane). On barstate.islast update at most 12 lines and 12 labels held in var arrays (line.set_xy1/xy2), dotted, theme dim colours, tiny right labels (W-PP, W-R1, ...), never in Clean style unless chosen. Tooltips: pivots 'reached at the rate its distance predicts; not a target'; PP/settlement 'prior-session value: slightly more often than distance (+2-4 pp, futures)'; VWAP 'moving benchmark; touches partly mechanical'.
proposals.risk: Clutter: off by default and capped at 12 drawings. Woodie cannot be 'developing' (keep developing = false).

result.summary:
I verified A's study, re-ran parts of it, added three new tests (B1-B3), and wrote one combined, corrected report.

1. No projection method in this domain predicts how far a leg goes better than a random level at the same distance. This covers Fibonacci and ICT SD extensions, AB=CD, Elliott and harmonic ratios, Brooks's breakout measured move, follow-through, H2/L2, 20-gap-bar, Always-In, and failed breakout to the other side (new test B3: +1.8 / −1.7 / +0.7 pp vs geometry on 1h / 5m / daily).
2. Several of A's numbers were corrected:
   - Bulkowski's measured-move target is half the first leg, and his full-leg target works only 45-56% of the time, which matches the 49-50% random-walk value.
   - The MQL5 Fibonacci result is a target-vs-stop race; its 2.0 target sat at geometry, so the grade drops to weak-moderate.
   - Prechter's CXO score is 17-22%, on a sample CXO itself calls low-confidence.
   - Brooks's 80% and 50% breakout-failure figures refer to different events.
3. The honest answer to "how far will this leg go" is still the directional-change overshoot law, with four corrections:
   - A left out its own shuffled null, which overshoots more than real data at k = 2 (1.16 vs 1.08 delta).
   - The scale differs by instrument (0.96-1.41).
   - It differs strongly by session hour on CME 1h: P(overshoot ≥ 1 delta) is 0.33 in Asia vs 0.45 in the London/NY morning.
   - The CME GC 1h file mixes contracts (1,429 bars with volume ≤ 10, 70-120 ATR jumps), so every 1h test was re-run without it.
4. New test B1 shows the leg-reach readout (PA-3) is already calibrated with no tuning: random levels 0.150 predicted vs 0.151 observed, pools 0.297 vs 0.278. A per-chart scale, an offset or a trend split adds nothing.
5. B1 also shows liquidity pools are not leg magnets. They are reached 1-2 pp less often than random levels at the same distance, and legs do not end just beyond them (no sweep-and-reverse signature).
6. New test B2 shows the current leg's direction carries no information about which pool goes first. At a fresh 1h extreme it slightly favours the other side (−2.8 to −4.3 pp), and not at all on 5m or daily. This agrees with REG-3's gating of the draw vector.
7. The one magnet with measured support is the prior RTH close / settlement (ORG). Three implementations converge (+3.4 to +3.5 pp clock-matched, +7 to +8 pp for gaps ≥ 0.5 ATR), so the grade rises to moderate.
8. A's PA-2 spec was wrong on that level. Through the registry the level becomes a trade-through BSL/SSL, but every test measured a touch. On 1H, time() also fires one bar late. The fix is ICTPD-6's gap-fill object with a gap gate, plus time_close() to detect the open.
9. The price-discovery projection fallback (PA-1) stays the top proposal, as a correctness/UX fix with zero edge, not a forecasting gain. It is re-coded to kinds 10/11 and src 14-17 to avoid collisions with ICTPD-5/6.
10. New PA-6 is the prerequisite for any new ledger family: today "ALL = index 4" is hard-coded in 12 places.

concepts.name: Brooks magnets (swing highs/lows, prior day H/L/C, open, measured moves, breakout points, gaps incl. MA gaps, range middle)
concepts.definition: Price levels Brooks expects price to retest. His 'Magnets: Support and Resistance' part covers measured moves (first leg, gaps, ranges) and 'other magnets': recent swing highs/lows, breakout points, gaps of any kind including moving-average gaps. The moving average itself is not confirmed there as a standalone magnet.
concepts.dolRole: Candidate target set: which level is taken next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Swing pools are reached at random-level rates (T2 row B −1.5 to +2.2 pp), and slightly below random in leg terms (B1: −1 to −2 pp). Of Brooks's magnets only the prior RTH close / settlement shows an edge (T5 +3.4 pp clock-matched; CL +3.46 pp; ICTPD gaps +7.4 pp). [CORRECTED] A listed the MA as a Brooks magnet.
concepts.engineNotes: Swings 1753-1789; PDH/PWH 944-961, 1790-1799. Opens and EQ are confluence anchors only (964-968, 1931). Prior close/settlement missing (PA-2). MA, breakout point and channel lines missing, correctly.

concepts.name: Brooks breakout-bar measured move (the '60%' claim)
concepts.definition: After a strong breakout bar (body >= m*ATR, body/range >= 0.6, close in the outer 25%, close beyond the 20-bar extreme), target = close + (close − open) or high + (high − low); stop = trade-through of the bar's low. Brooks: '60% chance of a measured move of the breakout size before the same distance the other way'.
concepts.dolRole: Probability the measured move is hit before failure after displacement.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T3: within ±1.5 pp of geometry at body >= 1 and >= 1.5 ATR. Follow-through gives 0.664 vs 0.663 geometry. Body >= 2 ATR gives +2.5 to +3.4 pp, inconsistent per series. [NEW-B] A Brooks-forum member's own backtest found 50-52% (via search summary). The 60% figure itself is weak.
concepts.engineNotes: No MM level; displacement only feeds D (897-904, 1536-1541, 1893).

concepts.name: Follow-through bar
concepts.definition: The bar after the breakout is a same-direction trend bar closing beyond the breakout close.
concepts.dolRole: Supposed confirmation that raises the MM probability.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T3: the win rate rises to 0.59-0.67, but geometry rises identically because the entry moves toward the target.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Leg 1 = Leg 2 / AB=CD measured move
concepts.definition: A (low) → B (high) → C (A < C < B); target D = C + f*(B − A), f = 1 (harmonic variants 1.272 / 1.618).
concepts.dolRole: Projection target beyond existing liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T1: P(leg2 >= leg1) 0.490 / 0.498 / 0.496 vs null 0.491 / 0.498 / 0.492. T2: MM 1.0 hit 0.451 vs base 0.448, no stall. Bulkowski: the full-leg target works only 45-56% (via search summary).
concepts.engineNotes: Correct as a scored source; missing as a price-discovery fallback (selection 1999-2005 falls back to a counter-draw target) → PA-1.

concepts.name: Bulkowski measured move up/down and measure rule
concepts.definition: MMU: first leg, corrective phase B-C, second leg. Current target = corrective low C + half of leg AB. Measure rule: breakout ± range height, scaled by a per-pattern 'percentage meeting target'.
concepts.dolRole: Target after a range breakout or a pullback.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [CORRECTED] MMU succeeds 60% in bull markets, MMD 43%; target = half the first leg; full leg 45-56%; deeper retrace → second leg >= first more often (31,000 MMU / 21,000 MMD). These are completed-pattern samples with no random baseline. T4 (1b): range-height MM +2.6 to +3.1 pp over geometry for 4-8 ATR ranges.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly not a level source; the small effect becomes a zero-prior feature (PA-5).

concepts.name: Measuring gap (Brooks) / FVG-midpoint projection
concepts.definition: Gap between the breakout point and the first pullback; target = 2*gap midpoint − leg origin.
concepts.dolRole: Projection target from a displacement FVG.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4 (3): vs random level −0.0 ± 0.6 pp (1h), +3.4 (5m, a time-of-day confound), +3.8 ± 1.7 (daily).
concepts.engineNotes: FVGs present (1868-1887); the projection is correctly absent.

concepts.name: Fibonacci extensions / ICT standard-deviation projections
concepts.definition: B + g*(B − A), g = 0.27, 0.62, 1, 2, 2.5, 4. ICT −0.27 = 127.2%, −0.62 = 161.8%, −1 = 200%. An ICT 'SD' is just the anchor-range height laddered outward; the anchor may be the CBDR, Asian range, opening range or manipulation leg.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed targets beyond the last swing.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T1: Fibonacci bumps 0.85-1.11 vs placebo 0.85-1.23. T2: edges flat across ratios. Batchelor & Ramyar: no clustering beyond chance. [CORRECTED] MQL5 is a race: 1.618 67% vs 71% geometry, but 2.0 at 35.5% vs 34.8% (n.s.); grade weak-moderate. No published SD hit rates.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; do not add as confluence anchors (1931).

concepts.name: Fibonacci retracement / OTE
concepts.definition: 0.382 / 0.5 / 0.618 / 0.705 / 0.786 retracements of the impulse as entry zones.
concepts.dolRole: Entry location; affects race geometry only.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T1 retracement bumps 0.83-1.11 with no Fibonacci excess; Tradeify: continuation falls smoothly with depth.
concepts.engineNotes: Correct; ICTS 1.10.

concepts.name: Elliott wave target rules
concepts.definition: Wave 3 = 1.618 x wave 1; wave 5 = wave 1; C = A; wave 2 retraces 0.5-0.618; wave 4 retraces 0.382; subjective counts.
concepts.dolRole: Leg-length targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No controlled test. [CORRECTED] CXO Prechter 17-22% vs 47% average, with a sample CXO calls 'very small … confidence very low'. Westland 2024 (Sci Rep): no Elliott autocycles in crypto/NFT. The ratios are rejected by T1 and L1.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Harmonic patterns (Gartley, Bat, Butterfly, Crab)
concepts.definition: XABCD with Fibonacci ratio windows (e.g. Gartley B = 0.618 XA, D = 0.786 XA); D is a reversal zone.
concepts.dolRole: Reversal zone / targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Only small-n student or blog tests (7-29 trades per pattern) plus a researcher-degrees-of-freedom critique; B found no peer-reviewed test.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Breakout test / breakout pullback
concepts.definition: After a breakout, price returns to test the breakout point.
concepts.dolRole: Magnet at the broken level.
concepts.evidenceNotes: WYK §2.5: throwback 0.870 vs random level 0.872.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Failed breakouts / Brooks 80% rule
concepts.definition: A close beyond a 20-bar range high/low; failure = a close back inside within 5 bars.
concepts.dolRole: Whether a raid holds (continuation) or fails (reversal).
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4 (1): back inside 53-62% vs 48-53% null. [CORRECTED] Brooks's 80% is for attempts (including probes that never close beyond); his 'actual breakouts fail about 50%' is closer to the data.
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt (1579-1582) treats a close beyond as hold = continuation. The sign and certainty are owned by BIAS-4 / ICTS-2 / REG-3.

concepts.name: Failed breakout → test of the other side of the range [NEW-B]
concepts.definition: After a close back inside a 2-8 ATR, 20-bar range within 5 bars, race the opposite range edge (touch) against a trade-through of the failed extreme.
concepts.dolRole: Which side's liquidity is taken next after a failed raid.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B3: diff vs geometry +1.8 ± 0.8 pp (1h, null +0.2), −1.7 ± 0.8 (5m, null −1.3), +0.7 ± 1.9 (daily, n 480). Geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; do not add a bonus.

concepts.name: Trading range vs trend (Brooks context)
concepts.definition: Range = an area of agreement where breakouts fail; trend = always-in, with breakouts that succeed.
concepts.dolRole: Regime that should modulate draw and hysteresis.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Regime labels do not persist (REG finding 1); T4 and B3 show only small or null breakout effects.
concepts.engineNotes: Covered by REG-2 and WYK.

concepts.name: Always In direction
concepts.definition: Sign of the latest strong two-bar breakout (each body/range >= 0.5, combined body >= 2 ATR, closing beyond the 20-bar extreme), held for 100 bars.
concepts.dolRole: Bias: which side's liquidity is taken first.
concepts.engineNotes: drawD / dirSide (1891-1895, 1975) is an always-in-like vote gating selection; REG-3 gates it.

concepts.name: Second entries H2/L2
concepts.definition: In a bull pullback, H1 = first bar with a high above the prior bar's high; after a lower low, the next such bar is H2.
concepts.dolRole: Which pool first: trend high vs pullback low.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: 20 gap bars / moving-average magnet
concepts.definition: >= 20 consecutive bars entirely beyond EMA20; the first EMA touch is expected to retest the trend extreme (forum: 70-75%).
concepts.dolRole: Conditional PoT boost for the trend-extreme pool.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Dow theory (trend definition, confirmation)
concepts.definition: Trend = HH/HL (LL/LH) until a failure swing breaks the prior low/high; two averages must confirm.
concepts.dolRole: Structural bias / side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Brown, Goetzmann & Kumar 1998: high Sharpe ratios and positive alphas 1902-29, out-of-sample neural-net replication; long horizon only (the +4.4 pp/yr figure was not re-verified). Intraday structure side votes are a coin flip (ICTS, REG).
concepts.engineNotes: f_structure 708-782 is sound; SMT confirmation needs a second symbol.

concepts.name: Dow with-trend leg length [NEW-B]
concepts.definition: An up-leg starting from a higher low (zigzag p(i) > p(i−2)) or a down-leg from a lower high, vs counter-trend legs.
concepts.dolRole: Reach of the current leg.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B1, 1h GC-free: overshoot mean 1.107 vs 1.044 delta, P(>= 1 delta) 0.373 vs 0.356; null 1.153 vs 1.176. Net about +2.6 pp. 1h k3 +2.1 pp; 5m +0.5 pp. A theta split gives no Brier gain.
concepts.engineNotes: Too small for the engine; a zero-prior learner feature (PA-5).

concepts.name: Directional-change overshoot law (leg reach before a pullback)
concepts.definition: After a delta = k*ATR reversal confirms a leg, the further extension before the next delta reversal is about Exp(theta*delta). For running extreme M, pullback u and target y beyond M: P = ((delta − u)/delta)*exp(−y/delta); for a target inside, a martingale race.
concepts.dolRole: Calibrated 'will this leg reach the target without a k-ATR pullback' probability.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Glattfelder et al. 2011 (E 1.04, C 1.06; verified in full text); Taylor/Lehoczky; Golub et al.: Exp(delta), Var = delta^2. T1 pooled theta 1.04-1.10, no leg memory. [CORRECTED] The shuffled null overshoots more at k = 2 (1.16-1.21 vs 1.06-1.10); per-instrument theta 0.96-1.41. [NEW-B] B1: theta = 1 is calibrated (random levels 0.150 → 0.151; pools 0.297 → 0.278); per-chart theta gives no gain.
concepts.engineNotes: Not present → PA-3, using the shared zigzag (step 9b).

concepts.name: Overshoot scale by session hour (volatility clock) [NEW-B]
concepts.definition: Mean overshoot / delta of legs grouped by the hour their DC confirms, with delta = k*ATR14.
concepts.dolRole: Calibration of leg reach and of distance-based PoT on intraday charts.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B1, CME 1h GC-free: P(OS >= 1 delta) 0.327 (00-06 UTC), 0.452 (09-12 UTC), 0.444 (12-16 UTC), 0.363 (16-24 UTC). Consistent with TIME/QPOT volatility-clock findings.
concepts.engineNotes: ATR14 and potSig are time-blind; PA-3 should use the QPOT-03 / TIME-2 clock multiplier when it lands.

concepts.name: Leg direction / position at the leg extreme as side information [NEW-B]
concepts.definition: Whether the nearest unswept pool on the current zigzag leg's side is traded through before the nearest opposite pool, vs martingale geometry, by pullback depth u/delta.
concepts.dolRole: Which liquidity is taken next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2: all bars −0.3 ± 0.4 pp (1h GC-free), 0.0 ± 0.5 (5m). At the extreme (u < 0.15 delta): −2.8 ± 0.9 (1h k2), −4.3 ± 1.1 (1h k3), null +0.2/+0.8; 5m −0.3; daily −0.6. Weak 1h-only reversion, BTC-weighted.
concepts.engineNotes: Not used; it supports gating momentum-type D votes (REG-3) and not chasing the leg.

concepts.name: Liquidity pools in leg terms (magnet or barrier) [NEW-B]
concepts.definition: For an in-progress leg, the nearest unswept 5-bar pivot beyond the running extreme vs a random level at the same distance in the same leg state; and whether legs that take it end within 0.5 delta beyond it.
concepts.dolRole: Whether pools attract legs or reverse them after a stop run.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B1 c2: pool − random −0.8 to −2.6 pp in 4 of 6 bins (1h), 14 of 18 real cells negative, null about 0. (d): end within 0.5 delta beyond 0.343 pool vs 0.361 random (1h), 0.363 vs 0.384 (5m); no sweep-and-reverse excess. Consistent with Osler 2000 (S/R interrupts trends 60.8% vs 56.2%).
concepts.engineNotes: Pools are the DOL universe; their displayed PoT (f_potModel 1303-1312) is calibrated on random levels, so it reads 1-3 pp optimistic for pools. CAL-4 and the family multiplier correct this.

concepts.name: Leg-time symmetry (leg 2 lasts as long as leg 1)
concepts.definition: Time from C to the MM touch is about the time from A to B.
concepts.dolRole: ETA / timing.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4 (4): Spearman +0.24 / +0.32 / +0.42, but the shuffled null gives +0.29 / +0.29.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; ETA belongs to the volatility clock (QPOT-06, TIME-6).

concepts.name: Prior RTH close / settlement / gap fill (ICT ORG)
concepts.definition: The previous regular-session close (16:00 ET) or settlement; live from the next RTH open if untouched and the gap is large enough; filled on a touch.
concepts.dolRole: Session target with a measured magnet effect.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T5: +3.4 ± 1.3 pp clock-matched (n 968), +4.2 / +4.8 pp at 0.5-2 ATR, −5.3 ± 3.1 under 0.5 ATR; the naive baseline overstates about 3x. [NEW-B] Convergent siblings: CL settlement +3.46 pp (z 3.7); ICTPD gaps >= 0.5 ATR +7.4 pp (z 2.2), NDX cash +7.9 (z 4.5). The effect may be 'prior-day value' in general (CL dayEQ +3.95). Grade raised from weak-moderate.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent. [CORRECTED] A's registry path (f_pushExt → step 11, 1834-1851) would make it a trade-through BSL/SSL, but T5 measured touches. time() fires one bar late on 1H. → PA-2 using ICTPD-6 kinds 8/9, src 13, time_close(), gap gate.

concepts.name: Price discovery (no draw-side liquidity)
concepts.definition: No unswept pool within maxATR on the trend side (new highs/lows, or after a cascade).
concepts.dolRole: State where a liquidity engine has no draw-side target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T6: 5.0% (1h), 5.8% (5m), 13.7% (daily) of bars; reach toward the blind side is about baseline (median 2.46 ATR in 30 bars).
concepts.engineNotes: Step 19 (1999-2005) falls back to a counter-draw target or nothing → PA-1. This persists after REG-3, whose gate opens in efficient trends.

concepts.name: Traders' equation / R:R race
concepts.definition: P x reward > (1 − P) x risk; race of target vs invalidation.
concepts.dolRole: Probability the target is hit before the stop.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Races are martingale races (QPOT); every Brooks setup tested here sits at geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: f_invalidation 1343-1364 calls f_raceH (defined 466; [CORRECTED] A cited 1343-1364 for it); HUD 2240-2246. Drift should be removed (QPOT-01).

concepts.name: Displacement / strong breakout as a draw vote
concepts.definition: Engine: body >= 1.2 ATR and body ratio >= 0.6, or a two-leg sum >= 1.8 ATR. Brooks-strength alternative: body >= 2 ATR, close in the outer quarter, beyond the 20-bar extreme.
concepts.dolRole: Direction of the draw vector D.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T3: 1-1.5 ATR bars at geometry; >= 2 ATR range-breaking bars +2.5 to +3.4 pp, inconsistent. [NEW-B] B1: reversal speed does not predict leg length (sign flips across sets); B2: leg direction carries no side information. ICTS B6: 51.3% null.
concepts.engineNotes: dispUp/dispDn 902-904, step 1 1536-1541, mV 1893, wM 0.20 (156); REG-3 gates D by default → PA-4 for legacy D only.

concepts.name: Trend-switching signatures at extremes (Preis et al.) [NEW-B]
concepts.definition: Volume and volatility peaks and inter-trade-time minima as functions of time to a local price extreme, claimed as universal power laws around switching points.
concepts.dolRole: Would-be 'leg is ending' predictor.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Filimonov & Sornette 2011 (full text): a Gaussian random walk reproduces the same power laws once extremes are selected after the fact; 'an artifact of their statistical analysis'.
concepts.engineNotes: Do not add climax or leg-end features as predictors.

concepts.name: Order clustering at round numbers (Osler) [NEW-B]
concepts.definition: Take-profit orders cluster at round numbers (trends reverse there); stop-loss orders cluster just beyond them (trends accelerate after crossing).
concepts.dolRole: The only documented mechanism for where legs stop or accelerate.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2003 J. Finance 58(5), RBS order book (via search summary). OF quantifies it: stop-buys 01-10 above '00' 14.4% vs 7.4% below; sweep wicks stop short of round numbers (−4 pp).
concepts.engineNotes: Owned by OF-4 / ICT-3 (round-number layer as geometry, not a score bonus).

proposals.title: Price-discovery projection targets (MM 1.0 / EXT −1 / MM 1.618 / LEG +1 delta) as an honest draw-side objective when no liquidity exists
proposals.rationale: On 5-14% of bars (T6) the trend side has no pool within maxATR, so step 19 (1999-2005) shows a '⚠ COUNTER-DRAW' target against a running trend, or nothing. REG-3 does not remove this: its gate opens in efficient trends, exactly where price discovery happens. Projections are reached at random-level rates (T2 −0.5 to +2.7 pp flat across ratios; L1; L2), so the existing PoT is already honest for them. P1 is for correctness/UX in a frequent, conspicuous state; the expected edge is zero.
proposals.spec:
0) Shared ATR zigzag, step 9b after 1776, every confirmed bar. Input zzK = 2.0 (G_LIQ, display.none). State zzMode/zzExt/zzExtB/zzOpp/zzOppB plus arrays zzPx/zzTy/zzBr (max 3). A bar that sets a new extreme never confirms; delta = zzK*atr (code in report §4).
1) Ladder (bull; mirror for bear) when zzTy = [−1, +1, −1], zzMode == 1 and A < C < B: MM1 = C + (B − A); EX1 = B + (B − A); MM16 = C + 1.618*(B − A). Fallback when there is no valid triplet: LEG1 = zzExt + zzK*atr (mean overshoot).
2) Rung = the lowest rung >= close + minDistATR*atr.
3) Activation, new step 16b inside inCalc: useProj, dirSide != 0 (REG-3's gated side once it lands), zzMode == dirSide, and no level with kind <= 9 on dirSide with 0 <= distance <= maxATR*atr (one pool pass).
4) Level: kinds 10 (above, side +1) / 11 (below); src 14/15/16/17 = MM 1.0 / EXT −1 / MM 1.618 / LEG +1 delta. Thin zone of width wPx; qual 0.5; anchorBar = zzBr.get(2); touch semantics via isArray(). At most one per side, moved in place (and t.edge in openT as at 1124-1126). Delete with a '⊘ REPLACED' ghost when real draw-side liquidity enters.
5) Touch points: f_newLevel side map 1085 adds kind 8 and 10; partial fill 1566 adds 'and lv.kind <= 7'; f_tierW(14-17) = 0.20; f_levelName/f_shortName names; the origin lockout is inert (src != 0); f_kzAff default.
6) Ledger: family 4 PROJ via PA-6 (grp(): kind >= 10 ? 4; cm4 = f_calMult(4) in step 17, 1935-1944).
7) Clean tooltip: 'Price discovery: no liquidity above within 10 ATR. Projection, not liquidity: reached like a random level at this distance.' Optional PRICE DISCOVERY tag.
proposals.risk: Users may over-read Fibonacci/MM labels; the tooltip states the measured rate. The rung changes at most once per leg; hysteresis and the two-bar challenger rule (2012-2018) prevent flicker. Kind/src codes must follow the central map (kinds 8/9 and src 8-13 are taken by ICTPD-5/6).

proposals.title: Prior RTH close / settlement (ORG) captured by session time, as ICTPD-6's gap-fill object with touch semantics and a gap gate
proposals.rationale: The one Brooks/ICT magnet with measured support: T5 +3.4 ± 1.3 pp over a clock-matched random level (n 968), concentrated at 0.5-2 ATR (+4.2 / +4.8 pp) and negative under 0.5 ATR (−5.3 pp). CL (+3.46 pp, z 3.7) and ICTPD (gaps +7.4 pp; NDX cash +7.9 pp) converge. On 23-hour futures charts no chart gap exists, so ICTPD-6's time-break detector never creates it. [CORRECTED] A's registry path gives trade-through BSL/SSL semantics, but every test measured a touch; and time() makes the open trigger one bar late on 1H.
proposals.risk: One year of correlated CME data plus one NDX-cash replication. Symbols whose RTH is not 09:30-16:00 ET need the input changed. The effect may be general 'prior-day value' (CL dayEQ +3.95 pp), so share the ledger family with CL-4. Settlement vs last trade differ by ticks. Crypto/FX are excluded by the type guard.

proposals.title: Ledger-family constant (NFAM / ALL) and a central kind/src code map, prerequisite for any new level family
proposals.rationale: [NEW-B] ALL is hard-coded as index 4 in 12 places, and step 17 applies cm0..cm3 only. Siblings already claim kinds 8/9 (gaps), src 8-10 (N-day extremes) and 11-13 (NDOG/NWOG/ORG), and both PA-1 and CL-4 want family 4. Without one refactor, each new family edit risks silent index errors (array out of bounds, or a family booked into ALL).
proposals.spec: Add 'const int NFAM = 5' (0 chart liq, 1 ext liq, 2 FVG/gaps, 3 OB/BRK, 4 PROJ) and 'const int ALL = NFAM'. Size stN/stK/stBars/stPE/stPV/stMae to NFAM + 1 (1066-1071). Replace the literal 4 with ALL at 1380-1381 (f_calMult), 1470 (f_book array.from(t.grp, ALL)), 2375-2376, 2384, 2388-2389, 2403, 2443 (data window). Loop 2411 becomes 'for g = 0 to NFAM − 1'. f_grpName (543-549) gets a 4 => 'PROJ' case. Step 17 (1935-1944): cm4 = f_calMult(4) and the ternary extended. grp() (635-636): kind >= 10 ? 4 : kind <= 1 ? (src == 0 ? 0 : 1) : (kind <= 3 or kind == 8 or kind == 9) ? 2 : 3. Central map: kinds 0-7 as now, 8/9 gap-fill (ICTPD-6), 10/11 projections (PA-1); src 0-7 as now, 8-10 N-day extremes (ICTPD-5), 11 NDOG, 12 NWOG, 13 ORG/settlement, 14-17 projections. Update f_newLevel 1085, f_tierW 506-516, f_levelName/f_shortName 518-541 and f_kzAff 597-602 together. If CL-4's SETT family is adopted, set NFAM = 6 with SETT = 4 and PROJ = 5.
proposals.risk: A mechanical edit across about 15 lines. Its main risk is a missed literal, so grep for '.get(4)' and 'array.new<.*>(5' after the change. Pine 'const int' is valid at global scope.

proposals.title: Leg-reach readout: 'reaches the target before a k-ATR pullback' (overshoot law, theta = 1), graded by the ledger
proposals.rationale: The honest answer to 'will this leg get there?'. B1 shows it is calibrated without tuning: random levels 0.150 → 0.151 (1h), 0.158 → 0.162 (5m); pools 0.297 → 0.278 and 0.310 → 0.305. A per-chart theta, an offset and a trend split give no Brier gain. [CORRECTED priority, P2 → P3] It changes no target choice, is equivalent to distance plus pullback depth, and on intraday futures it is miscalibrated by session hour (P(OS >= 1 delta) 0.33-0.45) until a volatility clock exists.
proposals.spec: PURE HELPERS: f_legReach(tgt, side, M, p, dl). If dl > 0: u = max(0, side*(M − p)); q = max(0, dl − u); y = side*(tgt − M); result = y > 0 ? (q/dl)*exp(−y/dl) : q / max(q + side*(tgt − p), 1e-9). Use M = zzExt and dl = zzK*atr (times the QPOT-03/TIME-2 clock multiplier when it exists), only when zzMode == activeLv.side; otherwise show '—'. Terminal HUD line after the PoT line (2240): 'LEG 41% before a 2.0-ATR pullback'; Clean: tooltip only. Ledger: Trial gains pLeg, lgExt, lgDl, lgY = −1. In f_step (1434-1459), while undecided: update the favourable extreme; lgY = 1 on hit; lgY = 0 when the pullback from lgExt reaches lgDl first (same-bar order by advFirst, 1441). f_book accumulates legSt [n, Σp, Σy, Σ(p−y)^2]. Full-view row 'LEG pred x% · obs y% · Brier z (n)'.
proposals.risk: Pools read 1-3 pp optimistic (B1 c2). The session-hour bias stays until the volatility clock lands. It adds HUD length, so Terminal only. It assumes zero drift, consistent with QPOT-01.

proposals.title: Displacement vote in the legacy draw vector only for Brooks-strength, range-breaking bars
proposals.rationale: dispUp/dispDn (902-904) fire on 1.2-ATR bodies with no close-location or structure requirement. T3: geometry below 2 ATR; only >= 2 ATR range-breaking bars show +2.5 to +3.4 pp, inconsistently. [NEW-B] B1/B2: reversal speed and leg direction carry no reach or side information. REG-3 gates D by default, so this matters only for legacy D (gate off) or if BIAS-2 / ICTS-1 keep D.
proposals.spec:
Input brkMult = 2.0 (G_FLOW, display.none). Reuse the existing hh20/ll20 (883-884) with [1] instead of new ta calls:
- brkUp = close > open and bodyB >= brkMult*atrP and bRat >= 0.6 and close >= high − 0.25*rngB and close > hh20[1];
- brkDn mirrored with close < ll20[1].
Replace dispUp/dispDn with brkUp/brkDn in step 1 (1536-1541). Keep dispMult for FVG quality (912) and the HTF FVG request (939). Lower the wM default (156) from 0.20 to 0.10. Measure with ICTS-1's skill gate or REG-2's ledger split (drawFlip count and edge by D component).
proposals.risk: Fewer displacement events. Almost no effect when REG-3's gate is on. Per-series results are mixed, so keep it behind the input.

proposals.title: Measured-move and ICT −1 SD rules as shadow roles in CAL-3's candidate ledger, plus zero-prior leg features
proposals.rationale: Brooks, Bulkowski and ICT traders ask whether the engine beats 'just aim at the measured move'; the random-level baseline does not answer that. The small T3/T4/B1/B2 effects belong in a zero-prior learner, not in hand-set multipliers: big breakout bars, range breaks, with-trend legs (+2.6 pp), pools beyond the extreme (−1 to −2 pp), and the 1h leg extreme (−3 to −4 pp).
proposals.risk: More per-probe state. Depends on CAL-3/CAL-9 and the shared zigzag being built first.

concepts.name: Trading day (day boundary) per asset class
concepts.definition:
Day boundaries by asset:
- CME futures: 18:00->17:00 ET with a 17:00-18:00 halt; Sunday 18:00 opens Monday's day.
- Spot FX: 17:00->17:00 NY on most feeds (FXCM documented); some feeds use 00:00 UTC, which creates a Sunday stub candle.
- Spot metals: 18:00->17:00 with a 17:00-18:00 break.
- Crypto: 00:00 UTC, 7 days.
- US stocks: RTH 09:30-16:00, extended 04:00-20:00, and an optional 24h (BOATS) view with 20:00-04:00 Sun-Thu.
- CME crypto futures: 24/7 since 2026-05-29.

In Pine, timeframe.change("D") and time_tradingday follow the exchange trading day. dayofweek uses the bar open, so it can name the previous calendar day on overnight sessions.
concepts.dolRole: Decides which extremes become PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL and when they are emitted.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Pine reference/time.md (time_tradingday example: FXCM:EURUSD Monday session starts Sunday 17:00). BTC: UTC-day vs NY-midnight-day high differs on 45.7% of days and low on 42.7% (n=2927) [A]. CME 24/7 launch date corrected by B: Friday 2026-05-29 (CME page; The Block; fxnewsgroup).
concepts.engineNotes: 945-946 use the exchange day via timeframe.change, run every bar at global scope. There is no choice of boundary (that is SESS-6) and no stub-day handling (ASSET-3).

concepts.name: RTH vs ETH key levels
concepts.definition: ETH = full exchange-day extremes. RTH = extremes of 09:30-16:15 ET (CME index futures; named session "us_regular") or 09:30-16:00 (stocks; session.regular). The prior RTH close is about the 16:00 ET settlement, which sibling CL-4 covers. ONH/ONL are TIME-7's.
concepts.dolRole: Two widely watched level sets. AMT and stock traders use RTH levels; ICT futures traders use ETH levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Index futures: the ETH high is printed outside RTH on 45.8% of days and the low on 50.0%; at least one extreme differs on 70-85% of days; median gap 0.19-0.28 ADR (n=216) [A rth_eth.py]. RTH levels are taken more often the next day (ES PDH 58.5% vs 50.9%), but that is geometry; no excess over distance has been shown. Practitioner usage is weak evidence.
concepts.engineNotes: 945 and 1790-1794 use the chart session only, so there are no RTH H/L on ETH futures charts and the stock ETH 'PDH' includes pre/post-market. B: A's named-session D request (ticker.new(...,"us_regular"), "D", [1], lookahead_on) has undocumented alignment outside RTH (it may lag a day overnight). f_anchorScan (1141-1160) also rejects an RTH high on 1H ETH charts when the 09:00 bar exceeded it. Use a chart-side RTH window tracker instead (ASSET-6).

concepts.name: Session clock and DST (local exchange time)
concepts.dolRole: Where Asia/London range pools, opens and killzones sit on the clock.
concepts.engineNotes: B-corrected from A's 'wrong'. One tz for all windows (107-109, 219-226, 799, 836, 948-950, 964-966, 971-974). The London mismatch weeks are fixed by TIME-1(e). The Asia definition is a convention with no measurable forecasting difference.

concepts.name: Sessions and killzones on 24/7 and RTH-only assets
concepts.definition: Crypto trades 7 days, but weekend activity is low; killzones and session pools should run on weekdays only. US stocks have no Asia/London/midnight sessions; their active windows are the open and the close. Session strings with no day digits apply every day. For overnight strings the day digit names the day the session ENDS ("1700-1700:23456").
concepts.dolRole: Avoids weekend noise pools and wrong hysteresis states.
concepts.evidenceNotes: BTC weekday 13-20 UTC share of activity 35.3% -> 43.7% (2017-19 -> 2023-25) [A]. Kaiko: weekend share of volume 28% (2019) -> 13-16% (2024). Baur et al. 2019 FRL: lower activity on weekends and local evenings across 7 exchanges. Pine concepts/sessions.md gives the overnight day rule.
concepts.engineNotes: 971-976: crypto sessions and killzones fire Saturday/Sunday. Stock RTH charts: Asia/London silently inert; 10:00-13:30 OFF-KZ. B-new: on stock ETH charts the London tracker records 04:00-05:00 and pushes it as LDN H/L, and the London KZ boosts Asia pools via f_kzAff. Stock 24h charts fire Asia and the midnight open on thin overnight prints.

concepts.name: Session coverage
concepts.definition: The share of a tracked window (Asia, London, NY AM, RTH) actually covered by chart bars = bars_in_window x chartS / window_length. Below about 0.6, the window's range is not the session's range.
concepts.dolRole: Stops partial windows from becoming full-tier session pools (stock pre-market as 'London', half-days, gaps in data).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional (B-new). On stock ETH charts on 1H, London 02:00-05:00 has coverage 1/3.
concepts.engineNotes: f_sessTrack (836-866) emits whatever bars fell inside; there is no count. Pushes at 1800-1809.

concepts.name: Midnight open availability per asset
concepts.definition: The NY midnight open exists only where a bar opens in 00:00-01:00 NY: futures, FX and crypto on charts of 1H or less. Stocks have no such bar; CME 4H bars open at 22:00/02:00. The stock substitute is the 09:30 RTH open (or 04:00 pre-market).
concepts.dolRole: A confluence anchor in the feature spec.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional. Sibling ict_time: MO is not special against neighbouring opens (+0.3 +- 1.1 pp, n=1,412). Sibling CL-2 neutralises the confluence pillar.
concepts.engineNotes: f_sessOpen (798-803) returns na and the anchor silently drops from 'anchors' (1931). The fix is labelling and a profile substitute only (ASSET-1).

concepts.name: Session-open gaps and gap-throughs
concepts.definition: Gap bar: time - time[1] >= max(2 x chartS, 1800 s). Gap-through: on that bar, open is already beyond the level's NEAR edge (side 1: open > bottom; side -1: open < top). The gap jumps over resting orders rather than running them.
concepts.dolRole: Decides whether a removed pool was taken by a run (raid evidence for D) or by a news gap.
concepts.engineNotes: The pool sweep loop (1554-1585) removes the level and adds evt x tier to liqEvt (1578-1582). B-corrected: the registry loop (1587-1592) does not feed liqEvt, and A's gap test used the far edge (top) instead of nearEdge(). f_step (1436-1460) counts a gap-through as a hit (correct) but nothing records that it was a gap.

concepts.name: FX rollover and metals reopen artefact
concepts.definition: At 17:00 NY spot FX rolls value date. Bank pricing engines restart, spreads widen from a fraction of a pip to several pips, and volume is under 0.6% of daily between 16:00 and 18:00 ET. Spot metals also reopen at 18:00 after a 1-hour break. Charts plotting the bid can show wicks that never traded at mid.
concepts.dolRole: Possible fake sweeps of pools near price on spot FX/metals.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanism moderate: CME 'When FX futures pause' (2026); BidFX; Krohn-Mueller-Whelan AEA draft (spreads highest and volume lowest at 17:00 NY). A: the 17:00 hour's median wick fraction is 0.70 vs 0.51-0.61. B fx_roll.py (EURUSD 1H 2017-18): at 17:00 the prior 24-bar extreme breaks on 10.1% of days vs a 18.9% median hour, with wick-only share 0.43 vs 0.52 median, so no excess fake sweeps at 1H. Charts at or below 15m are untested.
concepts.engineNotes: No rule; low impact at 1H and above. ASSET-10 (P3) adds close-confirm on charts of 15m or less.

concepts.name: Continuous-futures roll and back-adjustment
concepts.definition: On a contract switch the unadjusted continuous series jumps by the inter-contract spread, roughly the cost of carry S(r-q)T: ES about 0.6-0.8% of price (+35-55 points), NQ about +150-250 points at 2025-26 rates. TradingView rolls by a volume-based fitted rule at a session boundary; back-adjustment is OFF by default. In Pine, ticker.modify(tickerid, backadjustment = backadjustment.on) gives the adjusted series.
concepts.dolRole: The jump sweeps pools, creates fake FVGs and displacement, inflates the ATR and excursion surface, and shifts every stored distance by the basis.
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView support 43000685266 (back-adjust off by default) and 43000691027 (switch rule). Data: ES Dec-14-2025 +56.5 and NQ +260.75 (roll mixed with a weekend gap); Mar-15-2026 +34.5/+164.75 [A, B]. B-new: request histories are computed at load, so a roll during a live session shows no step in the back-adjusted request until a reload.
concepts.engineNotes: No detection. The sweep loop (1554-1592), FVG/OB creation (1600-1760) and atr (874) all absorb the jump. CAL-10 adds a 4-ATR gap filter only to the surface.

concepts.name: Holidays, half days, outages and stub days
concepts.definition: Holiday sessions are compressed (CME equity halts about 13:00 ET; NYSE early closes at 13:00 ET on 2026-11-27 and 2026-12-24). A stub day is a 'day' with under about 35% of the normal bar count: an outage day (CME 2025-11-27/28, about 10 h, a 4-bar day), a Sunday FX candle on a 00:00-UTC feed, or the partial first day on the chart.
concepts.dolRole: Stub days create fake PDH/PDL; holiday-day extremes are ordinary close levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: holiday days' median range/ADR is ES 0.76 and NQ 0.65. B-corrected from A's own output: their extremes are taken the next day as often as normal days' (either side 90.9% vs 87.6%, n=11), so A's 'weak PD liquidity' and tier demotion are unsupported. Outage and NYSE calendar facts from Fortune/MarketWatch and NYSE/BusinessWire.
concepts.engineNotes: 945 and 1790-1794 push stub days and the partial first period as full PDH/PDL with tier 0.80. The partial first period is also an overhaul P1. Fix: ASSET-3 stub merge.

concepts.name: Bars per period on session-limited assets
concepts.definition: Measured chart bars per trading day or week, not wall-clock seconds. On 5m: stocks 78/day and 390/week vs 288/2016 assumed; futures about 276/1380; FX 288/1440; crypto exact.
concepts.dolRole: The freshness (half-life) clocks of PD, PW and HTF levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Arithmetic: on stocks freshness runs sqrt(288/78) = 1.9x slow for D and sqrt(2016/390) = 2.3x slow for W; on futures/FX weekly about 1.2x.
concepts.engineNotes: f_tfRatio (567-568) and its callers at 1780-1781 and 1864, plus hmD (1792) and hmW (1797). Sibling CL-4 copies the same constant.

concepts.name: Bar alignment of 1H/4H by asset
concepts.dolRole: The STF=4H structure in Day Trading mode, and killzone/anchor membership on 1H.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Pine concepts/sessions.md: hourly RTH bars start at 09:30 'not on the hour'. B-new.
concepts.engineNotes: 923-925 build 4H structure from uneven bars on stocks; 1H membership via time() is TIME-1(a/b)'s domain. ASSET-7 adds a note.

concepts.name: Gap-contaminated ATR and volatility on session-limited charts
concepts.definition: True range includes the gap from the prior close, and potSig is the stdev of close changes. On RTH stock charts the overnight return lands in one bar per day.
concepts.dolRole: Distance units (ATR), eject distances, zone widths and the PoT sigma.
concepts.engineNotes: 874 (ta.atr) and 915-917 (chg, potSig). ASSET-9 is P3 and mostly stock-relevant.

concepts.name: Scheduled macro releases by asset
concepts.dolRole: Predicts WHEN pools near price get run, and by how much, per asset. A release-bar sweep is news repricing, not a raid.
concepts.engineNotes: No event awareness anywhere. TIME-8 adds one manual event plus an NFP rule; ASSET-5 extends it.

concepts.name: Pre-announcement drift
concepts.definition: About 9 of 20 market-moving US releases drift in the surprise's direction from about 30 min before, worth about 40-50% of the total adjustment (E-mini and T-note, 2008-14). Equities drifted +49 bp in the 24 h before FOMC in 1994-2011.
concepts.dolRole: A possible directional tilt into an event.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kurov, Sancetta, Strasser & Wolfe 2019 JFQA (the share is 40% in the 2017 draft and about half in the 2015/ECB versions). Lucca & Moench 2015; weak after 2011.
concepts.engineNotes: Not modelled. It is small and decaying; at most a ledger-gated term.

concepts.name: Session-directional drifts (overnight drift, FX fix cycle, intraday momentum, gold night)
concepts.dolRole: Would tilt D by time of day.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Boyarchenko et al. RFS 2023 and NY Fed 2026-07-01 ('Disappearing Overnight Drift'; A had 3.6%). Krohn, Mueller & Whelan 2024 JF 79(1) [B-new]. Gao, Han, Li & Zhou 2018 JFE 129(2) [B-new]. Breedon & Ranaldo 2013.
concepts.engineNotes: Deliberately not modelled. These are drifts of a few bp, not liquidity targets, and two are documented to decay.

concepts.name: Crypto weekend compression and weekend range
concepts.definition: Saturday and Sunday (UTC) ranges are compressed. The weekend high/low (Sat 00:00 to Mon 00:00 UTC) is a close, natural Monday pool.
concepts.dolRole: A close candidate on Monday. Weekend killzones and PD levels are thin-market noise.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Compression: Saturday 0.46 and Sunday 0.72 of a weekend-inclusive ADR in 2023-25 [A]. B-corrected: near side only and in weekday ADR, the weekend range is taken at the weekday rate at equal distance (91/88%, 76/75%, 52/52%, 36/34%); vol-neutral bins agree. The 2023-25 raw 75.5% vs 53.7% comes from median distance 0.18 vs 0.36 ADR. A's '+9-12 pp' is withdrawn.
concepts.engineNotes: Not tracked; on Monday, PDH/PDL = Sunday's range. ASSET-8 (P3) adds optional pools and a weekend-PD option.

concepts.name: Crypto funding times
concepts.definition: Binance perpetual funding at 00:00/08:00/16:00 UTC, moving to 4-hourly or hourly when the rate is capped.
concepts.dolRole: A possible timing anchor.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Funding-hour bars 1.05-1.12 vs 0.98-1.02, confounded with the 00 UTC day open and the 08 UTC Europe open [A].
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended.

concepts.name: Venue-specific wicks (crypto)
concepts.definition: Single-venue prints far beyond the market-wide price during liquidation cascades or depegs (2025-10-10/11: ATOM about -99.96% momentarily on one venue; USDe $0.65 on Binance vs about $0.99 on-chain).
concepts.dolRole: A wick through a pool on one venue is not market-wide liquidity being taken.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Secondary sources (CoinGecko, insights4vc, FTI); details disputed by the venues. B-new.
concepts.engineNotes: Documentation only. A cross-venue confirm feed is not recommended (request cost, basis, per-symbol mapping).

concepts.name: Volume availability by asset
concepts.definition: Cash indices have no volume; FX has tick volume; crypto has base or quote volume. syminfo.volumetype is populated by only some feeds ('mostly in the crypto sector').
concepts.dolRole: Whether the LVN zones and the volume-profile path factor can work at all.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Pine reference/syminfo.md remark on volumetype. B-corrected: 'n/a' does not mean 'no volume', so A's rule would have disabled VP on most futures and stocks.
concepts.engineNotes: Guards peak > 0 (2252-2254) and vpMean > 0 (1420) keep the engine from crashing, but nothing tells the user VP is inert. Use an empirical test, sum(lvV) == 0 (ASSET-7).

concepts.name: Settlement as close for futures daily bars
concepts.definition: TradingView uses the exchange settlement as the 1D close by default (ES settlement = 30 s VWAP ending 16:00 ET); intraday bars show last trades. Pine: ticker.modify(..., settlement_as_close).
