concepts.dolRole: Body-break structure on D uses settlement closes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView support 43000685268; Pine reference/ticker.md; classic_levels.final §1.10.
concepts.engineNotes: Matches what users see on a D chart. Documentation note only (ASSET-7).

concepts.name: Structural market changes 2025-26
concepts.dolRole: Day definitions and session sets change over time.
concepts.evidenceNotes: CME and trade press; Arnold & Porter / CLS Blue Sky; Cooley; TradingView support 43000790593. B-corrected: A had 2026-06-01 for CME and a 'proposed Dec 6' for Nasdaq.
concepts.engineNotes: Handle by detection (profile plus empirical flags), never constants.

concepts.name: Daily and weekly chart gating of key levels
concepts.definition: PDH/PDL are meaningful only below D, and PWH/PWL only below W. timeframe.change("D") is true on every D and W bar.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents every candle from becoming a 'PDH' pool.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional.
concepts.engineNotes: B-corrected: on a D chart, every candle's H/L is pushed as PDH/PDL (945, 1790-1794; overhaul P1). On a W chart, PDH = the prior week's high. Gate at 1790/1795 (ASSET-7).

concepts.name: Index option-expiry pinning
concepts.definition: On option expiration days the futures price is pulled toward the at-the-money strike.
concepts.dolRole: Would be a calendar-specific draw toward strikes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Golez & Jackwerth 2012 JFE: pinning in S&P 500 futures on serial expiries 1992-2009. Elms (SSRN 2026, secondary summary): none in 2016-25. B-new.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended: Pine has no open-interest data, and the effect has faded.

proposals.title: Market profile: auto-detection, per-asset session presets and a session-coverage guard
proposals.risk: Exotic CFDs are misclassified ('Other' = today's behaviour; manual override). Before the first Saturday bar, a misdetected 24/7 symbol behaves as today. The coverage guard can drop a few legitimate windows on charts with missing bars (covMin is exposed). mkt becomes series once sawSat is used.

proposals.title: Gap-through guard: a session-open gap is not a raid
proposals.rationale: 38% of stock PDH takes (29% of PDL takes) and 38% of futures Sunday-open PD takes are gap-throughs. The engine deletes the pool and adds evt x tier to liqEvt (1578-1582) for all of them, so weekend and overnight news gaps become 'raids that held' in D.
proposals.spec:
Global, at the top of SERIES before 874:
- gapBar = not na(time[1]) and (time - time[1]) >= max(2 x chartS, 1800) x 1000.

Sweep loop (1554-1585), liquidity levels only:
- gapThru = gapBar and (lv.side == 1 ? open > lv.nearEdge() : open < lv.nearEdge());
- run the existing evt/liqEvt update (1579-1582) only when not gapThru;
- on gapThru, remove the level as today but ghost it as '⤳ GAPPED'.
Arrays are unchanged.

Registry (1587-1592): no liqEvt there (B-corrected); optionally count gap removals.

Ledger: add bool gapHit to Trial; in f_step set t.gapHit := hit and tgtOpn and gapBar. The Full accuracy view shows 'HIT% ... (gapped k)'; hit semantics are unchanged.

The live sweep alert is unchanged.
proposals.risk: A genuine stop-run that opens just beyond a level counts as a gap (intended). Whether excluding gaps improves D is untested, but the siblings already found the raid->D mapping weak, so this removes noise. The 30-minute floor avoids false gaps on thin symbols with skipped bars.

proposals.title: Measured session clock: bars per day/week, stub-day merge, no partial first period
proposals.risk: f_tfBars is series-valued (callers already use series floats). The wall clock applies until one full day is seen. On D/W charts timeframe.change is true every bar, so ASSET-7's gating must land with it.

proposals.title: Continuous-futures roll handler with one back-adjusted request (phased)
proposals.risk: A roll during a live session is invisible to the request until reload (request histories are computed at load); ASSET-2 covers that bar meanwhile. Adds one request (about 8 of 40). Shifted zones sit off their anchor candles by the basis. Must be verified on ES1! and CL1! in TradingView.

proposals.title: Asset-aware scheduled-event calendar on top of TIME-8 (FOMC list, recurring presets, earnings, news-window rules, ledger split)
proposals.risk: Stale lists: the 2027 list is current as of 2026-11-12 and the tooltip says to update it. NFP/CPI dates are not computable reliably, so they stay manual. The multipliers are defaults until TIME-3 learns them. Parsing runs once.

proposals.title: RTH H/L key levels from a chart-side RTH window tracker
proposals.spec:
Input keySess = Auto | Chart | RTH | Both (G_KEY, display.none). Auto = Both for index futures, RTH for stkETH, Chart otherwise.

Window: rthWin = mkt == 0 ? "0930-1615" : "0930-1600" (America/New_York).

Tracking:
- charts <= 15m: f_sessTrack with TIME-1(a) overlap membership;
- 30m/1H: TIME-1(b) 30m-intrabar tracker (16:15 rounds to 16:30, stated in the tooltip);
- above 1H: off.
The tracker records anchor bars itself, so no f_anchorScan. Emits at RTH end, with the ASSET-1 coverage guard.

Push next to 1790-1794: f_pushExt(extReg, rthH, true, SRC_RTH, rthHB, (rthH - rthL)/atr x 0.5, sqrt(f_tfBars("D"))), and the same for the low.
- f_tierW(20) = 0.78; f_levelName 'RTH H'/'RTH L'; f_kzAff neutral.
- f_pushExt de-duplicates prices equal to the ETH PD levels.
- RTH mode on stock ETH charts replaces the chart PD push.

No new request.
proposals.risk: Depends on TIME-1(a/b). The preset is US-only: non-US futures (FDAX xetr_regular) default to Chart. On 1H the 16:15 end is approximate.

proposals.title: Data and chart-timeframe guards (D/W gating, empirical no-volume test, cash index, 24h stocks, 4H on stocks)
proposals.spec:
1. useKeyD effective only when timeframe.in_seconds() < 86400, and useKeyW only when < 604800 (gate at 1790/1795; merge with the overhaul fix).
2. vpDead = needVP and lvV.size() >= 24 and lvV.sum() == 0. When true: skip the VP build (1384-1414); the panel shows 'VOL n/a'; the LVN tooltip suggests the futures contract. volumetype == "tick" shows 'VOL tick'.
3. mkt == 5 (cash index): HUD note 'cash open stale; gaps unreliable'.
4. mkt == 4 with bars in 20:00-04:00 NY: panel 'SESSION 24h'; Asia and midnight stay off.
5. mkt == 4 and tfS == "240": tooltip about uneven 4H bars, suggesting Custom mode with 2H.
6. Tooltip on futures D structure: 'daily closes are settlement prices'.
proposals.risk: None material.

proposals.title: Crypto weekend handling: weekday gating plus optional weekend-range pools and a weekend-PD option
proposals.rationale:
Crypto weekends are compressed and thin (volume share 13-16%, and Baur et al. 2019 find lower weekend activity across exchanges). The engine runs killzones and sessions on them and uses Sunday's range as Monday's PDH/PDL.

B-corrected: the weekend range is NOT a stronger target than a weekday range at equal distance. Its high take rate is geometry, so this is UX and level-set completeness only.
proposals.spec:
Weekday gating comes from ASSET-1 (kz := 0 and session pushes suppressed when wkend).

Input wkPools (default false):
- track wkH/wkL and their bars over UTC Sat-Sun;
- on the first non-weekend bar, push SRC_WKND = 21 (tier 0.65, 'WKND H/L') with hlm = sqrt(f_tfBars("D")).

Input wkPD = Include | Skip (default Include). Skip suppresses pdEmit for trading days whose dayofweek(time_tradingday, "UTC") is Sat/Sun, so Friday's levels remain Monday's PD.

Note for TIME-3: on 24/7 symbols its weekly clock needs 7 day-buckets.
proposals.risk: NY-anchored users may define the weekend as Friday 17:00 to Sunday 17:00 NY (SESS-6 day anchor). Defaults keep today's behaviour.

proposals.title: Gap-aware ATR and PoT sigma on session-limited charts
proposals.rationale: On RTH stock charts the overnight return is about 38% of daily return variance (GOOG 2004-13), concentrated in one bar per day. ta.atr and potSig absorb it: the ATR jumps after every open and the bar sigma is inflated all day. On futures 1H the effect is small (ATR p90 +14-17% on Sunday-open bars).
proposals.risk: The ATR differs from the user's built-in ATR; the tooltip says so. Needs gapBar (ASSET-2) declared before 874.

proposals.title: Rollover/reopen close-confirm for liquidity sweeps on spot FX and metals, charts of 15m or less
proposals.rationale: At the 17:00 NY rollover (and the metals reopen at 18:00), bid-plotted spreads widen from a fraction of a pip to several pips on under 0.6% of daily volume. B's EURUSD 1H test found no excess fake sweeps (break rate 10% vs 19%, wick-only share 0.43 vs 0.52), so the guard is limited to fine charts, where a spread wick can be several bar ranges.
proposals.risk: A real rollover-minute run that closes back inside is ignored as a sweep (still recorded as a test). Not tested on charts of 15m or less; mid-priced feeds lose a little sensitivity.

result.summary: Two findings from Researcher A hold up, and one is overturned. SMT at a sweep has no reversal edge: 1-ATR race 50.5% for SMT vs 50.8% joint, difference CI [-2.2,+1.5] pp. Three public studies agree, and B's geometry controls remove A's small 'opposite pool first' tilt (logit +0.140 down to +0.016 [-0.064,+0.096]). A's main positive result, that the laggard's pool is hit about 1.05x more often once the sister sweeps, reproduces with A-style controls (B gets 1.051). It disappears once the chart's own path is controlled: at the moment the sister sweeps, the chart's wick has already come about 35% closer to its pool and it is in a range burst. With those controls the fresh-event Δlogit falls from +0.129 to -0.007 and the lift to 0.995. A small cross-asset effect remains while the sister state persists (sister swept 2-31 bars ago, chart pool intact): Δlogit +0.078 [+0.023,+0.133] at L3/H12 and +0.085 [+0.007,+0.163] at the engine's L5/H30, lift about 1.04 (+1.5 to +2 pp). The placebo is null (+0.014), all four asset classes are positive, and the effect builds after the sweep rather than decaying from it, so it is graded weak. The largest forecasting gain found here needs no second symbol: when the 3-bar mean true range exceeds 1.25x ATR14, pools are hit at 1.13x the distance-matched rate (1.075x at H30), and calm bars give 0.93x. The engine's 50-bar sigma and its bias-only empirical surface cannot see this. A's 'keep the raid-close classification as the reversal signal' is also wrong: in A's own events the geometry-neutral race is about 50% for reject, hold and mid, matching ict_liq ICT-9. Recommended order: first condition the PoT surface on range burst (no request). Then an optional SMT module: one request via ticker.inherit with [1] and lookahead_on, O(1) chart-swing twins, a corrected auto-pair map, a correlation gate and a sister state machine. The sister state feeds only a small persistent PoT logit shift (prior +0.08 for ages 2-31), calibrated against f_potModel rather than f_potBase, and never feeds D. The reversal reading stays behind a strict ledger gate.

concepts.name: SMT divergence (two-symbol swing SMT)
concepts.definition: Chart A has a pivot at bar T (L left/right bars), usable at T+L. The twin is R_B = extreme of B over [T-w, T+w] (w = 0-2) and must be intact over (T+w, T+L]. A sweeps on a strict wick trade-through (high_A > P). It is SMT when B has not traded through R_B by the decision bar (optionally after a grace period). Interval variant: XOR(A took its previous-interval extreme, B took its own), with intervals matched by open and close times. Statistics must be computed at the pivot-confirmation or decision bar, not the swing bar.
concepts.dolRole: Practitioners read it as proof of a stop run and expect a reversal toward the opposite liquidity, i.e. a flip of the draw side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Evidence is AGAINST a reversal edge. A: 1-ATR race 50.5% (SMT) vs 50.8% (joint), CI [-2.2,+1.5] pp; with Pine timing 49.7% vs 50.7%. mss-research ES/NQ: 49.5-51.8%, n = 11k-141k. Its README also shows that swing-bar look-ahead had inflated divergence win rates to 55-62%, falling to 49-51% once fixed. Genjutsu Kai: 47-51% over 88 tests, none beyond chance. charisjv19: -0.10 to -0.17 R, PF 0.75-0.85. B: A's nextLiq tilt is geometric (SMT coefficient +0.140 drops to +0.016 [-0.064,+0.096] once A's overshoot and raid class are controlled).
concepts.engineNotes: No second-symbol feed: all requests use syminfo.tickerid (L923-925, L939, L981-982). The step 3 sweep loop (L1558-1590) uses the chart's close only. The omission costs nothing for reversal prediction.

concepts.name: Sister-swept / laggard sync state (sick sister)
concepts.definition: B trades through its twin while A's matching pool is intact (sis = 2, sisBar = B's sweep bar, known 1 bar late in Pine). Sync = A later takes its pool; hold = it never does within the window. Genjutsu sync odds: logistic(-0.08 + 0.747*logit(2*Phi(-gap/(kappa*sigma*sqrt(t_left)))) + session).
concepts.dolRole: Picks WHICH same-side pool is the draw, as a weak continuation cue. B shows the useful part is persistent: Δlogit about +0.08 while the sister state is 2-31 bars old; there is no extra effect at the sweep bar once the chart's own path is accounted for.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: lift 1.054 [1.033,1.077] with Pine timing (B reproduces 1.051). B adds own-path controls (3-bar TR/ATR burst, wick proximity): fresh (age 0-1) Δlogit +0.129 drops to -0.007 [-0.062,+0.048], lift 0.995. Persistent (age 2-31): +0.078 [+0.023,+0.133] at L3/H12 and +0.085 [+0.007,+0.163] at L5/H30, lift 1.035-1.042 (1.04-1.05 for pools beyond 1 ATR). Placebo: +0.014. By asset class: metals 1.09-1.11, crypto 1.05-1.07, FX 1.01-1.05, index 1.03. Daily SPX/NDQ 1999-2018 is mixed: L5 +0.30 [+0.15,+0.44], L3 +0.02 (n.s.).
concepts.engineNotes: Level (L317-347) and Ext (L365-373) have no twin or state fields. evaluate (L661-697), f_potModel (L1303-1312) and the live PoT (L2063-2067) cannot use the cue.

concepts.name: Own-path reach features: range burst and wick proximity
concepts.definition: vr = sma(TR, 3) / ATR14. States: calm < 0.8 (35% of bars), normal 0.8-1.25, burst > 1.25 (15%). Wick proximity = how much closer the last 3 bars' extreme came to the pool than the close.
concepts.dolRole: Large, always-available modulation of PoT and reachability. It explains most of what looked like an SMT sync effect.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B, about 430k intraday pool-bars: bursts are hit at 1.13x (H12) and 1.075x (H30) the distance x timeframe-matched rate, calm bars at 0.93x and 0.94x. Monotone in every distance bin: 1.5-2 ATR, H12: 38.7% calm vs 47.2% burst. Logit +0.16 to +0.35 per unit of vr; wick proximity +0.09 [+0.04,+0.15] per ATR with continuous distance terms. Single dataset with short samples, but large n and consistent across two horizons.
concepts.engineNotes: potSig = ta.stdev(chg, 50) (L916). The empirical surface sUp/sDn (L1061-1062) has rows only by HTF bias (bumped at L1531-1532, read by f_empPoT L1284-1300). The proximity reach (L665) uses the same sigma. Overlaps with the vol-clock proposals in quant_pot and ict_time (G1).

concepts.name: Inverse-correlation SMT (DXY vs EURUSD/GBPUSD)
concepts.definition: Mirror B (high_B' = -low_B, low_B' = -high_B) and apply the positive-correlation logic. The sign is manual or latched from rolling correlation (Auto). USDX = 50.14348112 x EURUSD^-0.576 x USDJPY^0.136 x GBPUSD^-0.119 x USDCAD^0.091 x USDSEK^0.042 x USDCHF^0.036.
concepts.dolRole: Lets FX charts use DXY as the sister. EUR is 57.6% of DXY, so GBPUSD or USDCHF carry more independent information.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The strong grade covers the ICE weights only. EURUSD-DXY rho -0.97 (Forex.com) is weak. B correction: the -0.93 'other vendor' figure is EURUSD vs the Broad trade-weighted dollar, not DXY (CONVEX: -0.82 / -0.905 / -0.918 for 2024-26). EURUSD-GBPUSD 60-day mean 0.79 (FXStreet). No predictive value is shown beyond the general SMT findings. DXY and spot FX keep different hours, so state must freeze on unaligned bars.
concepts.engineNotes: Proposal: sign-normalise the B feed once, latch the sign, and reset twins (sis := 0) when it re-latches.

concepts.name: Correlation regime gate
concepts.definition: rho = ta.correlation(log-return A, log-return B, 100) on time-aligned bars (bTr == time[1]). Live only when |rho| >= 0.5; a negative rho means inverse in Auto mode. Show rho and the % of aligned bars in the panel.
concepts.dolRole: Stops spurious sister states when the pair decouples, rolls, or has bad data.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's measured rho: ES-NQ 0.96-0.97; ES-YM 0.90-0.92; NQ-YM 0.81 (1h rolling p10 0.37); 6E-6B 0.86-0.90; MBT-MET 0.82-0.90. The GC/SI 1h file is broken through 2025 (rho about 0.1), showing why the gate is needed. B: correlations rise after down-trends and fall after up-trends (Karami/Bouchaud 2019, 84 futures) and drift over decades (Toth & Kertesz 2005).
concepts.engineNotes: Not present.

concepts.name: Raid-close classification (hold = continuation, reject = reversal)
concepts.definition: On a liquidity sweep: a close beyond the zone top is HOLD (+1); a close back inside is REJECT (-1). Accumulated by tier into liqEvt with a half-life and fed into D.
concepts.dolRole: Currently 30% of D (wL), so it influences side selection.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B correction: A called this the primary reversal signal (11-15 pp nextLiq gap), but that gap is geometric. In A's own events the geometry-neutral 1-ATR race gives reject 50.3-50.4%, hold 49.5-50.3%, mid 49.2-50.5%; logit reject-vs-mid +0.038 [-0.038,+0.113]. This agrees with ict_liq.final ICT-9 (neutral REJECT). The evidence is moderate AGAINST the reversal reading.
concepts.engineNotes: L1579-1582 (evt by close vs lv.top / lv.price), decay L1535, wL = 0.30 (L157), D at L1894. Fix through ICT-9; the SMT module must not rely on it.

concepts.name: SMT at key levels (PDH/PDL, sessions, HTF) and in killzones
concepts.definition: The same SMT test at previous-day, session or HTF extremes, with B's own range extremes as twins, optionally restricted to the London or NY AM killzones.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed to make the reversal read reliable at higher-timeframe liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: PDH/PDL (922 events): 1-ATR reversal SMT 44.0% vs joint 44.8%. 2-ATR race SMT 41.6% vs joint 59.2% (g = 0), 46.9% vs 50.3% (g = 1). Killzones, SMT vs joint: NY AM 44.3% vs 48.4% (CI [-8.6,+0.1]); London 51.0% vs 48.4%; Asia 49.7% vs 50.7%; NY PM 52.2% vs 51.1%.
concepts.engineNotes: f_rangeTrack (L807-833) and f_sessTrack (L835-859) track chart data only; f_kzAff (L597) has no SMT term and should get none. Key-range twins are needed only for correct sister states.

concepts.name: PSP (precision swing point)
concepts.definition: At a swing or sweep bar, the correlated assets' candles close in opposite colours; some versions add a pin-bar filter.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed one-candle reversal confirmation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: 1-ATR race 50.4% (PSP) vs 49.8% (no PSP), n = 6,039 / 41,481, CI [-1.4,+2.7] pp. Within SMT events: 49.8% vs 49.6%.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended.

concepts.name: Hidden SMT (close-based)
concepts.definition: SMT on closing prices instead of wicks: bearish when A's closes make a higher high and B's closes make a lower high (TradingFinder HSMT).
concepts.dolRole: Claimed reversal confirmation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor construct; no statistics found. Neither close-based raid classes nor wick SMT carry reversal information in A's data, and nothing suggests the close-based variant does better.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended.

concepts.name: FVG SMT ('SMT-Fill')
concepts.definition: Simultaneous FVGs on correlated assets: one asset touches or fills its gap while the twin does not (thomas-quant/SMT check_fvg_smt; SMT-Fill [Oracle] touch and full-fill variants).
concepts.dolRole: PD-array analogue of the sister state: which FVG gets delivered next. DukeSong reads it as continuation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Could reuse the SMT-2 twin machinery later. Not proposed until the ledger confirms the pool-level effect.

concepts.name: Triad SMT (one vs two sisters)
concepts.definition: ES/NQ/YM: track whether one or both sisters took their twins while the chart's pool is intact.
concepts.dolRole: Would be a stronger laggard cue.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's lifts (one sister 1.046, both 1.062, CIs overlapping) use A-style controls. B shows the single-sister fresh effect disappears under own-path controls, so the triad increment is unproven. Graded down from weak.
concepts.engineNotes: Dropped (it would need a second request).

concepts.name: Sync timing / lead-lag hazard
concepts.definition: After B leads, the number of bars until A trades through its pool, and the hazard by bar.
concepts.dolRole: An ETA readout for laggard targets only. B: not the decay of the incremental lift, which plateaus over 2-31 bars.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: within 1 / 6 / 12 / 30 bars: 5m 21/49/61/73%, 15m 22/51/61/73%, 1h 20/44/54/69%; never within 300 bars 9-11%; median given sync 5 bars (5m/15m) and 7 (1h). Descriptive only. Microstructure: Huth & Abergel find the leader predicts the lagger's next mid-quote 60-64% of the time, not tradable after spread; lead-lag is stronger for larger leader moves.
concepts.engineNotes: The engine has an ETA from ttHit/dHit (L1072-1075, L2116-2126) for DOL hits, with no cross-asset timing.

concepts.name: Continuous divergence measures (lag magnitude, pair residual, B overshoot)
concepts.definition: (A overshoot - B overshoot) in ATR at the sweep; the pair residual (B's 12-bar move minus A's, own-ATR units, signed toward the pool); B's distance beyond its twin.
concepts.dolRole: Would grade SMT strength or add a drift term.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: race1 flat across divergence quintiles (50.2-51.3%). B: pair residual +0.014 [-0.004,+0.031] logit; B overshoot +0.044 [-0.025,+0.114]. Genjutsu: the minimum-lag filter 'is not an edge filter'.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended beyond a de-clutter threshold for marks.

concepts.name: Dow-theory confirmation / pairs convergence (background)
concepts.definition: Correlated averages must confirm each other's highs (Dow). Matched pairs whose normalised prices diverge by more than 2 sigma tend to re-converge (pairs trading).
concepts.dolRole: Theory for why a lagging leg tends to catch up. The persistent sister-state tilt is consistent with it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B correction to A's 'strong': Brown, Goetzmann & Kumar 1998 test Hamilton's editorial calls (positive risk-adjusted returns 1902-29; Cowles 1934 disagreed), not the confirmation rule in isolation. Gatev et al. 2006: up to about 11% annualised for daily equity pairs 1962-2002 (strong for that setting). Do & Faff 2010: profitability declining through 2009. Neither tests intraday SMT.
concepts.engineNotes: Context only.

proposals.title: Condition the empirical PoT surface on the 3-bar range burst (the no-request part of 'laggard sync')
proposals.rationale: B's panel shows that most of A's sister-sync lift is the chart's own range burst and wick approach. That effect is large and available on every chart: bursts (TR3/ATR > 1.25) are hit at 1.13x (H12) and 1.075x (H30) the distance-matched rate, and calm bars at 0.93-0.94x. The engine's 50-bar sigma and bias-only surface cannot see it.
proposals.spec:
SERIES after L917: float vr = ta.sma(ta.tr(true), 3) / nz(atr, 1e-9); int vrS = vr < 0.8 ? 0 : vr <= 1.25 ? 1 : 2.
STATE L1061-1062: sUp/sDn become array.new<int>(9 * NB1, 0); row = biasRow * 3 + vrS.
ENGINE step 0 (L1527-1532): int vH = vrS[H]; f_bump(sUp, (bH + 1) * 3 + vH, ...) and f_bump(sDn, (1 - bH) * 3 + vH, ...).
f_empPoT (L1284), fallbacks: (1) use the row if n >= nMin; (2) else the bias-pooled surface x clamp(kv, 0.85, 1.20), where kv is the burst-state hit ratio, with priors [0.93, 1.00, 1.10] while data are thin; (3) else all rows.
Analytic fallback and proximity reach (L665, L1304): sig *= math.pow(f_clamp(vr, 0.5, 2.0), 0.35), a prior to refit.
Coordinate with the time-of-day vol clock (ict_time G1, quant_pot): condition on burst within the clock state to avoid double counting.
proposals.risk: Thinner surface rows during warm-up (handled by the fallback). Bursts partly coincide with session opens, so there is some double counting if the vol clock is added naively. It changes PoT on every chart, so it must be checked with the EDGE and Brier readouts.

proposals.title: Optional correlated-symbol feed (ticker.inherit), O(1) twins, correlation gate and sister state machine
proposals.rationale: Infrastructure for every intermarket feature. One request, non-repainting, off by default. B corrections to A's spec: ticker.inherit keeps session and back-adjustment aligned; the auto-pair keeps the chart's prefix and contract suffix (A's CME_MINI map broke MES/MNQ/MYM/M2K and single-contract charts); chart-swing twins become O(1) instead of a 450-step loop; open[1] is dropped.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_SMT, all display = display.none): smtOn = false; smtSymIn = input.symbol('') (empty default verified in an open-source v6 script); smtCorr Auto/Positive/Inverse; smtRhoMin = 0.5; smtW = 2; smtMode Sync / Display only / Reversal (ledger-gated).
Auto pair: f_smtRoot(syminfo.root) (ES<->NQ, YM/RTY->ES, MES<->MNQ, MYM/M2K->MES, GC<->SI, 6E<->6B). Ticker = syminfo.prefix (CBOT->CME swap for YM/MYM) + ':' + root + str.replace(syminfo.ticker, syminfo.root, ''); spot pairs via str.replace (BTC<->ETH, EURUSD<->GBPUSD).
Feed (SERIES after L982): smtTk = smtReq ? ticker.inherit(syminfo.tickerid, smtSym) : '' ('' = the chart symbol per request.md L212); [bHr, bLr, bCr, bTr] = request.security(smtTk, timeframe.period, [high[1], low[1], close[1], time[1]], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on, ignore_invalid_symbol = true); bAl = bTr == time[1].
Gate: rho = ta.correlation(rA, rB, 100) on aligned log returns; latch the sign; smtLive = bAl and |rho| >= smtRhoMin. Sign-normalise: bHn = sign < 0 ? -bLr : bHr, and the mirror for bLn.
Types: twin / sis / sisBar with defaults appended to Level (L347) and Ext (L373); the positional Ext.new at L1224 stays valid.
Chart-swing twins (global, O(1)): smtWE = min(smtW, pivLen - 2), twLen = 2 * smtWE + 1, twOff = pivLen - smtWE - 1; twHi = ta.highest(bAl ? bHn : -1e10, twLen)[twOff]; twOk = math.sum(bAl ? 1 : 0, twLen)[twOff] == twLen; postHi = ta.highest(bAl ? bHn : -1e10, twOff). Set at L1761 / L1773.
MTF pivots and key ranges: f_twinState loop (cap 450, at birth only) and f_rangeLag (fold the shifted B bar into the old period, then emit). Extend f_pushExt (L1211) and the registry re-entry copy (L1846-1851).
Step 3a before L1558 (and step 4 for extReg): if smtLive and sis == 1 and B crosses the twin, set sis := 2 and sisBar := bar_index - 1. On smtFlip, set sis := 0 everywhere.
Chart-led sweep at L1579: push Pend{side, twin, bar, close, atr}; resolve as joint or SMT on the next confirmed bar.
proposals.risk: Auto pairs can miss on exotic feeds (show 'SMT: no data'; the user can override). Pairs with different hours freeze the state; show the % of aligned bars. Small per-bar cost of about 2 x pool comparisons.

proposals.title: Sister ledger calibrated against the engine's own PoT (fresh and persistent buckets), plus SMT-vs-joint reversal race
proposals.rationale: The cross-asset effect is small (Δlogit about +0.08) and chart-specific, so it must be learned live and shown honestly. B correction: calibrate against f_potModel (the model the shift corrects), not f_potBase, otherwise drift and regime credit leak into the SMT shift. Separate buckets because the fresh effect is zero once the own-path burst term exists.
proposals.spec:
Records: when an intact pool or registry entry with 0.25 < d <= maxATR reaches sister age 0 (bucket F) and age 2 (bucket P), push SisT{lvId, side, edge, bar0, pM = f_potModel(d, side, potMu * side), bkt}; cap 64 open records. Resolve on hit (side == 1 ? high > edge : low < edge) or after H bars; book n_b, K_b, P_b in var array<float> smtSt(12).
f_sisBeta(b, prior) = clamp(logit((K + 50 * pp) / (n + 50)) - logit(P / n), -0.2, 0.3), with pp = sigm(logit(P / n) + prior). Priors: P bucket +0.08; F bucket 0 when smt-ownpath-burst is on, else +0.10.
Race arms: each resolved Pend starts a 1-ATR race from the decision close; book reversal wins and n per arm (SMT, joint); z-score with the 2H-block cluster variance from f_book (L1463-1469).
Place after f_book (about L1500), which follows f_potModel (L1303).
Panel: 'SYNC P Δ+0.08 (n 212, z 1.1) · SMT-REV 49% (n 120) vs JOINT 51% (n 180)'.
proposals.risk: Small n on higher timeframes (hence the 50-record prior). Overlapping records share price paths (hence the clustered variance).

proposals.title: Small persistent PoT logit shift and near-tie score multiplier for sister-swept pools (ages 2-31 bars)
proposals.rationale: The only cross-asset effect that survives own-path controls and a placebo: Δlogit +0.078 [+0.023,+0.133] (L3/H12) and +0.085 [+0.007,+0.163] (L5/H30), lift about 1.04, rising to its peak at 8-15 bars and fading after about 32. A's 8-bar half-life decay from the sweep bar has the wrong shape (the effect is about 0 at age 0-1).
proposals.spec:
f_sisW(age) = age <= 31 ? 1.0 : age <= 47 ? (47 - age) / 16 : 0; bucket F (age < 2) uses f_sisBeta(0, freshPrior), bucket P uses f_sisBeta(1, 0.08).
PoT (after L2067): if smtOn and smtMode != 'Display only' and activeLv.sis == 2 and not sweptNow, then activePoT := min(0.95, f_sigm(f_logit(clamp(activePoT, 0.01, 0.99)) + beta * f_sisW(age))).
Score (step 17, L1938-1948): for liquidity pools with sis == 2, lv.mult *= clamp(1 + 0.5 * beta * f_sisW(age), 0.95, 1.10), about x1.04 at beta = 0.08.
No change to D.
proposals.risk: The effect is near the noise floor and can be swamped by other pillars, which is acceptable. The ledger shrinks it to 0 on charts where it does not hold. Bad data pairs can fake states (mitigated by the correlation gate and ticker.inherit).

proposals.title: Keep SMT out of D and the raid classification; strict ledger-gated ICT reversal option
proposals.rationale: Prevents a popular but unsupported rule from degrading D. SMT minus joint race CI [-2.8,+0.7] pp (Pine timing); B's geometry controls remove the nextLiq tilt; Genjutsu found 0 of 88 tests beyond chance. The engine's REJECT = reversal mapping is itself unsupported (about 50% for every class), so coordinate with ICT-9.
proposals.spec:
Sync mode (default): a chart-led SMT never touches liqEvt (L1579-1582) or D (L1892-1895).
'Reversal (ledger-gated)' mode: at Pend resolution add evt = -side * tier * 0.5 to liqEvt only if SMT-REV minus JOINT-REV > 0 with z >= 2.5, n >= 100 per arm, and the same sign in both halves of the record history. Otherwise the panel says 'ICT reversal: not supported on this chart (z = …, n …)'.
proposals.risk: Users expect 'SMT = reversal'; the tooltip and panel must explain the reason in one line.

proposals.title: SMT alerts, Clean label tag, Terminal rows and optional marks with honest wording
proposals.rationale: Surfaces the intermarket events traders look for without cluttering the Clean look, and without implying a reversal edge the data does not support.
proposals.spec:
Two alertconditions after L2093, plus alert() calls at bar close:
- 'SMT · Sister Took Liquidity' (a draw-side or active pool turns sis = 2; the message includes the ETA and the PoT shift in pp);
- 'SMT · Divergence at Sweep' (a Pend resolves as SMT; the message includes this chart's SMT-REV vs JOINT-REV rates).
Never write 'reversal expected'.
Clean style: '· SMT↻' suffix on the DOL label (L2225) when activeLv.sis == 2, plus a tooltip line.
Terminal style: row 'SMT NQ1! ρ .96 · 98% aligned · ▲LAG BSL 1.2ATR · ETA 5b', plus the ledger row.
Marks: at most 12 in a FIFO like f_ghost (L1253); off by default in Clean.
proposals.risk: Clutter and the 500 line / 500 label caps.

proposals.title: Exact interval matching for key-range twins (PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL, sessions)
proposals.rationale: Pairs with different hours (FX vs DXY, crypto vs CME) misalign day and session ranges. Exact matching keeps the highest-tier pools' sister states correct. It adds no new signal (key-level SMT has no reversal edge).
proposals.spec: Optional toggle. Add B's time and time_close (or session flags) to the smt-core tuple, still one request. Emit B's range twin via f_rangeLag only when B's interval boundaries equal the chart's; otherwise twin = na and sis = 0.
proposals.risk: Extra complexity for a minority of pairs.

proposals.title: Sync ETA readout from the live sister-to-chart hazard
proposals.rationale: Answers WHEN for laggard targets. Descriptive: 20-22% sync within 1 bar, about 50% within 6, median 5 bars (5m/15m) and 7 (1h). B correction: do not use it as the decay of the PoT shift.
proposals.spec: Record the bars from sisBar to the chart's own sweep for synced pools in an array capped at 300 (like ttHit, L1072). ETA = median; prior 5 bars intraday and 7 on 1h while n < 30. Show 'sync ETA ~5b' in the HUD and tooltip.
proposals.risk: Right-censoring biases the ETA short; minor for an indicative readout.

result.summary:
1. The engine's EV readout (2245 and 2359, `invWin·RR − (1 − invWin)`) is a geometric artefact. It reads 0 for near targets and −0.34R to −0.97R for far ones in a fair market, and its correlation with realized R is +0.02 on 163k records. [A✓]
2. [B-fix] A's TM-1 fix would have put a smaller version of the bias back. It used the breakeven win rate BE = r/(r+d) as the ledger's race baseline, but the ledger only counts races decided within H, and those sit 2.1 pp (5-min) and 1.9 pp (1h) below BE. The HUD would then show −0.05R to −0.07R for R:R > 1 while realized R is about 0. The corrected TM-1 keeps the driftless conditional race as the baseline, shows BE beside it, and replaces the EV with the ledger's measured average R (R̄) and its standard error.
3. [B-new] On 61.8k paired 5-min records with the real 1-minute path, no management rule moved mean R by more than 0.01R: break-even after +1R, break-even at half-way, partials, a 1R trailing stop, or fixed shadow stops from 0.5 to 3 ATR. They only cut the spread of R by 8-26%. This agrees with optional stopping, Carr & López de Prado (no optimal profit-take/stop pair under a random walk; optimising one is overfitting), Glynn & Iglehart (trailing stops) and Shiryaev-Xu-Zhou (no optimal time stop).
4. [B-new] Trailing stops look profitable on OHLC bars only because of the assumed intrabar path: +0.016R (3.2 SE) on the same 5-min data with the engine's path, against +0.001R on the real path. The Pine ledger may grade fixed-level rules only, never trailing ones.
5. [B-new] After the opposing level is taken first, the target is still reached 21-23% of the time, exactly what geometry predicts from the new distance. The plan status should read "STOPPED · target PoT x%", not "draw failed".
6. [B-new] Costs matter intraday. With $4.50 per round turn plus 1 tick, the engine's 5-min stop costs a median 0.027R per trade (0.087R at a 0.5 ATR stop) and turns mean R from −0.002 to −0.05. New TM-8 adds cost-adjusted breakeven, (1 + c)/(1 + RR), and position size from syminfo.pointvalue.
7. [B-new] The engine's intrabar rule (bull bar O-L-H-C) matches the optimum for a random-walk bar: 0.887 correct vs 0.806 for TradingView's rule, the same as A's real-data result. It always assumes the shorter path, and no rule using only open, high, low and close does better. Keep it.
8. [B-fix] A said obstacles add nothing beyond distance. That holds for inner same-side pools, but untouched opposing FVGs cost −0.5 to −3 pp, in line with sibling proposal ICT-5. TM-3 shows obstacles as TP1 candidates; ICT-5 keeps the small penalty.
9. [B-fix] A's TM-2 showed plan statuses that can never appear on a live trial, and it failed when the ledger is off. It is re-specified with an always-open trial carrying a `graded` flag, a window counter and a shared bar-race helper.
10. [B-fix] The stop is not always a pool: it can be an array (often the trader's own entry zone), the execution swing or a 1.5 ATR fallback. TM-7 labels it by source.
11. Mechanical sweep → MSS → FVG entries show no edge over geometry, and the limit-fill formula d/(d+e) is calibrated. Pre-commitment evidence is now moderate (Fischbacher et al. 2017, Richards et al. 2017).
12. Eight proposals, best first: TM-1, TM-2, TM-7, TM-8, TM-5, TM-3, TM-4, TM-6.

concepts.name: R-multiple, expectancy, SQN, profit factor
concepts.definition: R = side·(exit−entry)/|entry−stop|. Expectancy = mean R; SQN = √N·mean/sd; PF = gross win R / gross loss R. A time-out is marked to market at H. The spread of R grows with R:R (sd 0.73 / 1.11 / 1.52 / 2.40 for R:R ≤1 / 1-2 / 2-4 / >4 at 5-min), so a ±0.1R standard error needs about 50-580 independent trades.
concepts.dolRole: The common unit for comparing targets at different distances. A ledger average R with a standard error is the only honest per-chart expectancy.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Tharp definitions. A: realized R −0.008 (5-min) / −0.001 (1h). B2: −0.002 / +0.001 with cluster standard errors 0.006.
concepts.engineNotes: rOut 1457-1458 and raceSt 1489-1498. Average R and PF are shown in the Full view only (2419-2426), with no standard error, no drift adjustment and no R:R split.

concepts.name: Breakeven win rate and the martingale identity
concepts.definition: BE = 1/(1+RR). For an eventually decided driftless martingale race, P(target first) = r/(r+d) = BE exactly. Among races decided within H the nearer barrier is favoured: decided races ran 2.1 pp (5-min) and 1.9 pp (1h) below BE.
concepts.dolRole: Answers whether the target is worth trading (WIN vs BE). It is the wrong null for a ledger that only counts races decided within H.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Optional stopping theorem; quant_pot 1.3. B1 on A's records: wins − BE = −0.021 / −0.019, while wins − driftless conditional = −0.006.
concepts.engineNotes: BE is not shown anywhere.

concepts.name: Two-barrier race with horizon (triple barrier)
concepts.definition: Target near edge = upper barrier, invalidation = lower, H bars = vertical. pW = f_raceH(d,r,σ,0,H) and pL likewise. WIN≤H = pW/(pW+pL) is conditional on a decision within H. Brownian motion over-predicts P(decided) (0.84-0.87 vs 0.80 observed).
concepts.dolRole: The literal 'which liquidity first' answer and the ledger's grading unit.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Brownian first-passage maths, Monte-Carlo verified. The driftless version has better log-loss: 0.568 vs 0.582 (5-min), 0.577 vs 0.593 (1h).
concepts.engineNotes: f_race/f_raceH 447-482 are correct. f_invalidation 1359-1364 injects drift potMu·side (917) and is recomputed from the live close every tick (2127).

concepts.name: Optional stopping: brackets cannot create expectancy
concepts.definition: For a martingale and a bounded stopping time, E[X_τ] = X₀. Every stop, target, partial, break-even, trailing or time stop has E[R] = 0 before costs. Kaminski & Lo's negative stopping premium is relative to holding an asset with a positive premium (stopping into bonds).
concepts.dolRole: Edge can only come from target selection or race information, never from exit mechanics. This defines what the ledger must measure.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kaminski & Lo 2014; Lo & Remorov 2017; Carr & López de Prado 2014; Glynn & Iglehart 1995; Shiryaev-Xu-Zhou 2008. B2: every management rule within ±0.01R on 61.8k / 110k paired records.
concepts.engineNotes: The EV readout at 2245 and 2359 implies that geometry determines expectancy.

concepts.name: Displayed EV formula
concepts.definition: Engine: EV = invWin·RR − (1−invWin), with invWin the conditional race after f_raceAdj.
concepts.dolRole: Supposed to tell the trader whether the trade is worth taking.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A T2: reads 0 to −0.97R in a fair market. A T4-B: correlation with realized R +0.02. B1: even with a corrected baseline, an intercept-only shift has correlation about 0 with realized R, so the EV cell should show measured R̄ ± SE.
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 2245-2246 and 2359-2363. The panel colours EV > 0.2 green, so far targets are always red. Fix in TM-1.

concepts.name: Ledger race baseline (f_raceAdj null)
concepts.definition: The probability stored as pRace at trial open is the null that the logit shift learns against. For races decided within H the correct null is the driftless conditional pW/(pW+pL), not BE.
concepts.dolRole: Decides whether the learned 'race edge' is real or a conditioning artefact.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B1: logit shift −0.089 / −0.078 with BE as the null (spurious EV −0.05 to −0.07R) vs −0.025 / −0.026 with the driftless conditional. The latter is the strict trade-through rule.
concepts.engineNotes: pRace at 1430 is the drift conditional. Switch it to the driftless conditional, not to BE.

concepts.name: Invalidation = nearest opposing level (race barrier)
concepts.definition: Just beyond the nearest pool-list level with side = −target side: a liquidity zone, or the far edge of any FVG/OB/breaker, including draw-aligned entry arrays. Buffer 0.1 ATR, within maxATR. Fallbacks: execution swing, then 1.5 ATR. Risk floor 0.25 ATR.
concepts.dolRole: Defines plan failure: the opposing level traded before the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A T3: once a pool is swept, a stop 0.3 ATR beyond it is hit 64-70% of the time on the sweep bar and 92-95% within 12-30 bars (random levels 57-62% / 90-93%). Median risk 1.53-1.77 ATR; fallback in 5-7% of cases.
concepts.engineNotes: f_invalidation 1343-1358. The label is always '⊗ INVALIDATION' (2212) whatever the source, and the source is not returned. The distance gate uses atr while ejection uses atrE (1350).

concepts.name: Sweep penetration depth and buffers
concepts.definition: Maximum excursion beyond the level after the first trade-through, in ATR. Rejected = the bar closes back inside; accepted = it closes beyond.
concepts.dolRole: No affordable buffer survives a sweep, so the stop is a race barrier.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Median depth 0.43 / 0.60 ATR on the sweep bar and 2.84 / 2.87 ATR within 30 bars. Pools close back inside less often than random levels (44.9 vs 52.7%), consistent with Osler 2005 cascades (+0.27 to 2.35 hundredths of a percent).
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed zoneATR 0.2 (93) plus a 0.1 ATR buffer (1344).

concepts.name: Post-raid stop (beyond the sweep extreme)
concepts.definition: After the opposing pool is raided and the bar closes back inside, the stop goes beyond the raid extreme, which is extended for up to raidWin bars.
concepts.dolRole: The ICT trader's stop. It changes R:R, not the odds.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A T4-A: win minus model +1.2 pp (SE 1.9) on 5-min and −2.7 pp (SE 1.5) on 1h. Rejected-sweep wicks are exceeded later 76-82% of the time, as for random levels. GBB: best variant, still unprofitable.
concepts.engineNotes: The raid event at 1579-1582 does not store its extreme.

concepts.name: Protected-swing stop
concepts.definition: Stop beyond the strong extreme of the current structural leg.
concepts.dolRole: The SMC risk anchor.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional only; ict_struct found weak-before-protected odds follow geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: exeProtL/H are returned at 925 but unused. Only exeRL/RH serve as a fallback (1354). See ICTS-5.

concepts.name: Sweep → MSS → FVG entry model
concepts.definition: An unswept pivot(5) pool is traded through and the bar closes back inside. MSS = a close beyond the last fractal(1) within 12 bars. Entry = limit at the last FVG formed in [s+2, m+1], valid 20 bars. Stop at the sweep extreme, the FVG far edge or the engine rule. Target = nearest opposing pool; H = 30.
concepts.dolRole: How ICT traders execute toward a DOL. It does not improve which-liquidity-next prediction.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: 853 / 1,124 setups, win within ±3 pp of the model and a random-entry null, mean R −0.06 to +0.05. GBB (2 ticks + $4.50): Silver Bullet hours not special, no variant profitable. 25,000-variant study: 1.7% survived (about what multiple testing alone leaves). Other public numbers are A's and were not re-opened.
concepts.engineNotes: Components exist (raids 1579-1582, BOS 1542-1547, FVG 1867-1889). Correctly not used as a score bonus.

concepts.name: iFVG continuation retest
concepts.definition: An FVG inverted by a body close beyond its far edge. Enter on the retest with a hold; stop beyond the iFVG; target internal liquidity, then the DOL.
concepts.dolRole: A continuation entry toward the DOL.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published statistics. ict_pd found broken gaps hold on retest about as often as random zones.
concepts.engineNotes: iFVGs are drawn (1598-1644) but never offered as entry zones.

concepts.name: Breaker retest / Unicorn
concepts.definition: Breaker = an OB whose leg swept liquidity and was then broken. Unicorn = breaker overlapping a same-direction FVG. Entry in the overlap, stop beyond the breaker.
concepts.dolRole: Entry inventory behind price.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner descriptions only.
concepts.engineNotes: Breakers exist as targets only (1646-1661).

concepts.name: Limit-entry fill probability and limit-order risks
concepts.definition: P(fill before target) = d/(d+e). Given a fill, P(target before stop) = 1/(1+RR_zone) with RR_zone = (d+e)/(r−e). The risks are non-execution and adverse execution (Handa & Schwartz 1996; Linnainmaa 2010).
concepts.dolRole: The trade-off between a better R:R and missing the move to the DOL.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A T4-A: fill 0.696 vs 0.735 (5-min), 0.752 vs 0.774 (1h); win given fill with the FVG stop 0.195 vs 0.181 model and 0.170 vs 0.189. No measurable adverse selection.
concepts.engineNotes: No entry-zone concept. f_invalidation often selects the would-be entry zone itself as the 'opposing' level, because a bullish array below price has side −1.

concepts.name: Partials, break-even and trailing stops
concepts.definition: Take 50% at TP1 (first obstacle or half-way) and move the stop to entry for the runner. Break-even after +1R; trail 1R behind the peak after +1R.
concepts.dolRole: Variance management on the path to the DOL. EV-neutral.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2 paired, 5-min real path: BE after +1R −0.008 (SE 0.003); BE at half-way −0.003; partial −0.004; trail +0.001; sd 1.42 → 1.05-1.31. 1h: +0.003 to +0.004. A's +0.107R partial (n = 226) did not replicate. Trailing gains appear only on the OHLC pseudo-path (+0.016 / +0.035).
concepts.engineNotes: No TP1 and no partial accounting. A Pine ledger can grade fixed-level rules only.

concepts.name: Next obstacles (path map)
concepts.definition: Pool levels on the target's side nearer than the target: inner same-side pools and opposite-polarity arrays (for a buy-side target, bearish FVG/OB/breakers above price), plus volume walls.
concepts.dolRole: Natural TP1 points and stall zones. Opposing untouched FVGs slightly lower reach.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Inner pools: residual −0.018 vs −0.019 (no effect). Opposing untouched FVG: −1.7 pp (5-min, 1.4 SE) and −0.5 pp (1h) in A's race test; −2 to −3 pp of reach in 11 of 12 datasets (ict_liq B5).
concepts.engineNotes: Inner pools ×0.70 as targets (684-685, 1240-1248); f_pathVol multiplier (1945-1947). No opposing-FVG path cost (ICT-5); obstacles are never listed.

concepts.name: MAE / MFE and MAE-based stops
concepts.definition: MAE = maximum adverse excursion before exit; MFE = maximum favourable. Sweeney-style rules put the stop at p90-p95 of winners' MAE. That is circular, because winners are the trades the stop did not take.
concepts.dolRole: Describes the path to the DOL. The honest stop test is the unconditional shadow-stop curve.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner only. A, engine stop: winners' MAE p50/p80/p90 = 0.27/0.60/0.76R. SKEP-1: hits-only heat is about half the all-record p80.
concepts.engineNotes: t.mae 1442-1443 and the p80 'heat' (2404-2408) are hits-only, in ATR, and include post-stop excursions. No MFE.

concepts.name: Stop-distance expectancy curve (shadow stops)
concepts.definition: For stop s in ATR: R = −1 if MAE ≥ s before the target; d0/s if the target was hit; MTM/s otherwise. Exact from per-trial MAE, d0 and the MTM at H.
concepts.dolRole: A per-chart, overfitting-guarded answer to stop placement. A departure from flat would be a selection edge.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2: s = 0.5-3 ATR all within ±0.01R (5-min +0.009 / −0.002 / −0.004 / −0.003 / −0.005); after costs 0.5 ATR gives −0.12R. Carr & López de Prado: optimising the mesh on a random walk is overfitting.
concepts.engineNotes: t.mae and t.d0 exist; the MTM at H is not stored.

concepts.name: Time stop, time left and race duration
concepts.definition: Vertical barrier H; time left = H − (bar_index − bar0). Closed-form driftless durations: E[τ] = dr/σ², E[τ|target first] = d(d+2r)/(3σ²), E[τ|stop first] = r(r+2d)/(3σ²).
concepts.dolRole: Timing of the plan; how much of the forecast horizon is left.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: time exits at 5/10/20 bars changed R by −0.012 to +0.004. No interior optimal sell time (Shiryaev-Xu-Zhou). B3 Monte Carlo confirms the formulas. B2: median decided race 4.8-5.3 bars; 58-62% resolved within 10 bars.
concepts.engineNotes: Grading window 1455-1456; consecutive windows 2038-2045. The live PoT is a rolling H window (2067), and time left is not shown.

concepts.name: ETA (time to touch)
concepts.definition: Engine: median bars-to-hit of past hits whose activation distance was within ±0.5 ATR of the current distance (n ≥ 5).
concepts.dolRole: Timing of the draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: quant_pot: constant-σ ETA rank-correlation −0.09, volatility-time +0.11 to +0.22. SKEP-1: hits-only ETA is 2-3× optimistic.
concepts.engineNotes: 2116-2126, HUD 2240. Owned by QPOT-06 / SKEP-1 / UX-4.

concepts.name: Intrabar path rule for double touches
concepts.definition: Engine: bull bar O-L-H-C, bear bar O-H-L-C (the shortest-path rule, since len(OLHC) − len(OHLC) = 2(O−C)); a gap is settled at the open. TradingView emulator: open nearer the high → O-H-L-C.
concepts.dolRole: Decides the race label when both barriers fall inside one bar.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A on 1-minute truth: 88.1-88.7% vs 80.6-80.7%. B3 random-walk bars: 0.887 vs 0.806. A 10×10 Bayes rule on the open and close positions gets 0.884, so it is the optimum for OHLC data.
concepts.engineNotes: f_step 1438-1441. Keep; lower-timeframe resolution is not worth a request.

concepts.name: Hit-rule asymmetry
concepts.definition: The target needs a trade-through for liquidity (strict >); the stop triggers on touch (≤). This matches limit-exit versus stop-order fills.
concepts.dolRole: Realistic fills; costs about 0.6 pp of race win.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B1: driftless conditional residual −0.6 pp; f_raceAdj absorbs it (logit −0.025).

concepts.name: Frozen trade plan and pre-commitment
concepts.definition: Entry reference, stop, target, R:R, BE and window frozen at activation (the open Trial), shown with live progress, heat, time left and status. Only OPEN and STOPPED can appear on a live trial.
concepts.dolRole: Makes the graded forecast visible and stable.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Fischbacher, Hoffmann & Schudy 2017 RFS: automatic stops causally reduce the disposition effect. Richards et al. 2017 EJF (field). Odean 1998: PGR 0.148 vs PLR 0.098. The chart-UX effect itself is untested.
concepts.engineNotes: The ledger freezes the bracket at 1426-1431 but the HUD re-runs f_invalidation each tick (2127). Trials open only if accView != Off or useCal (2038).

concepts.name: Post-stop target odds
concepts.definition: P(target reached later | opposing level hit first) over the rest of the window, compared with the one-barrier touch probability from the stop price.
concepts.dolRole: The correct wording after a stop-out: target still live with geometric odds, not 'draw failed'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2: 0.228 vs 0.208 predicted (5-min), 0.212 vs 0.215 (1h); a fresh H window 0.278 vs 0.256 and 0.267 vs 0.267.
concepts.engineNotes: No status display. The trial keeps running after race = −1 (correct).

concepts.name: Costs, cost-adjusted breakeven and position size
concepts.definition: c = round-trip cost / risk. BE_net = (1+c)/(1+RR) and E[R]_net = E[R] − c. Size = cash at risk / (risk × syminfo.pointvalue).
concepts.dolRole: An honest breakeven for near, tight-stop plans, and a usable size.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2 with $4.50 + 1 tick: 5-min median 0.027R (p90 0.11R), 0.087R at 0.5 ATR; 1h 0.009R. ES all-in $2.80-5.76 per round turn (2026 fee schedules). Lo & Remorov: costs are why tight stops lose.
concepts.engineNotes: syminfo.mintick and syminfo.pointvalue (simple float) are available.

concepts.name: Actionable alerts with a plan payload
concepts.definition: Events: new plan, entry zone tapped, TP1, plan stopped, target reached, window rolled. Payload: stop and its source, R:R, BE (net), WIN, R̄ ± SE, PoT(left), bars left, zone and fill probability, size. alertcondition needs const messages with {{plot()}} placeholders.
concepts.dolRole: Lets the trader manage the plan without watching the chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner conventions. Platform facts verified: more than 15 alerts in 3 minutes halts alerts (faq/alerts.md:201); const message for alertcondition (concepts/alerts.md:266).
concepts.engineNotes: 2077-2093: new target / iFVG / sweep / flip carry only tag, price, score and PoT.

concepts.name: Meta-labelling (learned trade filter)
concepts.definition: A secondary model learns P(the primary bracket wins) from features.
concepts.dolRole: Turns ledger outcomes into context-aware race probabilities.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Method reference (AFML ch. 3); feature learning belongs to calib_ml.
concepts.engineNotes: f_raceAdj 1367-1371 is the intercept-only version; its baseline should be the driftless conditional race.

concepts.name: Kelly sizing
concepts.dolRole: None for forecasting. With p from geometry, f* = 0.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kelly maths. A ledger p without confidence intervals invites over-sizing.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended; TM-8 sizes by cash risk only.

concepts.name: ICT standard-deviation projections
concepts.definition: Extend the manipulation leg by −2 to −2.5 of its range as exhaustion or partial targets. It is a measured move, not a statistic.
concepts.dolRole: Practitioner partial targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: LuxAlgo and community notes; no statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Not proposed; COMP-12 covers a liquidity ladder.

proposals.title: Honest race economics: driftless conditional race, breakeven, measured R̄ ± SE instead of model EV
proposals.rationale: The engine's EV is a geometric artefact: 0 to −0.97R in a fair market, correlation +0.02 with realized R. A's fix (BE as the ledger baseline) still showed −0.05R to −0.07R for R:R > 1 where realized R is about 0, because races decided within H sit 2 pp below BE (B1). An intercept-only shift cannot predict R. Drift costs 2.4-3.6% log-loss (QPOT-01/02). The honest numbers are the calibrated conditional race, geometric BE, and the ledger's model-free average R with its standard error.
proposals.spec:
1. f_invalidation (1343-1364): set mu = 0. Loop `for [i, lv] in pool` and record `src` (0 liquidity, 1 array, 2 exec swing, 3 ATR fallback) and `oppI`. Compute pW = f_raceH(d,risk,sg,0,H), pL = f_raceH(risk,d,sg,0,H), pC = pW+pL > 1e-9 ? pW/(pW+pL) : risk/(d+risk). Return [inv, d/risk, pC, src, oppI]. This is shared with TM-7 and ICTS-3. Call sites: 1428 `[inv, rr, pR, iSrc, iOpp]`; 2127 `[i0, i1, i2, i3, i4]`.
2. f_openTrial keeps pRace = pR, now the driftless conditional. Never store BE as the baseline.
3. raceSt grows from 7 to 9 entries: [7] = Σp(1−p) over decided races; [8] = ΣrOut².
4. Last bar: invWin = f_raceAdj(i2); invBE = 1/(1+i1); mR = raceSt[3]/raceSt[4]; seR = sqrt(max(0, raceSt[8]/n − mR²)/n · max(1, deff)), with deff = vEdge/vInd moved out of the panel (2386-2388). Show rBar only if seR ≤ 0.15R; otherwise 'R̄ — (n x, SE y)'. Replace with SKEP-4's drift-adjusted cluster R̄ when available.
5. HUD 2244-2246: 'R:R 1.6 · BE 38% · WIN≤H 39%' / 'R̄ +0.03R ±0.05 (n 212)'. Panel 2357-2363: col1 'RR · BE', col2 'WIN≤H', col3 'R̄ ±SE', coloured only when |R̄| > 2 SE. Gate the HUD and panel the same way (showInv).
6. Full RACE row: EDGE = 100·(wins − Σp)/n pp and z = (wins − Σp)/sqrt(raceSt[7]); keep PF.
7. Tooltip explaining BE, WIN≤H and R̄.
proposals.risk: R̄ shows '—' for a long time (100-500 trials before SE ≤ 0.15R). Raw R̄ carries trend beta (GC 1h +0.31R) until SKEP-4's Wald adjustment. Old raceSt sums are stale after the semantics change (they reset on reload). Must ship with QPOT-01/02 and coordinate the tuple change with ICTS-3 and TM-7.

proposals.title: Frozen trade plan from an always-open trial: progress, heat, time left, honest OPEN/STOPPED status
proposals.rationale: The HUD recomputes R:R/WIN/EV from the live close each tick (2127) while the ledger grades a bracket frozen at activation (1426-1431). The numbers jump and describe no trade taken. Pre-commitment devices causally reduce the disposition effect (Fischbacher et al. 2017; Richards et al. 2017). B fixes A's spec: (a) target-first and window-ended are booked and replaced on the same bar, so only OPEN and STOPPED exist on a live trial; (b) trials do not exist when accView is Off and useCal is false; (c) after a stop-out the target is still hit 21-23% of the time, exactly the geometric rate, so the wording is 'STOPPED · target still x%', not 'draw failed'.
proposals.spec:
1. Trial gets `bool graded = true`. At 2038 always open a trial for activeLv (drop the accView/useCal condition from opening), with graded = (accView != 'Off' or useCal) and warmup passed. Step 2 (1554-1556): if f_step(t) != 0 → if t.graded → f_book(t); then remove.
2. STATE `var int planWin = 1`. In step 2, when booking t.lvId == activeId and status == 3: planWin += 1. At 2031-2035, when pickId != activeId: planWin := 1 (global engine scope).
3. Last bar: find aT in openT with lvId == activeId. prog = side·(close − entry)/risk; heatR = max(mae·atr0, live-bar excursion)/risk; used = bar_index − bar0; left = max(0, H − used); pLeft = activePoT·f_pot(dNow,σ,0,max(left,1))/max(f_pot(dNow,σ,0,H),1e-6) (f_pot at 434, capped at 0.95).
4. Status: race 0 → 'PLAN w{planWin}'; race −1 → '✕ STOPPED · target still {pLeft}% in {left}b'. Reached and expired outcomes are shown by the ghost / COMP-5 stamp.
5. Terminal HUD: 'PLAN w1 · ref … · stop … (TM-7 tag) · R:R 1.8 · BE 36%' / 'NOW +0.42R · heat 0.31R · 18/30b · PoT(left) 41%'. Clean only via cleanPlan (default false), in the tooltip, never a third label line.
6. Dotted plan reference and plan stop lines from f_x(aT.bar0) to xR; they replace the live invalidation line at 2210-2213.
7. Global `var float planStopOut, planRROut`, updated on confirmed bars and plotted with display.data_window as 'DOL Plan Stop' and 'DOL Plan R:R'.
8. Factor f_step's hit/stop/advFirst logic (1436-1441) into a pure helper f_barRace(side, edge, inv, liq, entry), reused by TM-3, TM-4 and TM-5.
proposals.risk: Two R:R values (plan vs from here) can confuse: show the plan, put the from-here value in the tooltip. Small CPU cost for trials when the ledger is off. Status semantics must reuse f_barRace exactly.

proposals.title: Invalidation semantics: label by source, optional post-raid-extreme and protected-swing modes
proposals.rationale: The stop is a race barrier: once a pool is swept, a stop 0.3 ATR beyond it is hit 64-70% of the time on that bar and 92-95% within 12-30 bars. Its source varies: a pool, an array (often the trader's own entry FVG/OB, since bullish arrays below price have side −1), the exec swing or 1.5 ATR. The single '⊗ INVALIDATION' label (2212) hides this. A post-raid stop matches ICT practice and keeps geometric odds (A T4-A within ±3 pp).
proposals.spec:
1. Use TM-1's i3 (src) and i4 (oppI): label '⊗ OPP. ' + f_shortName(...) for liquidity, '⊗ BEYOND ' + name for arrays, '⊗ EXEC SWING', '⊗ 1.5 ATR'. Tooltip: 'If price trades here first the plan is stopped; once a pool is swept a stop this close is taken ~9 in 10 times, and the target is still reached ~1 in 5 afterwards.'
2. Input invMode = ['Opposing Level', 'Post-Raid Extreme', 'Protected Swing'] (display.none), shared with ICTS-5.
3. STATE before f_invalidation: var float raidX, var int raidSide, var int raidBar. In step 3 (1579-1582, global scope), on a liquidity hit that closes back inside (evt == −lv.side): raidSide := lv.side, raidX := bar extreme, raidBar := bar_index. Extend raidX while bar_index − raidBar ≤ raidWin (input, default 20).
4. f_invalidation: Post-Raid mode with raidSide == −tgt.side, a recent raid and raidX beyond close → inv = raidX − side·buf, src = 4. Protected Swing → exeProtL/H, src = 5.
5. Store the mode on the Trial so race and R̄ stats can be split per mode.
proposals.risk: Changing the mode shifts R:R and the ledger stats (reset or split by mode). Wider stops show lower R:R, which is honest.

proposals.title: Cost-aware breakeven and position size
proposals.rationale: On 5-min CME futures the engine stop pays a median 0.027R per trade in costs ($4.50 RT + 1 tick; p90 0.11R), 0.087R at 0.5 ATR stops. Net mean R moves from −0.002 to −0.05 (B2). Lo & Remorov: costs are why tight stops lose. A gross BE flatters near, tight-stop plans. Traders also need the size for their cash risk, which syminfo.pointvalue makes exact.
proposals.spec:
1. Inputs (G_DOL, display.none): costTk = input.float(0, 'Round-Trip Cost (ticks)', minval 0, step 0.5; tooltip: ES ≈ 1.5, NQ ≈ 2, 0 = off); riskCash = input.float(0, 'Risk per Trade (account ccy)').
2. Last bar with plan risk rk (TM-2 aT.risk or |close − invL|) and rr: cR = costTk·syminfo.mintick/max(rk, syminfo.mintick); beNet = (1+cR)/(1+rr); size = riskCash > 0 ? riskCash/(rk·syminfo.pointvalue) : na.
3. Display 'BE 38% (net 40%)' when costTk > 0 and 'size 2.4' when riskCash > 0. Tooltip: size ignores currency conversion and margin.
4. Optional: accumulate cR of graded trials in raceSt[9] and show R̄ net = R̄ − mean cost. TM-4 and TM-6 subtract the per-plan or per-cell cost.
proposals.risk: Users must enter their own costs (default 0 leaves the display unchanged). Currency conversion is ignored for FX and crypto.

proposals.title: Plan events and a trade-plan payload for alerts (on top of COMP-2)
proposals.rationale: Alerts carry only tag, price, score and PoT (2079-2093): no stop, R:R, BE, TP1, zone or time left, and no plan-management events. COMP-2 builds the framework (toggles, JSON, placeholders, reached/approaching/abandoned). This adds the plan fields and the plan events that exist (TM-2 states), within the platform throttle (more than 15 alerts in 3 minutes halts alerts).
proposals.spec:
1. Confirmed-bar events, alert.freq_once_per_bar_close, with per-trial once-flags (Trial fields stopAnn, tp1Ann, zoneAnn, set in the engine block): Plan Stopped (active trial race → −1; message with stop, plan R, 'target still x% in yb'); TP1 Reached (TM-3 tp1Hit); Entry Zone Tapped (TM-4; optional live freq_once_per_bar); Plan Window Rolled (active-level trial booked with status 3, MTM R plus new stop and R:R). Target reached stays COMP-2 'reached' with the plan R added.
2. JSON payload adds entry_ref, stop, stop_src, tp1, target, rr, be, be_net, win, rbar, rbar_se, n_ledger, pot, pot_left, bars_left, zone_top, zone_bot, p_fill, size (str.tostring / format.mintick).
3. alertcondition with const titles and messages embedding {{plot("DOL Plan Stop")}} and {{plot("DOL Plan R:R")}} (TM-2 plots).
4. Toggle alPlan default false; never alert.freq_all.
proposals.risk: Alert noise and the user's alert budget (defaults off). JSON validity. Depends on COMP-2 and TM-2.

proposals.title: Path map: next obstacles as TP1 candidates, partials graded as fixed-level rules only
proposals.rationale: Traders scale out at the first liquidity or opposing array on the path; the engine knows these levels but never shows them. Inner pools carry no information beyond distance. Opposing untouched FVGs cost −0.5 to −3 pp, handled by ICT-5's ledger-guarded penalty, not here. Partials are EV-neutral at scale (−0.004R ± 0.004 on 5-min, +0.004 ± 0.003 on 1h) with about 20% lower spread of R (B2), so show and measure them. Trailing rules must not be graded: on OHLC paths they show a spurious +0.016R to +0.035R.
proposals.spec:
1. Helper f_obstacles(Level tgt, int nMax): up to nMax pool indices with side == tgt.side, id != tgt.id, 0.25·atr ≤ distance < target distance − 0.10·atr, nearest first (array.includes for exclusion; O(nMax·pool)).
2. Inputs obsN (0-3, default 1, Terminal) and obsClean (false).
3. Dotted tick at nearEdge to xR with label 'TP1 · code · x.xR · PoT%' (f_potModel with mu 0); mark ICT-5's opposing-FVG bit with '▲ resist'. At most 3 lines and 3 labels.
4. Ledger: Trial fields tp1, tp1Liq, tp1Hit, tp1Bar, beHit. f_openTrial sets tp1 from the first obstacle. f_step uses f_barRace with edge = tp1 (advFirst decides same-bar TP1/stop); break-even is armed from the next bar only. f_book: rP = tp1Hit ? 0.5·|tp1−entry|/risk + 0.5·(race == 1 ? rr0 : beHit ? 0 : rOut) : rOut; tpSt = [n, TP1-first, ΣR, ΣR², ΣrP, ΣrP²].
5. Full panel row 'TP1 1ST x% | PART avg sd | FULL avg sd'.
6. No trailing-stop grading; no obstacle penalty in evaluate().
proposals.risk: Clutter (default 1 tick, Terminal only). The f_step ordering must reuse f_barRace. O(pool) loop on the last bar.

proposals.title: Entry zone with fill probability and an explicitly derived zone plan
proposals.rationale: ICT traders enter on a retracement into a draw-aligned array. The fill law d/(d+e) is calibrated within 2-4 pp and win given a fill matches geometry (A T4-A), so both limit-order risks (non-execution, adverse execution; Handa & Schwartz 1996, Linnainmaa 2010) can be shown and measured. B fix: f_invalidation usually picks the zone itself as the 'opposing' level (side −1 for a bullish array below price), so the zone stop must be derived explicitly.
proposals.spec:
1. Helper f_entryZone(Level tgt): nearest pool array with draw-aligned polarity (buy target: kinds 2/4/6; sell: 3/5/7), side == −tgt.side, e = distance ≥ 0.10·atr and ≤ maxATR. A parallel loop over ifvgs (dir == tgt.side) keeps the nearer. Origin-locked arrays are allowed.
2. Zone plan: zNear/zFar; invZ = long ? min(invL, zFar − 0.1·atr) : max(invL, zFar + 0.1·atr); rkZ = max(|zNear − invZ|, 0.25·atr); pFill = d/(d+e); rrZ = (d+e)/rkZ; beZ = 1/(1+rrZ); beZnet per TM-8.
3. Dotted box to xR with label 'ENTRY · BUFVG · fill ≈72% · R:R 4.8 · BE 17%' (Terminal; Clean via cleanPlan); +1 box, +1 label.
4. Optional ledger stage: limit trial (limE, filled, missed, pFill, invZ); before the fill a target hit means missed; after a touch the race runs from limE vs invZ via f_barRace. Book fill rate vs ΣpFill and win given fill vs ΣbeZ: 'FILL 70% (exp 73%) · WIN|fill 18% (BE 17%)'.
5. Input: zone pick 'Nearest' or 'Best R:R'.
proposals.risk: Zone choice is a design choice. The FVG-stop geometry gives high R:R with win rates of about 0.17-0.20; always show BE beside it. Adds a box and a label.

proposals.title: Stop-distance expectancy curve from the ledger (shadow stops), with a multiple-comparison guard
proposals.rationale: Traders ask where the stop should go. On these markets the curve is flat: every s from 0.5 to 3 ATR within ±0.01R, |z| < 1.5 (B2); after costs, tight stops lose (−0.12R at 0.5 ATR on 5-min). A per-chart departure from flat would be a measurable selection edge. Carr & López de Prado warn that picking the best cell is overfitting. The ledger already holds MAE and d0; only the MTM at H is missing.
proposals.spec:
1. Trial field endA; in f_step at status 3: endA = side·(close − entry)/atr0.
2. STATE var array<float> sgSt = array.new<float>(11, 0.0): [ΣR, ΣR²] × grid (0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3 ATR) plus [10] = n (an array, because functions cannot modify globals; language/user_defined_functions.md:29).
3. f_book (graded trials only): for [k, s] in array.from(0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0,3.0): r = mae ≥ s ? −1 : status == 1 ? d0/s : endA/s, minus TM-8 cost/s; accumulate.
4. Full panel row 'STOP·ATR 0.5 x | 1 x | 1.5 x | 2 x | 3 x (n)'. Highlight a cell only if |mean| > 2.6·SE (Bonferroni over 5 cells) and SE ≤ 0.1R.
proposals.risk: High variance at small s (show SE). MAE after an engine stop-out includes post-stop excursions, which is still exact for the stopped condition. Users may still try to optimise: the tooltip must warn.

result.summary: The non-repainting core is sound, so leave it alone. HTF/MTF reads use [1] with lookahead_on (782, 796, 923-925, 939, 981), the engine runs only on barstate.isconfirmed (1518), and B re-checked every loop and every and/or against the v6 lazy-evaluation and dynamic-for semantics. B also measured what is at stake: on 6 CME futures, leaking the current day's direction turns a no-edge 1-ATR race (49.6%) into a 59.5% 'hit rate'. That is a +10 pp illusory edge the ledger would report as real. B reverses A's PENG-9. On about 140k bars with 1-minute ground truth, the engine's candle-colour rule orders the bar's high and low correctly 88.1-88.6% of the time, against 80.5-81.8% for TradingView's open-proximity rule. It also wins 14 of 15 asymmetric target/stop race setups (70-87% vs 53-79%). Keep the rule and add an ambiguity counter. B found a new risk: an alert runs a server 'mirror image' of the script whose history grows from launch, and the learned state (cumulative f_calMult and f_raceAdj, a ledger start that moves with last_bar_index) has unbounded memory. Chart, alert and Bar Replay can therefore name different targets. PENG-10 adds a start-point parity test plus a bounded-memory fallback. Settings hygiene stays the P1 visible defect: 76 inputs leak to the legend. The overhaul already carries display.none and active= patches, but the CW10026 inline-row fix is missing, and the active map has four errors (obQMin, priorM, trackAge, accView), plus COMP-1's LVN pair. B corrected several of A's claims. The -33% tuple-merge figure comes from a 9-to-1 merge, while the engine's merge is 2-to-1. The 20/40/100 s budgets are third-party numbers (weak). The reference discourages the global max_bars_back=500 in favour of targeted max_bars_back() calls. The engine's 6 requests exceed the Pine Screener's 5-call cap. Runtime is likely fine (static estimate a few seconds on 20k bars), so PENG-2 asks for measurement first. Telemetry (PENG-6) and the PineTS harness (PENG-7) are the main engineering levers for WHERE, WHEN and HOW LIKELY. B validated the overhaul's bias-at-HTF-close fix (time_close gating) as non-repainting.

concepts.name: Non-repainting HTF reads ([1] + lookahead_on)
concepts.definition: request.security(sym, tf, expr[1], lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_on) returns the last confirmed HTF value from the first chart bar of each new HTF period, identically on historical and realtime bars. The offset goes inside the requested expression. Never request below the chart TF. Freshness cost: the final state of HTF bar N first appears on the first chart bar of bar N+1, so it is stale while the market is closed.
concepts.dolRole: Bias, HTF pools and HTF FVGs feed draw vector D, the registry and selection. Leaked future data would inflate the ledger's hit rate and edge, so this is the precondition for an honest HOW LIKELY.
concepts.evidenceNotes: other_timeframes_and_data.md:1398 ('most reliable approach'). B replication: on 6 CME futures (1H, ~33k signals), a leaked daily direction lifts a 1-ATR/10-bar race win rate from 0.496 to 0.595 (+10 pp illusory edge).
concepts.engineNotes: 782, 796, 923-925, 939, 981; f_tfSafe 564. Staleness at HTF close is fixed by overhaul struct-F2/rp-bias-done, which B validated as non-repainting.

concepts.name: Bias freshness at HTF close via time_close gating
concepts.definition: On the chart bar where barstate.isconfirmed and time_close == time_close(tf), the HTF bar is complete. Reading the unshifted lookahead_on value there is final on historical bars and on the realtime closing tick. On other bars keep the [1] value. The == comparison returns false on na, so holidays and gaps fall back to [1].
concepts.dolRole: Removes the one-HTF-candle lag in the bias table and drawD overnight and on weekends, when traders prepare (WHERE/side).
concepts.evidenceNotes: time.md:383-392 (time_close(tf)); execution_model.md rollback; overhaul struct-F2 evidence. Mechanism checked by B.
concepts.engineNotes: 782 and 926-931 use only [1] values; the table at 2299-2304 lags. Overhaul patch adds 6 tuple elements (52 -> 58 of 127).

concepts.name: Confirmed-bar gating, realtime rollback, varip
concepts.definition: barstate.isconfirmed is true on all historical bars and on the closing update of a realtime bar. Before each realtime re-execution, rollback reverts var variables and any changes on the open bar to objects referenced by var, and removes objects created on the open bar. varip, Pine Logs, alert logs and runtime errors survive.
concepts.dolRole: WHEN: targets, sweeps at close and ledger outcomes change only at bar close; the live PoT and the sweep alert are deliberately tick-level. The current delete-and-recreate rendering is functionally correct under rollback.
concepts.evidenceNotes: execution_model.md:375-416; bar_states.md:91,102.
concepts.engineNotes: Engine gated at 1518; live sweep reads var activeLv (1504); announcement gated on confirmation (2071).

concepts.name: v6 lazy and/or evaluation
concepts.definition: In v6 the right operand of and/or is skipped when the left operand decides the result. ta.* calls or history-dependent UDFs placed there miss bars and corrupt their history. Hoist them to global variables.
concepts.dolRole: Silent mis-computation of pivots, ATR and bias, which would corrupt WHERE without any compile error.
concepts.evidenceNotes: to_pine_version_6.md:777-830. B grep: no ta.*, f_changed*, f_sessOpen, f_rangeTrack, f_sessTrack, math.sum or request.* after and/or/?.
concepts.engineNotes: All stateful calls are global and unconditional (874-975).

concepts.name: v6 dynamic for-loop bounds
concepts.definition: A for loop re-evaluates to_num before every iteration. If to < from, Pine counts down, so 0..size-1 loops need a size-0 guard. Never mutate the collection a for...in loop is iterating.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents runaway or skipped loops over the pool, registry and ledger.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Release notes March 2025; loops.md. B inspected all loops.
concepts.engineNotes: Descending removal loops end at the constant 0 (1551, 1560, 1593, 1600, 1631, 1648); ascending loops are guarded (1095, 1002, 1393, 1816, 1954, 1973, 2051, 2153, 2161, 2176, 2260, 2274); ixs is pushed only after its own loop ends (1839/1852).

concepts.name: Historical buffers and max_bars_back
concepts.definition: Buffers are sized from references in the first 244 bars; exceeding them later restarts the script (8x executions in the docs' demo). Realtime overruns raise RE10143. max_bars_back(var, num) allows num <= 5000. OHLC and time can reference 10,000 bars. The reference discourages the global indicator(max_bars_back) parameter unless most series need the same size, because it increases memory use and can hurt performance.
concepts.dolRole: Deep offsets (close[H], atr[H], OB scans) must not cause load blow-ups or realtime crashes, nor waste memory or time.
concepts.evidenceNotes: core.md:179, 259-273; RE10143.md; profiling_and_optimization.md:1560ff. The engine-specific cost of the global 500 is unmeasured.
concepts.engineNotes: Global max_bars_back=500 (31) plus time 5000 (37). Real maxima: H<=450 (atr/close/htfBias), OB scans <=66, coilScore/indScore <=67, f_anchorScan <=32, time[lim] <=450. It works with no restarts, but this is the discouraged pattern; Profiler A/B in PENG-2. [B-corr from 'present']

concepts.name: Drawing x-coordinate limits and time-based anchoring
concepts.definition: xloc.bar_index drawings can sit at most 10,000 bars in the past and 500 in the future. All drawings convert x to time through the time buffer, so realtime drawings need a time buffer as deep as the oldest anchor. time(tf, bars_back=-n) gives the expected future bar time for n from 1 to 500, enabling xloc.bar_time drawings.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps the zone anchored at the candle that printed it. The clamp only misplaces anchors more than 4,999 bars back, which are off screen in practice.
concepts.evidenceNotes: limitations.md (max bars back/forward; time can reference 10,000); RE10143.md 'Historical buffer errors in realtime drawings'; time.md:298.
concepts.engineNotes: f_x clamps at 4999 (404-405) with the time buffer at 5000 (37). A cheap 10k time-buffer variant is in PENG-8 (verify).

concepts.name: Reducing drawing updates and avoiding redrawing
concepts.definition: Historical drawing changes are invisible, so restrict updates to the last bar. Setters are cheaper than delete plus *.new: the box.new line takes close to double the combined time of two setters in the docs' demo. Budgets: 500 lines, boxes and labels, 100 polylines, 9 tables; na-property drawings still count.
concepts.dolRole: UX stability (tooltip, flicker) and load time. The absolute per-tick cost is small here.
concepts.evidenceNotes: profiling_and_optimization.md:1072-1199 (vendor demo); limitations.md.
concepts.engineNotes: islast-only rendering (2111, 2132). Delete and recreate of 8 objects per tick (2132-2141, 2216-2248); table.clear every tick (2296, 2311). Historical iFVG churn (1611-1623) is negligible.

concepts.name: Request budget, tuple merging, dynamic requests
concepts.definition: Limits: 40 unique request.*() calls (64 on Ultimate), 127 tuple elements in total, 100k/125k/200k intrabars by plan. Merging same-context expressions into one tuple request cuts runtime, memory and compiled size; the docs' demo went from 340.8 to 228.3 ms for a 9-to-1 merge. calc_bars_count limits a request's history. A dynamic request's expression cannot depend on loop variables.
concepts.dolRole: Load time and headroom for MTF features. The 2-to-1 merge also enables the Pine Screener.
concepts.evidenceNotes: limitations.md; profiling_and_optimization.md:991-1070. [B-corr] The -33% figure is a 9-to-1 merge; the engine's 2-to-1 gain is unquantified.
concepts.engineNotes: 6 calls (923, 924, 925, 939, 981, 982), 52 tuple elements. 923 and 939 share the context f_tfSafe(tfH).

concepts.name: Whole-script budget: execution time, chart bars, calc_bars_count, compile limits, Profiler
concepts.definition: Loops: 500 ms per bar. Total time varies by plan, and the current docs defer to the pricing page; 20/40/100 s are third-party numbers. Chart bars: 5k/10k/20k/25k/40k. indicator(calc_bars_count = const int) adds a 'Calculated bars' input. Compile: 2 min, with a one-hour ban after 3 consecutive warnings; 100,256 IL tokens; 1,000 variables per scope. The Pine Profiler gives per-line runtime and execution counts.
concepts.dolRole: A timeout is the worst failure ('does not run'). Measurement replaces guesswork.
concepts.evidenceNotes: limitations.md:23-27,412 and script compilation; core.md:183. Budget numbers are third-party. Overhaul static estimate: 5-8e7 primitive operations on 20k 1m bars, 'a few seconds'.
concepts.engineNotes: No calc_bars_count; never profiled. Only scoring, selection and the ledger are limited by Calculation Depth (85, 1519). All-bar hot loops: registry re-entry (1825-1852), f_bump (1265-1271), trackers.

concepts.name: Input display / active / inline alignment
concepts.definition: display defaults to display.all (status line plus Data Window) for every input type except bool and color. active (input bool, July 2025) greys inputs out. Inline rows align only when the first input has a title and the rest use ""; otherwise warning CW10026.
concepts.dolRole: No forecasting role; it is the most visible clutter versus the reference legend.
