concepts.evidenceNotes: inputs.md:112-118; input.md; errors/CW10026.md; release notes Oct 2026.
concepts.engineNotes: 76 of 104 inputs leak (59-237). The overhaul has display/active patches, but its active map needs fixes: obQMin<-useOB; priorM<-Empirical or accView!=Off or useCal (f_potBase 1321); trackAge and accView always active; lvnHours/lvnRows<-showLVN or usePathVP. CW10026 x4 at 230-237 is not patched.

concepts.name: Alerts and server-side execution
concepts.definition: alert(series msg, freq) fires on realtime bars; freq_once_per_bar_close fires when the realtime bar closes. alertcondition takes a const message, with dynamic values only via {{plot_n}} or {{plot("title")}}. Creating an alert saves a mirror image of the script and its inputs on TradingView's servers; later input changes do not affect it. The alert's bar count only grows after launch, so its results can diverge from the chart's. The alert dialog's repaint mark is a conservative static heuristic.
concepts.dolRole: WHEN the trader is notified. Alert-versus-chart divergence reads as 'the targets are wrong'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: alerts.md:23, 53-76, 336-396 (strong); TradingView support 43000773984 via search summary (moderate); PineCoders on the repaint heuristic.
concepts.engineNotes: Correct frequencies (2079-2093). No placeholders and no per-event toggles (COMP-2); README lacks recreate-after-change and repaint-mark notes (PENG-12).

concepts.name: Reload, alert and replay path dependence
concepts.definition: The dataset's starting point varies with plan and alignment, a server alert's history grows from creation, and Bar Replay starts elsewhere. Any state with unbounded memory, or a start tied to last_bar_index, gives different outputs on the same prices. Bounded memory (e.g. exponential forgetting) makes runs converge after about 3/(1-lambda) trials.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps the target shown on the chart, the alert's target and the accuracy panel consistent (WHERE and HOW LIKELY stability).
concepts.evidenceNotes: repainting.md:268-297 (strong); alerts.md:23 (strong); support 43000773984 (moderate); magnitude for this engine unmeasured (needs PENG-10 Step 1).
concepts.engineNotes: f_calMult reads cumulative stN/stK/stPE (1376-1382, x0.8-1.2); f_raceAdj reads cumulative raceSt (1367-1371); inCalc and ledger start move with last_bar_index (1519, 2038); 2-bar hysteresis (2014). Run ids (nextId) differ across runs.

concepts.name: Live visibility filter stability
concepts.definition: Take show/hide decisions on confirmed bars with a hysteresis band, so a live metric crossing a threshold does not toggle visuals intrabar; text may still update live.
concepts.dolRole: A target that flickers in and out reads as 'targets jump around' although selection is stable at bar close.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanism from the rollback docs (strong); perception impact inferred. Only relevant when minPoT > 0 (default 0).
concepts.engineNotes: dolShown from live activePoT (2066-2068), used at 2202, 2185, 2349; annNow is already confirmed (2071).

concepts.name: Non-standard chart handling
concepts.definition: chart.is_standard (simple bool) is false on HA, Renko, Kagi, Line break, P&F and Range. syminfo.tickerid carries the chart type, so requests inherit it. Real OHLC comes from request.security(ticker.new(syminfo.prefix, syminfo.ticker, syminfo.session), ...). ticker.new without adjustment uses the instrument default, and backadjustment/settlement_as_close default to the symbol's settings. ticker.standard also strips the session and adjustments.
concepts.dolRole: On HA charts the close-based rules (BOS/CHoCH, raid hold or reject, iFVG inversion, breaker flip) use HA close = OHLC/4, wicks are only approximately real, and the ledger grades distorted candles.
concepts.evidenceNotes: chart.md:71; syminfo.md:809; faq/general.md:5-28; ticker.md:167-178, 273. Prevalence of HA use unknown.
concepts.engineNotes: No chart-type check; all six requests (923, 924, 925, 939, 981, 982) use syminfo.tickerid; the ledger runs regardless. [B-corr] six calls, not five; 'distorted' rather than 'fiction'.

concepts.name: Volume-less symbols
concepts.definition: syminfo.volumetype is 'n/a' when there is no volume or its type is unspecified; volume-profile features should then be disabled and the user told.
concepts.dolRole: Stops path-cost and LVN logic from silently doing nothing on some FX symbols and indices.
concepts.evidenceNotes: syminfo.md:837-839.
concepts.engineNotes: nz(volume) leads to the neutral f_pathVol=1.0 (1417-1424); LVN is silently empty; 1H requests still run.

concepts.name: Same-bar double-touch convention
concepts.definition: When one bar touches both target and invalidation, OHLC alone cannot tell which was first. Engine rule: bull bar O-L-H-C, bear bar O-H-L-C, with a gap settling at the open. TradingView broker emulator: open closer to the high means O-H-L-C, otherwise O-L-H-C. Measured on 1-minute ground truth, the colour rule is the more accurate heuristic.
concepts.dolRole: Decides WIN<=H, race R and MAE in the ledger when one bar spans both barriers.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B replication, CME ES/NQ/YM/RTY/GC/CL Jan-Apr 2026, ~140k bars: extremes ordered correctly by colour 0.881-0.886 vs TradingView 0.805-0.818; where they disagree (~15% of bars) colour is right 0.72-0.78; asymmetric races colour 0.70-0.87 vs TradingView 0.53-0.79 (14 of 15 configurations). strategies.md:204-205 is a convention, not a measurement.
concepts.engineNotes: f_step 1440-1441 uses the better rule. Missing: an ambiguity counter (PENG-9). [B-corr] A proposed switching to TradingView's rule, which would degrade accuracy.

concepts.name: Diagnostics: Pine Logs and chart-data export
concepts.definition: log.info(format, args) writes to Pine Logs, which survive rollback; the pane shows the most recent 10,000 historical logs plus realtime logs. 'Download chart data' exports OHLC plus indicator values to CSV; whether data-window-only plots are included is undocumented. Hidden plots can carry one record per forecast, keyed by (kind, price, anchor time), since run ids differ across runs.
concepts.dolRole: Audits WHY a target was chosen. Allows offline calibration and per-family statistics, and is the data source for parity tests.
concepts.evidenceNotes: log.md; execution_model.md:414; debugging.md:183,205; TradingView help 43000537255; data_window inclusion weak.
concepts.engineNotes: Only 5 data-window plots (2444-2448); no per-trial record, no decision log.

concepts.name: Pine Screener constraints
concepts.definition: Premium plan or higher; computes only the last 500 bars; the first 10 plots become columns (display.pine_screener); at most 5 request.* calls; input.timeframe values are ignored.
concepts.dolRole: Multi-symbol scanning for active DOLs. The empirical PoT (needs >= 600 windows) and the ledger cannot warm up there.
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView help 43000742437/43000742436 via search summary; constants.md:125.
concepts.engineNotes: 6 request calls exceed the cap of 5; the 923+939 merge (PENG-2) brings it to 5 (COMP-9).

concepts.name: Offline Pine v6 runtime (PineTS)
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo PineTS 0.14.0 (2026-11-13, AGPL plus a commercial licence) transpiles native v6 (README: experimental) and runs it with Pine time-series semantics. Its parity changelog covers ta.* history from the first call, v6 dynamic for, tick rollback, barstate.isrealtime with the market closed, negative bars_back, security_lower_tf edge cases and alertcondition placeholders.
concepts.dolRole: The only way to execute the engine in CI: smoke tests, repaint regression, start-point parity and multi-symbol ledger A/B.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Verified from the local clone's package.json and CHANGELOG; not executed (npm install denied in this session).
concepts.engineNotes: Only a syntax parser (pynescript) is available.

concepts.name: Script size and scope limits
concepts.definition: 100,256 compiled IL tokens (unused code discarded first), 1,000 variables per scope, no scope-count limit since Feb 2025, 5 MB compilation request, 2-minute compile limit, collections <= 100,000 elements.
concepts.dolRole: Compile-risk headroom for adding features to a 2,450-line engine.
concepts.evidenceNotes: limitations.md; debugging.md:1429; release notes Feb 2025.
concepts.engineNotes: About 300 global declarations plus ~80 tuple names; largest collections tfOpenBar 4000 pairs and lv* <= 5x1000. Token margin unknown without a compiler.

concepts.name: behind_chart and drawing z-order
concepts.definition: behind_chart (default true) draws all plots and drawings behind the price display when overlay=true.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps candles readable over zones and iFVG boxes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: core.md indicator() behind_chart; release notes Oct 2024.
concepts.engineNotes: Default at line 31; the label sits in the empty future area (xR = bar_index + extBars).

concepts.name: In-platform test instruments (Bar Replay, Profiler, alert log)
concepts.definition: Bar Replay 'Forward' runs the script in realtime mode and is the official way to reproduce realtime-only behaviour (RE10143.md). The Profiler gives per-line runtime and global execution counts (count = bars means no buffer restarts). The alerts log records realtime WHEN.
concepts.dolRole: Verifies non-repainting, rollback and closing-tick logic, and the timing of notifications, without waiting for live markets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: RE10143.md; profiling_and_optimization.md:17-760.
concepts.engineNotes: No documented test protocol; added to PENG-2 and PENG-7.

proposals.title: Settings hygiene: land the overhaul display.none/active patches with a corrected active map, and fix the 4 CW10026 inline rows
proposals.rationale: 76 of 104 inputs print their values in the status line and Data Window (default display.all), which is the most visible 'cluttered' difference from the reference legend. The overhaul (TE1/VIS/ux-statusline-inputs) already has display.none and active= patches. Its active map, A's map and COMP-1's map contain errors that would grey out settings that still matter. The four colour inline rows raise CW10026, which no patch fixes. Merges with COMP-1.
proposals.spec: (1) Literal display = display.none on all 76 int/float/string/session/timeframe inputs (60-226); after patching, grep must count 76 (input.md). (2) active= (input bool; every dependency is declared earlier): cHTF/cSTF/cEXE <- modeIn == "Custom"; sessAs/sessLo/sessNA <- useSess; fvgQMin <- useFVG; obQMin <- useOB (breakers never read it, 1701/1742); obLook <- useOB or useBRK; delivIn <- useFVG or useOB or useBRK or useHTFFVG; ifvgMaxIn/ifvgMax <- showIFVG; trackAge always active (feeds the iFVG alert 1624-1627); lvnThr/lvnN <- showLVN; lvnHours/lvnRows <- showLVN or usePathVP; ghostMax <- showGhost; hudSize <- uiStyle == "Terminal"; accView always active (it switches the ledger, 2038); warmup <- accView != "Off" or useCal; priorM <- potModel == "Empirical" or accView != "Off" or useCal (f_potBase reads it, 1321); tablePosIn <- showTable; uAbove..uText <- theme == "Custom". (3) CW10026: in each inline pair c1-c4 (230-237) keep the title only on the first input ('Custom · Buy / Sell-side', 'Custom · Bull / Bear', 'Custom · LVN / Ghost', 'Custom · Panel / Text'), pass "" on the second, and add a tooltip naming both (errors/CW10026.md steps 1-2).
proposals.risk: None functionally. Users lose input values in the legend, which is intended to match the reference.

proposals.title: Reload and alert parity: start-point invariance test plus bounded-memory learned state
proposals.rationale: An alert runs a server mirror image of the script whose bar count grows from launch (alerts.md:23; support 43000773984). A chart reload starts at a different dataset point (repainting.md), and Bar Replay starts elsewhere again. The engine's learned state has unbounded memory: cumulative stN/stK/stPE in f_calMult (x0.8-1.2 score multiplier) and raceSt in f_raceAdj, with a ledger start that moves with last_bar_index. So the alert, the chart and replay can name different targets for the same prices, which reads as 'the targets are wrong or jump'. Coordinated with calib_ml section 1.33.
proposals.spec: Step 1, parity test (needs the PENG-6 export): load the same chart with 'Calculated bars' (or Bar Replay start) at N and at N-1000. Over the last 1000 confirmed bars, compare the active target per bar by (kind, price, anchor time); ids are not comparable across runs. Accept if >= 98% of bars agree and the first disagreement dies out within 2*H bars. Run with useCal on and off to isolate calibration. Step 2, only if Step 1 fails: keep the displayed stats cumulative and feed the learners from decayed sums. Add var arrays cuN, cuK, cuE (size 5) and rcN, rcW, rcP. In f_book (1461), for g in [t.grp, 4]: cuN[g] := lambda*cuN[g] + 1, cuK[g] := lambda*cuK[g] + y, cuE[g] := lambda*cuE[g] + t.pBase, with const lambda = 0.99 (~100-trial memory); the race sums work the same way. f_calMult (1376) and f_raceAdj (1367) read the decayed sums, and the n >= 10 gate uses cuN. Runs converge after ~3/(1-lambda) = 300 shared trials. Any calib_ml learner adopted instead must pass Step 1. README: 'recreate alerts after changing inputs; the accuracy panel depends on the loaded history'.
proposals.risk: Low. Forgetting trades drift adaptation against noise (calib_ml found it neutral to slightly negative at these sample sizes), so use the gentlest lambda that passes Step 1. The magnitude of the problem is unknown until Step 1 runs.

proposals.title: Forecast telemetry: per-forecast export record (data-window plots) and opt-in log.info decision trail
proposals.rationale: The ledger only summarises. Nobody can audit why a target was chosen or switched, replicate calibration or per-family stats offline on the forecasts the user saw, or run the PENG-10 parity test. Pine Logs survive rollback (10,000 historical messages), and Download chart data exports plot values.
proposals.spec: New group 'Diagnostics': dbgExport and dbgLog (bool false, display.none). (1) On the f_openTrial bar (2045), set and plot, AFTER the existing 5 plots so {{plot_0..4}} stay stable: xPx (target price), xKind (kind*10+src), xAnchorT (time[bar_index-anchorBar], exact inside the 5000-bar time buffer), xSide, xEdge, xInv, xD0 (distance in ATR), xPoT (model PoT at assertion), xBase (pBase), xGrp, xScore. All display=display.data_window, na elsewhere or when disabled: 11 plots, 20 of 64 total. Outcomes are recomputed offline from the CSV OHLC. Verify once that data-window-only plots reach the CSV; fallback is display.all with transparent colour. (2) When dbgLog and inCalc, on each confirmed activeId change (2030): log.info('{0} DOL {1}→{2} {3} score {4,number,0.0} chall {5} side {6} D {7,number,0.00} why {8}', ...), with reason in {sweep, eject, invalid, lead2, counter, none}. Also log sweeps and ejections (step 3) and ledger bookings (step 2). Cap the volume with inCalc plus an optional last-N-bars input (debugging.md:183).
proposals.risk: Low. Hidden plots are na unless enabled. Plot order must stay stable for alert placeholders (COMP-2/COMP-9 output contract).

proposals.title: Offline PineTS harness: smoke, repaint regression, start-point parity, ledger replay; plus in-platform Replay and alert checks
proposals.rationale: Only a syntax parser exists, so there is no runtime check of na handling, bounds, buffers, repainting or parity, and no way to A/B forecasting changes across symbols. PineTS 0.14.0 (2026-11-13) runs native v6, and its parity fixes target exactly the constructs the engine uses.
proposals.spec: Dev-only (AGPL, never shipped; npm install needs the user's approval, it was denied this session). Custom BaseProvider fed by the local CME 1m/1h CSVs (study/amt_data/cme) and synthetic GBM; HTFs via PineTS aggregation. Test 1 smoke: every Trading Mode x both styles x accView Full over 20k bars, no runtime errors, non-na DOL plots after warm-up. Test 2 repaint: run() on N bars vs N-k bars + k stream()/update() calls; DOL price, score, (kind, price) identity and ledger plots identical on every confirmed bar. Test 3: PENG-10 parity automated over 20 symbols. Test 4: ledger replay A/B of other studies' proposals over 20-50 symbols (hit %, edge z, race win %). Test 5: wall time per 10k bars per commit. In-platform complement: Bar Replay 'Forward' over 200 bars vs a fresh load (RE10143.md), and one live alert log compared with the chart after a reload.
proposals.risk: Runtime parity is not guaranteed (native v6 is experimental), so failures need triage against TradingView.

proposals.title: Measure first: merge the two HTF requests, Profiler/Replay protocol, conditional calc_bars_count and targeted max_bars_back
proposals.rationale: Runtime has never been measured. The static estimate is low (~5-8e7 primitive operations on 20k 1m bars), and the plan budgets are third-party numbers, so measure before changing. Merging 923 and 939 (same context) removes a request; it is a 2-to-1 merge, so the gain is less than the docs' 9-to-1 demo (-33%). It also brings the engine to 5 requests, the Pine Screener's cap. The reference discourages the global max_bars_back=500. Two of A's sub-items are dropped: lazy iFVG (negligible) and Clean gating (already overhaul perf-1).
proposals.spec: (1) After f_htfFvg (~797): f_htfPack(len, minAtr, dm) returns f_structure's 12 values followed by f_htfFvg's 5. Replace 923 and 939 with one request.security(syminfo.tickerid, f_tfSafe(tfH), f_htfPack(biasLen, fvgMin, dispMult), lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_on). Requests 6 -> 5; tuple total unchanged (52, or 58 with struct-F2); both inner functions are already [1]-shifted. Regression: ledger n, hit % and edge identical on the same chart. (2) Profiler protocol: BTCUSD 1m 20k (Scalping), ES 5m (Day), EURUSD 1h (Day, no volume), SPY 4h (Swing, lower-TF path), each in Clean and Terminal-Full at calcBars 5000 and 20000, three runs each. Record total ms, global execution count (= bars means no restarts) and the top-5 lines; add a Bar Replay pass to time realtime ticks. (3) Conditional levers, only if needed (e.g. total > ~50% of the slowest plan's budget on 40k bars): indicator(calc_bars_count = 20000) (const int, core.md:183); replace the global max_bars_back=500 with max_bars_back(high/low/close, 500), (open, 70), (atr, 460), (htfBias, 460), (coilScore/indScore/ll20/hh20, 70), keeping time at 5000, and confirm the execution count still equals bars; throttle registry re-entry (1825) to regNew or bar_index % 10 == 0 outside inCalc; cache f_pathVol per profile rebuild.
proposals.risk: Low. Tuple order must match exactly. Targeted buffers that miss a series cause restarts (visible in the Profiler) or RE10143, so verify with the execution count.

proposals.title: Non-standard chart and data guard: chart.is_standard, real-price requests on all six calls, ledger off, volume check
proposals.rationale: On Heikin Ashi (and Renko etc.) the close-based rules (BOS/CHoCH 747-770, raid hold or reject 1581, iFVG inversion 1603, breaker flip 1651) run on HA close = OHLC/4. The six requests inherit the HA context through syminfo.tickerid, and the ledger grades distorted candles. The official FAQ prescribes ticker.new plus request.security for real OHLC.
proposals.spec: (1) After 309: bool stdChart = chart.is_standard (chart.md:71). (2) string tkr = stdChart ? syminfo.tickerid : ticker.new(syminfo.prefix, syminfo.ticker, syminfo.session) (ticker.md:167; faq/general.md). Use tkr in ALL SIX requests (923, 924, 925, 939, 981, 982); never ticker.standard. (3) Warning row in both styles mirroring tfWarn (2305-2307, 2431-2433): 'NON-STANDARD CHART | levels use synthetic candles'. AND ledgerOK = stdChart into the trial-open condition (2038), and show 'LEDGER OFF · use candles'. (4) needVP := (showLVN or usePathVP) and syminfo.volumetype != "n/a" (syminfo.md:839), with an LVN tooltip 'needs volume'. (5) Optional (M-L): drive the engine from real same-TF OHLC on HA charts; invasive because ta.atr/ta.tr read chart OHLC internally. Default is warn only.
proposals.risk: ticker.new without adjustment uses the instrument default, and its backadjustment/settlement_as_close follow the symbol default, not the user's chart setting (ticker.md:177-178). Exposure is small (non-standard charts only); document it.

proposals.title: Same-bar double touch: KEEP the candle-colour rule (measured better than TradingView's), add an AMBIG counter, optional LTF resolution
proposals.rationale: A proposed adopting TradingView's open-proximity rule. B measured both on ~140k CME bars with 1-minute ground truth. The engine's colour rule orders the extremes correctly 88.1-88.6% vs 80.5-81.8%, and wins 14 of 15 asymmetric race configurations (0.70-0.87 vs 0.53-0.79). Switching would degrade WIN<=H and race stats. Users should still see how much of the race stat rests on the heuristic.
proposals.spec: No change to f_step's ordering rule (1440-1441). raceSt = array.new<float>(8, 0.0) (1079); add Trial field bool amb = false. In f_step (1444-1446), when t.race == 0 and hit and stp and not tgtOpn and not stpOpn, set t.amb := true before applying the colour rule. In f_book, if t.amb add 1 to raceSt[7]. The Full view's RACE row shows 'AMBIG x%' = raceSt[7]/raceSt[0]. Optional (M, only if AMBIG > ~5%): request.security_lower_tf(tkr, timeframe.from_seconds(math.max(60, timeframe.in_seconds()/10)), [high, low], ignore_invalid_timeframe=true), read when hit and stp. It costs one more request (screener cap) and intrabar budget.
proposals.risk: None for the counter. Evidence covers 6 CME futures over one quarter; crypto and FX are untested.

proposals.title: Confirmed-bar visibility with hysteresis for the Minimum-PoT filter
proposals.rationale: dolShown (2068) comes from the live PoT. With minPoT > 0, the zone, label and secondary targets (2185) toggle between ticks when PoT hovers near the threshold. Default minPoT is 0, hence P3.
proposals.spec: STATE: var bool showC=false, var int showId=-1. After 2067, on barstate.isconfirmed with pp = nz(activePoT)*100: if na(activeLv) then showC := false; else if activeLv.id != showId then showC := pp >= minPoT and showId := activeLv.id; else showC := showC ? pp >= minPoT - 2.0 : pp >= minPoT. Rendering (2202), the Terminal FILTERED cell (2349) and annNow (2071) use showC; the label text keeps the live PoT. Secondary targets use their PoT cached at bar close.
proposals.risk: A target whose live PoT drops below the filter stays visible until the close (intended).

proposals.title: Alert and README engineering notes: server mirror image, repaint-mark heuristic, alert() bundling, synthetic-candle warning
proposals.rationale: Alerts run a server copy of the script with the inputs at creation time, and the alert dialog's 'may repaint' mark is a conservative heuristic that fires even on correct [1]+lookahead_on scripts. Without notes, users report 'the alert disagrees with my chart' or 'it repaints'.
proposals.spec: README 'Alerts' section: (a) 'Alerts run a server copy of the script with the inputs at creation; after changing settings, delete and recreate the alert' (alerts.md:23). (b) 'The repaint mark is generic: PoT and DOL Target Swept are intentionally live; everything else is computed at bar close.' (c) 'Any alert() function call' bundles all four alert() events; use COMP-2's per-event toggles. (d) Heikin Ashi/Renko note (pairs with PENG-3). Keep alertcondition titles and plot order stable; once COMP-2 lands, add '{{plot("DOL Price")}}' and '{{plot("DOL PoT %")}}' in single quotes (alerts.md:362-372).
proposals.risk: None.

proposals.title: Persistent render objects updated with setters; incremental table writes
proposals.rationale: Each realtime tick deletes and recreates 6-10 drawings (2132-2141, 2216-2248) and clears the 4x22 table (2296, 2311). This is functionally correct under rollback, and the absolute cost is tiny (the docs measure box.new at ~2x two setters). The remaining benefit is a stable label object for the hover tooltip, which is unverified.
proposals.spec: Declare once: var box rZone = box.new(na,na,na,na, border_style=line.style_dashed); var array<line> rGlow (5 lines created on barstate.isfirst); var line rTeth; var label rLab. On barstate.islast, when shown, update with box.set_lefttop/set_rightbottom/set_bgcolor/set_border_color, line.set_xy1/set_xy2/set_color/set_width and label.set_xy/set_text/set_textcolor/set_tooltip/set_size. Otherwise use one hide path (na coordinates or transparent colours; verify once). Clean uses 5 glow layers, Terminal 3 plus 2 transparent. Keep the dB/dLn/dLb pools for variable-count objects. Table: overwrite with table.cell and clear only rows past var int lastRows.
proposals.risk: Moderate: stale-object bugs on style switches or when there is no target.

proposals.title: Far anchors: cheap 10k time-buffer variant first, full xloc.bar_time anchoring only if needed
proposals.rationale: f_x clamps anchors more than 4,999 bars back (e.g. PWH on 1m charts), so the zone starts on the wrong candle. The misplaced edge is far off screen, so the visible value is low. limitations.md says the time series can reference up to 10,000 bars, although max_bars_back() caps at 5000.
proposals.spec: (1) Cheap variant: replace line 37 with an early-bar reference that sizes the buffer (RE10143.md 'larger historical reference on early bars'): int tBuf = time[barstate.isfirst ? 9999 : 0]. Raise f_x to bar_index - 9999. Verify once in the editor and revert if it errors. (2) Full variant (M): int anchorT on Level/Ext/Zone (chart pivots time[bar_index-aBH], MTF htfPvHT/stfPvHT, session/PD tracker times); draw with xloc=xloc.bar_time, right edge time(timeframe.period, bars_back=-extBars) (time.md:298).
proposals.risk: Variant 1: undocumented edge, so verify. Variant 2: mixed-xloc bugs are easy to introduce.

result.summary: I verified A's study, extended it and merged both into one corrected report. Fidelity: I re-sampled the reference screenshot myself and confirmed A's pixel audit for the fill, every glow layer, the border, the iFVG, the label and the table. A composited the box fill under the lines, but Pine always draws boxes above lines, so the engine's white core actually renders #D3FACB, ΔE 6.7 from the reference's #DDFCD8. Changing the core to white t10 gives ΔE 0.9 (new UX-10). The reference's candles also draw unblended over its zones, which confirms the default behind_chart=true (keep it). The status line is still the biggest visible gap: about 411 characters of default values print beside the name. I corrected A's line range (60-229) and three errors in A's `active` map (useBRK must not depend on useOB; fvgMin must stay active; obLook depends on useOB or useBRK). I also found that the four colour rows misalign under the October 2026 inline-input rules and trigger compiler warning CW10026. The light-theme failure (every Clean element 1.04-1.37:1 on white) stands. The docs resolve A's open risk: scripts that read chart.fg_color or chart.bg_color reload when the chart background changes. Text on the dark label and table must stay neon, because the light variants drop to 2.8-3.98:1 there. Evidence corrections: A's "7%→45%" natural-frequency figure is unverified (meta-analysis 4%→24%). The 97% payoff figure belongs to quantile dotplots with 50 outcomes (CI 95-98%). The red-colour risk effect (8 experiments, n=1,451) is strong in the lab but transfers weakly to a target colour. MacEachren rated transparency only moderately intuitive and blur reads as more uncertainty, so confidence-weighted glow is downgraded to weak and may vary transparency only, never halo width. New evidence: uncertainty forecasts raise trust and soften the damage from forecast errors (Joslyn & LeClerc), clutter slows visual search (Rosenholtz), a unique bright target pops out in under 250 ms (Healey & Enns), and attractive interfaces are rated more usable (aesthetic-usability effect). A survey of 24 recent open-source Pine v6 indicators found none that hide inputs from the legend and only 4 that adapt to the chart theme, so these are cheap differentiators. The research ran with limited tools: Firecrawl had no credits, the WebSearch budget ran out after about 17 calls, and paper hosts were blocked, so some literature figures come from search summaries and are flagged.

concepts.name: Status line (legend) hygiene
concepts.definition: The script status line prints the title plus every input whose display includes status_line. The Pine default is display.all for int/float/string/session/timeframe/source/price/enum inputs and display.none for bool and color (reference/input.md:27; concepts/inputs.md:112). The parameter is const plot_display, so the literal must be written in each call. The chart-wide 'Indicator arguments' setting can hide them, but the author's default decides what most users see.
concepts.dolRole: Indirect: about 411 characters of numbers wrap over the candles and compete with the single target; the reference legend shows only the name.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanism from official docs. TradingView publishing guidance says the script's status line should show its name (publishing.md:122). OSS survey: 0 of 24 v6 indicator files hide their inputs. The benefit itself is convention (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: 76 of 104 input calls (lines 60-229, including tz, sessions and theme; A said 59-216) lack display.none. The default values print as about 411 characters. Plots 2444-2448 are correctly display.data_window.

concepts.name: Input UX: groups, inline alignment, tooltips, active, progressive disclosure
concepts.definition: Groups are ordered by the first input of each group. Inline rows align with other inputs only when the first input on the row has a title and the others use "" (October 2026 model; otherwise compiler warning CW10026). Only the last tooltip on a row shows. active (input bool) greys out dependent inputs. Advanced internals go last, optionally greyed out behind an unlock toggle.
concepts.dolRole: Indirect: mis-set sessions or timezone silently mislabel PDH, Asia and killzone levels and corrupt target selection.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanisms official (release notes, errors/CW10026.md, input.md:28). The benefit is HCI convention (Nielsen heuristics, not re-verified). OSS: 22/24 files use tooltips, 1/24 uses active.
concepts.engineNotes: 16 groups (42-57). 76 of 104 inputs have no tooltip (54 of them legend-type), including all sessions and tz. active is unused. The colour rows c1-c4 (230-237) title both inline fields, giving CW10026 x4 and misalignment. Internals come before the display groups. Corrected active map: obLook = useOB or useBRK; useBRK independent; fvgMin always active; ifvgMaxIn/ifvgMax = showIFVG; trackAge and accView always active; warmup = accView != 'Off' or useCal.

concepts.name: Reference-fidelity palette and layered glow
concepts.definition: A neon line is co-linear lines of increasing width and transparency plus a near-white 1 px core. Engine Clean: fill c t92; dashed border c t75; glow (t,w) = (90,10), (80,7), (60,4), (30,2); white core width 1; dashed tether c t30 to the centre at xR = bar_index + 20; #161616 label at size.normal, centred, style_label_left.
concepts.dolRole: WHERE: makes the single target the brightest object on the chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B re-sampled a profile at x = 800/900/1000: border 497, fill 498-503, glow 504-513, core at 509. All layers match within +-1 RGB. Correction: Pine draws the box fill above lines, so the engine's t15 core is #D3FACB (dE 6.7 vs the reference #DDFCD8). White t10 gives dE 0.9. Same-colour glow layers commute, so A's glow match stands.
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 2214-2226, 293-299 and 1609-1615 are exact except the core at 2223 (t15 should be t10; UX-10). For far-anchored targets the 10-px band spans the whole pane (edge case).

concepts.name: Layering, z-order and drawing behind price
concepts.definition: Z groups in ascending order: bgcolor < fills < plots < hlines < linefills < lines < boxes < labels < tables. Within a group, the last created is on top. Only plot, hline and fill can be reordered. indicator(behind_chart = true), the default, draws all visuals behind the chart bars (visuals/overview.md:36-38, 230-246).
concepts.dolRole: WHERE: overlays must not dim the target, and candles must stay readable inside zones.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Official docs. The reference shows pure #FFFFFF candle pixels inside its iFVG box, so it also draws behind the bars.
concepts.engineNotes: Line 31 uses the default behind_chart (correct; keep it). The glow and tether (lines) sit under iFVG (t75, 1613), LVN (t91, 2276-2286) and ghost (t94, 1254) boxes where they overlap, typically during iFVG retests. The table (z 9) can cover the DOL label.

concepts.name: Visual hierarchy, pre-attentive pop-out and clutter
concepts.definition: Visual weight (contrast x area x saturation) should rank elements by importance. A unique-luminance or unique-hue target is found pre-attentively in under about 200-250 ms, independent of the number of distractors. Clutter (feature congestion, edge density, colour variability) slows search. Engine on black: core 18.9:1 > glow 11.9 > tether 7.5 > iFVG border 3.4 > DOL border 2.15 > fills 1.1-1.4.
concepts.dolRole: WHERE: one committed, pre-attentively salient target instead of a menu of levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Healey & Enns 2012 (IEEE TVCG 18(7)); Rosenholtz, Li & Nakano 2007 (J Vision 7(2):17), replicated with eye movements. Tsai, Klayman & Hastie 2008: more information raised confidence more than accuracy (3 studies; football numbers via a blog). Strong as perception mechanisms, moderate in transfer.
concepts.engineNotes: Extras are off by default (162-171, 203, 210). When they are enabled, LVN #FFC400 (13:1) and the ghost labels compete with the core.

concepts.name: Contrast and theme adaptivity
concepts.definition: WCAG contrast = (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05). Text needs 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text). Graphical objects required for understanding need 3:1 (SC 1.4.11); 'all chart lines' is a conservative practice, not the normative text. Pine: chart.bg_color and chart.fg_color are input color; fg is #0f0f0f on light backgrounds and #dbdbdb on dark ones. The script reloads when the user changes the background (execution_model.md:498). label.style_text_outline can halo text over any background.
concepts.dolRole: WHERE: below 3:1 the target is not perceived on light charts.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Computed: on white, buy #39FF14 is 1.36, the rendered Clean zone 1.04-1.37 and iFVG 1.29/1.89. Light variants #0B7A2E 5.47 and #C8102E 5.88 on white, but only 2.8-3.98 on the dark label and table. Generic from_gradient(0.55 to black) gives at least 5.08 on white for all 25 theme colour values. The manual asks authors to test both light and dark themes (colors.md:394).
concepts.engineNotes: Theme palettes 240-299 are dark-only, with no use of chart.fg_color or bg_color. The white core (2223), transparent-bg labels (1256, 2166, 2189, 2212) and LVN text (2278) are unreadable on white. OSS: 4 of 24 files adapt to the chart theme.

concepts.name: Colour semantics: side, affect and cultural convention
concepts.definition: The engine colours by draw side (above price = buy-side lime, below = sell-side red), not by kind, which is why 'Target: BEFVG' above price is green in the reference. Red carries an affective 'loss' meaning in Western markets. In CN/JP/KR/TW markets red means up.
concepts.dolRole: WHERE and direction at a glance; colour may also shift willingness to act.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bazley, Cronqvist & Mormann 2021 (Mgmt Sci 67(9)): 8 experiments, n = 1,451. About 15-30% less risk-taking (press figure) and about 25% higher risk premium for losses in red; absent in colour-blind subjects, muted in China. Strong in the lab, weak in transfer to a target colour. The red-up convention is widely known, but the source found is a weak explainer.
concepts.engineNotes: Side-coded at 2203, 2154, 2164 and 2183. There is no red-up option for East Asian users.

concepts.name: Colour-vision-deficiency safety and redundant encoding
concepts.definition: Hue-only cues fail for red-green CVD: about 8% of European men and 0.4% of women (4-6.5% of Chinese and Japanese men). Deuteranomaly is about 5% of men; protanopia, deuteranopia and protanomaly about 1% each. Remedy: a blue/orange palette plus redundant cues (position, text, glyph, line style).
concepts.dolRole: WHERE and bias readable for every user.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Birch 2012, JOSA A 29:313-320; U. Arizona and MUN type breakdowns. Simulated bias pair dE: 129.5 normal, about 53 for deuteranomaly (approximation), 17.1 for deuteranopia. The proposed #2F9BFF/#FF8A1F keeps dE 134 under deuteranopia.
concepts.engineNotes: Redundancy comes from position and the BULLISH/BEARISH words. There is no CVD theme or glyph option.

concepts.name: Typography
concepts.definition: v6 sizes accept size.* or int points. Labels: tiny ~7, small ~10, normal 12, large 18, huge 24. Tables and boxes: tiny 8, small 10, normal 14, large 20, huge 36. text_formatting sets bold or italic; text_font_family is default or monospace.
concepts.dolRole: Readability of target name, PoT and bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Official docs (text_and_shapes.md:488-500; label.md:177; table.md:67). The reference's label-to-table text height ratio of 1.2 matches 12/10.
concepts.engineNotes: Clean label size.normal (2226); table size.small in the default font (604-610); Terminal monospace. There is no size input for 4K or mobile screens.

concepts.name: Probability communication (value, precision, horizon, reference class)
concepts.definition: A PoT readout should carry its horizon ('within H bars') and reference class ('K of N similar targets hit'), with precision no finer than the calibration supports. A dual verbal-plus-numeric format improves consistent interpretation.
concepts.dolRole: HOW LIKELY: lets the trader weigh the target correctly.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's natural-frequency figure '7%->45%' is unverified; the meta-analysis gives 4%->24% (McDowell & Jacobs 2017), moderate for our use. Precision is read as confidence (Jerez-Fernandez 2014). Budescu et al. 2014 (24 countries): numbers added to verbal terms raised consistency to about 40% from 26% (secondary source).
concepts.engineNotes: 'PoT: 70.1%' carries no horizon or n (2225), and a reached target shows 95.0% (2067). The tooltip lacks price, horizon and calibration (2206-2209; COMP-4 owns these). Terminal's '70.1% · CORE' is already a dual format.

concepts.name: Uncertainty display, trust and display stability
concepts.definition: Showing forecast uncertainty improves decisions and protects trust when forecasts miss. False alarms (cry-wolf) and unstable displays erode compliance.
concepts.dolRole: HOW LIKELY and trust: about 30% of 70%-PoT targets will miss, and flicker or silent target changes read as false alarms.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Fernandes et al. CHI 2018: quantile dotplot-50 reached 97% of optimal payoff (CI 95-98), +5 pp vs control, with CDFs nearly as good and text worse. Joslyn & LeClerc 2012 (3 experiments): uncertainty forecasts improved decisions and trust and attenuated forecast-error effects. LeClerc & Joslyn 2015: cry-wolf effect. Strong in domain, moderate in transfer.
concepts.engineNotes: The live dolShown (2068) flickers at the minPoT threshold (PENG-4). Clean has no visible calibration record (COMP-4/COMP-5) and no state cues (UX-3).

concepts.name: Timing communication (ETA)
concepts.definition: Empirical median and p80 of bars-to-hit for past hits from a similar ATR distance (+-0.5 ATR, n >= 5), conditional on a hit, with coverage checked by the ledger (about 50% and 80% of hits should arrive by p50 and p80).
concepts.dolRole: WHEN: expected time to reach the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Fernandes 2018 is itself an arrival-time task, so a time band is directly supported. The validity of this tool's ETA is unmeasured, hence the coverage check.
concepts.engineNotes: etaHit is computed at 2117-2126 but shown only in the Terminal HUD (2240). There is no p80 and no calibration, and the Clean right edge (extBars = 20) carries no time meaning.

concepts.name: Tooltips as progressive disclosure
concepts.definition: Keep the chart minimal and put detail on hover: label.new(tooltip) and table.cell(tooltip) (table.md:53, 69). Boxes and lines have no tooltips. Whether mobile shows tooltips is undocumented, so assume it does not; essentials stay in the visible text.
concepts.dolRole: Answers why this target, at what price, by when and how calibrated, without clutter.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Convention. That rollback makes a recreated label a new object every tick, closing an open tooltip, is a hypothesis (text_and_shapes.md:478).
concepts.engineNotes: Label tooltips exist (2206, 2226, 2248). Table cells have none (604-610, 2294-2307).

concepts.name: Right-edge layout, label collisions, clipping and table overlap
concepts.definition: Labels at xR with style_label_left collide when their price gap is less than the label height (2-line normal label ~36 px, about 4-7% of the visible range). The label body (~91 px, about 20 bars) can be clipped at the price scale when the chart's right margin is small. Tables (z 9) can cover labels. Pine cannot read the visible range without reloading on every scroll.
concepts.dolRole: Legibility of the target label and of any optional extras.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner convention. OSS practice either places labels by priority against already-used prices with a minimum gap and drops clashes, or merges labels within 1 ATR. TradingView's default right margin (~10 bars) is unverified. execution_model.md:497 confirms the visible-range reload.
concepts.engineNotes: Secondary (2188), objective (2166), invalidation (2212) and LVN text (2278) all anchor at xR with no de-overlap. No tooltip warns about clipping or table overlap. The Clean default (one label) is unaffected by collisions.

concepts.name: Drawing-object lifecycle
concepts.definition: Limits are 500 lines, boxes and labels, with GC of the oldest, and x <= bar_index + 500. Setters cost about half as much as box.new (official profiler example). On realtime bars, objects created on an unconfirmed update are rolled back. The OSS pattern pre-creates objects with label.new(na, na, '', style = label.style_none), then shows and hides them via setters, style_none and na colours.
concepts.dolRole: Smooth realtime updates and possibly stable hover tooltips.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Cost difference is official. The tooltip benefit is a hypothesis. The hide pattern appears in published v6 OSS (10 of 24 files use setters).
concepts.engineNotes: iFVG boxes use set_right (1638-1641, 2145-2149). The Clean zone, 5 glow lines, tether and label (8 objects) are deleted and recreated every tick (2132-2141, 2214-2226). Caps are safe.

concepts.name: Data Window and plot formatting
concepts.definition: plot(format, precision 0-16) sets the digits in the Data Window, status line and scale. plot display is input plot_display, so an input can switch on a price-scale tag (COMP-7).
concepts.dolRole: Clean numeric readouts for score, PoT and D.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Official docs (mechanism); the benefit is weak.
concepts.engineNotes: Plots 2444-2448 have no precision and inherit the symbol's (5 decimals on FX). 'DOL Price' leaks filtered targets (COMP-2).

concepts.name: Bias table design and alignment cue
concepts.definition: Two-column Timeframe | Bias table. Reference colours: header #25272C / #D5D5D6, body #1B1F24, grid #3A3C43, frame #303136, BULLISH #00C864, BEARISH #E63C3C, 20 px rows. Usage doctrine: act when the Execution TF bias aligns with the HTF bias.
concepts.dolRole: A bias and direction filter for the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Alignment is practitioner doctrine. B's histogram confirmed the colours. BEARISH at 4.00:1 is faithful to the reference.
concepts.engineNotes: The look is exact (293-299, 2294-2307). There is no alignment cue, no cell tooltips, no size option and no ledger split by alignment.

concepts.name: Autoscale compression
concepts.definition: Drawings far from price widen the auto-scale range and squash candles; the user's fix is 'Scale price chart only'.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps the price action readable around the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView help 43000762934 (via competitors.final.md); mechanism only.
concepts.engineNotes: LVN (2251-2287), objective and reach bands are not distance-capped; COMP-7 owns the fix.

concepts.name: Target state communication
concepts.definition: States: draw-side active, counter-draw active, reached (intrabar), stale (age > H with no hit), filtered (PoT < min), none. Each should be visible without relying on hue.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents silent state changes from reading as 'the target jumped' and flags weaker counter-draw picks.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Visibility of system status is a heuristic. The cost of silent changes to trust is supported indirectly by Joslyn & LeClerc (moderate). A counter-draw ledger split would measure it.
concepts.engineNotes: Terminal shows COUNTER-DRAW and SWEPT (2237). Clean shows counter-draw only in the tooltip (2206), a reached target as 95% (2067), and stale or filtered states silently.

concepts.name: Confidence encoded as visual weight
concepts.definition: Map PoT to visual weight, bounded so low-confidence targets stay visible. Use transparency at fixed widths: blur/halo width reads as MORE uncertainty, and saturation is a poor cue.
concepts.dolRole: HOW LIKELY, pre-attentively.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Correction to A: MacEachren et al. 2012 rated fuzziness and location most intuitive, transparency only moderate and saturation low, using point symbols, not lines. Downgraded from moderate to weak.
concepts.engineNotes: Terminal maps score to zone opacity (2228); Clean uses fixed weights.

concepts.name: Aesthetic-usability and premium perception
concepts.definition: Users rate attractive interfaces as more usable (a halo effect). Aesthetics have a small positive effect on objective performance, and the perceived-usability effect fades with longer use.
concepts.dolRole: Adoption and trust, not accuracy: a faithful, clean look buys the time the ledger needs to show whether there is an edge.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kurosu & Kashimura 1995 (252 participants, 26 ATM layouts), Tractinsky 1997 CHI (3 experiments), and the Thielsch et al. 2019 meta-analysis (25 studies, 101 effects, about 3,025 participants), all via search summaries.
concepts.engineNotes: Clean matches the reference, but the legend clutter and light-theme failure undermine the premium perception.

concepts.name: Settings defaults as product decisions
concepts.definition: Most users never change the defaults, so the defaults are the product: style, extras, theme, filters, extension and legend.
concepts.dolRole: Indirect: what most users see and trade from.
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView publishing guidance asks authors to show default behaviour (publishing.md:124). The default effect is established in other domains, not re-verified here.
concepts.engineNotes: The defaults are sensible (Clean, extras off, Classic, minPoT 0, extBars 20). Legend clutter and the light-theme failure are on by default.

proposals.title: Legend and settings hygiene with the corrected active map: display.none, inline alignment, group order, tooltips, text-size inputs, Data Window precision
proposals.rationale: About 411 characters of input values print beside the name, while the reference legend shows only the name: the most visible deviation and the cheapest fix. It is rare even in modern OSS (0 of 24 files hide inputs). Greyed-out irrelevant inputs and session/timezone tooltips prevent silent misconfiguration that corrupts PDH, Asia and killzone levels. Same fix as COMP-1/PENG-1: implement once, using this corrected dependency map.
proposals.spec: (1) Add the literal display = display.none to all 76 input.int/float/string/session/timeframe calls on lines 60-229, including tz, the sessions and theme. (2) Inline rows c1-c4 (230-237): the first input keeps a combined title (e.g. 'Custom · Buy / Sell-side'), the second gets "", which fixes CW10026 under the October 2026 alignment model; put one tooltip on the second input. (3) active map, verified by grep: cHTF/cSTF/cEXE = modeIn == 'Custom'; sessAs/sessLo/sessNA = useSess; obLook = useOB or useBRK (1669, 1712); obQMin = useOB; useBRK has no dependency; fvgQMin = useFVG; fvgMin stays active (feeds the iFVG tracker at 1877/1887 and the HTF FVG at 939); ifvgMaxIn/ifvgMax = showIFVG; trackAge stays active (iFVG alert, breakers); lvnHours/lvnRows = showLVN or usePathVP; lvnThr/lvnN = showLVN; ghostMax = showGhost; hudSize = uiStyle == 'Terminal'; priorM = potModel == 'Empirical'; tablePosIn = showTable; warmup = accView != 'Off' or useCal; accView stays active; uAbove..uText = theme == 'Custom'. (4) Group order: move only the input lines of DOL Display, PoT, Theme and Panel up after Trading Mode, since group order follows each group's first input; derived tfH/tfS/tfE and the colour switches stay where they are. Rename the internals 'Advanced · Engine/Scoring/Order Flow/Accuracy' and place them last. Optional advOn = input.bool(false, 'Unlock advanced tuning') used as active on about 40 internals. (5) Tooltips: sessions 'HHMM-HHMM in Session Timezone; Asia crosses midnight'; tz as an IANA name; weights 'normalised, only ratios matter'; potH 'chance of touch within N chart bars'; extBars 'reference look 20; if the label is cut off at the price scale, scroll left or raise the chart's right margin'; tablePosIn 'move the panel if it covers the target label'. (6) lblPt = input.int(12, 'Label Text (pt)', 6, 24) used as size at 2226; tblPt = input.int(10, 'Panel Text (pt)', 6, 20) used as text_size in f_cell/f_cellC (604-610); the defaults equal size.normal/size.small. (7) Plots 2445-2448: precision = 1 (score, PoT, hit %) and 2 (D).
proposals.risk: Users lose inputs in the legend. An active argument that names a later input would be a forward reference; all of these name earlier inputs. Run pine_parse.sh. Zero effect on selection.

proposals.title: Theme-aware rendering for light charts: auto detection, two colour roles, a light glow recipe and neutral text
proposals.rationale: On white every Clean element is 1.04-1.37:1, so the target is invisible. The manual names light and dark as the most common themes and asks authors to test both. A single swap (COMP-8 v1) breaks the dark label and table, where the light variants reach only 2.8-3.98:1, so graphics and text need separate colour roles. The docs confirm that a background change reloads scripts using chart.fg_color (execution_model.md:498), which resolves A's open risk.
proposals.spec: After line 299: bgMode = input.string('Auto', 'Chart Background', ['Auto','Dark','Light'], group = G_COL, display = display.none); lightBg = bgMode == 'Light' or (bgMode == 'Auto' and chart.fg_color == #0f0f0f) (input-qualified; chart_information.md:430-449). Declare f_onLight(color x) => color.from_gradient(0.55, 0.0, 1.0, x, #000000) right there, not in PURE HELPERS (398+), because there are no forward references; it gives at least 5.08:1 on white for all 25 theme colour values. Graphics roles: gAbove = lightBg ? (classic ? #0B7A2E : f_onLight(cAbove)) : cAbove; gBelow likewise with #C8102E; gIBull #00875A; gIBear f_onLight; gLVN #9A6B00; gGhost #5F6B7A. Use g* for the zone, glow, tether, Clean iFVG colour ic (1609-1613), ghosts (f_ghost calls 1586/2023), LVN (2276-2286), the pool/objective/secondary/invalidation lines, and the text of the transparent-bg labels (1256, 2166, 2189, 2212). Optionally use label.style_text_outline with color = chart.bg_color for a halo (verify the outline semantics in the editor). Keep c* neon for the Clean label text (2225), the table (2294-2307) and the Terminal HUD panel. Light glow (replaces 2219-2223 when lightBg): halo g t85 w8, g t70 w4, core g t0 w2, no white filament; fill t90, border t45, tether t20. On white: core 5.47, tether 3.75, border 2.57, fill 1.15. iFVG light: fill t80, border t40. Optional panelMode 'Reference dark'/'Match chart', where the latter uses color.new(chart.bg_color, 10) and chart.fg_color text.
proposals.risk: Gradient backgrounds return the midpoint (the override covers this). About 8 extra colour variables. The glow layer count differs (5 vs 3), which matters for UX-7.

proposals.title: Clean label state grammar (counter-draw, reached, stale) with confirmed-bar visibility and a counter-draw ledger split
proposals.rationale: Clean hides states a trader must know: counter-draw looks like draw-side, a reached target reads 95.0%, and over-horizon targets look fresh. Silent changes and flicker cost trust (Joslyn & LeClerc; cry-wolf). The split tests the decision rule 'draw-side first, counter-draw fallback' with data. Coordinates with COMP-4 (reached text, tooltip) and PENG-4 (visibility hysteresis).
proposals.spec: Clean branch 2214-2226. Counter-draw (activeCtr, 2029): line 1 'Target: BSL ⚠', tether line.style_dotted, tooltip first line 'Counter-draw: order flow D = -0.42 points the other way'. Reached (sweptNow): line 2 '✓ Reached', core c t0. Stale (bar_index - activeSince > H, no hit): line 2 'PoT: 41.0% · late', textcolor color.new(c, 35). Visibility: adopt PENG-4, where var bool showC is updated on confirmed bars with a 2-pp hysteresis around minPoT and used at 2202 instead of the live dolShown; the label text stays live. Ledger: add bool ctr = false to Trial (375-396) and set ctr = activeCtr in f_openTrial (1426); the global is declared at 1038, before the function, and assigned at 2029, before the call at 2045. In f_book (1461) add var array<float> ctrSt(6): [n, k, ΣpBase] for draw-side and for counter-draw. Tooltip line 'Counter-draw targets here: 18 of 47 hit (38%) · edge -2.1 pp vs random'; Terminal Full row CTR/DRAW. The glyph ⚠ already renders (2237, 2306).
proposals.risk: The ⚠ suffix changes the reference text in the counter-draw state only. The stale threshold equal to H is a choice.

proposals.title: Bias table: alignment cue, cell tooltips, optional target and accuracy rows, and a ledger split by MTF alignment
proposals.rationale: The spec's usage advice is to act when the Execution bias aligns with the HTF bias, but the table never states alignment or ties it to the target, and nobody knows whether aligned targets do better on this symbol. The split turns the doctrine into per-symbol evidence. The cell tooltips here supersede COMP-4 item 5.
proposals.spec: At commit (after 2029): bH = htfBias != 0 ? htfBias : htfIB; bE likewise for exe; algn = na(activeLv) ? 0 : (bH == side and bE == side) ? 1 : bH == -side ? -1 : 0. Pass it to f_openTrial(activeLv, algn) and add int algn to Trial. In f_book accumulate var array<float> alSt(9): [n, k, ΣpBase] for aligned, neutral and against. Terminal Full: 'ALIGN +9.2pp (n 88) · AGAINST -1.0pp (n 41)'. Clean: tblExtra = input.string('None', 'Clean Table Extras', ['None', 'Target row', 'Target + Accuracy'], display = display.none). Target row: 'DOL' | '✓ ▲ BEFVG' (✓ aligned, ⚠ against) in the side colour. Accuracy row: 'Hit 62% · Edge +8pp' from stK, stN, stPE; 'calibrating' under 20 trials. f_cellC gains string tip = '', passed as table.cell(..., tooltip = tip). TF tooltip: 'Swing BULL (body break of X) · internal BEAR · price at 62% of range (premium)' from htfRH/htfRL/htfIB and the other TFs; build it only at barstate.islast.
proposals.risk: Extra rows deviate from the 3-row reference, so they are off by default. The split needs enough trials per class; show n.

proposals.title: Time projection (WHEN): ETA band in the tooltip or as markers, plus an ETA coverage check in the ledger
proposals.rationale: The engine already computes the median bars-to-hit for similar distances (2117-2126), but Clean never shows it. Showing a p50-p80 band matches the closest experimental evidence (Fernandes 2018, a bus-arrival-time task). The ledger can verify calibration: about 50% and 80% of hits should arrive by p50 and p80.
proposals.spec: Helper after dHit (1075) and before f_openTrial (1426): f_eta(float dNow) collects ttHit where |dHit - dNow| <= 0.5; float p50 = na, p80 = na; if sim.size() >= 5 then p50 := sim.median() and p80 := sim.percentile_linear_interpolation(80); return [p50, p80]. Use an if-block, not a tuple ternary. It replaces the loop at 2120-2126. etaMode = 'Off'/'Tooltip' (default)/'Marker'. Tooltip: 'Typically reached in 6-14 bars (≈30-70 min) when reached · n 37'. Marker: dotted vertical lines at bar_index + min(500, p50) in color.new(c, 40) and at p80 in color.new(c, 70) across the zone height; extend the zone's right edge to p80 if that is beyond extBars. Ledger: Trial gets eta50/eta80 set in f_openTrial via f_eta(d0) (one loop of <= 300, at commit only); in f_book on a hit, etaSt += [1, bars <= eta50, bars <= eta80]. Terminal Accuracy row 'ETA cover 48% / 79% (n 63)'.
proposals.risk: The ETA is conditional on a hit and must say 'when reached'. It needs n >= 5. Bars are not clock time (use COMP-4's f_dur with '≈'). Marker mode changes the look, so the default is Tooltip.

proposals.title: Reference-fidelity regression baseline and core-line correction (white t15 -> t10, keep behind_chart default)
proposals.rationale: The user's hard requirement is that Clean looks like the screenshot. Under Pine's real z-order (box fill above lines) the engine's core renders #D3FACB, dE 6.7 from the reference's #DDFCD8; t10 gives dE 0.9. Every other element is exact and should be protected against later 'improvements'. The reference also draws candles over its zones, as the default behind_chart = true does.
proposals.spec: (1) Line 2223: color.new(color.white, 15) -> color.new(color.white, 10). (2) Add a comment block above 2214 listing the regression constants with their measured pixels: fill t92 #041402; glow (90,10) #0A2B04, (80,7) #135508, (60,4) #229A0D, (30,2) #32E113; core white t10 1 px #DDFCD8; border t75 dashed; tether t30 dashed to the centre at xR; label #161616 12 pt centred style_label_left at bar_index + 20; iFVG #00B478 t75/t50 -> #002D1E/#00704B; table #1B1F24/#25272C/#3A3C43/#303136, text 10 pt. (3) Keep indicator() without behind_chart (default true), with a comment explaining why. (4) Regression check: screenshot the engine on a black chart and compare the zone profile with study/ux_b_tools/sample_ref.py; any row off by more than dE 3 is a regression.
proposals.risk: None functionally; the core becomes about 2% brighter.

proposals.title: Persistent DOL drawing objects updated with setters (implement as PENG-5, with the OSS hide pattern)
proposals.rationale: Clean deletes and recreates 8 objects on every realtime tick (2132-2141, 2214-2226). Setters cost about half of box.new (official profiler). Because of rollback, a recreated label is a new object every update, which plausibly closes an open hover tooltip (hypothesis). Published v6 OSS creates labels with na coordinates and hides them with style_none, which answers PENG-5's feasibility question.
proposals.spec: type DolGfx (box zone, line teth, label lbl, array<line> glow); create it once with var: label.new(na, na, '', style = label.style_none), box.new(na, na, na, na, bgcolor = na, border_color = na), and 5 line.new(na, na, na, na). Show on barstate.islast: box.set_lefttop/set_rightbottom/set_bgcolor/set_border_color/set_border_style; line.set_xy1/set_xy2/set_color/set_width/set_style; label.set_xy/set_text/set_textcolor/set_color/set_style(label.style_label_left)/set_tooltip/set_size. Hide via a single f_hideDol(): label.set_text('') plus set_style(label.style_none), box set_bgcolor(na) and set_border_color(na), line.set_color(na). Light mode (UX-2) uses 3 glow lines and sets the other 2 to na colour. Keep dB/dLn/dLb for the variable-count extras. Validate with the Pine Profiler.
proposals.risk: Stale objects if a hide path is missed; route every non-show branch through f_hideDol. The UX benefit is unverified.

proposals.title: Layering and right-edge management: fade overlapping iFVG fills, merge colliding labels into the tooltip, table-overlap guard
proposals.rationale: Lines render below boxes, so iFVG (t75), LVN and ghost boxes dim the DOL glow and tether during the iFVG retests the product promotes. Optional right-edge labels overprint each other, and a top-right table (z 9) can cover the DOL label. OSS practice drops or merges labels rather than staggering them, and staggering pushes labels further into the clip zone.
proposals.spec: Add color col to Zone (351-362), set to ic at creation (1609-1621). In the barstate.islast loop (2145-2149): dolVis = showDOL and not na(activeLv) and dolShown; ov = dolVis and z.top >= activeLv.bottom and z.bottom <= activeLv.top; onTeth = dolVis and z.top >= min(close, price) and z.bottom <= max(close, price); box.set_bgcolor(z.bx, color.new(z.col, ov ? 92 : onTeth ? 85 : base)), with base 75 for Classic Clean, else 85; v6 lazy 'and' prevents na access. Skip LVN zones overlapping the active zone (2276-2286). Label manager when extras are on: global minSep = 0.05 * (ta.highest(high, 150) - ta.lowest(low, 150)); place in priority order DOL > invalidation > objective > secondaries; a label within minSep of a placed one is dropped and its text is appended to the DOL tooltip ('Also near: PDH 5,131.5'), while its line stays. Table guard: if tablePosIn is a top position and the DOL price is within 2·minSep of ta.highest(high, 150), add 'Panel may cover the label: move it to Bottom Right' to the label tooltip. Never use chart.*_visible_bar_time, which reloads on every scroll (execution_model.md:497).
proposals.risk: minSep is a zoom-dependent heuristic. The fade alters the look only while an iFVG overlaps the target.

proposals.title: Colour conventions: colour-blind theme, direction glyph and an East-Asian red-up option
proposals.rationale: About 2% of men (dichromats) see the bias pair at dE 17 and about 5% (deuteranomaly) at dE ~53. Red carries a documented risk-aversion effect in the lab. In CN/JP/KR/TW market convention red means up, so a red sell-side target reads backwards there. All three are cheap and leave the default untouched.
proposals.spec: Theme 'Colorblind' added to the options at 229 and to each switch (240-292): above/bull #2F9BFF, below/bear #FF8A1F, LVN #F0E442, ghost #7D8799, panel #0B0F14, text #E6EDF3. Computed: deutan dE 134, protan dE 119; 6.25/7.68 on the label and 5.72/7.02 on the table. Light variants with UX-2: #0072B2/#C25400 (5.19/4.60 on white). glyph = input.bool(false, 'Direction Glyph in Label') prefixes '▲ '/'▼ ' to Clean line 1, forced on when the theme is Colorblind. redUp = input.bool(false, 'Red = up (East Asian convention)', group = G_COL): after the theme switches, reassign the swapped pairs (cAbove <-> cBelow, cIBull <-> cIBear) with := at global scope, since they are plain, non-const globals.
proposals.risk: None to the default theme. The red-up swap must be applied before any derived colour (cLblBg etc. do not depend on side colours).

proposals.title: Confidence-weighted glow (bounded, transparency only; reference look at PoT >= 70%)
proposals.rationale: Clean renders a 35%-PoT target as brightly as an 85% one. Transparency is a moderately intuitive uncertainty cue. Blur or halo width reads as more uncertainty, so widening the glow for high PoT would point the wrong way (MacEachren 2012). The cue is bounded and keeps the reference look for high-PoT targets.
proposals.spec: confGlow = input.bool(false, 'Confidence-Weighted Glow', group = G_DOL). g = na(activePoT) ? 1.0 : f_clamp((activePoT - 0.40) / 0.30, 0.0, 1.0). Outer-layer transparencies 90 + 6(1-g), 80 + 10(1-g), 60 + 15(1-g) at unchanged widths; the t30 layer and the core stay unchanged, so the line stays crisp and above 3:1. color.new accepts a float transp (color.md:116). Applies to the dark recipe (2219-2221) and to the UX-2 light halo. Never vary width or saturation.
proposals.risk: Low-PoT targets look dimmer but never vanish. Off by default for exact fidelity. The evidence comes from point symbols, not lines.

result.summary: Almost every tested ICT/SMC "magnet" claim reduces to geometry. B re-checked the key sources: Nordman FVG 73.0% vs 72.9% and OB 73.7% vs 73.7% against random levels, Trader Markus S&P 69% vs 69%, Barot about +5 pp reaction with no tradeable edge, and Tangirala's 44 SMC detectors, none of which beats random. Base rates are pure Brownian first passage. With ATR ≈ 1.4-1.6σ, `2Φ(−κd/√H)` reproduces the measured 75-80%, 54-62% and 39-47% touch rates at 1, 2 and 3 ATR within 30 bars. Random levels are touched within 300 bars 87%, 81% and 68% of the time at 2, 3 and 5 ATR, so "eventually swept" is nearly vacuous. The engine's ledger is leak-free, and its distance-, side- and regime-matched baseline is the right kind. Four readouts are biased by construction: ETA|hit (8.7 vs 22.4 bars at 2 ATR, in theory), heat over hits only, the EV built from decided races, and the raw L50. B's new real-data test (288 null and 96 informed paths) shows the EDGE verdict fails in two separate ways. Peeking at z ≥ 2 gives a false "✓" on 13.5% of paths. Even a proper anytime-valid boundary gives 4.5%, and 23% for busy-hour pickers, because the baseline is miscalibrated by clock, volatility state and roll gaps, all of which are direction-free. A same-distance mirror control cuts false alarms to 0.3-0.7% and raises power on side skill (5m: 44% to 71%), so the mirror plus a three-way materiality verdict (BEATS / NO MATERIAL EDGE / INCONCLUSIVE) is the core fix. After Holm correction, only EQ survives among the scoring pillars. Confluence, tier and tests are "unsupported", not "contradicted" as A said, while D-first selection does lose 9-12 pp against geometry. B found a new visual survivorship trap: targets out-scored by a same-side challenger leave no ghost, and "SWEPT" ghosts carry no time to hit. B also removed intrabar ordering as a risk: double-touch bars are 0.6-1.7% of trials, the engine's bar-colour rule is right 80-88% of the time (TradingView's rule 72-78%), and the R bias is at most 0.02R. The defensible product claim is a calibrated touch probability for a sensibly chosen destination, not a predictive edge. The 10 proposals make every number honest and test the scoring against strong naive selectors.

concepts.name: Stop clusters beyond extremes / round numbers (liquidity mechanism)
concepts.definition: Stop-loss orders cluster just beyond round numbers and old extremes (stop-buys in 01-10 above '00', stop-sells in 90-99 below); take-profits cluster exactly at the round number. Crossing a stop cluster triggers a short cascade.
concepts.dolRole: Explains why pools beyond swing highs/lows are plausible targets and why trade-through accelerates price (15 min to 2 h); it is a mechanism, not a magnet claim.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2003 (SR125 re-fetched by B): about 9,700 RBS orders, Sep 1999-Apr 2000. Take-profits 9.3% at 00 (stops 4.4%, uniform 1%). Stop-buys 14.4% vs 7.4% (p 0.029); stop-sells 10.0% vs 5.1% (p 0.064, marginal). Osler 2005: +0.27 to +2.35 hundredths of a percent from 15 min to 2 h, mixed signs at 1 day. [B-CORRECTED] A's '8.7% of all orders at 00' is not in the paper.
concepts.engineNotes: Pools beyond pivots with a strict trade-through hit rule (623-624). No round-number source.

concepts.name: Pools as magnets (reach beyond geometry)
concepts.definition: Claim: an unswept BSL/SSL/PDH/session extreme is reached within H more often than a random level at the same distance, side and regime.
concepts.dolRole: Would justify ranking pools above plain distance for WHERE.
concepts.evidenceNotes: External pools −0.14/−0.27 logit vs random (Holm p 0.07, so not significant). PDH/PDL take rates within ±3 pp of a day-bootstrap null on 7 markets. [B-CORRECTED] Unsupported, not 'less than random'.
concepts.engineNotes: Tier adds density (1.2·tier, 682, f_tierW 506-516) and confluence weight 15 (674-680, 143), asserting an unmeasured magnet effect. Self-confluence: key pools match their own anchors (1793-1799 vs 1931).

concepts.name: Equal highs/lows (EQH/EQL)
concepts.definition: Two or more pivots within eqTol (0.10 ATR), merged into one pool that moves to the outermost print.
concepts.dolRole: Small positive modifier on reach for WHERE.
concepts.evidenceNotes: +0.08/+0.29 logit (5m/1h). The only pool feature surviving Holm correction (1h, p 0.007; calib_ml B).
concepts.engineNotes: eqCount ×0.9 in density (682); f_mergeAt. The weight is hand-set, not learned.

concepts.name: Sweep → reversal (turtle soup / raid-and-reverse)
concepts.definition: Price trades through a pool and closes back inside within 1-2 bars; the claim is that it then runs to the opposite pool.
concepts.dolRole: Would flip the draw side after a raid (WHICH side next).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Post-sweep ±1 ATR race 0.497-0.510 for hold and reject alike (quant_regime). Mahadzva SSRN abstract re-fetched: 65 of 66 folds favour continuation in G10 FX (weak-moderate preprint). Mesfin MNQ grabs: gross 0.2-0.8 pts either way, below a 2-pt friction; the T-stats are net of friction. Open-source 1m gold/BTC/ETH test: −0.13 to −0.59 R net.
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt (1579-1582) adds +tier for a raid that holds and −tier for one that rejects into D, without support.

concepts.name: FVG fill / magnet
concepts.definition: 3-candle gap (low > high[2], engine gates fvgMin 0.15 ATR plus quality); claim: price returns to fill it more often than a same-size random zone at the same distance.
concepts.dolRole: Array targets for WHERE.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Re-fetched by B. Nordman: 73.0% vs 72.9% (38,114 vs 380,599, ES/NQ/6E/6A). Trader Markus S&P daily: bullish 69% vs 69%, bearish 81% vs 72%. ict_pd B replicated the null.
concepts.engineNotes: FVG targets with a quality gate (1867-1887); touch hit rule. Fine as a level source; needs no magnet bonus.

concepts.name: FVG / CE reaction
concepts.definition: Price reacts at the gap or its 50% midpoint; edge ratio = average MFE ÷ average MAE after a fill.
concepts.dolRole: Timing/turn points, not reach.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Nordman (re-fetched): +3.7% at 5 min, +2.5% at 15 min, −0.2% at 1 h, −0.9% at 1 day; red after costs. Barot (re-fetched): ≈ +5 pp vs random, PF 2.4 → 1.0 on 1-minute data.
concepts.engineNotes: The engine targets arrays; it does not trade reactions.

concepts.name: iFVG polarity flip
concepts.definition: A body close through an FVG inverts it into opposite S/R; retests are claimed to hold.
concepts.dolRole: Continuation retest zones shown to the trader.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Trader Markus (re-fetched): 38% vs 38% and 47% vs 47% random. ict_pd B: first retest holds 49-50% (n ≈ 25,000).
concepts.engineNotes: iFVG tracker and boxes; no retest statistic against random.

concepts.name: Order blocks / breakers
concepts.definition: OB = last opposite candle before the displacement leg that broke structure; breaker = failed OB that took liquidity.
concepts.dolRole: Array targets for WHERE.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Nordman (re-fetched): 73.7% vs 73.7% revisit (10,986 touches); edge +4.8%/+3.3% at 1/5 min; after costs −$24 ES, −$17 6E, −$15 6A, NQ ≈ +$0.82. Breakers untested.
concepts.engineNotes: OB/breaker targets with quality gates; no evidence-based prior.

concepts.name: Killzone volatility (timing)
concepts.definition: Volatility concentrated at session opens (Asia 20-00, London 02-05, NY AM 07-10 ET).
concepts.dolRole: WHEN: speed of reach and PoT within H depend on the volatility clock.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ES 5m variance at 09:30 is 4.7× the mean and 0.20× at 23:30; 2.1-4.0× peak/quiet across 10 instruments (Andersen-Bollerslev; quant_pot; ict_time).
concepts.engineNotes: Used for hysteresis (kzHx, 976) and affinity. PoT uses a trailing 50-bar σ (916) and no clock.

concepts.name: Session raid affinities
concepts.definition: Fixed ×1.05-1.20 multipliers on session/PD pools in killzones (London raids Asia, NY raids London/PD).
concepts.dolRole: WHICH key level is targeted per session.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Within ±3 pp of a clock-matched null; exception: the opposite Asia-range side on index futures, +3.5-6.2 pp (session_stats).
concepts.engineNotes: f_kzAff 597-602 applied unconditionally at 1941.

concepts.name: AMD / Power of 3 / Judas swing
concepts.definition: London breaches one side of the Asia range by δ (10 NQ pts, before 04:00 ET) and closes back inside before 05:00; claim: NY delivers to the opposite side. Tested outcome: the 16:00 close vs the Asia midpoint.
concepts.dolRole: Directional bias and timing for the NY session.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Taylor 2026 (re-read by B), N = 484: bullish 46.9%, bearish 39.9% (inverted). Trend-aligned 61.6/70.8%, opposed 29.6/24.8%. 57% of targets delivered before 09:40; 6 valid trades in 4 years.
concepts.engineNotes: Not implemented; do not add it as a directional rule.

concepts.name: Structure-based draw vector (BOS/CHoCH)
concepts.definition: sV = 0.5·HTF + 0.3·STF + 0.2·exe internal bias, blended with displacement and liqEvt; dirSide from |D| ≥ 0.35; draw-side-first selection.
concepts.dolRole: Chooses WHICH side's liquidity is targeted.
concepts.evidenceNotes: D-first 0.550-0.652 vs geometry 0.645-0.706 (−9 to −12 pp). The gated D agrees with geometry on 99.5% of races. Displacement and NR7 continuation races 0.48-0.52 (quant_regime B).
concepts.engineNotes: 1892-1895, 1975, 2012 (2× side-flip hysteresis), counter-draw ×0.5 at 693.

concepts.name: Premium/discount
concepts.definition: Above 50% of the dealing range = sell zone; below = buy zone.
concepts.dolRole: Bias for which side to target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No ICT statistics. The academic analogue (52-week high, George & Hwang 2004) shows continuation, the opposite.
concepts.engineNotes: Dealing-range EQ used as a confluence anchor (1931) and in the Terminal panel.

concepts.name: S/R tests and bounce memory
concepts.definition: b_prev = prior bounces on a level, a bounce/cross being decided against a tolerance stripe with no time limit (literature); engine: approaches within 0.30 ATR without taking the pool.
concepts.dolRole: Whether a tested pool is more or less likely to be traded through within H.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Memory is real at HF: Garzarelli 2014 (re-read) p < 0.0001 at 45-90 s but not at 180 s; Chung & Bellotti (re-read): decays to 0.5 at ≈350-900 min. Direct engine-style test: 5m +0.03, 1h −0.43 logit, Holm p 1.00/0.19. [B-CORRECTED] The sign for strict trade-through within H is weak evidence, not strong.
concepts.engineNotes: +0.35 per test in density (652-656, 682): a positive weight with no support.

concepts.name: Random-walk touch probability in ATR units
concepts.definition: P(touch d within H) = 2Φ(−κd/√H) with κ = ATR/σ_bar ≈ √(8/π) = 1.60 in theory, 1.39-1.54 measured; median time to touch (κd/0.6745)².
concepts.dolRole: The base rate any PoT must match (HOW LIKELY) and the honest ETA.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Brownian 77/56/38% at 1/2/3 ATR vs measured 75-80/54-62/39-47% (A, 7 sets); B's κ measurement; quant_pot ECE 0.004.
concepts.engineNotes: f_pot 434-444 and f_empPoT 1284-1300. The drift term is wrong (QPOT-01).

concepts.name: Recurrence ('eventually swept')
concepts.definition: A 1-D random walk touches every level eventually; a hit with no horizon carries no forecast information.
concepts.dolRole: Defines why every DOL claim needs a horizon H.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B, CME 1h/5m: random levels at 2/3/5 ATR touched within 300 bars 87/81/68%; 60-75% of 30-bar misses are touched by bar 300.
concepts.engineNotes: Ghost '✕ SWEPT' (1586) has no time to hit; the ledger itself uses H correctly.

concepts.name: Gambler's ruin and the finite-horizon race triple
concepts.definition: P(up first) = b/(a+b) for any martingale. Within H there are three outcomes (target first, stop first, neither), given by f_raceH with μ = 0.
concepts.dolRole: Strong naive baseline for WHICH side is taken next; honest race readout.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Real races within 0.4-1.2 pp of b/(a+b) (quant_pot); nearer-first 0.645-0.706 (quant_regime); driftless 1:1.5 win rate 40% (Hall 2026).
concepts.engineNotes: f_race/f_raceH 447-482 exist, but WIN≤H (2246, 2362) is conditional on a decided race, uses drift, and hides 'neither'.

concepts.name: Martingale expectancy (optional stopping / Wald)
concepts.definition: For any bounded exit rule E[R] = side·μ·E[τ]/risk; with no drift E[R] = 0 for every target/stop choice.
concepts.dolRole: Model-free test of whether targets pay.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Theory. B, 1-minute truth: random-picker mean R within 2 SE of 0 in 33/36 cells; the exceptions are negative (GC stop gaps); coarse-bar booking bias ≤ +0.02R.
concepts.engineNotes: rOut (1457-1458) and avg R/PF in Full view only (2419-2425); no band, drift adjustment or cost.

concepts.name: Arcsine law for timing of extremes
concepts.definition: The time of a Brownian max on [0,T] has density 1/(π√(t(T−t))); window edges are over-represented.
concepts.dolRole: WHEN: separates real timing effects from arithmetic.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Weekday-of-extreme stats equal a day-order shuffle (session_stats, ict_time).
concepts.engineNotes: No timing claims beyond killzones.

concepts.name: Base-rate trap
concepts.definition: Reporting a hit rate without the expected rate for the same distances.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents mistaking geometry for skill.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Random 1-ATR levels are hit 75-80% within 30 bars.
concepts.engineNotes: EDGE pp shown (2398-2401), but DOL HIT (2393), L50 (2395-2396) and the family rows (2410-2418) are raw.

concepts.name: Survivorship in time-to-hit and adverse excursion
concepts.definition: Statistics over hits only, ignoring censored misses; with a fixed H, Kaplan-Meier equals the empirical CDF of min(T, H+1).
concepts.dolRole: Honest WHEN (ETA) and pain (heat).
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: ETA|hit 9 vs a true median of 19-25 bars at 2 ATR; heat|hit 1.6-2.3 vs 3.2-5.1 ATR for all trials. B: Brownian 8.7 vs 22.4 bars (structural).
concepts.engineNotes: ETA|hit 2116-2127, shown at 2240; heat from maeHit (1481-1483, 2404-2408).

concepts.name: Visual survivorship in the ghost trail
concepts.definition: A chart history that keeps successes and lets failures vanish biases users' judgement of accuracy.
concepts.dolRole: An honest audit of past DOLs by eye.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B's code read plus recurrence data: replaced targets leave no ghost, SWEPT carries no time, ghost boxes start at the level's origin, not the commit bar.
concepts.engineNotes: 1584-1586 and 2021-2023 ghost only swept/ejected/invalidated targets; same-side replacements (2014-2020) vanish; f_ghost anchors at anchorBar (1254).

concepts.name: Decided-race conditioning (EV bias)
concepts.definition: EV = P(win | decided by H)·rr − P(loss | decided) ignores the undecided mass.
concepts.dolRole: Honest trade expectancy.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's MC: shown −0.62R (a = 2R, σ√H = 1R) and −0.97R (3R) while the true E[R] = 0.
concepts.engineNotes: ev at 2245-2246 (HUD) and tEV at 2359 (panel), from f_invalidation (1343-1364) with drift.

concepts.name: Overlap / cluster-robust (batch-means) variance
concepts.definition: Variance of Σ(y − p) for overlapping H-bar windows: blocks keyed by open bar, centred, W ≥ 2H (prefer ≥ 4H or a session), at least about 20 blocks.
concepts.dolRole: Correct uncertainty for every ledger statistic.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A's simulation: engine z sd 0.76 under a seasonal null, +3.3 pp detected 10% vs 30%. B: neighbouring-block covariance ≈ 10% at W = 2H, 4.5% at 4H. Few-clusters bias (Cameron et al. 2008).
