concepts.engineNotes: cluSt 1463-1469: uncentred, booking-keyed, 2H, no block-count guard (about 5 blocks at H = 450).

concepts.name: Baseline miscalibration and the mirror control
concepts.definition: The baseline's bias for the picker's mix of distances, hours, volatility states and sides shifts the excess. Mirror = a level at the same ATR distance on the opposite side, same bar, same hit rule; the paired residual cancels direction-free errors.
concepts.dolRole: Makes EDGE measure skill, not model error.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Baseline off −4 to +1 pp per dataset, ±2-3 pp by clock, +3 to −8 pp by volatility state. B, 288 real null paths: false '✓' with a valid boundary 4.5% one-sample (23% in busy hours) vs 0.7% mirror; power on side skill 44% → 71% (5m).
concepts.engineNotes: No placebo, mirror or baseline check.

concepts.name: Self-normalised symmetric null for paired tests
concepts.definition: Under 'the side label carries no information', D = r − r_mirror is conditionally symmetric, so ΣD is sub-Gaussian with V = ΣD² and no moment assumptions (de la Peña 1999; Howard et al. 2020 Lemma 3(d)).
concepts.dolRole: A rigorous, non-asymptotic anytime verdict for the mirror test.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Theory (lemma re-read by B); B's sim: 0.3% false alarms, power 17%/63% (1h/5m) vs 23%/71% for the centred version.
concepts.engineNotes: Not present; documented as the conservative variant in SKEP-2.

concepts.name: Beta masquerading as skill
concepts.definition: A trend-side bias in a trending sample looks like directional skill.
concepts.dolRole: Separates trend beta from level/side skill.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Always-long vs mirror +8.3 ± 3.9 pp (EURUSD 1h), +10.8 ± 6.2 (GC 1h). Chen et al. 2026: a zero-centred paired test credits exposure as skill in 11.6% of no-skill replications vs 5.3% when composition-matched.
concepts.engineNotes: Regime-split surface (1059-1062, 1284-1300) absorbs it for hits; the R test needs a Wald drift adjustment (missing).

concepts.name: Peeking / anytime-valid inference
concepts.definition: A fixed-α test re-checked continuously inflates false positives. Fix: confidence sequences, e.g. |S| < √((V+ρ)ln((V+ρ)/(ρα²))).
concepts.dolRole: An honest verdict on whether the engine's edge is real.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Johari et al. (re-read): Type I error 'can easily increase fivefold'. B real paths: z ≥ 2 peeking gives a false '✓' on 13.5%, |z| ≥ 2 on 36%. [B-CORRECTED] The '20% → under 5%' figure is vendor-reported.
concepts.engineNotes: z ≥ 2 / z ≥ 1 verdict at 2390, re-evaluated continuously.

concepts.name: Multiple testing / forking paths / α budget
concepts.definition: Many charts × families × settings; the best-looking result is selected. With confidence sequences, split α across claims (Σw ≤ 1) for anytime FWER control.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents users from trusting a lucky chart, row or setting.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Sullivan-Timmermann-White; Bailey MinBTL; Coqueret 4.5 vs 8.2; A: 10 charts → 21% (80% with peeking); best of 45 settings E[max z] 2.21. Benhamou 2026: 94.5% vs 0.0% false family crossings.
concepts.engineNotes: Family rows without correction (2410-2418); f_calMult acts on noisy family rates (1376-1382).

concepts.name: Power, MDE and the three-way materiality verdict
concepts.definition: MDE ≈ (z_crit + z_power)·SE. Verdict: SUPPORTED if the lower bound > 0; REFUTED ('no material edge') only if the upper bound < δ; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.
concepts.dolRole: Distinguishes 'no edge' from 'not measurable'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Active-ledger MDE 5.5-9.5 pp anytime at default depth (A); Darmanin 2026 (re-read): 4 REFUTED, 2 INCONCLUSIVE, 0 SUPPORTED retail families.
concepts.engineNotes: '✕ NO EDGE' printed regardless of MDE (2390).

concepts.name: Destination vs next liquidity
concepts.definition: 'Next taken' is a first-passage question over all pools (nearest first); a destination is the outermost pool of the leg.
concepts.dolRole: Defines what the DOL claims and how it is graded.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional: inner pools on the same side are necessarily taken first.
concepts.engineNotes: Inner-pool penalty ×0.70 (685) targets a destination; the README claims 'most likely drawing to next'; the ledger metric fits a destination.

concepts.name: Look-ahead, repainting and intrabar order
concepts.definition: Future bars in pivots, HTF leakage without [1], unknown intrabar order on OHLC bars, coarse-bar exits.
concepts.dolRole: Validity of every accuracy claim.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gençay 2026: a leaky Sharpe-35 oracle survives DSR/PBO; Mahadzva: a detector bug caught only by eye. B vs 1-minute truth: double-touch bars 0.6-1.7% of trials; engine colour rule 80-88% right vs TradingView 72-78%; R bias ≤ +0.02R.
concepts.engineNotes: Leak-free ledger (1426-1431, 1527-1532, 1549-1557, 2038); [1] + lookahead_on; f_tfSafe; near-optimal O-L-H-C / O-H-L-C rule (1440-1441).

concepts.name: Costs in trade claims
concepts.definition: R and EV are trade claims; friction (spread, commission, slippage) must be subtracted or the readout labelled gross.
concepts.dolRole: Honest 'do these targets pay'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mesfin 2026: gross 0.07-1.50 pts vs a 2-pt friction on MNQ 5m; open-source sweep test: most short-TF edge disappears when cost > 10% of risk.
concepts.engineNotes: rOut and EV are gross; no cost input.

concepts.name: Data integrity (roll gaps)
concepts.definition: Unadjusted continuous futures carry roll gaps that corrupt the excursion surface, σ and every PoT; cue: share of bars with |Δclose| > 4 ATR, or ATR/σ well below 1.4.
concepts.dolRole: Tells the user when PoT and EDGE are unreliable on this chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B: clean CME 1h 0.3-0.5% of bars with > 4-ATR jumps and κ ≈ 1.4; GC 1h 2.2% and κ = 0.86, where the baseline is off −4 pp. TradingView continuous futures are not back-adjusted by default (calib_ml B).
concepts.engineNotes: No warning; calib_ml CAL-10 proposes a surface guard.

concepts.name: In-sample vs forward, and sub-period stability
concepts.definition: Settings were chosen on the same history; only realtime-opened records are out-of-sample. A split-half check discloses one strong period masking weak ones.
concepts.dolRole: An honest statement of how much the ledger can be trusted.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Zhang 2026 (Sharpe ≈ 3 → 0.26 on holdout); Mesfin year-stability failures; the open-source sweep test's variant positive out of sample only, 'reported, not adopted'.
concepts.engineNotes: No forward sub-ledger, split-half row or in-sample disclosure.

proposals.title: Survivorship-free and martingale-consistent readouts (ETA, heat, race triple instead of EV, L50 excess, hit/exp, PoT HIT)
proposals.rationale: Four trader-facing numbers are biased by construction. ETA|hit is 2-3× too optimistic and never says '>H' (Brownian 8.7 vs 22.4 bars at 2 ATR). Heat over hits is about half the real p80 adverse excursion. EV conditioned on decided races shows −0.3 to −1.0R for fair targets. L50 tracks distance.
proposals.spec: State after 1079: ttDist = array.new<int>(4*(H+2)) for buckets 0-1/1-2/2-3/3+ ATR × slot 1..H (hit bar) or H+1 (miss); maeAll (last 300); roll50x (last 50 of y−pBase). In f_book (role 0): bkt = min(3, floor(d0)), slot = y==1 ? max(1, min(bars, H)) : H+1; push mae and residual. Helper f_ttStats(bkt) after f_book returns [median or na (>H), P(T≤H), n]. HUD 2240: 'ETA 19b · 62% ≤H' or 'ETA >30b · 45% ≤H'; while n < 20 fall back to the Brownian median (dNow·atr/(0.6745·potSig))² labelled 'model'. Replace ev/tEV (2245-2246, 2358-2363) by the drift-free triple pT = f_raceH(d, risk, σ, 0, H), pS = f_raceH(risk, d, σ, 0, H), neither = 1−pT−pS. The ledger's observed triple comes from raceSt[0..4] (no new state). heat = maeAll p80 '(all)' (2404-2408). Hit row 'hit / exp' with stPE[4]/nA. L50 = mean of roll50x in pp. Show 'PoT: HIT' when sweptNow (2067).
proposals.risk: Numbers look worse but are true; the tooltip must explain. Compile risk is limited to new arrays and one helper declared after f_book.

proposals.title: Mirror-controlled, anytime-valid EDGE with a three-way materiality verdict, a baseline check and a data-gap cue
proposals.rationale: B measured on 288 real null paths: z≥2 with peeking gives a false '✓' on 13.5% of paths. A valid confidence-sequence boundary alone still gives 4.5% (23% for busy-hour pickers), because the baseline is miscalibrated by clock, volatility state and roll gaps, all direction-free. A same-distance mirror control cuts this to 0.7% (0.3% self-normalised) and raises power on side skill (5m: 44% → 71%). 'NO EDGE' must become an equivalence-style verdict.
proposals.spec: Append `int role = 0` to Trial. Global after 307: blkW = max(2H, min(max(4H, 86400/chartS), calcBars/25)). STATE: var arrays blkE, blkD, blkP, blkN, blkV, blkR; var int jumpN and barN. f_blk(b0) (before f_book) maps open bar → block and grows all arrays. f_csBound(v, ρ, α) = √((v+ρ)·ln((v+ρ)/(ρα²))). f_book replaces cluSt (1463-1469): role 0 adds r = y−pBase to blkE/blkD/blkP, 1 to blkN and p(1−p) to blkV; role 1 subtracts r from blkD, adds it to blkP and adds p(1−p) to blkV; the old stats are guarded by role == 0. Step 20 (2039-2045): the cap becomes max(160, 4H+4); push the DOL Trial plus a mirror Trial.new(lvId = −id−1, side = −side, edge = close − side·d0·atr, pBase = f_potBase(d, −side), liq = same, role = 1). Engine step 0: if inCalc, barN += 1 and jumpN += 1 when |close−close[1]| > 4·atr[1]. f_cluVar(X, gMax) after f_book returns [ΣX, ΣN, centred G/(G−1)Σ(X_g−N_g m)², G] over closed blocks g < gMax = f_blk(bar_index−H). Panel: Δ̄ = 100·S/N, hw = 100·b(V)/N, MDE = 100·(b+0.84√V)/N, n_eff = N·Σp(1−p)/V. Verdict: G < 20 or n_eff < 30 → CALIBRATING; lo > 0 → ✓ BEATS MIRROR; hi < 0 → ✕ WORSE; hi < matPP (new input, default 2 pp) → ✕ NO MATERIAL EDGE; else ~ INCONCLUSIVE (MDE x). Baseline bias = ΣP/(2N); warn '⚠ BASELINE OFF' if |bias| > 2SE and > 2 pp. Warn '⚠ DATA GAPS' if jumpN ≥ 10 and > 1% of barN. The one-sample row becomes 'vs RANDOM', marked UNRELIABLE when either warning is on. ρ = 10; α = 0.05 (0.025 under SKEP-9). Optional rigorous variant: self-normalised V = ΣD_g².
proposals.risk: A genuine pool-magnet effect is credited as edge (intended). Side-asymmetric miscalibration is not cancelled. Open records double. Very long H binds the block count (CALIBRATING with a reason).

proposals.title: Correct the overlap variance: open-keyed, centred, wide blocks with a block-count guard
proposals.rationale: cluSt (1463-1469) is uncentred, booking-keyed and 2H wide. It is conservative under seasonality (z sd 0.76) and detects a +3.3 pp edge 10% vs 30% of the time. It has no guard against few blocks (about 5 at H = 450). A's width rule gave only 2.8 h blocks on 1m charts. It feeds the Wilson design effect and CAL-1/CAL-2.
proposals.spec: Use blkW, f_blk, blkE, blkV and f_cluVar from SKEP-2 (minimal subset if SKEP-2 is deferred). Remove cluSt (1077, 1463-1469). Panel 2384-2389: [sE, nE, vE, gE] = f_cluVar(blkE, f_blk(bar_index−H)); vEdge = na(vE) ? vInd : max(vE, 0.25·vInd); deff = vEdge/vInd for the Wilson CI and z. Show CALIBRATING while gE < 20 ('H too long for the window' when G binds). With calcBars 5000 and H 30 this gives 200-bar blocks on 1m/5m and 120 on 15m-D, so G ≥ 25.
proposals.risk: With few blocks the variance is noisy; the G ≥ 20 gate and the 0.25·vInd floor handle it.

proposals.title: Model-free R-expectancy test with a Wald drift adjustment and an optional cost
proposals.rationale: Under any martingale every target/stop/time-out rule has E[R] = 0. On 1-minute truth, random pickers average −0.03 to +0.03R and the coarse-bar booking bias is ≤ 0.02R. So average R is an edge test with no baseline model, immune to baseline miscalibration and to the decided-race bias. Drift is removed by Wald's identity, and costs decide whether a short-timeframe target pays.
proposals.spec: Trial: append `float mu0 = 0.0`, `int rBars = 0`. Input costTk (G_ACC, default 0 = gross). State driftSt = [ΣΔclose, n], updated at the top of the engine block; sideSt = [long records, all records]. f_openTrial: mu0 = running mean. f_step (1434-1459): after the race block, if race != 0 and rBars == 0 then rBars := bars. f_book role 0: tau = rBars > 0 ? rBars : bars; R_adj = rOut − side·mu0·tau/risk − costTk·mintick/risk, added to blkR[g]. Panel: [sR, nR, vR, gR] = f_cluVar(blkR, gMax) → R̄ ± b(V)/N. Verdict ✓ PAYS / ✕ LOSES / ~ INCONCLUSIVE. Compact row 'R̄ +0.06R ±0.11 (gross) · PF 1.12 · long 62%'. pRace stored at open becomes drift-free (QPOT-01), so f_raceAdj is relative to geometry (CAL-11 gates it).
proposals.risk: On gappy contracts with tight stops the null is E[R] ≤ 0 (GC 5m tight −0.15R), which costs power there. R depends on the invalidation rule (a design choice). Intrabar ordering is not a material risk (B).

proposals.title: Null-default ICT modifiers: unsupported multipliers start neutral and must earn weight
proposals.rationale: Hard-coded modifiers assert effects the evidence does not show: drift in PoT; fixed killzone affinities; tests and tier as magnitude; confluence 15 with self-confluence; liqEvt raid mapping; ungated draw-side-first. Each moves scores by more than the 4-point hysteresis, so each causes target switches with no measured benefit. After Holm correction only EQ survives.
proposals.spec: Default edits: driftW (185) 0.5 → 0; wConf (143) 15 → 5 plus CAL-5 (exclude a level's own anchor); wL (157) 0.30 → 0. New inputs wTests = 0.0 and wTier = 0.4 replace the literals 0.35 and 1.2 at 682. New useKzAff = false gates f_kzAff at 1941 (`lv.mult *= useKzAff ? f_kzAff(kz, lv.src) : 1.0`). The draw vector follows REG-3: it does not steer selection unless it passes the ledger, with a hard ER20 ≥ 0.40 gate as the legacy option. Keep the old constants as scoreOld, computed in evaluate (O(1)), and run it as a SKEP-5 shadow role. Restore old defaults only if the old score wins beyond the anytime bound on most charts.
proposals.risk: Changes which target shows; the brief's 'draw-side first' is preserved as an option and behind REG-3's gate. The reference product markets session confluence, so keep every option.

proposals.title: Honest visual record: audit step line, ghosts for every outcome with time to hit, commit-anchored ghosts
proposals.rationale: Users judge indicators by scrolling history. Today a target replaced by a same-side challenger vanishes without a ghost (2014-2023). '✕ SWEPT' carries no time to hit, although 87% of 2-ATR levels are touched within 300 bars. Ghosts start at the level's origin, not at the commit bar. Failures disappear while successes stay.
proposals.spec: (1) Input showAudit = false (G_GHOST after 211). At 2438-2444 plot activeLv.nearEdge() with style plot.style_steplinebr, colour by side, display = showAudit ? display.all : display.data_window (docs: display is 'input plot_display', style 'input plot_style'). (2) At 1586 the reason becomes '✕ SWEPT ' + (bar_index−activeSince) + 'b' + (≤H ? ' ≤H' : ' >H'). (3) After 2021-2023: if showGhost and curI ≥ 0 and curElig and pick != curI, then f_ghost(old, (pick ≥ 0 ? '↷ REPLACED ' : '⊘ DROPPED ') + age + 'b'). (4) f_ghost gets an `int fromBar` parameter; callers pass activeSince so a ghost spans the bars the engine asserted it. (5) Clean tooltip (2206) adds 'selected N bars ago'.
proposals.risk: Clutter (default off; capped by ghostMax). The DOL Price data-window value changes from price to the near edge; note it in the release notes.

proposals.title: Strong-baseline league: DOL vs NEAREST, GEO (max d·PoT), TREND, RUNNER-UP and OLD-SCORE on the same bars (paired)
proposals.rationale: Beating a random level is a low bar. Pickers' hit rates all match their baselines, but they differ in delivery: max-reach 1.10-1.43 ATR per target, hand score 0.86-1.09, nearest 0.66-0.93. D-first loses 9-12 pp to geometry. A paired Diebold-Mariano-style comparison on identical bars cancels shared-path noise and is the A/B harness for every scoring change.
proposals.spec: At each DOL opening (step 20), one O(pool) pass over levels with minDistATR ≤ dA ≤ maxATR picks: NEAREST (role 2); GEO = argmax dA·f_potBase (3); TREND = nearest on the htfBias side (4, skipped at 0); RUNNER-UP by score (5); OLD-SCORE by scoreOld (6, with SKEP-6). Open a role record even when it equals the DOL, so pairs stay aligned, with its own f_invalidation for R. lvId = −1000000−role so the has-check (2040-2043) ignores it. Flat arrays blkE8/blkR8/blkY8 are indexed g·8+role and grown in f_blk; f_book routes by role and skips the main stats. Cap openT < 512 ('league paused' when full). Full-view rows: 'vs NEAREST Δexc +0.4pp ±3.1 · ΔR +0.03 ±0.09 · ATR 1.02 vs 0.81', with SKEP-3 variance and SKEP-2 bound. Build it on CAL-3's Probe mechanism if CAL-3 lands first.
proposals.risk: Up to five extra f_invalidation calls per opening (negligible). Panel length (Full view only). Overlaps CAL-3, so implement one shared role mechanism.

proposals.title: Honest claims: DOL = destination, PoT = distance probability, PoT filter = distance filter, no 'NO EDGE'
proposals.rationale: The words overstate. The DOL is a destination: inner pools are taken first by design (685). PoT under the empirical model is the random-level touch rate at that distance plus drift. minPoT filters by distance. '✕ NO EDGE' is printed when the edge is merely not measurable. The reference product's 'highly probable target' wording is unfalsifiable.
proposals.spec: README intro: 'highlights the highest-scoring destination for the current leg; inner pools on the way are usually taken first'. PoT label tooltip and potModel tooltip (181-182): 'how often price on this symbol travelled this distance within H bars in the same regime; it measures distance and volatility, not level quality; random levels 1/2/3 ATR away are touched ~75-80/55-60/40-45% within 30 bars'. minPoT tooltip (180): 'filtering by PoT filters by distance'. Accuracy tooltip: 'hit rates are not skill; a random level at the same distance would score the exp figure'. Verdict words only from SKEP-2/4 (BEATS / NO MATERIAL EDGE / INCONCLUSIVE (MDE x)); no verdicts in the Clean style.
proposals.risk: None technical; less 'magical', which is the honest outcome.

proposals.title: Forward-only sub-ledger, split-half stability and in-sample disclosure
proposals.rationale: Historical records are in-sample to settings tuned on the same chart: the best of 45 settings has E[max z] = 2.21 under the null. Only realtime-opened records are out-of-sample, and a settings change resets them. The commonest failure in recent falsification studies is one strong sub-period masking weak ones.
proposals.spec: Trial.fwd = not barstate.ishistory at open. fwSt = [n, k, Σp, ΣR_adj] updated in f_book for role 0. Row 'FORWARD n 9 · hit 56% / exp 51% · R̄ +0.2' or 'waiting for live bars'. Split-half from the block arrays: blocks < gMax/2 vs the rest, row 'HALVES +1.8pp / −0.6pp ✕ unstable'. Global nTuned counts inputs that differ from their literal defaults (wProx, wFresh, wConf, wDens, wDraw, minScore, hyst, maxATR, minDistATR, halfLife, potH, dGate, pivLen, eqTol, fvgQMin, obQMin; all names verified). The ACCURACY header tooltip (2377) states the in-sample caveat.
proposals.risk: Forward n grows slowly and resets on reload. The literal defaults in nTuned must track the inputs (and SKEP-6 changes).

proposals.title: Multiple-comparison discipline: an α budget across panel verdicts, exploratory family/league rows, gated f_calMult
proposals.rationale: Five at-a-glance family/race tests give an 11% chance of a spurious standout at one look, more with peeking; the league adds more. f_calMult tilts families by ±20% on noise. With confidence sequences, splitting α with Σw ≤ 1 bounds the chance of ever a false claim under any dependence and peeking (weighted Ville; PROMOTE: 94.5% vs 0.0% false family crossings).
proposals.spec: Declared budget α = 0.05: mirror edge (SKEP-2) 0.025, R̄ (SKEP-4) 0.025; only these rows carry verdict words. Family and league rows are 'exploratory': 'hit / exp · excess ± band' in neutral colour, with bands from f_csBound(v, 10, 0.05/k). Per-family block array indexed g·4+fam, grown in f_blk and filled in f_book. f_calMult(g) (CAL-1) returns 1.0 unless that family's mirror excess passes its band at α = 0.0125.
proposals.risk: Family multipliers will rarely activate at default depth, which is the honest outcome given the MDE.

extraLenses.title: Option-implied volatility, expected move and event-aware sigma
extraLenses.prompt:
DOMAIN: OPTION-IMPLIED VOLATILITY, EXPECTED MOVE AND EVENT-AWARE SIGMA. The study found that distance and volatility explain almost all of 'which pool is hit next'. The engine's sigma and PoT are backward-looking and time-blind (see ict_time.final.md TIME-3 volatility clock, quant_pot.final.md). quant_regime dismissed implied vol in one line as 'index-specific, monthly horizon', and quant_pot only notes that IV-based touch odds run high. Study forward-looking volatility from options as a PoT input:
- Implied-vol indices reachable from Pine via request.security: VIX, VIX1D, VIX9D, VIX3M, VVIX, VXN, RVX, VXD, OVX, GVZ, MOVE, crypto DVOL/BVIV, CME CVOL, FX vol. Give the exact TradingView tickers, data availability and delay by plan, history length, session coverage and bar alignment.
- Evidence on IV vs realised volatility as a forecaster, with numbers: Christensen & Prabhala 1998; Blair, Poon & Taylor 2001; Busch, Christensen & Nielsen 2011 HAR-IV; Cboe and academic work on VIX1D 2023-26. Cover the variance-risk-premium scaling needed to turn IV into an unbiased sigma, and intraday IV dynamics.
- How to map an index IV onto a futures, ETF, stock or crypto chart: beta and root mapping via syminfo.root / syminfo.type, with a fallback when nothing maps.
- Term-structure signals (VIX1D/VIX, VIX9D/VIX inversion) as an automatic scheduled-event detector, to check or replace the manual FOMC/CPI list (asset_specific ASSET-5, ict_time TIME-8).
- Event-day volatility premia: FOMC, CPI, NFP, earnings.
- Calendar volatility events: OPEX, triple witching, month-end and quarter-end rebalancing, index reconstitution, turn-of-month.
- The options 'expected move' (+/- IV*sqrt(t), straddle-implied) bands: how often price touches them or closes beyond them, compared with ADR-remaining (session_stats) and the Zarattini noise area.
- The market-implied probability of touch (about 2x delta) as an external benchmark for the engine's PoT.
Test on real data: download daily VIX/VIX1D/VIX9D history from Cboe if reachable, and use the local SPX/NQ/BTC files in study/bias_data and the ES/NQ 1h files in study/smt_data/cme. Propose exactly how the engine should blend implied and realised sigma, gated by the ledger's proper scores, with a clean fallback. Say how to make the PoT horizon variance event-aware, and what to display (an expected-move band, an event flag), all within the request budget and the [1]+lookahead_on non-repainting rule.

extraLenses.title: Derivatives positioning and crowding (gamma, open interest, funding, COT)
extraLenses.prompt:
DOMAIN: DERIVATIVES POSITIONING AND CROWDING. Already covered, do not redo:
- strike pinning on expiry (classic_levels P15, asset_specific H3);
- crypto liquidation heatmaps (orderflow_micro B9, a null result).
Study what remains:
- Dealer gamma exposure (GEX), the zero-gamma/flip level, call wall and put wall, vanna and charm flows, 0DTE, and max pain. Give definitions and how vendors compute them.
- Evidence that net dealer gamma changes intraday volatility and mean reversion vs momentum, and therefore which side's liquidity gets taken: Barbon & Buraschi 'Gamma fragility'; Ni, Pearson, Poteshman & White 2021; Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens 2021; Dim, Eraker & Vilkov 2024; the 0DTE literature; the SqueezeMetrics white paper.
- Whether max pain predicts anything. It is likely folklore: test it.
- Futures open interest and how TradingView exposes it (the _OI symbol suffix and the built-in Open Interest indicator).
- Crypto perpetual futures: open interest, funding rate, premium/basis and long/short ratios. Say which TradingView symbols exist and what plan limits apply.
- CFTC Commitments of Traders: TradingView COT symbols or library, and the hedging-pressure evidence (Bessembinder 1992; de Roon, Nijman & Veld 2000).
- Short interest for stocks.
Test the crowded-side hypothesis: does extreme positioning (funding extremes, an OI build, COT extremes) predict which side's stops are run first? Does an open-interest flush at a sweep mark the pool as spent and separate a raid from a breakout?
Also design how to ingest external positioning levels that Pine cannot compute. Users would paste GEX, OI-wall or max-pain levels via input.text_area, date-stamped and auto-expiring. They would form an optional level family that the candidate (shadow) ledger grades per chart before it may affect scoring.
Run tests where data allows: public exchange funding/OI history if reachable, and the local BTC/ES data in study/bias_data, study/session_data and study/smt_data. Propose concrete, ledger-gated, non-repainting designs, and say plainly which ideas are folklore.

extraLenses.title: US market internals and breadth
TradingView-native validation: Strategy Tester, Deep Backtesting, Bar Magnifier, libraries
extraLenses.prompt:
DOMAIN: TRADINGVIEW-NATIVE VALIDATION AND EVALUATION AT SCALE. There is no offline Pine compiler (PineTS is experimental), and the in-script ledger only sees the loaded chart history (5k-40k bars by plan, pine_eng.final.md section 1.8). Per-chart samples are therefore small (see the power/MDE and overlap discussion in skeptic.final.md and calib_ml.final.md). Study how to evaluate the DOL forecasts on TradingView itself at much larger scale:
- A companion strategy() script, or a strategy mode, that turns each committed target into a triple-barrier trade: target limit, invalidation stop, time stop, via strategy.exit, with commission and slippage.
- What the Strategy Tester reports, and its pitfalls when used to evaluate an indicator rather than a trading system.
- Deep Backtesting: history range and plan limits.
- Bar Magnifier (use_bar_magnifier): intrabar resolution of same-bar double touches. Compare with the pine_eng same-bar convention and the hit-rule asymmetry in trade_mgmt.
- Fill assumptions: calc_on_every_tick, process_orders_on_close; strategy.closedtrades.* statistics; exporting the List of Trades.
- Pooled multi-symbol evaluation: request.security over a symbol list, the Pine Screener, running across a watchlist.
- Sharing the engine core between the indicator and the strategy through a Pine library: export/import rules, library limitations, versioning, and what cannot be exported (drawings, inputs, var state).
- A forward-testing protocol on live charts (alert log, Pine Logs export).
- How a published script can present honest, reproducible statistics without breaking the House Rules on performance claims.
Propose a concrete evaluation harness: files, scripts and metrics, scored against the random-level, nearest-pool and mirror baselines the study defined. List any engine refactor it needs (for example, extracting pure scoring and PoT functions into a library) and how it changes the user's experience. Quote the local v6 docs (docsrc mirrors) for every compile-relevant claim.

extraLenses.title: Other retail schools with stop-hunt / next-side claims
extraLenses.prompt:
DOMAIN: OTHER RETAIL TRADING SCHOOLS NOT YET COVERED. Study the schools that are popular with retail traders, are absent from the study so far, and make explicit claims about stop hunts, which side is taken next, or reversal timing:
- Beat The Market Maker / Steve Mauro market-maker method: Asian range, peak formation high/low, three levels of rise/drop, M/W at session extremes, the weekly cycle.
- Stacey Burke: the 3-day and 5-day cycles, first red/green day, inside days, session highs and lows.
- The Strat (Rob Smith): the 1/2/3 bar typology, 2-1-2 and 3-1-2 combos, full timeframe continuity (FTFC), broadening formations, and the claim that the previous candle's high or low gets taken.
- Tom DeMark: TD Sequential and TD Combo 9/13 exhaustion, TDST levels, TD lines, TD price projections.
- Ichimoku: Kijun/Senkou equilibria, cloud edges, time theory.
- Darvas boxes and Livermore pivotal points.
- Gann: Square of 9, angles, time cycles.
- Hurst cycle analysis.
- Murrey Math.
For each, give the exact algorithmic definition, what it predicts about the next liquidity taken or its timing, any published statistics, and an honest evidence grade. Then test the most DOL-relevant claims on local data against distance-matched random baselines, reusing the study's methods (skeptic.final.md, bias_dol.final.md). Daily data: study/bias_data (SPX, NASDAQ, BTC, EURUSD, WTI, GOOG). Intraday data: study/smt_data/cme. Map overlaps with what is already covered (Taylor 3-day cycle, CRT and previous-candle states, AMD and the Asia range, open-relative bias), so that only genuinely new information leads to proposals. Examples: FTFC as a bias-table mode, TDST as a level source, exhaustion counts as a reach cap. Each proposal must be gated by the engine's ledger.

extraLenses.title: Behavioural finance and crowd reflexivity at liquidity levels
extraLenses.prompt:
DOMAIN: BEHAVIOURAL FINANCE AND CROWD REFLEXIVITY OF LIQUIDITY. Study the behavioural mechanisms that decide where orders rest and whose stops get run:
- Disposition effect and capital-gains overhang / reference (cost-basis) prices: Shefrin & Statman; Odean 1998; Grinblatt & Han 2005; Frazzini 2006.
- Evidence from intraday futures traders: Locke & Mann 2005; Coval & Shumway 2005 (CBOT traders take more afternoon risk after morning losses).
- Break-even supply and 'trapped traders' after failed breakouts.
- Cost-basis distributions: the anchored-VWAP cost basis of recent buyers, and crypto on-chain realised price or in/out-of-the-money address maps where TradingView offers such data.
- Attention and salience (Barber & Odean 2008): which levels are 'obvious' on standard charts and in popular free indicators.
- Herding and retail flow: retail options/0DTE, retail apps.
- Reflexivity of the SMC/ICT crowd. Since about 2020 many traders watch the same EQH/EQL/FVG/PDH levels. Has that crowding moved stops further away, made micro-sweeps deeper, or led to front-running of obvious levels? Test pre-2019 vs post-2021 sub-periods on the local data (study/bias_data, study/smt_data/cme) with the study's distance-matched random-level baseline.
- Cognitive biases of the indicator's own user that ux_design.final.md does not already cover: automation bias, outcome bias from reached-target stamps, overreaction to live PoT ticks.
Grade the evidence with numbers. Propose only designs that could change scoring or the trader's experience, each measurable by the engine's ledger: for example, an 'obviousness' or cost-basis feature, era-aware priors, or display safeguards.

result.summary: Option-implied volatility is a real but second-order PoT input once the engine has a good realised forecast, and it matters most at daily horizons. Against the current engine (ATR14 unit, flat 50-bar sigma), an IV level shaped by a time-of-day clock cuts H-bar touch log-loss by 2.5-6.8% on ES/NQ/RTY 1H. This lens's first pass overstated IV, because it only compared against a slow realised level. Against the TIME-3-style clock with a fast deseasonalised level, IV alone is 1.5-6% worse on ES 1H, NQ, ES 5m, CL and BTC. A geometric blend L^(1-w)*(kappa*IV^2)^w adds +0.3 to +1.6% (ES +0.5-0.6%, RTY +1.3-1.6%, CL +0.5%, BTC +0.3-0.5%; NQ and ES 5m n.s.). At 1 day on SPX, VIX1D, VIX9D and VIX beat ATR14 by 5.4%, 3.4% and 1.3%, and HAR+VIX1D lifts the out-of-sample R2 of next-day variance from 0.32 to 0.50. Alignment decides the value: request.security("D", close[1], lookahead_on) on an RTH-only index is stale from 16:15 to 09:30. That costs 1-1.5 pp intraday, and on daily charts VIX1D's edge falls from +5.4% to +0.9% while VIX9D keeps +2.5%. The fix is a fresh 16:15 close latched from an hourly [close[1], time_close[1]] request. Raw IV overstates touches (VRP: realised variance is 0.51-0.75 x IV^2; sd scale about 0.70 for VIX and 0.83 for VIX1D), so the options-implied "2 x delta" PoT is a biased-high benchmark. The VRP scale depends on the term structure: about 0.63 in contango and about 0.90 in backwardation for both IV and ATR, and a VIX/VIX3M or VIX9D/VIX state key adds +0.4 to +1.6% out of sample in two periods. Release bars carry 3.9x (08:30 CPI/NFP) and 4.8x (FOMC 14:00) the normal variance, and VIX1D already prices event days (excess only x1.06-1.15 vs x2 against RV). So event variance must be added with a realised level, redistributed with a VIX1D level, and redistributed in proportion w with a blend. log(VIX1D/VIX) flags event eves with AUC 0.87, but recall drops to 45-65% in 2025-26, so it can only cross-check the manual calendar. Calendar effects are small and contradict the folklore: OPEX Friday variance x0.86, first trading day x1.31, no post-OPEX range expansion, and no pinning beyond the null. Expected-move bands (SPX +/-1 sigma from VIX: one side touched on about 33% of days, close inside 80%) are context lines, not liquidity.

concepts.name: Implied-volatility index as forward sigma (VIX family, OVX, GVZ, DVOL)
concepts.definition: Annualised option-implied sigma of the underlying over a fixed tenor. Daily sigma = IV/100/sqrt(252) (sqrt(365) for 24/7 DVOL). TradingView tickers: CBOE:VIX, CBOE:VIX1D, CBOE:VIX9D, CBOE:VIX3M, CBOE:VVIX, CBOE:VXN, CBOE:RVX, CBOE:VXD, CBOE:OVX, CBOE:GVZ, TVC:MOVE (bp yield vol, not mappable), DERIBIT:DVOL. Cboe indices are delayed for free users. VIX1D is RTH-only with TV history from 2023-04 (Cboe backfill from 2022-05).
concepts.dolRole: Sets the variance scale of the PoT horizon: how far price is likely to travel within H bars, hence which pools are reachable and how likely each touch is.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Daily-to-monthly horizons: Poon & Granger 2003 (93 studies), Christensen & Prabhala 1998, Blair Poon Taylor 2001, Busch et al. 2011; counter-evidence Becker et al. 2007. [T] 1-day SPX touch vs ATR14: VIX1D +5.3%, VIX9D +3.4%, VIX +1.3%. Intraday the increment over a fast deseasonalised realised level is only +0.3 to +1.6% (moderate-weak).
concepts.engineNotes: No IV request. Requests are at 923-925, 939 and 981-982 (6 of 40).

concepts.name: Variance risk premium and the unbiased-sigma scaling
concepts.definition: Risk-neutral variance exceeds realised variance on average, so sigma_P = s*IV. [T] Realised/IV^2 = 0.51-0.66 for VIX and 0.75 for VIX1D. Touch-fitted sd scale is about 0.67-0.74 for VIX (0.57-0.89 by year) and 0.83-0.84 for VIX1D (0.79-0.86 by year). Learn kappa online as a slow EWMA of realised level / IV^2.
concepts.dolRole: Without scaling, IV-based PoT overstates every touch; with a learned kappa, IV can enter the engine's units without recalibrating the surface.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Carr & Wu 2009 (strongly negative index VRP); Albers 2025 (VIX1D overestimates); [T] raw IV PoT mean 0.37 vs 0.25 observed (VIX, 1-day) and 0.31 vs 0.24 (VIX1D).
concepts.engineNotes: Not applicable until IV is fed; X1-1 adds a unit-preserving kappa.

concepts.name: VIX1D (1-day implied vol) and its intraday artefact
concepts.definition: SPX same-day IV from 0DTE+1DTE SPXW options. The 16:15 close prices the next session. Because of its methodology it rises through RTH and falls overnight ([T] non-event days: log(open/prev close) -0.19, log(close/open) +0.21), so only the daily close is usable.
concepts.dolRole: Best 1-day sigma for S&P-linked charts. It already prices scheduled events at the day level.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Albers 2025 JFM; Zhang, Ruan & Zhang 2023 FRL; overnight-bias paper summary. [T] HAR R2 0.32 to 0.50; 1-day touch +5.3% vs ATR14; event-day excess variance only x1.06-1.15 vs VIX1D.
concepts.engineNotes: none

concepts.name: Non-repainting IV alignment (fresh vs stale close)
concepts.definition: request.security(sym,"D",close[1],lookahead_on) on an RTH-only index returns close(D-1) from 16:15 on D to 09:30 on D+1 (Thursday's close over weekends). The fresh alternative: request [close[1], time_close[1]] at f_tfSafe("60") and latch the value when the closed bar's NY close time is 16:00-16:30.
concepts.dolRole: Decides whether IV improves or degrades PoT.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [T] ES 1H H6 vs the TIME-3 level: VIX1D stale -3.7% vs fresh -0.8%. Daily chart: VIX1D +5.4% (same close) vs +0.9% (lagged); VIX9D +3.4% vs +2.5%.
concepts.engineNotes: Existing requests use the [1]+lookahead idiom (923-981); there is no IV request yet.

concepts.name: Root mapping of index IV to chart symbol, with fallback
concepts.definition: syminfo.root/ticker/basecurrency mapping: ES/SPX/SPY to VIX1D (horizon <= 1.5 days, intraday), VIX9D (<= 9 days) or VIX; NQ/NDX/QQQ to VXN; RTY/IWM to RVX; YM/DIA to VXD; CL/USO to OVX; GC/GLD/XAUUSD to GVZ; BTC to DERIBIT:DVOL. Custom override via input.symbol. Unmapped symbols get no IV (w=0); beta-scaled VIX is not used.
concepts.dolRole: Makes forward sigma available on most liquid charts without user setup.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [T] Proxy VIX on NQ +0.1% (n.s.) and RTY +0.9 to +1.6% over TIME-3. Ratio modulation ATR*sqrt(VIX/EMA60) lost 0.2-1.0% (ES, NQ, ES 5m, BTC), so beta mapping for stocks is rejected. VXN, RVX and VXD were not testable natively (Cboe CDN blocked).
concepts.engineNotes: none

concepts.name: Fast deseasonalised realised level x volatility clock (realised benchmark)
concepts.definition: Per-bar Garman-Klass-plus-gap variance divided by the bucket's expected share, EWMA span 50, times the share of the next H bars (TIME-3).
concepts.dolRole: The dominant PoT improvement. IV is an add-on to it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [T] vs ATR14: ES 1H +7.6% (H6), +4.8% (H12); NQ +5.4%; RTY +5.9%; ES 5m +1.4%; BTC +0.6%. Session_stats and ict_time agree.
concepts.engineNotes: potSig = ta.stdev(chg, potLen) at 916 is flat and time-blind and was the worst model; the surface unit is ATR14 (1284-1300, 1527-1532); the horizon is fixed bars (183, 305).

concepts.name: Geometric IV-realised blend gated by proper scores
concepts.definition: Lb = L^(1-w) * (kappa*IV_day/bpd)^w with w in {0, 0.25, 0.5} chosen by TIME-4 probe log-loss (>= 2000 resolved probes, z <= -2 vs w=0); fwdV = clockShare(H) * Lb.
concepts.dolRole: Adds forward-looking level information where it helps on the user's own chart, and is a no-op where it does not.
concepts.engineNotes: No per-model proper score; f_calMult (1376-1384) is a hit/expected ratio.

concepts.name: Term-structure state (VIX/VIX3M, VIX9D/VIX) as a PoT calibration key
concepts.definition: Three states: VIX9D/VIX < 0.95, 0.95-1.05, >= 1.05 (or VIX/VIX3M < 0.90, 0.90-1.00, >= 1.00). The sd scale rises from about 0.63 (contango) to about 0.90 (backwardation) for both IV and ATR models.
concepts.dolRole: In backwardation trailing sigma and IV both under-reach, so far pools are more reachable than the model says.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [T] OOS log-loss +0.4 to +1.6% for ATR and IV models in 2011-18 and 2022-26. Mechanism: Johnson 2017 JFQA (slope = price of variance risk).
concepts.engineNotes: Surface rows are keyed by htfBias only (1286).

concepts.name: Options-implied event detection (VIX1D/VIX inversion)
concepts.definition: lr = log(VIX1D/VIX) at the prior 16:15 close; z = lr - median of the previous 20; flag when z >= 0.20. Raw lr is about +0.07 before events vs -0.21 otherwise.
concepts.dolRole: Warns that the next session holds a scheduled catalyst (bigger, earlier runs) and catches calendar gaps.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [T] AUC 0.87 (FOMC 0.86, CPI 0.84, NFP 0.83), 2022-25. z >= 0.20: precision 0.45-0.58, recall 0.70-0.71 (2022-25), 9/20 events in 2025-26. Raw >= 0 recall fell from 0.79 to 0.60. Detector-driven variance bumps hurt with a realised level.
concepts.engineNotes: No calendar or flag; TIME-8 and ASSET-5 propose manual lists.

concepts.name: Event-day and event-hour volatility premia (FOMC, CPI, NFP)
concepts.definition: The release bar's variance multiple vs the same hour on other days, and day-level excess. Event variance must be added with a realised level and redistributed (day total kept) with an implied level; a blend redistributes the share w.
concepts.dolRole: Concentrates the probability of reaching distant pools into the release window; fixes timing and ETA.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Ederington & Lee 1993/1996, Lee 2012. [T] ES 1H: 08:30 bar x3.87 (median x6.7), FOMC 14:00 x4.75 (median x8.0). Event-window log-loss improves 7.6% (realised level, add m=7) and the rest of the event day 0.5389 to 0.5293 (VIX1D level, redistribute). SPX event days run about x2 vs RV and x1.06-1.15 vs VIX1D.
concepts.engineNotes: none; the horizon is fixed bars (183, 305).

concepts.name: Calendar volatility events (OPEX, triple witching, turn of month, month/quarter end, Russell recon)
concepts.definition: Third Friday (quarterly = witching), first trading day of the month, last trading day, last Friday of June. Measured as daily variance vs a 22-day RV forecast.
concepts.dolRole: Small adjustments to expected reach on those days; dispels the OPEX target folklore.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [T] OPEX Friday x0.86 [0.76, 0.99], witching x0.81, TOM day 1 x1.31 [1.19, 1.45], month-end x0.98, quarter-end x0.92 (n.s.), Russell x1.25 (n.s.). Post-OPEX weekly range x0.97 (t -1.9): no window of weakness. Golez & Jackwerth pinning was 1992-2009 only.
concepts.engineNotes: none

concepts.name: Option pinning / max pain as a target
concepts.definition: The expiry close is drawn to the large-open-interest or ATM strike.
concepts.dolRole: Would make a strike a Friday DOL target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [T] Close within 0.5% of the strike nearest Monday's open: 20.0% on OPEX weeks vs 20.3% on other weeks (SPX). Pinning documented only for 1992-2009 serial expiries; Whelan 2025 disputes it. No open-interest data in Pine.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; do not add.

concepts.name: Expected-move bands (+/- IV*sqrt(t), straddle-implied)
concepts.definition: EM = S*IV*sqrt(t/252) anchored at the prior close (IV measurement) or the open. A straddle-based EM is about 0.8 sigma.
concepts.dolRole: Forward-looking stretch context next to the historical reach bands; not liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [T] SPX 1-day +/-sigma(VIX): either side touched 0.33, close inside 0.80. VIX1D: 0.47 and 0.73. Weekly +/-VIX*sqrt(5/252): 0.32-0.37 touched, 79-82% inside. Open +/- 1 ADR touched 0.26-0.29; noise area 0.68-0.72. tastytrade straddle-EM weekly 57%; FlashAlpha 0DTE 71%.
concepts.engineNotes: Reach bands (showReach 173; f_reachD 1325-1338; 2112-2115) are historical ATR-unit excursion quantiles.

concepts.name: Market-implied probability of touch (about 2 x delta)
concepts.definition: Driftless reflection: P(touch) = 2*Phi(-d/(sigma_IV*sqrt(T))), about 2*|delta|.
concepts.dolRole: External benchmark the engine's PoT should beat in log-loss.
concepts.evidenceNotes: tastylive 20-year SPY: touch about 2x expiry-ITM, IV overstated, put side about half of theory. [T] Raw IV PoT log-loss 3% (VIX1D) to 10% (VIX) worse than calibrated; bins 0.71 predicted vs 0.58 observed.
concepts.engineNotes: Trial (375-395) stores only pBase; no displayed-PoT grading.

concepts.name: Earnings event variance (stocks)
concepts.definition: Expected jump on a known report date; options price it via the term structure. earnings.future_time gives the next report (live); request.earnings gives history.
concepts.dolRole: Stock pools reached through earnings are news gaps; the horizon variance must include the jump.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Dubinsky, Johannes, Kaeck & Seeger 2019 RFS; ORATS actual/implied about 0.85 (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: none

concepts.name: Intraday IV dynamics and IV crush after releases
concepts.definition: IV falls after scheduled releases as uncertainty resolves (VIX decline over about 45 minutes after FOMC); VIX1D has a methodological intraday drift.
concepts.dolRole: Only daily closes should feed the level; post-release variance is lower than the pre-release IV implies.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Ederington & Lee 1996; FRBSF WP 2019-12; VIX1D overnight-bias paper summary; [T] VIX1D OHLC shape.
concepts.engineNotes: Handled by the latch design in X1-1.

proposals.title: Implied-level blend in the forward variance: root mapping, fresh 16:15 latch, unit-preserving kappa, w gated by proper scores
proposals.rationale: IV adds level information the realised forecast lacks: +0.5-0.6% (ES 1H), +1.3-1.6% (RTY), +0.5% (CL), +0.3-0.5% (BTC) over the TIME-3 level; +2.5-6.8% over the current engine on 1H index futures; +2.5-5.4% at daily horizons. It is a clean no-op where no IV maps or where the scorecard rejects it.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_POT, display.none): ivMode Auto/Custom/Off; ivCust = input.symbol; ivWIn Auto/0/0.25/0.5. Pure helper f_ivMap(hDays), with hDays = H*chartS/86400: S&P roots to CBOE:VIX1D (intraday and hDays <= 1.5), CBOE:VIX9D (<= 9) or CBOE:VIX; NQ to VXN; RTY to RVX; YM to VXD; CL to OVX; GC to GVZ; BTC to DERIBIT:DVOL (ann 365, no latch). One request after line 939: [ivC1, ivTc1] = request.security(ivSym, f_tfSafe("60"), [close[1], time_close[1]], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on, ignore_invalid_symbol = true). Latch ivDay := ivC1 when the NY minute of ivTc1 is in [960, 990] (official close; never intraday VIX1D); ivVar = (ivDay/100)^2/ivAnn. Learn kappa (slow EWMA, half-life about 250 days, cumulative warm start) of clkLf*bpd/ivVar. Lb = clkLf^(1-w)*(kappa*ivVar/bpd)^w; TIME-3 fwdV = v(H)*Lb. Without TIME-3: surface unit = aU^(1-w)*(kappa_a*close*sqrt(ivVar/bpd))^w at 1307, 1318 and 1527-1532, with sigma consistent at 1304 and 1360. w is chosen daily from TIME-4 probes (6 per bar, k = 1, 2, 3 ATR x side, 2H-block clustered log-loss): the lowest log-loss with >= 2000 resolved probes and z <= -2 vs w=0, held 5 days. QPOT-04 pPot grading measures the displayed effect on DOL trials. Display: Terminal 'sigma CLOCK+IV(VIX1D .25)'; Clean tooltip only.
proposals.risk: Holiday half-days (add a 13:00-13:30 latch fallback). No gain on NQ and ES 5m (the gate keeps w = 0). VXN, RVX and VXD only proxy-tested. Data permissions handled by ignore_invalid_symbol (w = 0). Daily charts get a one-day-stale latch, hence VIX9D there.

proposals.title: Event-aware horizon variance: release-bar multiplier with add-vs-redistribute rule
proposals.rationale: Release bars carry 3.9-4.8x (median 6.7-8x) normal variance. Event-window log-loss improves 7.6% (realised level, additive) and the whole event day improves with an implied level when redistributed. Plain addition double-counts because VIX1D already prices the event day.
proposals.spec: In TIME-3's f_fwdVar walk, a bucket containing an ASSET-5/TIME-8 event timestamp gets variance factor m (default 4.0, i.e. sigma x2; allowed 1-8; grid optimum 7 on ES 2025-26). Other buckets of the same trading day get 1 - wIv*(m-1)*s_e/(S_day - s_e), clipped to [0.2, 1], with s_e and S_day from clkA*clkD. So wIv = 0 means pure add and wIv = 1 means pure redistribute (day total kept). On charts <= 15m spread over [evT, evT + evMin). No new request. The ledger uses ASSET-5's t.news split and probe log-loss within event windows.
proposals.risk: Stale or wrong date lists (user-maintained). The m magnitudes rest on n = 20 ES events. Requires TIME-3 (fallback: apply m to bars inside the horizon in the aU unit sum).

proposals.title: Term-structure state (VIX9D/VIX or VIX/VIX3M) as a PoT calibration key
proposals.rationale: In backwardation both IV and ATR under-reach (sd scale 0.87-0.93 vs 0.62-0.64 in contango). A state-keyed scale improves log-loss out of sample by +0.4 to +1.6%, replicated in 2011-18 and 2022-26.
proposals.spec: Requests (deduplicated with X1-1/X1-4) with the same 16:15 latch for CBOE:VIX and CBOE:VIX9D (or VIX3M). tsState = 0/1/2 at VIX9D/VIX < 0.95, 0.95-1.05, >= 1.05 (VIX/VIX3M: 0.90/1.00). Add as the QPOT-03 potKey option 'Term structure': 3 surface rows plus the pooled row, partial pooling n/(n+40), bump with tsState[H] in step 0 (1527-1532), query rows in f_empPoT (1284). Alternative: per-state sigma multiplier learned from TIME-4 probes, clipped to [0.8, 1.6]. Default on for US-index-linked symbols; offered to the scorecard elsewhere. Terminal row 'TERM BACKWARDATION/CONTANGO'.
proposals.risk: Backwardation cells are thin (5-8% of days). Index-specific. +2 requests (about 9-10 of 40 total).

proposals.title: Options-implied event flag (VIX1D/VIX relative inversion) as a calendar cross-check
proposals.rationale: Calendars break (shutdown shifts, Fed revisions). The options market prices tomorrow's event at the 16:15 close (AUC 0.87), but recall is 45-71% and regime-dependent, so the flag is a check, not a variance source.
proposals.spec: On each new latched VIX1D/VIX close push lr = log(v1d/vix) into array tsHist (size 21); zEv = lr - array.median of the previous 20; evLikely = zEv >= 0.20. If evLikely and no ASSET-5 entry in the next session: HUD/Clean tooltip '⚑ Options price an event next session' and an optional alert() 'Implied event not in calendar'. If an entry exists but zEv < 0: tooltip 'calendar event, options calm'. No variance change from the detector alone. Works for all USD-linked symbols (SPX options as macro barometer); 1-2 requests shared with X1-1/X1-3.
proposals.risk: False flags on unlisted releases (useful anyway). Recall falls in high-VIX regimes.

proposals.title: Expected-move band display (+/-1 sigma options-implied, day or week)
proposals.rationale: Traders reason with the expected move. A forward-looking companion to the historical reach bands, with honest measured coverage (SPX one side touched about 15-24% of days, close inside 73-80%), so it is framed as context, not a target.
proposals.spec: Input emShow Off/Day/Week (G_DOL, display.none, default Off so the Clean look is unchanged). On each new latched ivDay: emAnchor := close, emBar := bar_index, em = emAnchor*ivDay/100/sqrt(ivAnn) (raw, market convention). Week mode: on the Friday latch use the 30-day index x sqrt(5). Two dotted lines from emBar to bar_index+extBars at emAnchor +/- em plus a small 'EM ±x%' label; delete the previous set (3 drawings). Tooltip states the measured coverage and that it is not a target.
proposals.risk: Clutter (default off). Users may treat it as a target.

proposals.title: Options-implied PoT graded in the ledger as an external benchmark
proposals.rationale: Shows the user the market's touch odds and, on their own chart, that raw options odds overstate touches (log-loss 3-10% worse than calibrated) and whether the engine beats them.
proposals.spec: pIV = f_erfc(d/(sqrt(2)*close*sqrt(v(H)*ivVar/bpd))), raw (no kappa). Trial gets float pIV (375-395), set in f_openTrial (1426). f_book (1461) accumulates the log-loss of pIV next to QPOT-04's pPot. Full panel 'PoT vs OPTIONS LL .58 vs .63 · opt. mean 47% vs obs 33%'. Tooltip 'options-implied touch ≈ 48% (raw)'.
proposals.risk: Users may confuse it with the engine's PoT (label clearly). Depends on QPOT-04.

proposals.title: Calendar variance cells in the clock (turn-of-month day 1, monthly OPEX Friday)
proposals.rationale: Reliable daily-variance shifts that VIX does not price: TOM day 1 x1.31 [1.19, 1.45], OPEX Friday x0.86, witching x0.81. It also replaces OPEX folklore with measured effects (no post-OPEX range expansion, no pinning).
proposals.spec: In TIME-3's day factor add clkT[3] (normal/TOM1/OPEX), learned like clkD (additive EWMA, cumulative warm start, floors, shrink n/(n+20)). tom1 = month(time_tradingday, tz) != month(time_tradingday[1], tz) on the first bar of the day; int dom = dayofmonth(time_tradingday, tz); opex = dayofweek(time_tradingday, tz) == dayofweek.friday and dom >= 15 and dom <= 21. Default for index-linked symbols; the scorecard decides elsewhere.
proposals.risk: Thin cells. TOM is confounded with the ISM release (harmless for variance).

proposals.title: Earnings-aware horizon variance for stocks
proposals.rationale: Earnings sessions carry several times normal variance (Dubinsky et al. 2019); stock pools taken through earnings are news gaps, and the PoT horizon should know about them.
proposals.spec: Live: ne = earnings.future_time; if inside the horizon, the reaction session (the next one for after-close reports) gets variance factor mE (X1-2 add rule). mE is learned per symbol from history via request.earnings(syminfo.tickerid, earnings.actual, barmerge.gaps_on, barmerge.lookahead_on): at each past report, the ratio of reaction-session range^2 to the median of the prior 20 sessions; EWMA of the last 8, clipped to [1, 25]. HUD '⚑ EARNINGS in 2d'. ASSET-5 t.news split for trials spanning a report.
proposals.risk: Before/after-market timing ambiguity. +1 request. Stocks only.

result.summary: Positioning data mostly tells you how volatile the next session will be, not which way it goes or where the target is. I tested this on SPX daily data from 2011 to 2026 (n = 2,665 days) using yesterday's SqueezeMetrics GEX. The day's range in ATR20 units falls from 1.154 in the lowest GEX quintile to 0.803 in the highest. That effect adds to the VIX-implied daily σ (R² 0.192 → 0.231, t = -10.8). Low gamma also raises the upside reach: P(PDH traded) at a fixed distance moves with t = -6.3, while P(PDL) does not move. PDH breaks hold more often under low gamma (36.5% close back inside vs 44.9% under high gamma). Pine-computable proxies (VIX/VIX3M plus the VIX-implied σ in ATR units) recover about 75% of the GEX gain. 0DTE studies mostly find damping, not amplification, and Cboe puts market-maker hedging at about 0.2% of SPX liquidity. Max pain is folklore for indices: 46.9-74.8% of SPX closes already land within 1% of an earlier price with no options data, which matches the vendors' "48%" claims. The vanna/charm "window of weakness" shows no effect that holds in both 1999-2018 and 2019-2026. The only weak calendar effect: monthly-OPEX Fridays have a 6-8% smaller range. COT extremes do not predict which side of the weekly range ES takes first (723 weeks, null). An OI flush on the sweep bar does not mark the pool as spent (217 BTC sweeps); an OI build may lean toward breakout, but the sample is too small. Real Binance funding data (BTC 1h, 2019-2025, 7,444 races) partly supports the crowded-side idea. Negative funding gets BSL run first +5.2 ± 2.1 pp more often than geometry predicts. SSL sweeps continue (cascade) +6.1 ± 2.5 pp more often when longs are crowded and reverse more often when they are not. Both signs hold in both halves of the sample. Options OI by strike is not available in TradingView, so GEX walls, zero gamma and max pain can only come in as pasted text. The recommended design: a date-stamped, auto-expiring text box that forms an "OPT" level family, graded per chart by the shadow ledger before it may affect scoring, with max pain shadow-only by default.

concepts.name: Dealer gamma exposure (GEX) regime
concepts.definition: Classic GEX = Σ sign_i · Γ_i · OI_i · 100 · S² · 0.01, with calls +1 and puts -1 (dealers assumed long calls and short puts). Flow-signed variants infer the dealer side from trade data. Normalise with a trailing 252-day rank. Publication is after the close, so use GEX[t-1] for session t.
concepts.dolRole: A volatility state: it scales how far price travels in H bars (PoT, reach) and whether a level break holds. It does not pick the side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T1 on SPX 2011-26: range/ATR from Q1 to Q5 = 1.154 to 0.803. Incremental to the VIX-implied σ: t = -10.8, R² 0.192 → 0.231. P(PDH) t = -6.3; P(PDL) no effect. Next-day autocorrelation -0.21 (t = -2.5) when gamma is low. Literature: Ni, Pearson, Poteshman & White RFS 2021 (negative gamma means larger absolute returns); Barbon & Buraschi (momentum vs reversal); Baltussen et al. JFE 2021 (intraday momentum stronger on negative-gamma days).
concepts.engineNotes: potSig (916) and f_empPoT/f_potModel/f_potBase (1284-1323) are realised-only and keyed only on HTF bias. evaluate's reach (665) uses the same σ. No VIX or GEX request (923-982). Proxy route: VIX/VIX3M recovers about 75% of the GEX gain.

concepts.name: Zero-gamma / gamma flip / HVL / Volatility Trigger
concepts.definition: The spot S' at which total dealer GEX, recomputed on a grid of hypothetical spots (±10%, 0.1-0.5% steps, sticky-strike IV), crosses zero, interpolated linearly. SpotGamma's Volatility Trigger is proprietary and sits near or above it.
concepts.dolRole: Used as a regime boundary: ranges and fades above it, trends and the put wall or PDL as the draw below it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published test of the level as a target or barrier. The regime evidence is GEX's (above). The level moves by tens of points with the IV and sign assumptions.
concepts.engineNotes: Cannot be computed in Pine (no options OI by strike). Only as a pasted level (X1P-2) or a GEX NEG/POS token feeding X1P-1.

concepts.name: Call wall / put wall / absolute-gamma strike / OI walls
concepts.definition: The strike with the largest call gamma (or call OI or net call gamma), the largest put gamma, the largest |Γc|+|Γp|, or the largest OI. Aggregated over all expiries or the front expiry. Recomputed daily.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed as intraday resistance, support or magnet, and as range bounds.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor claims only. Historical high-OI strike pinning (Ni, Pearson & Poteshman 2005; Golez & Jackwerth 2012: at least $115 m per expiry 1992-2009) faded after 2016 (classic_levels P15). Round numbers act as barriers, not magnets (classic_levels 1.6).
concepts.engineNotes: No input.text_area and no level src for external levels (src 0-7, line 316; f_tierW 506-516). Would plug into the registry and pool (1211-1228, 1824-1856) or the anchors list (1931-1933).

concepts.name: Vanna flows
concepts.definition: Dealer VEX = Σ sign · vanna · OI · 100 · S · Δσ. Falling IV shrinks short-put deltas, so dealers buy back hedges (a 'vanna rally'). Vendors assume 1% spot ⇒ -10% IV.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore bias after event vol-crush: upside drift.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No peer-reviewed index test found. Mechanism only.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Charm and OPEX-week flows / 'window of weakness'
concepts.definition: Dealer CEX = Σ sign · charm · OI · 100 · S per day. OTM deltas decay into monthly OPEX, so hedges unwind ('supportive'). The 1-2 weeks after OPEX are said to be weak and wider.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed calendar bias for side and range.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T6 on SPX weekly 1999-2026: no OPEX or post-OPEX effect stable across the two halves. Post-Q weeks 1999-2018 had smaller ranges (0.938, t = -1.8), the opposite of the claim. For stocks, Stivers & Sun JBF 2013 find higher OE-week returns in S&P 100 names.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent. Folklore for index charts.

concepts.name: OPEX-day range compression
concepts.definition: Monthly option expiration Friday (third Friday; Thursday if a holiday). Day range relative to the trailing 20-day mean range.
concepts.dolRole: A small σ multiplier for the PoT on 12 days a year.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own: SPX OPEX Friday range ratio 0.940 vs 1.006 for other Fridays (2004-18, t = -1.6) and 0.995 vs 1.085 (2019-26, t = -1.4). The Monday after shows no effect. GEX drops 5.5% on the first post-OPEX session.
concepts.engineNotes: Belongs in the event calendar (asset_specific ASSET-5 / TIME-8), as a σ multiplier of about 0.93.

concepts.name: 0DTE gamma
concepts.definition: Same-session SPX/SPY options: 59% of SPX volume in 2025 (Cboe). End-of-day GEX misses them.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed intraday amplifier. The evidence says it is a damper, if anything.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Dim, Eraker & Vilkov: high 0DTE OI gamma does not propagate volatility. Adams, Fontaine & Ornthanalai: dealers are net long gamma, which lowers volatility for about 10-60 minutes. Cboe: MM hedging at most about 0.2% of SPX liquidity. Against: Brogaard, Han & Won (+1 sd volume ≈ +14% daily volatility).
concepts.engineNotes: No data in Pine. Justifies no gamma-amplification term.

concepts.name: Max pain
concepts.definition: MP = argmin_X Σ OI_call(K)·max(0, X-K) + OI_put(K)·max(0, K-X) for one expiry: the settlement price minimising holders' intrinsic value.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed expiry magnet / target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Index: own T6 base rates show 74.8% / 61.2% / 46.9% of SPX closes within 1% of the close 1 / 2 / 4 days earlier (no options data). That equals or beats vendor claims ('48% within 1% of max pain'). Only Filippou, Garcia-Ares & Zapatero 2022 (single stocks, about 0.4%/week reversal, small and illiquid names) supports a weaker form.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent. If pasted (X1P-2) it is shadow-only by default.

concepts.name: Futures open interest (TradingView _OI, end of day)
concepts.definition: Open contracts. The CME prints a daily value, published the next morning. TradingView: ticker.standard(syminfo.tickerid)+'_OI', e.g. CME_MINI:ES1!_OI, requested at '1D' on intraday charts. Use close[1] (or [2] to be strict) with lookahead_on.
concepts.dolRole: The practitioner price-OI quadrant (new longs, short covering, ...) as trend-quality context.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Hong & Yogo JFE 2012: OI growth predicts monthly commodity and macro returns (not intraday). No study on DOL or intraday targets.
concepts.engineNotes: No request. Proposed only as a shadow covariate (X1P-4).

concepts.name: Crypto perp OI intraday and the OI flush at a sweep
concepts.definition: Intraday OI candles, e.g. BINANCE:BTCUSDT.P_OI. Flush = ΔOI on the sweep bar ≤ -1 sd (trailing 48 bars); build ≥ +1 sd.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: a flush means the pool is spent (raid, reversal); a build means a breakout.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T4 (217 BTC sweeps, 2026 Binance OI): closed back inside 0.54 (flush) / 0.62 (flat) / 0.51 (build); breakout-first 0.44 / 0.44 / 0.58. So flush means spent is not supported; build means breakout is underpowered (n = 47). OI is misquoted on some venues (Giagkiozis & Said 2023) and clears 25-70% in cascades.
concepts.engineNotes: Sweep handling (1566-1585) is price-only. Proposed only as a covariate (X1P-4).

concepts.name: Funding rate / premium index (crowded side)
concepts.definition: Binance funding F = P̄ + clamp(0.01% - P̄, ±0.05%) per 8h, settled at 00/08/16 UTC. F < 0 iff the 8h premium P̄ < -0.05%. TradingView: BINANCE:<PAIR>_PREMIUM. Extremes: F < 0 (shorts crowded), F ≥ 0.03%/8h or top decile of the trailing 180 days (longs crowded).
concepts.dolRole: Side tilt (a crowded side's stops get run) and the reading of SSL sweeps (crowded-long sweeps cascade).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own T3 (BTC 1h 2019-25, 7,444 races): F < 0 gives BSL first +5.2 ± 2.1 pp (sweep bars +5.9 ± 3.0). Joint with momentum: funding rank -0.062 (t = -2.2), z72 +0.036 (t = 4.3). SSL swept with rank ≥ 70% gives continuation +6.1 ± 2.5; rank < 30% gives -5.2 ± 2.5. Signs hold in both halves. Memon et al. 2026: +0.51%/24h after extreme negative funding, none for positive. Moderate-weak: one asset, one venue.
concepts.engineNotes: Draw vector D (1891-1897) and liqEvt raid mapping (1579-1582) carry no positioning term.

concepts.name: Long/short ratio
concepts.definition: Accounts or positions net long / net short (exchange-reported, e.g. Binance). TradingView suffix _LSR (community scripts).
concepts.dolRole: Claimed contrarian side signal.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published validation found. Not testable here (no history).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: CFTC COT hedging pressure and positioning extremes
concepts.definition: Weekly Tuesday positions released Friday 15:30 ET. Williams COT index = (net/OI - min_156w)/(max_156w - min_156w). TradingView: LibraryCOT tickers 'COT{,2,3}:<code>_<F|FO>_<metric>{_L|_S}', e.g. COT:13874A_F_NCP_L.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: an extreme picks which side of the weekly range is taken.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Hedging-pressure premia are strong at monthly horizons (Bessembinder 1992; de Roon, Nijman & Veld 2000; Kang, Rouwenhorst & Tang 2020). Wang 2003: speculators show continuation, hedgers are contrarian (S&P futures). Sanders, Irwin & Merrin 2009: null. Own T5 (ES 2008-26, 723 weeks): speculator slope -0.017 (t = -0.3), hedger +0.073 (t = 1.4), non-monotonic. Null for DOL use.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent. Not worth request slots.

concepts.name: Short interest / days to cover
concepts.definition: Shares short (FINRA, twice monthly); short ratio; days to cover = SI / ADV. TradingView only has FINRA:<SYM>_SHORT_VOLUME (daily short-sale activity).
concepts.dolRole: None at intraday horizons.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Rapach, Ringgenberg & Zhou JFE 2016: annual out-of-sample R² 13.24% for aggregate returns (monthly horizon). Hong et al.: days to cover in the cross-section. Not relevant to which pool is hit next.
concepts.engineNotes: Data not available as short interest. Irrelevant to the forecasting problem.

concepts.name: Crowded side via price momentum proxy
concepts.definition: Trailing return z-score (24/72/168 bars) as a crowding proxy. Race the nearest unswept BSL against the nearest unswept SSL, compared with calibrated gambler's-ruin geometry.
concepts.dolRole: Side selection: whether the crowded side's stops are run or the trend continues.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Earlier run of this lens (re-run identical): BTC z72 top decile gives BSL first +8.1 ± 2.3 pp (continuation, t = 4.6). Pooled CME/FX: no consistent effect; after sweeps, a weak weekly-horizon contrarian lean (z168 ±5 pp).
concepts.engineNotes: D's structure sV and displacement mV (1892-1893) carry momentum. There is no explicit trailing-return term. Funding adds a contrarian term on top (T3).

concepts.name: Raid vs breakout conditioned on positioning
concepts.definition: After a pool is traded through: a close back inside (raid) vs a hold beyond it (breakout), and which next pool is reached first, conditioned on the gamma regime or the funding state.
concepts.dolRole: How a sweep should update the draw vector.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T1-D: PDH sweeps close back inside 0.365 ± 0.027 (low gamma) vs 0.449 ± 0.023 (high gamma); PDL shows no difference. T3: crowded-long SSL sweeps continue +6.1 pp; uncrowded ones reverse -5.2 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: 1579-1582 applies a uniform 'hold = continuation, reject = reversal' rule. Sibling lenses already found the reject → reversal mapping has no edge. The hold rate depends on the regime and on crowding.

concepts.name: External positioning level ingestion
concepts.definition: Levels or regime tokens pasted into input.text_area, one per line, as 'YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM]; TYPE; PRICE[; EXPIRY]'. Active from the stamp, auto-expiring. An OPT family graded per chart by the shadow ledger before it may score.
concepts.dolRole: Lets vendor GEX walls, zero gamma, OI walls or max pain compete as targets or anchors only if they beat a distance-matched random baseline on the user's own chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The infrastructure rests on ledger theory (calib_ml CAL-3). The levels themselves have weak evidence (walls) or none (max pain). input.text_area holds up to 40,960 characters and parses line terminators (docs mirror).
concepts.engineNotes: No text-area input. The ledger grades only the selected target per group 0-3 (Trial 372-393, f_book 1461-1500, f_calMult 1376-1382). There is no per-family shadow grading yet.

proposals.title: Gamma-regime volatility state (VIX/VIX3M proxy plus an optional pasted GEX token) scaling PoT and reach on index and equity charts
proposals.rationale: The strongest positioning effect found. Dealer gamma moves the next-day range about ±15-20% and P(PDH) about 16 pp at a fixed ATR distance, incrementally to VIX. About 75% of it is reproducible in Pine. The engine's σ (916) and empirical surface (1284-1323) are regime-blind. PoT calibration (Brier score) on the ledger measures the gain directly.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_POT, display.none): grOn, grSym = 'CBOE:VIX', grSym3 = 'CBOE:VIX3M'. SERIES, after 917, two top-level calls: iv1 = request.security(grSym, 'D', close[1], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on, ignore_invalid_symbol = true) and the same for iv3. grTS = iv1/iv3. grReg = 2 if grTS ≥ 1.0, 1 if ≥ 0.90, else 0. Use only when syminfo.type is index, futures, stock or fund; the user can override the symbols for other assets. A pasted 'GEX; NEG' token (X1P-2) can force grReg = 2. STATE: var array<float> grSt (18) holding, per (regime, side), [Σ realised squared H-bar excursion in ATR², Σ model σ²·H, n windows]. Update in step 0 next to f_bump (1527-1531) using grReg[H], fwdHi, fwdLo, potSig[H] and aH. Use: kσ = sqrt(r̃/ref), where r̃ = (n·ratio_bs + α·ref)/(n + α), α = 30·0.6·H, clamped to [0.75, 1.35] and 1 while n < 20·H. It multiplies the σ in f_potModel (1303) and in evaluate's reach (665). Optionally key the empirical surface on (HTF bias, grReg), with the existing fallback. Sub-item: in step 3 (1579-1582) on index charts, halve the 'reject = reversal' evt for buy-side sweeps when grReg = 2 (T1-D), shadow first. Ledger: add pReg to Trial next to pBase. Report the Brier score of pReg vs pBase with a block-bootstrap CI. Default on only if the CI excludes 0 on ES1!, NQ1!, SPY and an index. Merge with the x1_implied_vol VIX unit so VIX enters once.
proposals.risk: 2 requests (6 → 8 of 40). VIX is US-equity specific, so gate by syminfo.type and offer overrides (GVZ, OVX, BVIV untested). The daily state can lag intraday shocks. Bucket edges are fitted on SPX.

proposals.title: Pasted positioning levels (call/put wall, zero gamma, absolute gamma, OI wall, max pain): date-stamped, auto-expiring OPT family graded per chart before it may score
proposals.rationale: Traders want GEX levels and Pine cannot compute them. The levels' evidence is weak (walls) or none (max pain), so the honest design is ingestion plus per-chart grading against a distance-matched random baseline. It answers whether the vendor's wall works on this chart without letting folklore distort the DOL.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_POS, display.none): posOn; posTxt = input.text_area with lines 'YYYY-MM-DD[ HH:MM]; TYPE; PRICE[; EXPIRY]' (TYPE CW PW ZG AG OI MP LV, plus a 'GEX; NEG|POS' regime line); posMode = Display / Shadow (default) / Anchor when proven / Target when proven; posMul (SPY→SPX ×10); posOff (SPX→ES basis); posLife (sessions). Type PosLv{t0, t1, px, typ, lvId, probeBar}. Parse once on barstate.isfirst with str.split by '\n' and ';', str.trim, str.substring (guarded by length), str.tonumber and timestamp(syminfo.timezone, …). Count posErr and cap at 60 lines. Confirmed-bar step 4b (after 1586-1592): when time is in [t0, t1) and the level is within maxATR, create a pool Level with kind by side, src = next free code 'OPT', a touch rule like arrays, anchorBar = f_barAtTime(t0); remove or ghost '⌛ EXPIRED' at t1. Display = dotted lines only. Shadow = mult 0 for selection. Anchor = push px into anchors (1931-1933). Target = normal scoring with a bounded family lift. Grading: CAL-3 probes group OPT with a sub-key per type. Fallback mini-ledger posSt[g] = [n, k, Σpb, Σpb(1-pb)] per group (walls, flip, MP, generic), probe opened once per H bars when 0.25 ≤ d ≤ maxATR ATR, pb = f_potBase, outcome = touch within H, with 2H-block cluster residuals as in f_book, plus a barrier rate (close back on the approach side within 3 bars after a touch). Gate a mode beyond Shadow per group: n ≥ 40, z > 1.96 with design effect, and the lift's lower bound > 1. MP stays shadow-only unless a separate box is ticked. Panel row 'OPT 12 live · walls lift 1.08 (z 1.1, n 63) · MP shadow'. Look-ahead: levels exist only from their stamp.
proposals.risk: Daily user burden. Basis mapping changes with the futures roll. Small per-chart samples keep the gate closed for months, which is correct. The newline split must be checked on TradingView (docs say terminators are parsed). The src code collides with sibling proposals.

proposals.title: Crypto-perp funding state from the premium index: buy-side draw tilt when shorts are crowded, cascade reading of SSL sweeps when longs are crowded
proposals.rationale: Real Binance funding 2019-2025: negative funding gets BSL run first +5.2 ± 2.1 pp (sweep bars +5.9 ± 3.0). SSL sweeps continue +6.1 ± 2.5 pp when longs are crowded and reverse -5.2 ± 2.5 when they are not. Signs hold in both halves. Funding is contrarian net of momentum (t = -2.2). This matches Memon et al. 2026 (+0.51%/24h after extreme negative funding). The engine's D vector and sweep mapping ignore crowding.
proposals.spec: Input fdOn (G_FLOW, display.none). isPerp = syminfo.type == 'crypto' and str.endswith(syminfo.ticker, '.P'). premTk = syminfo.prefix + ':' + str.replace(syminfo.ticker, '.P', '') + '_PREMIUM'. fdTF = f_tfSafe('60'). prem8 = request.security(premTk, fdTF, ta.sma(close, max(1, round(28800/timeframe.in_seconds(fdTF))))[1], lookahead_on, ignore_invalid_symbol = true). fEst = prem8 + clamp(0.0001 - prem8, ±0.0005). fdSt = -1 if fEst < 0, +1 if fEst ≥ 0.0003, else 0. Detect units once (percent vs fraction) and show a warning if ambiguous. Effects, shadow first: (1) step 14 (1892-1894): drawD += wF·(fdSt == -1 ? +0.15 : fdSt == 1 ? -0.07 : 0), asymmetric like the evidence. (2) step 3 (1579-1582), kind-1 pools only: with fdSt == 1 set evt to continuation (-1) even on a close back inside; with fdSt == -1 keep the reversal evt. BSL sweeps unchanged. Ledger: store fd on Trial and CAL-3 probes. Turn wF live when, in state -1, the residual of BSL probes minus SSL probes has z > 2 with at least 100 probes per side. Turn it off if z < 0 over the last 300.
proposals.risk: The _PREMIUM ticker and its units are verified only from community scripts. Other venues may lack it, so fdSt = 0 via ignore_invalid_symbol. One asset, one venue, several cells (multiple testing). Funding regimes may shift. 1 request.

proposals.title: Log positioning covariates (ΔOI z-score, funding state, gamma regime, nearest pasted level) on every trial and probe, reported as per-bucket residuals with no scoring effect
proposals.rationale: OI flush (T4) and COT (T5) are null or underpowered on our data, but traders believe in them. Logging lets each user's ledger test them on their own market for free, turning folklore into per-chart evidence without risk to the DOL.
proposals.spec: One request: oiC = request.security(ticker.standard(syminfo.tickerid) + '_OI', syminfo.type == 'crypto' ? timeframe.period : '1D', close[1], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on, ignore_invalid_symbol = true). For CME futures this is the prior session's end-of-day value; for crypto it is intraday. dOIz = ΔOI / trailing 48-bar sd. Add fields dOIz, fd (X1P-3), gr (X1P-1) and opt (X1P-2 nearest type within 0.5 ATR, or -1) to Trial (372-393) and the CAL-3 Probe. Full accuracy view: residual Σ(y - pb)/n ± cluster SE per tercile and state, shown only when n ≥ 30 per cell. For sweep bars, add the breakout-vs-reversal residual (T4 design). Label it 'observational; no effect on targets'.
proposals.risk: 1 request. Clutter, so Full view only. Depends on CAL-3 for full value.

proposals.title: OPEX-Friday σ multiplier (×0.93) for US index and equity charts in the event calendar
proposals.rationale: Monthly-OPEX Fridays show a 6-8% smaller day range than other Fridays in both 2004-18 and 2019-26 (t = -1.6, -1.4). There is no post-OPEX weakness. A tiny, honest correction to the PoT volatility clock.
proposals.spec: Add the entry 'monthly OPEX Friday: σ × 0.93' to the asset_specific ASSET-5 / TIME-8 calendar table. Detection: dayofweek(time, 'America/New_York') == dayofweek.friday and 15 ≤ dayofmonth(time, 'America/New_York') ≤ 21; ignore holiday Thursdays. Apply only when syminfo.type is index, stock, fund or US index futures. Terminal style shows a '⚑ OPEX' tag. Scored by PoT calibration like the other calendar multipliers.
proposals.risk: Negligible: about 4% PoT reduction on 12 days a year. A weak effect could be noise.

proposals.title: Honesty notes: README and tooltips say which positioning tools are absent and why (max pain, window of weakness, COT, liquidation maps, long/short ratio)
proposals.rationale: Users expect these from commercial DOL tools, so their absence looks like 'missing features'. Our tests show them to be folklore, null, or only volatility states. Saying so builds trust and heads off complaints.
proposals.spec: README section 'Positioning data: what we use and what we don't', one line per item with the test result: max pain (T6 base-rate hurdle), OPEX window of weakness (T6), COT (T5), OI flush (T4), liquidation heatmaps (orderflow_micro B9), long/short ratio (no evidence), gamma regime (used as a volatility state, X1P-1). Tooltip on the MP type in X1P-2: 'no measured edge on indices; shadow only'.
proposals.risk: None.
